For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

authors.name: Michael Leyton, Stephen T. Dye

papers.title: Optical fiber shape sensing using picosecond spatiotemporal single-photon reflectometry
papers.summary: Inferring the three-dimensional configuration of a flexible optical fiber from a single accessible end remains a fundamental challenge in photonic sensing. Existing approaches typically require specialised multicore fibers, coherent interferometry, or distributed spectral encoding. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally different sensing paradigm in which fiber geometry is reconstructed from the spatiotemporal dynamics of returning single photons. Using a laser-engineered multimode fiber interrogated by a time-resolved 32x32 single-photon avalanche diode array, we show that fiber deformation imprints unique signatures onto the distribution and arrival time of back-reflected photons. We map these high-dimensional photon-return states onto a low-dimensional geometric manifold, enabling continuous bend-angle estimation and reconstruction of previously unseen two- and three-dimensional shapes from measurements acquired entirely at the proximal fiber end. Measurements show a median pixel-wise signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 26 dB and below 1% repeatability variation. Our results establish multimode single-photon dynamics as an information-rich channel for distributed geometric sensing, introducing a new framework for single-ended fiber shape reconstruction and minimally invasive photonic navigation.

authors.name: Harikumar K Chandrasekharan, Saba N. Khan, Muhammad Afnan Ansari, Robert R. Thomson

papers.title: Chiral high harmonic generation via coherent superposition of multi-channel interband transitions
papers.summary: Circularly polarized light, with its specific handedness, is a valuable tool for investigating the chirality related properties of materials, including their structural, electronic, magnetic and topological characteristics. This has led to efforts in creating wavelength-tunable coherent light with circular or elliptical polarization through a sub-cycle ultrafast process high-harmonic generation (HHG). Existing approaches to chiral HHG, however, typically rely on multidimensional driving fields, materials engineering or complex optical architectures. Here we uncover a distinct mechanism without such complexity, where a single linearly polarized driving field generates chiral HHG from a pristine crystal. We show that, in the Weyl semimetal NbP, one linearly polarized near-infrared driving field generates high harmonics with pronounced ellipticity. Semi-conductor Bloch equations (SBEs) reveal that this ellipticity originates from the coherent superposition of multiple interband transitions, each contributing harmonics with distinct linear polarizations and relative phases. We further substantiate this mechanism by shifting the driving photon energy into the mid-infrared, which strongly suppresses the ellipticity as the number of accessible interband transition channels is reduced. These results establish a simple and general mechanism for chiral HHG, and show that quantum materials can transform an apparently achiral driving field into polarization-tunable ultrafast chiral emission.

authors.name: Ruoxuan Ding, Chen Qian, Zhilin Li, Tianchen Hu, Chunmei Zhang, Tao Dong, Dong Wu, Li Yue, Nan-Lin Wang

papers.title: Understanding the normal state of cuprate superconductors
papers.summary: Doped holes in the CuO2 planes reside pairwise at O atoms. Their lack of net charge demotes the flanking Cu3d-O2p holes of half-filling. Below the doping-dependent pseudogap (PG) temperature, the latter are trapped between motted Cu2+ ions. Above the PG temperature, the remaining Cu3d-O2p holes are thermally demotted, initiating the strange metal (SM) phase. The PG energy at the antinodal points in the BZ decreases with increasing doping, as less Cu3d-O2p holes need to be thermally demotted. In the SM phase, the Cu3d-O2p holes hop, with Planckian scattering rate, by leaps of lattice-constant length. This gives rise to a linear resistivity. O atoms in the CuO2 plane, from Sr doping of 214 cuprates or from oxygen enrichment (OE), arrange to a charge order (CO). In 214 systems, an O superlattice (SL) forms of increasing incommensurability with doping. It saturates when a secondary SL forms. At the quantum critical point their incommensurabilities equal, causing collapse of the PG temperature. In OE cuprates, the CO dilutes the diagonal tilt of the host lattice CuO6 octahedra, causing a decreasing incommensurability with doping. Oxygen atoms are singlets in OE cuprates but triplets in 214 systems. The magnetic moment of the latter gives rise to a narrow 3D AFM doping range and to magnetic order accompanying CO (stripes). Charge-density fluctuations occur when double holes hop back and forth between O atoms of the SL and neighboring oxygen ions. Quantum oscillations result from Fermi surface reconstruction.

authors.name: Manfred Bucher

papers.title: Enabling Mie Resonances for Optomagnetism in Epitaxially Grown Garnet Nanodisks via Photonic Crystals
papers.summary: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate compatible with epitaxial growth on gadolinium gallium garnet is proposed for controlling the optomagnetic response of a single bismuth iron garnet nanodisk. The photonic environment modifies the spectral positions and relative strengths of the electric- and magnetic-dipole contributions and redistributes the optical field inside the disk. Compared with a reference nanodisk on a homogeneous substrate evaluated near the broad maximum of its summed multipolar response, the peak axial optical contribution to the inverse Faraday effect in the examined cross-sections is enhanced by factors of approximately 7.3 and 6.3 in the magnetic- and electric-dipole-dominated regimes, respectively. The enhancement reaches approximately 7.9 at the maximum of the summed multipolar scattering contributions. These results demonstrate spectral control of the magnitude and spatial distribution of the local optomagnetic response through the photonic environment, without changing the nanodisk geometry.

authors.name: P. V. Zorina, D. O. Ignatyeva, D. M. Krichevsky, V. I. Belotelov

papers.title: The landscape of quantum technology companies in 2026
papers.summary: We update our 2022 mapping of 441 quantum technology (QT) companies and examine how the industry has developed. The principal dataset now includes 1,092 companies founded with a QT focus, of which 935 remain active. Public sources and archived company websites provide evidence on company formation, technology fields and geography, alongside acquisitions, closures, valuations and involvement in artificial intelligence, defence and space. Company formation continued beyond the apparent 2018 peak in the earlier study. Computing software and applications remain the largest field, with suppliers and supporting businesses accounting for almost a third of active companies. Countries with similar company totals can have different technological profiles, and regional comparisons reveal concentrations obscured by country rankings. The first companies generally preceded the selected national policy milestones. Supporting businesses usually followed technical companies in the same jurisdiction. AI is more prevalent than defence in current company activities, while defence shows the larger increase from the earliest assessed evidence. Space relevance is documented for more than a quarter of active companies, often alongside defence involvement.

authors.name: Zeki Can Seskir, Orcun Kocak, Arsev Umur Aydinoglu

papers.title: Impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation on L-H transition in the KSTAR tokamak
papers.summary: The impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation (ERMP) on the low-to-high (L-H) confinement mode transition is investigated through dedicated experiments on the KSTAR tokamak with tungsten divertor and numerical simulations with a one-dimensional (1D) reduced transport model. Experimentally, under matched conditions, the ERMP inhibits the L-H transition, whereas the reference discharge without ERMP enters H-mode. The ERMP enhances edge electron temperature fluctuations and the turbulence decorrelation rate, and flattens the toroidal rotation, reducing the edge $E\times B$ velocity shear below the threshold required for turbulence suppression. An extended 1D predator-prey model, which incorporates toroidal flow evolution and realistic radial profile of the magnetic perturbation due to plasma response field, reproduces the experimental trends of enhanced turbulence, reduced ExB flow shear, and inhibited L-H transition. These findings contribute to a better understanding of how ERMP affects L-H transition dynamics in tungsten divertor environments and offer a valuable reference for the application of ERMP in current and future fusion devices.

authors.name: Y. Zhang, M. Jiang, K. X. Han, W. H. Ko, S. M. Yang, J. D. Hu, Z. B. Guo, M. J. Choi, J. W. Juhn, J. Lee, J. H. Lee, Y. H. Lee, Y. F. Liu, X. B. Li, Y. R. Zhu, G. Q. Dong, G. Z. Hao

papers.title: Ultracompact and Nonvolatile On-chip Switch Based on DBS and PSO Algorithms
papers.summary: A 1x2 photonic switch based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI)-Sb2Se3 hybrid platform is inverse-designed using direct binary search (DBS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms. The nonvolatile on-chip switch is designed to consist of minimum switchable phase-change units and operates based on the en-masse switching of all Sb2Se3 cells from crystalline to amorphous and vice-versa. The device has a small footprint of only 6.3umx31um. At the wavelength of 1550nm, it exhibits an insertion loss of less than 0.96dB, and its crosstalk is measured to be less than -12dB within the three-dimensional (3D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations.

authors.name: Sanaz Zarei

papers.title: Inverse Design of an On-chip Phase-Change Switch Composed of Sparse Heterogeneous Metasurfaces
papers.summary: Photonic switches are exploited for optical signal routing and control within optical communication systems. The integration of phase change materials with silicon photonic switches overcomes the drawbacks of the state-of-the-art photonic switches based on electro-optic and thermo-optic effects. In this work, a 1x2 on-chip switch with a footprint of 6.3umx31um based on on-chip one-dimensional metasurfaces is inverse-designed. The on-chip metasurfaces are heterogeneous, which their meta-atoms can be composed of either SiO2 or the phase-change material Sb2Se3. This helps to the realization of higher extinction ratio between the switch outputs, especially at the amorphous state which has a small refractive index contrast to that of the silicon. To benefit from structural, fabrication and switching simplicity, sparse parameterization is followed in the inverse design of the switch using ternary search (TS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms.

authors.name: Sanaz Zarei

papers.title: Rotationally Symmetric Lattice Boltzmann Pseudopotential Methods for Porous Media Applications
papers.summary: Pseudopotential models are a well established approach for multiphase and multicomponent simulations using the lattice Boltzmann method. Although not the most accurate, they are often chosen for ease of implementation and adaptability. A drawback of the models are spurious currents at the interfaces and particularly at solid walls which introduce numerical artifacts. An improved lattice Boltzmann pseudopotential model is presented. The discrete fluid density gradients in the coupling force are computed with rotationally symmetric gradient operators formulated as a convolution. As a result, spurious currents are reduced in settings where solid walls are unaligned with the lattice directions. Additionally, variations of introducing fluid-solid interaction either equally through both fluids or through a single fluid only are compared. Presented model variants are compared using droplets on walls as a common benchmark, analytically solvable capillary rise experiments (Jurin's law), and porous media imbibition as a practical application. Rotationally symmetric operators outperform the classical lattice weights approach in all tests in terms of accuracy, while avoiding extending the lattice to compute higher order gradients. The choice of the fluid-solid interaction variant depends on the problem under consideration and the desired properties of the resulting model.

authors.name: Benjamin Kellers, Arnulf Latz, Timo Danner

papers.title: Self-consistent thermal-runaway electron equilibria
papers.summary: In this work, we develop and solve a self-consistent equilibrium model for plasmas containing thermal and runaway electron (RE) populations, motivated by observations of residual plasma density during alternating-current (AC) transitions in ISTTOK. We adopt an existing monoenergetic, narrow-pitch guiding-center formulation, while retaining a spatially varying toroidal-field function, and show that prescribing the radius-weighted RE density by the orbit label alone conflicts with particle conservation and vector equilibrium wherever the thermal toroidal-field function varies along an occupied drift contour. Both conditions instead require the ratio of RE density to toroidal field to be constant along each drift contour. Taking this ratio as a function of the orbit label gives a compatible closure that relates the equilibrium RE density to a prescribed reference profile. Combined with Grad-Shafranov-Helmholtz thermal free functions, it yields a closed field equation that retains the displacement between drift and magnetic surfaces. At fixed thermal coefficients, we prove existence for every finite reference-profile amplitude under sign and spectral conditions. We also prove local constrained existence and uniqueness near a thermal equilibrium with a nonsingular current-beta response and derive a current-pressure bound. An ISTTOK ramp-down example with a prescribed 20% energetic-current fraction and 2 keV energy gives a magnetic-orbit axis separation of 2.39 mm. The resulting fields and current distributions can serve as initial conditions for studies of electron survival and plasma recovery through AC reversal.

authors.name: M. Keu, M. Hole, A. Malaquias

papers.title: Chlorophyll-a Fluorescence-Based Optical Temperature Sensor Using Food-Grade Chlorella Extract
papers.summary: This letter reports the development of an optical temperature sensor based on the fluorescence of an extract obtained from \textit{Chlorella}, a unicellular microalga commercially available as food-grade biomass. Using a straightforward ethanolic extraction route, the sensing platform exploits the characteristic emission of chlorophyll-\textit{a} as the optical transducing parameter. The operating principle relies on thermal fluorescence quenching, which promotes a decrease in emission intensity with rising temperature. In the temperature range from $28.6$ to $43.0~^{\circ}\text{C}$, the sensor exhibited a linear response ($R^2 = 0.9963$) with a sensitivity of $(-8.9 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-3}~^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$. Dynamic testing over consecutive heating--cooling cycles confirmed the sensor operation under sub-degree thermal oscillations and enabled the characterization of the system's photobleaching drift ($3.65\%\cdot\text{h}^{-1}$). The results reported herein demonstrate the feasibility of exploiting sustainable, bio-derived microalgal pigments as functional photoactive materials for optical thermometry.

authors.name: Sinei Felix Gon\c{c}alves Junior, Giovanna G. S. de Miranda, Leomar S. Marques, Flavio A. M. Marques, Alexandre A. C. Cotta, Jefferson E. Tsuchida, Julio C. Ugucioni, Lidia O. Rosa, Eric Fujiwara, Cristiano M. B. Cordeiro, Jonas H. Os\'orio

papers.title: Enhancing optomechanical oscillation amplitude and frequency comb bandwidth by intensity-modulated driving
papers.summary: Self-sustained oscillations in optomechanical systems are attractive as compact, low-noise sources of GHz signals and optical frequency combs for integrated photonic circuits. For these applications, the achievable oscillation amplitude directly sets clock power and comb bandwidth. This work studies the maximum amplitude that can be reached through combinations of cavity backaction and modulated optical driving, with realistic resources. For an optically driven mechanical resonator, the oscillation amplitude saturates at a level set by the finite cavity bandwidth. We show that modulating the input intensity near the mechanical resonance frequency raises the achievable amplitude toward this limit at equal mean input power and cavity linewidth. We use a cycle-averaged energy-balance analysis to identify the added power that shifts the stable periodic orbit to larger amplitudes. Numerical integration of the full equations of motion confirms the enhancement across two decades of cooperativity and sideband-resolution ratios from 0.1 to 10. The relative increase in amplitude is largest near the self-oscillation threshold and in the sideband-unresolved regime, enabling threshold-free large-amplitude oscillation where backaction alone fails to do so. The enhanced amplitude leads to a larger modulation depth of the optical field, enabling broader frequency combs, with improved stability of the comb spacing. Intensity-modulated driving thus offers power-constrained platforms a simple open-loop route to larger mechanical amplitudes and enhanced comb bandwidth.

authors.name: Menno H. Jansen, Ewold Verhagen

papers.title: Upscale energy transfer from mesoscale convective systems to African easterly waves
papers.summary: African easterly waves (AEWs) drive the synoptic variability of West African monsoon rainfall via intricate two-way interactions with mesoscale convective systems (MCSs). The composite MCS-AEW system is a canonical example of multiscale interactions in the tropical atmosphere, with upscale feedbacks from deep convection driving the evolution of a larger-scale circulation. Here we support this perspective through application of techniques from turbulence theory, calculating for the first time patterns of interscale kinetic energy transfer, $\mathcal{D}_L$, across different spatial scales $L$ around MCSs and AEW lifecycle phases. We study AEW and MCS dynamics in two pan-tropical 40 day Met Office Unified Model simulations with $\sim$5km grid spacings, for which $\mathcal{D}_L$ is calculated with the LoSSETT software package. We find explicitly-simulated MCSs show a distinctive vertical dipole structure of $\mathcal{D}_L$ at scales below 1000km, with strong upscale energy transfer located in the upper troposphere within storm anvils. Regionally, upscale energy transfer occurs most strongly where organised convection is active. We find 200hPa upscale transfer consistently leads AEW troughs, and that growing continental AEWs in the explicit simulation are characterised by strengthened upscale transfer of energy from MCS to AEW scales. Case-study analysis shows this transfer can contribute to the eddy kinetic energy growth of strengthening AEW troughs. These signals are weak in a simulation with parameterised convection: here, zonal mean energetics show enhanced barotropic conversion, caused by a stronger African Easterly Jet, provides a stronger AEW population. Our analysis of upscale energy transfers complements previous analysis of AEW potential vorticity dynamics, providing a route towards building new theoretical understanding of tropical dynamics from km-scale models.

authors.name: Ben Maybee, Elliot McKinnon-Gray, Dan Shipley, John Methven

papers.title: Thulium- and Holmium-Doped Silica Fibres for 2 {\mu}m High-Power and Highly-Efficient Lasers
papers.summary: Silica optical fibres, originally developed as a low-loss transmission medium for telecommunications, have evolved into a versatile platform for compact and efficient high-power lasers. This review discusses recent progress in thulium- and holmium-doped active fibres emitting within the 2 {\mu}m spectral band, with an emphasis on material and waveguide approaches that address power scaling through thermal-load mitigation and enhanced laser efficiency. In particular, the temperature dependence of absorption and emission cross-sections are reviewed, and their implications for spectral gain, amplified spontaneous emission and high-power laser operation are discussed. Structured-core thulium fibres are then considered as a route to combining the high local Tm3+ concentration required for efficient two for- one cross-relaxation with a reduced average dopant concentration, lower longitudinal heat load, and a pedestal-free waveguide design. Finally, recent results on holmium-doped silica fibres prepared by nanoparticle-assisted modified chemical vapour deposition are summarised. Crucially, the Al/Ho ratio is identified as a key compositional parameter governing laser efficiency, while a high absolute alumina content supports a long fluorescence lifetime and enables high Ho3+ concentrations without excessive clustering. These advances have enabled core-pumped holmium fibre lasers with slope efficiencies reaching 84% and output powers approaching 100W. Collectively, these development illustrate how control of spectroscopy, composition, and transverse dopant distribution can extend the performance of silica fibre lasers across the 1.7-2.2 {\mu}m spectral region.

authors.name: Richard Svejkar, Pavel Peterka, Bara Svejkarova, Michal Kamradek, Petr Varak, Martin Grabner, Jan Aubrecht, Ondrej Podrazky, Ivo Barton, Ivan Kasik, Pavel Honzatko

papers.title: Monolayer MoSe2 as an Attenuator of Spintronic Terahertz Emission
papers.summary: Understanding ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion at ferromagnetic/2D interfaces is critical for developing THz-frequency spintronic devices such as ultrafast memories, sensors, and compact THz sources. We investigate this by studying spintronic THz emission (STE) from Py/Au heterostructures capped with transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer MoSe2 using time-domain THz spectroscopy. We observe a pronounced reduction in emitted THz amplitude when a monolayer MoSe2 flake covers Py/Au or Py/Pt emitters compared with uncovered regions. A consistent, approximately fourfold attenuation occurs for both systems, despite an order-of-magnitude larger THz radiation from the bare Py/Pt emitter. These results indicate that the suppression is independent of emitter strength. We attribute the attenuation to THz absorption by free charge carriers and trions that are either present due to charge transfer from the metallic layer or photoexcited by the laser pulse, which can significantly diminish the detectable STE signal. This finding provides an explanation for the discrepancy between weak STE signals from FM/TMD heterostructures and magnetotransport reports of sizable spin-orbit torques in similar systems, and highlights the need to account for photoinduced THz attenuation when interpreting ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion measurements in 2D TMD heterostructures.

authors.name: Hatice Nur Koyun, Alexej Pashkin, Ruslan Salikhov, Artur Erbe, J\"urgen Fa{\ss}bender, Manfred Helm, Stephan Winnerl, J\"urgen Lindner

papers.title: Bayesian determination of structural ensembles from single-particle X-ray scattering images
papers.summary: Single-particle X-ray scattering with free electron lasers records snapshots of individual molecules with femtosecond time resolution and is therefore ideally suited to study structural heterogeneity or molecular motions. Current approaches to determine structural ensembles rely on prior classification of the scattering images, which is error-prone and becomes infeasible for single macromolecules, whose images contain too few coherently scattered photons. Here, we present a Bayesian approach that samples weighted ensembles of electron densities directly from the posterior probability distribution given all scattering images, thereby avoiding classification altogether. We demonstrate our approach in the low signal-to-noise high heterogeneity regime using synthetic scattering data of a small and flexible protein, as well as on published experimental scattering images for the coliphage PR772 virus.

authors.name: Steffen Schultze, Nicolai Kozlowski, Helmut Grubm\"uller

papers.title: UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
papers.summary: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively. Full-wave theoretical modeling of linear and nonlinear light-matter interaction in nanoscale structures validates the experimental results. We demonstrate that periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second and third-harmonic generation at wavelengths that can be tailored through the structural design, without requiring complex geometries or hybrid structures that pose fabrication challenges. The close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements further advances our understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights the potential of metallic nanostructures as ultrafast light sources in the UV and deep-UV.

authors.name: Shroddha Mukhopadhyay, Yuxuan Chen, Hooman Barati Sedeh, Natalia M. Litchinister, Michael Scalora, Jose Trull, Maria Antonietta Vincenti, Crina Cojocaru

papers.title: Pseudovortex-assisted generation of first-order vector modes
papers.summary: A practical method of generating first-order vector modes like radially and azimuthally polarized modes is using the so-called vortex waveplates. Shining these plates with Gaussian beams produces parasitic higher-order modes besides the target vector beam. The reason is that there is a mismatch between the incident Gaussian mode and the doughnut-shaped profile required for the vector beam. This imposes a limit on the fidelity of the generated mode with respect to the target vector beam. In this work we demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that this limit can be overcome if the input Gaussian beam is replaced with a pseudovortex beam, which is a doughnut-shaped mode without topological charge. We use a spatial light modulator to generate this input mode and a geometric-phase-compensated triangular cavity for mode analysis. We demonstrate vector mode fidelity as high as $0.921 \pm 0.013$, which is considerably better than $0.815 \pm 0.003$ obtained with Gaussian input. We also investigate the fidelity as a function of the input beam waist, leading to a theoretical upper bound for the fidelity of $8\pi/27 \approx 0.931$, in close agreement with the experimental results. This approach presents a reliable method of generating high-fidelity vector modes.

authors.name: L. Marques Fagundes, P. Schneider Lacerda, T. A. Petry Kock, N. Rubiano da Silva, P. H. Souto Ribeiro, R. Medeiros de Ara\'ujo

papers.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
papers.summary: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.

authors.name: Erwin Luesink, Archishman Saha, Tanya Schmah, Cristina Stoica

papers.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
papers.summary: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.

authors.name: Yao-Ting Wang, Emanuele Galiffi, Sander A. Mann, Mauro Antezza, Andrea Al\`u

papers.title: Development of a Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence System Based on Scintillating Crystals Read Out with Kinetic Inductance Detectors for BULLKID-DM
papers.summary: The BULLKID-DM experiment has been proposed to search for WIMP-like dark matter particles with a mass of 1 GeV or lower and with a WIMP-nucleon interaction cross section down to $10^{-43}$ cm$^2$. To achieve this goal, the experiment utilizes a detector consisting of a stack of 16 silicon wafers instrumented with phonon-mediated superconducting Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs), to be operated at the underground facility of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), Italy. To reduce the residual background arising from $\gamma$-rays, neutrons, and muons, a cryogenic active anti-coincidence system (veto) operating at mK temperature, surrounding the main detector, is under development. The veto detector consists of segmented scintillating crystals read out by phonon-mediated KID light detectors. Current status and future developments of the veto system are presented. In particular, we focus on cryogenic tests of both bismuth germanate (BGO) and gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) crystals, which had been previously chosen as veto candidate crystals according to our preliminary studies on the dependence of their optical properties (i.e. light yield and scintillation decay time) on temperature. We finally present the operation and preliminary tests of a two-module veto prototype with multiplexed readout.

papers.title: Adaptive carrier signal synthesis for frequency-division multiplexed cryogenic detector readout
papers.summary: Frequency-domain multiplexing is a fundamental technology for readout of cryogenic detector arrays on a single transmission line. Synthesizing a large number of static carrier tones for resonator stimulation eventually drives the cryogenic low-noise amplifier beyond its P1dB, introducing detector signal distortion. Scaling array sizes to O(10^6) detector pixels therefore demands minimizing the total power on the transmission line by continuous tracking of the resonances, which requires the readout electronics to be capable of updating the carrier tones dynamically. This work presents an scalable FPGA-based implementation for carrier signal synthesis based on a numerically controlled oscillator and a polyphase filter bank, enabling real-time frequency adaptivity as well as frequency resolution of 4 mHz to precisely tune the operating point, while simultaneously reducing resource usage compared to the current memory-based implementation.

authors.name: Timo Muscheid, Benedikt Keppner, Daniel Crovo, Robert Gartmann, Marvin Fuchs, Lukas Scheller, Oliver Sander, Luis E. Ardila-Perez

papers.title: Library of peptides: Analysis of a complex reactive mixture with the use of statistical physics and inference
papers.summary: Self-assembled mixtures enable the exploration of vast chemical diversity, yet characterizing the hundreds of coexisting species they contain remains a major challenge. Standard analytical techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy produce overlapping signals that cannot be resolved by conventional deconvolution methods, which neglect the concentration correlations imposed by the reactive network. Here, we introduce a framework that bridges statistical physics and analytical chemistry to deconvolute complex self-assembled mixtures from partial spectral data. Inspired by Potts models of protein folding, we express the chemical potential of each compound as a function of a reduced set of parameters-intrinsic building-block energies and pairwise coupling terms between neighboring building blocks in the sequence. Coupling this model with the law of mass action yields equilibrium concentrations across the entire reactive network. The model parameters can be infered by fitting predicted spectroscopic signals to experimentally measured partial data. We demonstrate this approach using dynamic combinatorial libraries (DCLs) of peptides as a model system. Applied to a DCL of 81 peptides, our method resolves the full mixture composition from just 13 overlapping peaks, revealing that lateral couplings dominate the assembly energetics. Beyond DCLs, this strategy offers a general route for analyzing self-assembled systems from partial data and extends naturally to target-driven identification of high-affinity binders.

authors.name: Laura Messio, Taleen Peker, Roba Moumn\'e, H\'el\`ene Berthoumieux

papers.title: The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
papers.summary: We report on a readout upgrade of Gator, a low-background high-purity germanium spectrometer operated at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso for material radioassay. The upgraded data acquisition records digitised waveforms, enabling noise rejection on an event-level basis, and offline energy reconstruction. Measurements before and after the upgrade show an improved energy resolution of 17% at the 2614.5 keV line of 208-Tl, with (2.14 +- 0.22) keV at FWHM, and suppression of electronic noise in the low-energy region. We assess the resulting sensitivity for a specified sample geometry, and present a new background measurement. The background rate in the (100-2700) keV range is (86.6 +- 0.5) counts/(kg day). We also show the radioassay results of sixteen Hamamatsu R17317 3-inch photomultiplier tubes with an improved stem design, which reduces the activities from the primordial 238-U and 232-Th chains by a factor of three, making them suitable candidate photosensors for the XLZD experiment.

authors.name: Laura Baudis, Sofia Calgaro, Jose Javier Cuenca-Garcia, Florian Joerg, Margherita Noia, Francesco Piastra, Aravind Remesan Sreekala

papers.title: A Feasibility Study of Whole-Cerebrum Task-Based fMRI at 0.55 T: Motor and Visual Tasks Using Single-Shot EPI
papers.summary: Purpose: To evaluate the feasibility of whole-cerebrum task-based fMRI on a modern 0.55T system, examining the effects of extended scan duration and within-session consistency on functional mapping outcomes and comparison to acquisition with matched tasks at 3.0T. Methods: Six healthy participants were scanned at 0.55T using a single-shot EPI sequence during bilateral finger-tapping and visual checkerboard tasks. Data were processed using an open-source pipeline. To investigate sensitivity improvements, two consecutive 5-minute runs were concatenated. Within-session consistency was also assessed. A representative 3T dataset provided additional reference context for temporal dynamics and statistical sensitivity. Results: Task-evoked activations were detected at 0.55T using Family-Wise Error (FWE) rate correction (p < 0.05) in both motor and visual cortices. While single 5-minute runs provided baseline detectability, extending the acquisition to 10 minutes increased t-statistic magnitudes and cluster extents while substantially reducing background noise (47% reduction in voxelwise dispersion). Run-to-run comparisons showed consistent peak locations and statistical significance across participants. Comparison with the 3T reference demonstrated that statistical significance increases with acquisition time so that a 0.55T scan approximately matches 3T significance levels at twice the scan duration across the range compared. Conclusion: Whole-cerebrum task fMRI is feasible at 0.55T using standard EPI and modern high-performance gradients. These results indicate that modest extensions in scan duration can compensate for reduced intrinsic BOLD sensitivity at lower field strengths.

authors.name: Parsa Razmara, Takfarinas Medani, Anand A. Joshi, Majid Abbasi Sisara, Ye Tian, Sophia X. Cui, Justin P. Haldar, Krishna S. Nayak, Richard M. Leahy

papers.title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
papers.summary: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

authors.name: Romit Chakraborty

papers.title: Active-space construction in single-fragment coupled-cluster embedding for chemical reactions
papers.summary: We benchmark single-fragment quantum embedding, in which electron correlation---at the level of coupled-cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]---is restricted to orbitals associated with a chosen molecular fragment, and the remaining orbitals are frozen at the Hartree-Fock level. We compare several methods for constructing fragment active spaces, and we test their performance on 60 organic reaction energies and three reaction profiles. A common fragment projection operator is used to relate several of the tested orbital constructions. Regional embedding, based on density matrix embedding theory, is shown to give accurate and robust performance when used for both the occupied and virtual active orbitals. For virtual orbitals, fragment-centered projected atomic orbitals and fragment natural orbitals (defined by eigenvectors of a fragment MP2 density matrix) also perform well, but the latter typically retains larger virtual spaces. Composite MP2 corrections yield the largest improvement: combined with fragment natural orbitals, they give average reaction energy errors below 0.3 kcal/mol relative to full-system CCSD(T), with all individual errors below 1 kcal/mol. Reaction profiles show that accurate endpoint energies can conceal substantial barrier errors, emphasizing the importance of approximating omitted correlation.

authors.name: Ardavan Farahvash, Timothy C. Berkelbach

papers.title: On stimulated scattering including harmonic generation in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths
papers.summary: A fully nonlinear analysis for the growth rate of the stimulated backscatter instability of an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave with arbitrary polarization in an unmagnetized pair plasma is presented. The connection of this instability to the FEL process is discussed and utilized. An intense EM wave causes an initially stationary pair plasma to drift forward with a speed near the speed of light. The resulting distribution function for both cold and warm pair plasmas is presented. It is shown that the frequency of the reflected light is thus Doppler downshifted from that of the incident wave. For a linearly polarized EM wave there is also an additional contribution to the forward drift at its second harmonic which leads to backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler downshifted frequency for sufficiently cold pair plasmas. Fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show how the instability depends on the pair plasma temperature. The effect of the intensity profile of the incoming EM wave as well as implications for astrophysical pair plasmas is discussed.

authors.name: Vijay Patel, Thomas Grismayer, Samuel Sebastian, Xinlu Xu, John Palastro, Paulo Alves, Warren B. Mori

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.summary: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.

authors.name: Mohammadreza Khellat, Mohammad Masoumi, Saman Nasoori, Soroush Nasoori

papers.title: Time-Domain and Spectral Decomposition of Dynamic Coupling with Instantaneous and Time-Lagged Causality: Methodological Evaluation and Application to Cardiovascular Variability
papers.summary: The quantification of dynamic interactions in coupled physiological time series is a central question in biomedical signal processing. A critical issue is the presence of instantaneous dependencies, often neglected in conventional Granger causality (GC) analyses despite potentially reflecting physiologically meaningful effects. We investigate time- and frequency-domain measures of causality within the linear autoregressive (AR) framework, treating instantaneous dependencies according to three formulations: (i) the classical strictly causal AR model, providing spectral measures of time-lagged GC and instantaneous interaction; (ii) the Geweke approach, assigning instantaneous dependencies to the direction opposite to that under investigation; (iii) a single extended AR model incorporating causally-oriented instantaneous dependencies, yielding spectral GC measures accounting for both instantaneous and time-lagged causality. The three approaches are evaluated in simulated Gaussian systems, where dynamic measures can be derived analytically and compared with the expected coupling structure. The single extended AR model emerges as the most consistent formulation when instantaneous dependencies have a physiologically meaningful causal direction and is then applied to cardiovascular interactions between heart period (HP) and systolic (SAP) or diastolic arterial pressure (DAP) in healthy subjects during postural and mental stress. Accounting for instantaneous dependencies substantially affects HP-SAP and HP-DAP interactions, enabling better quantification of baroreflex and cardiac run-off mechanisms and characterization of their responses to stress and of low- and high-frequency dynamics. Overall, the framework provides consistent representation of causal interactions across time and frequency and highlights the importance of accounting for instantaneous dependencies in physiological coupling.

authors.name: Gorana Mijatovic, Marta Iovino, Michal Javorka, Luca Faes

papers.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
papers.summary: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is almost an order of magnitude faster than a comparable FEM. Finally, the Neural Physics method is applied to a real-world test case with integrated experimental data and simulates the infiltration of water through a rain garden. This new approach therefore provides a route to efficiently and accurately solve Richards equation for a wide array of hydrological applications.

authors.name: Katherine MacKenzie, James Rand, Ben Ashby, Tristan Pryer, Claire E. Heaney, Christopher C. Pain, Thomas Rodding Kjelsden

papers.title: Rational layers in the low temperature expansion of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.summary: A low-temperature expansion orders Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can occur at the same order. We instead organize the zero-field simple-cubic model by the excess above the minimum wall area compatible with two prescribed spans. We prove that every fixed excess layer, including all logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, has a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1 - x, 1 - y and 1 - x - y. The proof compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations and assigns each unbounded interval to one monotone chain. A finite controller then enforces induced contacts and arbitrary cover-color reuse. We explicitly assemble the complete layers of excess zero through three over all widths, attributing their known geometric constituents to earlier polyomino enumeration. Exact lattice checks corroborate the formulas. A certified low-temperature comparison shows a modest hybrid accuracy gain at one sampling point and higher evaluation cost. The result establishes an exact layer structure; summation over unbounded excess remains a separate problem.

authors.name: Ran Huang

papers.title: Towards Distributed Quantum Computing: Quantum Gate Teleportation via Satellite-Distributed Entanglement under Atmospheric Depolarization
papers.summary: We investigate quantum gate teleportation as a primitive for satellite-enabled distributed quantum computing. In the considered architecture, a satellite distributes entangled photon pairs to two optical ground stations, which transfer the shared quantum resource to remote quantum processing units. This entanglement is then used to implement a nonlocal controlled-NOT gate between two circuit qubits located in different processors. We formulate the minimal four-qubit protocol, consisting of two network qubits that provide the entangled resource and two circuit qubits on which the distributed gate is performed. Atmospheric propagation effects in the gravitational field are modeled through an effective two-qubit depolarizing channel whose parameters depend on atmospheric and optical quantities, including the Fried parameter and receiver aperture. The performance of the protocol is quantified by the fidelity between the ideal CNOT output state and the state produced by noisy quantum gate teleportation. Our results show that the fidelity is governed by the quality of the distributed entanglement and depends jointly on atmospheric coherence, aperture size, and effective depolarization strength. These findings connect physical-layer modeling of satellite optical channels with gate-level performance in distributed quantum computing.

authors.name: Artur Czerwinski, Jakub J. Borkowski, Maciej Wi\'sniewski, Saeed Haddadi

papers.title: Gravitational observables from a post-Carrollian expansion
papers.summary: Einstein gravity, with a few exceptions, only admits nonlocal observables. This feature is often attributed to diffeomorphism invariance, since a gravitational field can thereby locally be transformed away. We show this attribution to be incorrect by constructing infinitely many exact ultralocal Dirac observables in (velocity dominated aka electric) Carroll gravity. The latter describes Einstein gravity's ultrarelativistic limit, is fully diffeomorphism invariant, and of independent interest in a variety of contexts. Starting from these Carroll observables a systematic construction of Dirac observables for Einstein gravity is outlined. The resulting "post-Carrollian" expansion is organized by the number of spatial gradients or fractional inverse powers of Newton's constant, where each partial sum is local.

authors.name: Max Niedermaier, Mahdi Sedighi Jafari

papers.title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots
papers.summary: Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power. Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware. Here, we present SunLightBots, a class of subgram, sunlight-powered, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion under continuous illumination near 1 Sun (100 mW/cm2). Their operation is enabled by a self-resetting snapping (SRS) mechanism that integrates liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) with snap-through instability to accumulate solar energy supplied at low power, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback. Through coordinated optimization of the LCE actuation temperature, photothermal conversion, actuation stress, and structural energy barrier, the system operates near 1 Sun and achieves a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg. At this irradiance, the optimized LCE generates an actuation stress of 0.1 MPa at approximately 60 deg C. SunLightBots demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated impulsive jumping. Under 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle. This work provides a materials-mechanics route toward autonomous soft robots powered entirely by the environment.

authors.name: Yoo Jin Lee, Melanie Torres Crespo, Zhongxiao Deng, Andrew Tejada-Vega, Rebecca Kramer-Bottiglio, Wenzhong Yan, Yimin Luo

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.summary: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\bar{\kappa} \equiv r_s\Delta y^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $\Delta y$ is the mesoscale length.

authors.name: Jake Willard, Yi-Hsin Liu

papers.title: Beyond Ground States: Learning Many-Body Hamiltonians for p-Bit Invertible Arithmetic
papers.summary: Probabilistic-bit (p-bit) invertible logic encodes a Boolean relation as an energy whose ground states are its legal assignments, computing in any direction by sampling. Traditional constructions target ground-state membership and a wide minimum energy gap, yet finite-time samplers traverse excited states. We cast Hamiltonian design as inverse statistical mechanics: fit an energy with interactions up to order four whose Gibbs law approaches uniformity on each clamp case's legal states, under a gap floor keeping every legal state below every illegal one. Constrained maximum likelihood with pruning and refitting fits terms from a fixed pool, and every delivered energy is audited exactly on all cases. Each energy is scored by time to a verified solution under restarts with its best of nine tuned samplers. In underdetermined modes, learned multipliers factor in 0.55, 0.44, 0.52 and 0.46 [0.38, 0.56] of the hand-written encodings' updates from 4x4 to 7x7, faster within every family below 7x7 at no resolved work penalty; learned adders solve the reverse mode in 0.71 of the updates at 8 bits and about a quarter at 24 and 32 bits, at 0.55 of the work at 32 bits. At 5x5 under equal pool, budget and floor, a gap-maximizing fit reaches 0.79 [0.73, 0.88] in updates and 1.26 in work against the hand-written encoding, while likelihood fitting takes 0.55 [0.46, 0.58] and 0.58 [0.48, 0.61] of the gap fit's updates and work. Rounding coefficients to the narrowest exact integer words tested, we run both energies at each pair's common word on one FPGA color-sweep SSA core, bit-exact with software: learned multipliers take 0.41 of the hand-written encoding's cycles at 4x4 and 0.057 [0.045, 0.068] at 7x7, at up to 2.4 times its lookup tables. The method requires only a circuit's legal assignments; in determined modes, hand-written encodings take less work, and from 12 bits on the adder fewer updates.

authors.name: Tian Feng, Xutang Fan, Yiyun Chen

papers.title: Selecting and verifying load-bearing periodic cells for elastic-wave band gaps with numerical acceptance checks
papers.summary: A lattice mount must be stiff enough to support equipment and block vibration over a specified frequency range. Fast simulations help rank designs, but their errors can lead to a wrong acceptance decision. We present AMM (AgenticMetamaterials), an open-source Python tool that searches repeating cubic cells for targets on stiffness, the fraction of the cell that is solid, and band gaps. A complete band gap is an interval with no elastic-wave propagation in any direction. A separate checker allows for changes as the simulation grid gets finer. For gaps, it also tests for modes at sampled wave directions and wavelengths, so it can miss modes between samples. In 1,500 near-threshold tests of stiffness and solid fraction, the checker accepted 454 of 750 claims supported by the reference and none of the 750 false claims. Using the finest grid estimate alone accepted 42 false claims. In an independent finite-element comparison on ten new cells built from cubes joined by bars, the checker accepted one of two true gap claims and left all 17 false claims undecided. The reference could not classify the remaining claim. The protocol required every reported edge to err on the side of a narrower gap. The checker failed this test when it placed one upper edge too high, even though it left that thin-bar cell's claim undecided. Separating search from acceptance shows which targets the evidence supports and where a calculation needs further refinement.

authors.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

papers.title: Soft material mechanical property degradation at high strain rates
papers.summary: The rheometry of soft, tissue-like materials at ultra-high strain rates is critical to biomechanics, materials science, and medical engineering. One approach for characterizing high-rate material response is Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry (IMR), which infers viscoelastic constitutive behavior from the measured radius-time history of a laser-induced cavitation bubble. At these rates, materials may exhibit history-dependent behavior, including damage, fracture, and plasticity. However, conventional IMR analyses typically assume constant material properties throughout the cavitation event, limiting their ability to capture such changes. We present an IMR framework for identifying effective time varying material properties from measured cavitation radius histories. The framework allows the shear modulus, viscosity, or both to evolve during the event using normalized sigmoid histories. Synthetic tests recover prescribed constant and time varying material histories. Application to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets yields effective material-property histories across formulations and experimental conditions. Viscosity decreased across the datasets, while the extent of shear modulus reduction varied with material and formulation. When both properties decreased, their reductions could occur at different stages of cavitation. This distinction in mechanical property degradation depends on both the property and its evolution during high-strain events.

authors.name: Victor Sanchez, Joseph Beckett, Aryan Shah, Sicong Wang, Jin Yang, Jonathan B. Estrada, Mauro Rodriguez Jr

papers.title: Optimal Driving between Nonequilibrium Steady States under a Dissipation Budget
papers.summary: Driving between nonequilibrium steady states incurs two thermodynamic costs: excess entropy production (EP) resulting from changing control parameters, and housekeeping EP required to sustain steady currents. Conventional fixed-duration optimization minimizes the former while neglecting the latter. Here, we instead optimize excess EP over both the protocol and its duration subject to a fixed leading order of housekeeping-EP budget, thereby minimizing total EP for that budget constraint. In the slow-driving regime, accumulated housekeeping EP acts as an entropic time, mapping the problem to a geodesic optimization under a friction metric weighted by the steady-state EP rate. This resource-based geometry determines optimal paths and schedules for systems that continue to dissipate even in steady states, establishing an intrinsic trade-off between housekeeping and excess EPs. Near equilibrium, this framework further yields geometric lower bounds on total EP, attained with equipartition at the optimal budget given by a modified thermodynamic length. Numerical simulations of a three-state model for an ATP-driven calcium pump reveal distinct optimal protocols compared to fixed-duration driving, confirming the total-EP bounds.

authors.name: Keisuke Sugie, Dimitri Loutchko, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi

papers.title: Improving Nonequilibrium Thermal Conduction in CaF2 by Breaking the Phonon Bottleneck Effect
papers.summary: Heat dissipation in laser optical materials depends not only on their thermal conductivity but also on how absorbed energy is redistributed among various phonon modes. In calcium fluoride (CaF2), rapid energy transfer from hot electrons to weakly propagating longitudinal optical (LO) phonons can create a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck effect that limits efficient heat removal. Here, we propose selective phonon excitation as an effective strategy to break this bottleneck. Combining electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we identify LO phonons as the primary modes that preferentially receive energy from hot carriers, leading to energy accumulation due to their inefficient transport and relaxation. Guided by three-phonon scattering phase-space analysis, selective excitation of transverse acoustic (TA) modes can accelerate LO relaxation and promote energy transfer toward heat-carrying acoustic modes. While sustained LO-phonon excitation reduces the thermal conductivity by approximately 12%, additional TA-mode excitation improves heat conduction by approximately 21% compared to the state limited by the LO-phonon bottleneck, surpassing the unexcited value. These findings demonstrate that controlling interbranch energy redistribution can counteract phonon-bottleneck-induced heat accumulation and reveal a working route for active thermal management in laser optical materials through selective control of phonon populations.

authors.name: Mingde Qu, Minghuan Song, Yuxing Wang, Wudi Wang, Chenbo Zhang, Jiamin Quan, Jun Xu, Zhongwei Zhang, Jie Chen

papers.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
papers.summary: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

authors.name: Lukas Fischer, Rouven Dreyer, Simon Arnold, Jae-Chun Jeon, Georg Woltersdorf, Stuart S. P. Parkin

papers.title: Influence of Assortativity on the SICP Spreading Process in Hypergraphs
papers.summary: Many real-world systems involve group interactions that cannot be captured by pairwise graphs. They can be better represented by hypergraphs where each hyperedge could connect an arbitrary number of nodes. The Susceptible-Infected Contact Process (SICP) has been proposed to model the spreading of information and epidemics on hypergraphs. However, how higher-order topological properties of a hypergraph influence the SICP spreading process remains understudied. In this paper, we examine the impact of hypergraph assortativity based on the Neighborhood Coefficient (NC)-the average size of hyperedges incident to a node-on the SICP spreading process. By introducing a low-complexity measure of hypergraph assortativity grounded in analysis of variance, we apply hyperdegree-preserving rewirings to real-world networks and synthetic hypergraph models to tune their assortativity. We find and explain why lower NC assortativity yields higher average epidemic prevalence and lower prevalence variance across different seed selections. This phenomenon is evident when hyperdegree-preserving rewirings are applied to real-world networks with heterogeneous topological structures, but it is largely absent when comparing synthetic random hypergraphs to their rewired counterparts.

authors.name: Jelmer Stolwijk (Bart), Renze Dijkhuizen (Bart), H. A. (Bart), Peters, Huijuan Wang

papers.title: The infrared vacuum reduces the laser energy needed to break molecular bonds of simple molecules
papers.summary: Vibrational strong coupling within a few molecules has recently been demonstrated in infrared nanocavities at room temperature, opening new alternatives to explore chemical reactions assisted by the confined electromagnetic vacuum. However, the intrinsic mechanisms of how the quantized electromagnetic mode modifies reactivity are not fully understood. We study infrared photodissociation of a single molecule strongly coupled to a resonant infrared nanocavity mode. The coupled system is driven by a monochromatic infrared laser that vibrationally excites the molecule directly or injects photons into the nanocavity field. We compare the intracavity dynamics of CO2 and H2O molecules and demonstrate that the driving energy required for dissociation is up to three orders of magnitude lower inside the cavity by injecting photons into the nanocavity than by driving the molecule directly. We show that photodissociation enhancements are due to the interplay between nuclear anharmonicity, stronglight-mattercoupling, and vacuum field polarisation according to the dipolar nature of the molecular bond. Our results provide the conceptual and numerical tools for understanding how to control chemical processes and to design nanophotonics experiments at the few-molecule level within a cavity quantum electrodynamics perspective.

authors.name: Johan F. Triana, Felipe Herrera

papers.title: Chaos without Local Spectral Instability in a Kicked Oscillator
papers.summary: A damped harmonic oscillator kicked by a pulsed periodic potential can be chaotic although every local Jacobian has eigenvalues inside the unit circle. Damped rotation between kicks lets non-normal shears of opposite curvature compound, so ordered products of contracting Jacobians amplify perturbations. We derive the exact joint spectral radius of the Jacobian family and an exact Lyapunov-exponent decomposition showing how this geometric pumping overcomes dissipation. The proposed mechanism can be realized with laser-cooled trapped ions in a pulsed optical lattice.

authors.name: Vincenzo Citro, Giuseppe Petrillo, Didier Sornette

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.summary: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(\rho)=1+a^2/(4\rho^2)$. Through the Pleba\'nski correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=\mu_r=n(\rho)\,\mathbb{1}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(\omega a/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $\pi a^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

authors.name: Abdullah Guvendi, Claudio Furtado, Omar Mustafa

papers.title: Critical excited states in quantum metrology
papers.summary: We investigate criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, we design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to enhance signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation using experimentally relevant generators. We show that the excited-state criticality provides a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that circumvent the 'death of adiabaticity', limiting conventional critical quantum metrology with ground-state criticality.

authors.name: Marek Kucha\v{r}, Michal Macek

papers.title: Zero-Field Optical Readout of Quintet States in Through-Space Coupled Tetracene Oligomers at Room Temperature
papers.summary: Optically addressable electron spins are promising platforms for quantum technologies, with molecular systems offering chemical control over their spin and optical properties. Achieving optical readout of molecular spin states at room temperature and without an applied magnetic field is an important step towards their practical implementation. Quintet states generated via singlet fission are promising optically addressable multilevel qudits, but their intrinsic spin transitions at zero and weak magnetic fields remain largely unexplored, while substantial room-temperature quintet coherence has predominantly been demonstrated in structurally constrained molecular architectures. Here, we combine zero-field optically detected magnetic resonance (zero-field ODMR) with transient and pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to investigate the magnetic-field dependence and coherent spin properties of quintet states in conformationally flexible, through-space coupled tetracene oligomers. We demonstrate zero-field optical readout of quintet states at room temperature in both tetracene dimers and hexamers, and map the response of optically detected transitions to weak applied magnetic fields. Complementary EPR measurements support quintet formation through stochastic exchange fluctuations and demonstrate a room-temperature phase-memory time of 446 ns, showing that the conformational dynamics enabling high-spin formation remain compatible with substantial spin coherence. Together, these results integrate field-free optical readout, weak-field response and room-temperature spin coherence within a chemically modular, through-space coupled molecular architecture, expanding the design space for optically addressable molecular qudits and quantum sensors.

authors.name: Jeannine Gr\"une, Maciej Majdecki, William K. Myers, Przemys{\l}aw Gawe{\l}, Hannah L. Stern

papers.title: The Role of Precursors and MHD Instabilities in Distinguishing Confined and Eruptive Solar Flares
papers.summary: Identifying pre-flare magnetic conditions that determine whether a flare will be eruptive (associated with a coronal mass ejection) or confined remains a major challenge in solar physics. Motivated by previous statistical results showing that some eruptive flares occur under ideal MHD-stable conditions, we investigate the roles of kink instability (KI), torus instability (TI), preflare reconnection traced by precursor brightenings (PBs) and magnetic nonpotentiality in solar eruptiveness using an expanded sample of 68 flares above GOES class M4 from 2011--2024. To characterize the nonpotentiality of each active region (AR), we calculate the relative helicity $H_R$, current-carrying helicity $H_J$ and free magnetic energy. We find that, (1) 17 of 18 TI-unstable events and 12 of 19 KI-unstable events are eruptive, indicating that the TI parameter outperforms the KI parameter (2) although PBs are more commonly found in the MHD-unstable regime, only 3 of the 12 eruptive events in the TI/KI-stable regime show PBs, suggesting that preflare reconnection may play a secondary role compared with other factors. (3) The strongest indicator of eruptiveness is obtained by combining the TI parameter with magnetic nonpotentiality. Specifically, 24 of 36 eruptive flares satisfy $\sqrt{\left| H_J \right|}/\phi \geq 0.1$ or $n \geq 1.13$, whereas 24 of 25 confined flares satisfy $\sqrt{\left| H_J \right|}/\phi \le 0.1$ and $n \le 1.13$, where $\phi$ is the total unsigned magnetic flux and $n$ is the decay index. These results suggest that the overall magnetic environment of ARs may play a significant role in determining the eruptiveness, in addition to the effect of MHD instability and reconnection.

authors.name: Wen He, Ju Jing, Jeongwoo Lee, Haimin Wang

papers.title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
papers.summary: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) enable programmable gene silencing, but candidates targeting the same transcript can differ markedly in potency. Existing predictors range from interpretable empirical rules with limited accuracy to high-capacity models that can lose performance when datasets or targets change. We present Silscore, a guide-only model that combines a quadratic preference for overall duplex stability, a position-resolved profile of nearest-neighbour stacking energies and sparse nucleotide-identity terms selected from residuals left unexplained by thermodynamics. Its main fit uses 26 parameters, fewer than half as many as any trainable comparator evaluated here. We evaluate Silscore on the canonical split of the Huesken dataset, two external datasets (Mixset and Katoh-Suzuki), and an evaluation in which the same guides are tested after training on dissimilar targets. Silscore attains the highest observed Pearson correlation in all three transfer evaluations, and the data support an advantage over every applicable comparator on Katoh-Suzuki. For a fixed evaluation set, we compare two equally sized training sets with higher or lower sequence similarity to the evaluation sequences. After training on the less similar sequences, Silscore has the highest observed correlation, and the data do not establish a change in its performance. The fitted parameters can also be interpreted directly: identity terms locate sequence effects that base-pairing energies cannot express, global stability has a data-estimated intermediate optimum, and local energy profiles recover terminal asymmetry and a preference for weaker seed and stronger central pairing. Silscore thus provides a compact, data-driven model that combines strong predictive performance with robustness when tested in new settings and expresses previously reported empirical preferences as quantities estimated from data.

authors.name: Giuseppe Sacco, Isabella Baldini, Riccardo Paone, Mattia Capulli, Guido Sanguinetti, Giovanni Bussi

papers.title: Non-Bloch Topology of Frustrated Non-Hermitian Flat Bands
papers.summary: Frustrated lattices with exactly flat bands and compact localized states provide an ideal setting to uncover the topology of flat bands, leading to intriguing physics in two dimensions. Extending from Hermitian to non-Hermitian systems, however, band structures are drastically changed by the non-Hermitian skin effect, which is less well understood beyond one dimension. Here, we construct a broad class of two-dimensional frustrated non-Hermitian lattice models with exactly flat bands which can be naturally described in a non-Bloch band theory. Using non-Hermitian breathing Kagome and checkerboard models as illustrations, we reveal how flat bands acquire a basis-independent skin effect induced by the other bands; in the breathing Kagome model it appears exactly when the flat band enters the area spanned by the periodic-boundary spectra of the dispersive bands. A flat band becomes singular when its eigenvectors hold immovable discontinuities at band crossings. Such singularity in non-Hermitian systems is sensitive to boundary conditions and unprotected by band flatness. Non-Bloch topology underlying is uncovered in a bulk-boundary correspondence with the formation of a singular band touching in the bulk and a robust flat band skin mode on the boundary. We present a geometric approach to construct this boundary skin mode from a macroscopic sum of compact localized skin modes and trace its topological origin to two linearly independent noncontractible loop states on a non-Bloch torus.
