The self-absorption of the IR emission could be achieved through sub-band-gap excitations due to defects, creating carriers. In a heavily doped p-n junction device, some of the IR-generated carriers diffuse into the junction which has a built-in field. The built-in field sweeps out the carriers, creating IR photocurrent. The reverse leakage current of the p-n junction is regarded as the IR photocurrent according to a precedent where impurity-photovoltaic-effect is used to explain circuit devices (arXiv:2510.18226). Heavy doping results in not only a great many IR-generated carriers but also an avalanche effect at low voltage, producing Zener breakdown. Additionally, the impurity-photovoltaic-effect can make a reasonable contribution to explaining the temperature dependence of Zener breakdown. If the doping is very heavy, the heavily doped p-n junction can be altered to create an ohmic contact, which can also be explained in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect. Not only quantum mechanics, but also this photovoltaic mechanism in particle description can explain the above devices. Considering the wave-particle duality, the combination of quantum-mechanical and photovoltaic mechanisms is suggested to explain these devices. Each mechanism plays a big or small role in the explanation.

authors.name: Jianming Li

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Ising-Bloch Transition in Polarization Cavity Solitons
papers.summary: Polarization cavity solitons in coherently driven Kerr resonators undergo a sequence of dynamical bifurcations as the cavity detuning is increased. Here we show that a stationary localized state containing an Ising wall first becomes a fixed breather and then develops finite chirality and drift motion through a spontaneous non-equilibrium Ising-Bloch transition. Stability analyses identify the modes responsible for the breathing and the motion, revealing controllable dynamics of polarization cavity solitons.

authors.name: Juan Diego Mazo-V\'asquez, Lewis Hill, Flore K. Kunst, Gian-Luca Oppo

papers.title: Direct Multispectral Satellite Nowcasting of Gridded Surface Solar Radiation
papers.summary: Surface shortwave radiation (SWR) can change within minutes as clouds evolve, but operational forecasts often trade spatial detail and update frequency for forecast range. Here, we present a numerical-weather-prediction-independent, observation-to-forecast framework that converts sequences of Himawari-9 Level-1 multispectral imagery and solar geometry directly into 24 gridded SWR fields at 10-min intervals for the next 4 h. A controlled six-model experiment in eastern China separates the effects of satellite information from those of temporal self-attention. In the 0-1 h window, the full-multispectral attention model achieves a mean absolute error of 37.9 W/m2 and a root mean square error of 63.7 W/m2, reductions of 21.0% and 19.5% relative to a historical-SWR baseline. Improvements extend across nine subregions and include weaker spatial bias and better structural consistency. Temporal attention does not improve forecasts from historical SWR alone, but becomes effective when supplied with multispectral cloud and thermodynamic signals. Direct multispectral observations therefore provide the precursor information required for high-frequency, spatially resolved SWR nowcasting.

authors.name: Tianyu Xie, Zhaoliang Zeng, Zhehao Liang, Ke Gui, Xutao Zhang, Yaqiang Wang, Dabo Guan, Huizheng Che

papers.title: Coupled Cluster Simulations of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra
papers.summary: We report the first simulations of vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) spectra at the coupled-cluster level of theory. We generalize Stephens's magnetic-field perturbation theory framework for the magnetic-dipole vibrational transition moment to biorthonormal wave functions. The resulting atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors collapse to Stephens's expressions for real, Hermitian states. Adapting these exact-state expressions to coupled-cluster left- and right-hand biorthonormal wave functions and using our recently developed density-based formulation yields compact equations that involve only perturbed ground-state amplitudes, as well as unperturbed and perturbed, unrelaxed one-electron densities; two-electron-density contributions vanish exactly. We have validated the resulting AATs by comparison with our previous configuration interaction formulation for a two-electron system, size-intensivity tests, a translational sum rule, and other tests. Simulated VCD spectra for (S)-3-chloro-1-butyne at the coupled-cluster singles and doubles level with the correlation-consistent triple-zeta basis set reveal significant discrepancies between length and velocity gauges. We find that the addition of large-exponent functions via a core-valence basis set for the Hartree--Fock reference components yields substantially improved gauge invariance without the need for gauge-including atomic orbitals.

authors.name: T. Daniel Crawford, Aparna Krishnan, Brendan M. Shumberger

papers.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
papers.summary: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

authors.name: Nicholas Kamp, Louis Deslauriers, Carlos A. Arg\"uelles, Gonzalo Herrera, William G. Thompson

papers.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
papers.summary: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

authors.name: Lei Hou, Xiang Zhang, Qiang Zhu, Xiang-Pei Liu, Fa-Xi Chen, Wen-Xuan Song, Zhuan-Xian Xiong, Jian-Yu Guan, Yu-Chen Zhang, De-Quan Kong, Jia-Hao Zhang, Long-Fei Liao, Shao-Mao Wang, Bing Wang, De-Zhi Xiong, Xing-Yang Cui, Ping Xu, Peng Liu, Jie Li, Xiao Jiang, Hua-Qing Zhang, Ling-Xiang He, Li-Bo Li, Qi Shen, Youchao Xie, Lei Wang, Sheng-Kai Liao, Juan Yin, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Wen-Bin Shen, Baolong Lyu, Han-Ning Dai, Qiang Zhang, Yu-Ao Chen, Hai-Feng Jiang, Jian-Wei Pan

papers.title: Interface Energy and Phase Transformations: A Comparative Analysis of Cahn-Hilliard and CALPHAD-based Models in Ternary Substitutional Alloys
papers.summary: Diffusional phase transformations in alloys are modeled either by phase-field methods of Cahn-Hilliard type, in which a double-well free energy and a gradient term impose an interface energy, or by reactive diffusion models, in which the driving forces follow from the CALPHAD methodology, the convex hull of the molar free energy, and the interface carries no energy. Their numerical schemes are tied to their free energies: phase-field schemes break down when the interface energy is set to zero, and reactive diffusion codes rely on finite differences. We derive, from the thermodynamic extremal principle, a single finite element scheme that covers both limits: the stationarity of the Rayleighian functional (free energy rate plus one half of the dissipation, with mass conservation imposed by multipliers) with respect to the rates, fluxes and multipliers at a frozen state. Fluxes and chemical affinities are primary unknowns, so no derivative of the affinity is required. The time-discrete scheme is the corresponding incremental minimization; it conserves mass exactly and satisfies a discrete energy-dissipation inequality for every convex molar free energy, including the convex hull without regularization. We make explicit that this last case is a degenerate parabolic problem of Stefan type, whose degeneracy can be removed, without altering the free energy, only by a moving mesh; since our aim is the coupling to continuum mechanics and damage on a fixed mesh, we operate at the boundary of degeneracy and show that mass conservation, the energy balance and the second law remain intact there. Thermodynamic consistency is proved for multi-component systems, a scheme relating Onsager and diffusion coefficients is proposed, and the role of interface energy is studied in binary and ternary examples, the latter with vacancies as a non-conserved component.

authors.name: Wolfgang Flachberger, Thomas Antretter, Swaroop Gaddikere-Nagaraja, Silvia Leitner, Manuel Petersmann, Jiri Svoboda

papers.title: The amplifier effect of artificial agents in social contagion
papers.summary: Individuals and organizations increasingly consider delegating decision-making to AI agents, which may significantly alter social contagion dynamics. We ask whether artificial agents exhibit different adoption thresholds from those of human subjects when making decisions and, if so, how such differences may affect the spread of social contagions. To answer these questions, we conduct two choice experiments - recently administered to human participants - with artificial agents powered by large language models (LLMs). Across two domains and five LLMs, artificial agents exhibit systematically lower adoption thresholds than human subjects. Simulations of diffusion calibrated with the experimental findings show that, holding network structure fixed, even a modest share of artificial agents leads to higher total adoption. Our findings suggest that the presence of artificial agents in social networks can alter diffusion.

authors.name: Mingmin Feng, Eric Hitz, Luca Lazzaro, Radu Tanase, Ren\'e Algesheimer, Manuel S. Mariani

papers.title: Viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges to benchmark fluid simulations
papers.summary: We present semi-analytical solutions for the evolution of both the temperature and chemical potentials for viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges. Such a solution can be especially useful in testing numerical codes intended to simulate relativistic fluids with large chemical potentials. The freeze-out hypersurface profiles for constant energy density are calculated, along with the corresponding normal vectors and presented as a new unit test for numerical codes. We also compare the influence of the equation of state on the semi-analytical solutions. We benchmark the newly developed Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code CCAKE that includes both shear viscosity and three conserved charges. The numerical solutions are in excellent agreement with the semi-analytical solution and also are able to accurately reproduce the hypersurface at freeze-out.

authors.name: Kevin Ingles, Jordi Salinas San Mart\'in, Willian Serenone, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler

papers.title: Probing chiral topological order of the Kitaev honeycomb on a trapped ion processor
papers.summary: Kitaev's honeycomb model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable system hosting a quantum spin liquid with non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected edge modes, offering a platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, real candidate Kitaev materials invariably include complex secondary interactions that obscure the realization of spin-liquid behavior and demand novel quantum computational approaches for efficient simulation. Here we report quantum simulations of a 22-site Kitaev honeycomb lattice on a trapped-ion quantum processor, without and with non-integrable Heisenberg interactions that are present in real materials. We develop efficient quantum circuits for ground-state preparation, achieving high accuracy with energy errors equivalent to an effective temperature $\approx 0.2$ (in units of the Kitaev interactions), consistent with the experimentally relevant spin-liquid regime. Starting from these states, we apply controlled perturbations and measure time-dependent spin correlations along the system's edge. In the non-Abelian phase, we observe chiral edge dynamics consistent with a non-zero Chern number, a hallmark of chiral topological order, which vanishes upon transition to the Abelian toric code phase. Extending to the non-integrable Kitaev-Heisenberg model, we find that weak Heisenberg interactions preserve chiral edge dynamics, while stronger couplings suppress them, signaling the breakdown of topological protection. These simulations establish edge-mode dynamical simulations on quantum computers as a staple technique to understand the topological and chiral phases of matter in Hamiltonians beyond integrability.

authors.name: Ammar Ali, Joe Gibbs, Keerthi Kumaran, Varadharajan Muruganandam, Bo Xiao, Paul Kairys, G\'abor Hal\'asz, Arnab Banerjee, Phillip C. Lotshaw

papers.title: Optimal Calibration of Qubit Detuning and Crosstalk
papers.summary: Characterizing and calibrating physical qubits is essential for maintaining the performance of quantum processors. A key challenge in this process is the presence of crosstalk that complicates the estimation of individual qubit detunings. In this work, we derive optimal strategies for estimating detuning and crosstalk parameters by optimizing Ramsey interference experiments using Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound. We compare several calibration protocols, including measurements of a single quadrature at multiple times and of two quadratures at a single time, for a fixed number of total measurements. Our results predict that the latter approach yields the highest precision and robustness in both cases of isolated and coupled qubits. We validate experimentally our approach using a single NV center as well as superconducting transmons. Our approach enables accurate parameter extraction with significantly fewer measurements, resulting in up to a 50% reduction in calibration time while maintaining estimation accuracy.

authors.name: David Shnaiderov, Matan Ben Dov, Yoav Woldiger, Assaf Hamo, Eugene Demler, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre

papers.title: Probing tensor monopoles and gerbe invariants in three-dimensional topological matter
papers.summary: We show that momentum-space tensor monopoles corresponding to nontrivial vector bundle generalizations, known as bundle gerbes, can be realized in bands of three-dimensional topological matter with nontrivial Hopf invariants. We provide a universal construction of tensor Berry connections in these topological phases, demonstrating how obstructions therein lead to $\mathbb{Z}$-quantized bulk magnetoelectric and nonlinear optical phenomena in the presence of spacetime inversion ($\mathcal{PT}$) symmetry. We then pinpoint that these quantum effects are supported by intraband and interband torsion leading to nontrivial Dixmier-Douady classes in most known Hopf phases and in more general topological insulators realizing gerbe invariants falling beyond the tenfold classification of topological phases of matter. We furthermore provide an interacting generalization upon introducing many-body gerbe invariants by employing twisted boundary conditions. This opens an avenue to study gerbe invariants realized through higher-dimensional charge fractionalizations that can be electromagnetically probed.

authors.name: Wojciech J. Jankowski, Robert-Jan Slager, Giandomenico Palumbo

papers.title: Globalizing the Carleman linear embedding method for nonlinear dynamics
papers.summary: The Carleman embedding method is a well-known technique for linearizing a system of nonlinear differential equations, but fails to converge in regions where there are multiple fixed points. We prove that the need for the solution to be expressible as a convergent Taylor series of the initial conditions leads to restrictions on the stability and convergence of the Carleman algorithm. Inspired by this realization, we propose and test three different versions of a global piecewise Carleman embedding technique, based on partitioning space into multiple regions where the center and size of the embedding region are chosen to control convergence. The first method switches between local linearization regions of fixed size once the trajectory reaches the boundary of the current linearization chart. During the transition, the embedding is reconstructed within the newly created chart, centered at the transition point. The second method also adapts the chart size dynamically, enhancing accuracy in regions where multiple fixed points are located. The third method partitions the state space using a static grid with precomputed linearization charts of fixed size, making it more suitable for applications that require high speed. All techniques are numerically tested on multiple integrable and chaotic nonlinear dynamical systems demonstrating their applicability for problems that are completely intractable for the standard Carleman embedding method. Simulations of chaotic dynamical systems such as various types of strange attractors demonstrate the power of the adaptive methods. However, global Carleman methods face fundamental limitations when simulating chaotic nonlinear systems on quantum computers due to overhead during nonlinear remapping.

authors.name: Ivan Novikau, Ilon Joseph

papers.title: HelioFill: History-Conditioned Diffusion Estimation of Solar Far-Side EUV Emission
papers.summary: The loss of STEREO-B in 2014 created a persistent blind spot in Extreme UltraViolet imaging of the solar far-side. We present textbf{HelioFill}, to the authors' knowledge, the first denoising-diffusion inpainting model that estimates the unobserved sector of full-Sun 304 A maps from the current Earth-side (SDO) and STEREO-A views. Because these views cannot constrain structures fully enclosed in the unobserved sector, HelioFill's diffusion stage is also conditioned on the sector's own rotation history, supplied as causal persistence and information-age maps; a rectified-flow refinement then adds realistic small-scale texture. Test rotations are separated from the diffusion stage's training timestamps by full-rotation guard bands. Over the unobserved sector, HelioFill's estimate correlates with the three-view truth at rho=0.520, above persistence and the input-independent climatological mean on 97.9% of the test maps, which conditioning on the current views alone does not achieve; in peak signal-to-noise ratio it exceeds them by 2.27 and 0.66 dB and matches a direct observation of the sector made approx 29h before or after it. The refinement lowers learned perceptual image patch similarity by 11% at a cost of 0.50 dB and 0.055 in correlation. HelioFill localizes active regions better than persistence (Dice score 0.449 vs. 0.384) and detects fully enclosed ones, although persistence detects more individual regions and coronal holes remain poorly reproduced. Against near-simultaneous far-side Solar Orbiter/EUI observations from 2022-2025, HelioFill correlates with the truth at rho=0.375, above climatology and level with persistence, which it exceeds in PSNR and structural similarity index; its diffusion stage alone reaches 0.460, above both, and the refinement stage costs the difference. HelioFill thus provides observationally plausible global EUV context within quantified limits.

authors.name: Firas Ben Ameur, Rayan Dhib, Yahia Battach, Andrea Lani, Matteo Parsani, Omar Knio, Stefaan Poedts

papers.title: Inaccessibility in public transit networks: A study of the London and New York City subway networks
papers.summary: The study of networks derived from infrastructure systems has received considerable attention, yet the accessibility of such systems, remains comparatively underexplored. This study examines infrastructure-based accessibility in two major legacy transit systems, the London Underground and the New York City Subway. We construct accessibility-restricted subnetworks in which nodes represent accessible stations and edges represent connections between them, and compare them with the corresponding full transit networks. We analyze the cyclomatic number, betweenness, and closeness centrality to identify key accessible hubs and differences in network organization. London has a larger share of accessible stations, and its accessible network retains more of the alternative routes of its full network, whereas New York City has a more compact accessible core concentrated around central Manhattan and major interchanges. Comparing the observed accessible stations with random sets of the same size, we find that in London they have higher betweenness centrality than random allocations, but more of their stations are beyond two stops of an accessible station, consistent with accessibility concentration at major interchanges and along fully step-free lines. In New York City, their higher betweenness centrality is fully explained by their concentration at interchanges, and their coverage is similar to that of random allocations. We also examine income and daytime activity around accessible stations. In both systems, several of the most central accessible stations are in high-activity locations, whereas accessible stations show no consistent relationship with median income. Our findings highlight substantial differences in accessibility between and within the two systems and demonstrate the utility of network-theoretic methods for understanding and improving transit infrastructure.

authors.name: Katherine Betz

papers.title: QuantGraph: A Receding-Horizon Quantum Graph Solver
papers.summary: Dynamic programming is a cornerstone of graph-based optimization. While effective, it scales unfavorably with problem size. In this work, we present QuantGraph, a two-stage quantum-enhanced framework that casts local and global graph-optimization problems as quantum-searches over discrete trajectory spaces. The solver is designed to operate efficiently by first finding a sequence of locally optimal transitions in the graph (local stage), without considering full trajectories. The accumulated cost of the resulting candidate acts as a threshold that prunes the search space (up to 60% reduction for certain examples). The subsequent global stage, based on this threshold, refines the solution. To achieve scalability and robustness, we draw on principles from control theory and embed QuantGraph's global stage within a receding-horizon model-predictive-control scheme. This classical layer stabilizes and guides the quantum search, improving precision and reducing computational burden. In practice, the resulting closed-loop system exhibits robust behavior and lower query complexity. Notably, for a fixed control horizon and query budget, QuantGraph supports approximately twice as many control discretization bits while still benefiting from Grover-search's inherent quadratic speedup compared to classical methods.

authors.name: Pranav Vaidhyanathan, Aristotelis Papatheodorou, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur, Mark T. Mitchison, Natalia Ares, Ioannis Havoutis

papers.title: No prior over nuisance parameters is required for credible intervals and Bayes factors
papers.summary: This work shows that there are procedures that maintain the subjective Bayesian property of coherently informing decision making under uncertainty (i.e., if they tell you to take a certain bet, you should) without needing to assign a prior distribution over nuisance parameters, only over the parameter(s) of interest. We first carefully define this sense of 'credibility', and show that within this framework one can condition on any statistic of choice rather than only on the full dataset. This relaxation of credibility is a natural middle ground between Bayesian and frequentist statistics in the following sense: To a p% Bayesian credible set we should assign a p% belief after observing both the dataset and the interval, to p% frequentist sets we can generally only assign a p% belief before observing either the data or the interval, while to the statistical sets proposed here we can assign a p% belief after observing the set, but not necessarily after inspecting the full dataset ourselves. We then show that choosing a conditioning statistic whose distribution we know, or can bound, for each value of the parameter of interest leads to prior-free Bayes factors even for composite hypotheses, and to non-parametric credible sets with priors only over the parameter of interest. We derive such procedures for several (groups of) statistical problems. Particularly noteworthy is that any frequentist test gives a Bayes factor of the power over the size of the test, and that anytime-validity of E-process-based tests can be carried over to this Bayes factor.

authors.name: Tim Ritmeester

papers.title: Confinement Limits Cell Shape and Mitotic Pressure During Division
papers.summary: Cells often divide under mechanical confinement, where surrounding structures restrict shape changes during cytokinesis. We analyze a minimal model of a dividing cell as an incompressible volume bounded by an interface with effective isotropic tension, and show that confinement imposes a minimum attainable furrow radius. Beyond this limit, the cytokinetic ring can continue to contract within a septum without further furrow ingression, leaving the cell shape, mitotic pressure, and transmitted force unchanged. We determine this confinement-limited state for rigid parallel walls, soft axial confinement, and three-dimensional enclosures. Between parallel walls, the limiting force and minimum furrow radius collapse onto universal curves when scaled by surface tension and cell size. In soft confinement, environmental stiffness and spindle forces select the operating point. In three-dimensional confinement, the free volume between the cell and the confinement controls force transmission and cell shape. This yields a method for inferring the mechanical state of a cell dividing in deformable three-dimensional confinement from its shape. The radius and tangent angle of the cell surface at the stalled furrow and at the point where the cell detaches from its surroundings determine the mitotic pressure and the axial force carried by the cell surface, relative to the cortical tension.

authors.name: Amit Singh Vishen

papers.title: peapods: A Rust-Accelerated Monte Carlo Package for Ising and XY Spin Systems
papers.summary: We present peapods, an open-source Python package for Monte Carlo simulation of classical spin models with arbitrary couplings, whose sampling loop runs in Rust. It samples Ising models on periodic Bravais lattices given by user-specified neighbor offsets, optionally with open or antiperiodic boundaries, and XY models with signed couplings and site dilution on hypercubic lattices. Besides Metropolis and heat-bath sweeps, Swendsen-Wang and Wolff cluster updates and parallel tempering, it provides a family of replica cluster moves for spin glasses: the Houdayer, J\"org and Chayes-Machta-Redner moves, multi-pair variants of the first two, replica-permutation moves and a gauged form of them, and Swendsen-Wang replica Monte Carlo across temperatures. The same-temperature moves share one construction, a symmetry of the replicas' joint energy applied on clusters, and one-step stationarity tests from exact Boltzmann samples on small lattices check each family of moves that satisfies detailed balance. The package measures overlap distributions, spin-glass correlation lengths, autocorrelation times, equilibration and tempering-flow diagnostics, and jackknife errors over disorder samples. It reproduces the exact critical temperatures of the square and triangular Ising lattices, and its Binder curves for simple-cubic, BCC and FCC lattices agree at the literature critical temperatures. For the three-dimensional $\pm J$ spin glass, the crossings of $\xi_{\mathrm{SG}}/L$ for $L \le 12$ extrapolate, with the Janus correction exponent held fixed, to $T_c = 1.085(42)$, consistent with the Janus value $1.1019(29)$. For the two-dimensional XY model, the helicity modulus, correlation length and structure factor agree with high-precision reference data within $1.9$ standard errors. This article describes version 0.3.0.

authors.name: Yan Ru Pei

papers.title: A Reduced Order Model for First-Principles Atomistic Simulations
papers.summary: To leverage the redundancy between the electronic structure computed for various model parameters such as varying atomic positions, we present a data-driven modeling framework for Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory that bypasses the explicit optimization of electronic wavefunctions. We sample \textit{a priori} representative atomic configurations and construct a low-dimensional basis that efficiently approximates the electronic structure subspace. Subsequently, we employ this reduced basis in an iterative solver for the electronic single particle density matrix, thereby enabling the efficient determination of ground state without iterative wavefunction optimization. We demonstrate the accuracy of our approach in a Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics of a water molecule, showing that the resulting simulations accurately reproduce key structural properties, such as bond lengths and bond angle, obtained from full first-principles molecular dynamics. This work highlights the potential of data-driven approaches to develop low-dimensional electronic structure representations for first-principles simulations.

authors.name: Siu Wun Cheung, Youngsoo Choi, Jonas Kaufman, Daniel Osei-Kuffuor, Jean-Luc Fattebert

papers.title: Digitally Optimized Initializations for Fast Thermodynamic Computing
papers.summary: Thermodynamic computing harnesses the relaxation dynamics of physical systems to perform matrix operations. A key limitation of such approaches is the often long thermalization time required for the system to approach equilibrium with sufficient accuracy. Here, we introduce a hybrid digital-thermodynamic algorithm that substantially accelerates relaxation through optimized initializations inspired by the Mpemba effect. In the proposed scheme, a classical digital processor efficiently computes an initialization that suppresses slow relaxation modes, after which the physical system performs the remaining computation through its intrinsic relaxation dynamics. We focus on overdamped Langevin dynamics for quadratic energy landscapes, analyzing the spectral structure of the associated Fokker-Planck operator and identifying the corresponding optimal initial covariances. This yields a predictable reduction in thermalization time, determined by the spectrum of the encoded matrix. We derive analytic expressions for the resulting speedups and numerically analyze thermodynamic implementations of matrix inversion and determinant computation as concrete examples. Our results show that optimized initialization protocols provide a simple and broadly applicable route to accelerating thermodynamic computations.

authors.name: Mattia Moroder, Felix C. Binder, John Goold

papers.title: Neural and Tensor-Network Representations of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Cluster and Dipolar-cluster SPT States
papers.summary: The $\mathbb Z_N$ cluster state is a paradigmatic example of symmetry-protected topological (SPT) order with $\mathbb Z_N\times\mathbb Z_N$ symmetry. We express its wavefunction and those of dipolar cluster states as a projector-based realization of correlator product states, which we dub the $P$-representation. The local projector $P$, also known as the copy tensor, can have multiple legs connecting a site to neighboring sites depending on the model and its deformations. We construct explicit wavefunctions of cluster and dipolar cluster states under deformation using the $P$-representation. The transition to the neural quantum state representations of the same state occurs by splitting the interaction matrices between $\mathbb{Z}_N$ spins into a pair of weight matrices. We derive these weight matrices explicitly for the cluster and dipolar cluster states, thus generalizing previous works on $\mathbb{Z}_2$ cluster states. The projector scheme then leads to the tensor product state (TPS) representation of the cluster-state wavefunctions. We benchmark the resulting TPS construction against conventional MPS representation using density-matrix renormalization group simulations and argue that the TPS could offer efficient representations for some modulated and deformed SPT states.

authors.name: Seungho Lee, Daesik Kim, Hyun-Yong Lee, Jung Hoon Han

papers.title: What Can Actually Be Proved About the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Paradox? Operational Consistency, Locality, and Quantum Completeness
papers.summary: The Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) argument concerns whether accurate quantum predictions imply a complete description of physical reality. We distinguish predictive adequacy, operational no-signalling, EPR elements of reality, and ontological completeness. We formalize the EPR reality criterion using observable-, value-, and context-dependent predicates and prove that its incompleteness implication does not entail a prohibition on objectively stochastic origins of outcomes. A two-observable stochastic-source countermodel establishes this limited logical non-entailment, without addressing randomness generated at measurement or reproducing the full quantum assemblage. We illustrate the latter distinction using an established two-setting qubit steering inequality. For continuous variables, we derive inferred-variance and Gaussian-steering criteria for a stipulated instantaneous elastic-collision map, studying mass ratios, incident wave-packet spreading, covariance inflation, and readout noise. We distinguish losses of fixed-axis Reid violations from losses of optimized Gaussian steering. These results are conditional benchmarks, not predictions for the proposed finite-duration ion-collision apparatus, whose scattering dynamics and preparation and measurement parameters remain unspecified. We also show why uncertainty inequalities and exponential decay memorylessness alone do not establish intrinsic ontological randomness. The analysis delimits the logical and physical assumptions needed for claims about EPR completeness without proposing a new hidden-variable dynamics.

authors.name: Miko{\l}aj Sienicki, Krzysztof Sienicki

papers.title: Giant spontaneous Kerr effect and its self-doping dependence in altermagnetic MnTe
papers.summary: Altermagnetism, a third class of collinear magnetism with spin-split bands and vanishing net magnetization, has emerged in hexagonal {\alpha}-MnTe, a promising platform for ultrafast, stray-field-free spintronics. Whether MnTe's macroscopic symmetry-breaking signatures reflect ideal altermagnetic order or are activated by defects remains open. Here we report giant spontaneous Kerr rotations of up to 1500 rad in {\alpha}-MnTe single crystals at the telecommunication wavelength of 1550 nm, onsetting precisely at the N\'eel temperature TN = 307 K. The signal appears in disjoint macroscopic patches whose amplitude tracks the sample conductivity, and a hole-conducting {\alpha}-MnTe film reproduces this response together with an anomalous Hall effect. Within a single crystal, Kerr-active regions are optically distinct from their Kerr-silent surroundings in co-registered reflection maps. These observations indicate that carrier self-doping, rather than ideal altermagnetic order alone, governs the giant magneto-optical response, and establish telecom-wavelength Kerr imaging as a practical readout for altermagnetic spintronics.

authors.name: Weitung Yang, Choongjae Won, Cory Cress, Weihang Lu, Xiaochen Fang, Shelby Fields, Nicholas Combs, Shaofeng Han, Marshall Zachary Franklin, Steven P. Bennett, Sang-Wook Cheong, Jing Xia

papers.title: Angular-momentum quantization as intrinsic reference for complete RF polarimetry with Rydberg atoms
papers.summary: Rydberg electrometry leverages non-metallic vapor cells with highly excited atoms to link RF field properties to a spectroscopic readout in the optical domain. Demonstrations have so far mainly addressed linearly polarized fields inducing a rotationally invariant atomic dressed-level splitting. Here we report on measurements of RF fields in a general state of polarization (SOP) which we map onto the Poincar\'e sphere through spectroscopic fingerprints characteristic of a member of an angular-momentum hierarchy. For SOPs circumnavigating the Poincar\'e sphere's prime meridian, we witness a continuous transformation of the member's eigenenergy spectrum. Conversely, such fingerprints can be used as input to a protocol for polarimetric characterization of the RF field, and we demonstrate its extension to SOPs beyond the prime meridian. Because the relative positions of eigenenergies are locked in place by angular-momentum quantization, the framework is universal and calibration-free, and our specific demonstration in rubidium generalizes to all systems with a single valence electron.

authors.name: Matthew Chilcott, Laurits N. Stokholm, Matthew Cloutman, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, Niels Kj{\ae}rgaard

papers.title: Evolution of cooperation in multiplex interaction networks
papers.summary: Across biological and social systems, preferential interactions among similar individuals can promote cooperation. To account for real-world interactions unfolding across multiple, simultaneous dimensions, we develop a framework for the evolution of cooperation in multiplex networks. Each layer is defined by a distinct phenotypic trait, with homophily favoring encounters between similar partners. We derive analytical conditions for natural selection to favor cooperation when phenotypes are independent or exhibit epistasis, allowing for different modes of mutation coupling. Despite payoffs being aggregated across layers, the cooperation conditions separate by layer under weak selection. Each condition depends on local payoffs and a structure coefficient determined by the effective number of phenotypes and the mutation rates. Epistasis restricts the phenotypes available on a layer and can thus shift its strategy distribution relative to that of its isolated counterpart. We show that phenotypic diversity fosters cooperation by partitioning populations into assortative niches. Furthermore, in finite populations, intensifying the prisoner's dilemma shifts the dependence of cooperation on strategy mutation from a monotonic decrease, through a U-shaped response, to a monotonic increase. Beyond weak selection, simulations show that accumulated payoffs across layers can alter mean cooperation relative to isolated systems even when phenotypes are independent. Our study unravels how homophily based on multiple phenotypes can shape the evolution of cooperation in heterogeneous populations.

authors.name: Zijie Chen, Xingru Chen, Feng Fu

papers.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
papers.summary: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.

authors.name: Xijia Miao

papers.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
papers.summary: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

authors.name: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu

papers.title: Broadband High-Level Squeezed Light using Waveguide Optical Parametric Amplifiers with External Dispersion Compensation
papers.summary: We demonstrate broadband phase-sensitive amplification (PSA) measurement of squeezed light generated by a waveguide optical parametric amplifier (OPA) with external dispersion compensation. In broadband systems, group velocity dispersion (GVD) induces a frequency-dependent rotation of the squeezing axis, which limits the observable bandwidth in PSA measurements. While dispersion compensation between two OPAs has been demonstrated previously, we show that the quantity to be compensated is not the material group-delay dispersion $D$ itself but a gain-dependent effective value $D\tanh r/(2r)$, where $r$ is the squeezing parameter, and realize the compensation with free-space fused-silica plates whose insertion loss is $0.4\%$. As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of $5.9\pm0.2$~dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5~dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of $5.9\pm0.1$ THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of $6.9\pm0.1$ THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.

authors.name: Takumi Suzuki, Shotaro Oki, Kazuki Hirota, Takaya Hoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Taichi Yamashima, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Mamoru Endo, Akira Furusawa

papers.title: Quantum Beam-Splitter Cooling and Thermometry in Large Trapped-Ion Crystals
papers.summary: We propose and characterize a protocol for rapid near-ground state cooling of the center-of-mass (c.m.) mode of a large trapped ion crystal. When the initial mean thermal occupation of the mode $\bar{n}_i$ is small compared to the number of ions $N$ ($\bar{n}_i \ll N$), a red sideband drive implements a beam-splitter type state exchange (SWAP operation) between the mode and the collective spin of the $N$ ions, with the latter effectively serving as a quantum harmonic oscillator. Subsequently, a reset of the spins removes the entropy, leading to near-ground state cooling of the c.m. mode. We term this protocol as quantum beam-splitter cooling (QBSC). We analyze the impact of several practical imperfections on the final temperature achievable under QBSC, including finite ion number, off-resonant carrier and blue-sideband contributions, the sideband drives arising from spectator modes, and spatially inhomogeneous driving across the crystal. We outline practical strategies to eliminate the carrier drive. We extend our analysis to multiple cycles of QBSC and also generalize the analysis to demonstrate the cooling of non-c.m. modes using this protocol. Furthermore, we show that measuring the population statistics of the ions at the end of the SWAP operation can enable near-optimal quantum beam-splitter thermometry (QBST), with the classical Fisher information approaching the quantum Fisher information of a thermal state. We discuss the connection of QBSC with continuous sideband cooling and compare QBST with a recently proposed rapid adiabatic passage-based thermometry scheme. Our work constitutes an example of harnessing many-body effects to open new routes to laser cooling and thermometry in large trapped ion crystals.

authors.name: Kirthik Rajakumar, Ansh Das, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar

papers.title: Absolute displacement calibration of a levitated nanoparticle with real-time heterodyne demodulation
papers.summary: We report a heterodyne scheme for the position readout of an optomechanical system, in particular an optically levitated nanoparticle, based on digital in-phase and quadrature demodulation on a field-programmable gate array. Compared to the standard homodyne approach, it offers three key advantages: it requires no phase lock, it produces a signal linearly proportional to the particle displacement, and its calibration is immune to drifts in the optical power of the local oscillator and of the scattered field. Combined with a vectorial model of the focal field, it measures the displacement in length units without free parameters. Through simultaneous homodyne and heterodyne measurements on the same trapped particle we demonstrate these advantages: the heterodyne follows a driven particle linearly up to amplitudes at which the homodyne response folds back, and calibrates the homodyne, whose standard thermometric calibration we find biased by 33 %. Inverting equipartition, the calibrated readout measures the mass of the particle with an uncertainty below 1 %, after removing a bias of up to 20 % caused by absorption heating at 1550 nm. The method can be used in any optomechanical system based on phase readout.

authors.name: Daniel Tandeitnik, Gabriel Dias, Thiago Guerreiro

papers.title: Track fitting at the full LHC collision rate
papers.summary: The LHCb experiment at the Large Hadron Collider underwent a major upgrade before the LHC Run 3 data-taking period, employing an all-software approach in its trigger system. Here we present a fast implementation of a Kalman filter, used in the first trigger stage since the 2025 data-taking period, allowing to determine parameter estimates of charged-particle trajectories at the full LHCb collision frequency of 30 MHz. This approach replaces computationally expensive magnetic field map lookups and numerical integration methods with fast analytical parameterisations while maintaining the mathematical framework of Kalman filtering. Implemented on approximately 500 GPUs within the first-level trigger, the algorithm has replaced the previous partial track fitting algorithm in the real-time trigger environment at the cost of a 2% increase in processing time. Compared to the previous fitter this parameterised Kalman filter shows a significantly improved momentum resolution, resulting in a factor of two improvement in the invariant mass resolutions for reconstructed D0 and J/{\psi} hadrons. It additionally demonstrates greater robustness against detector misalignment effects and substantially sharpens the discrimination between genuine particle trajectories and accidental background, more than doubling the rejection of the latter at no cost to genuine-track efficiency, for a standard selection working point.

authors.name: Pierre Billoir, Thomas Boettcher, Michel De Cian, Lennart H. Uecker

papers.title: Embedded quantum computing for many-body surface reaction
papers.summary: Predictive simulations of catalytic interfaces require correlated electronic-structure treatments that describe localized chemical transformations while retaining the influence of the extended metallic environment. We introduce QC-DFET, a quantum-computing density-functional embedding framework that maps surface-reaction active spaces to compact, environment-aware qubit Hamiltonians. A reaction-consistent active-space protocol preserves orbital continuity along reaction coordinates, while quantum-selected configuration interaction based on measurements from the Zuchongzhi superconducting quantum processor and strongly contracted perturbation theory capture static and dynamic correlation. On Cu(111), QC-DFET treats active spaces up to 28 qubits and is validated through a hierarchy of experimentally constrained surface-chemistry challenges. H2 dissociation/desorption tests balanced bond breaking and recombination barriers, CO adsorption tests site selectivity and metal-adsorbate bonding, and formate hydrogenation tests competing hydrogenation branches with different kinetic and thermodynamic signatures. Across these cases, QC-DFET reproduces bidirectional H2 barriers, recovers the observed top-site preference and adsorption strength of CO, and reconciles the experimentally benchmarked H2COO* reverse barrier with the lower forward barrier to HCOOH*. These results establish embedded quantum computing as a practical route to correlated surface-reaction energetics.

authors.name: Dedong Wan, Xiaopeng Li, Yi Fan, Jie Liu, Xiongzhi Zeng, Zhenyu Li

papers.title: Magneto-optical signal from $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler thin films in MOKE and BLS
papers.summary: $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds offer a versatile, composition-tunable platform for magnonics and spintronics. Among them, the half-metallic $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ is of particular interest for magnonics owing to its ultralow Gilbert damping, yet its weak magneto-optical response in the visible challenges optical probing such as Brillouin light scattering (BLS). We study the magneto-optical response of epitaxial $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}X$ films ($X = \{\mathrm{Al}_x\mathrm{Si}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Ga}_x\mathrm{Ge}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Sn}\}$) by magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy and BLS. Angle-resolved MOKE resolves a significant, wavelength-dependent quadratic MOKE (QMOKE) only for $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$, whereas $\mathrm{Co_2MnAl}$, $\mathrm{Co_2MnGa}$ and $\mathrm{Co_2MnSn}$ respond dominantly linearly. Comparing BLS intensities of thermal magnons at two wavelengths, $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ gives the weakest signal at 532 nm yet among the strongest at 457 nm, tracking the spectral dependence of its Kerr angle. These results emphasise the relation between the two magneto-optical techniques, guiding the choice of probing wavelength for $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds, and provide a transferable approach for other magnetic materials.

authors.name: Anna Maria Friedel, Nicolas Fermon, Tobias B\"ottcher, S\'ebastien Petit-Watelot, St\'ephane Andrieu, Philipp Pirro

papers.title: Local molecular motions encode time-resolved infrared spectra of proteins
papers.summary: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy probes protein dynamics over timescales spanning more than ten orders of magnitude, yet the molecular motions underlying the observed kinetic signatures have remained elusive. Here we combine transient infrared spectroscopy with nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to establish a direct connection between experimental relaxation times and local structural motions. Studying single-domain allosteric proteins, we find that inter-residue contact distances provide the structural representation that most faithfully reproduces the experimental dynamics. Correlation analysis identifies localized networks of coordinated contacts that mediate long-range coupling between secondary-structure elements. The characteristic timescales of these contact networks quantitatively match the experimentally observed relaxation processes, enabling each kinetic step to be assigned to a specific molecular motion. Applied to allosteric signal propagation in PDZ3 and photoinduced perturbation of the binding pocket of PDZ2 or a ligand binding to PDZ2, this framework provides an atomistic picture of hierarchical protein relaxation and establishes a general framework for connecting transient infrared spectroscopy with the molecular mechanisms of protein dynamics.

authors.name: Emanuel Dorbath, Peter Hamm, Gerhard Stock

papers.title: Simultaneous measurements of enzyme propagation and biopolymer mobility elucidate the directional degradation of a dense biopolymer matrix
papers.summary: Enzymatic degradation of dense biopolymer matrices is central to natural processes like digestion and cancer progression, as well as applications in biomedicine, biomass valorization, and nanotechnology. Yet, it remains unclear how enzyme propagation and substrate degradation interact, and especially whether and how enzymatic activity shapes the propagation process. Here, we bridge this gap by employing Fluorescence-Photon Correlation Imaging to simultaneously track directional enzyme propagation and biopolymer degradation in a model system. We use viscoelastic solutions of arabinoxylan, a hemicellulosic polysaccharide with a xylan backbone substituted by arabinose and ferulic acid, and a fluorescently labeled arabinoxylanase, an enzyme that randomly cleaves the xylan chain. To resolve enzyme propagation and biopolymer degradation with spatiotemporal precision, we combine fluorescence imaging of the enzyme with speckle-based photon correlation imaging, a technique to quantify biopolymer mobility, which we show is a proxy for biopolymer degradation. Our experiments reveal that enzyme diffusion is decoupled from catalytic activity, with no evidence of activity-enhanced diffusion. Instead, the progression of the degradation front is governed by a combination of enzyme diffusion, reaction kinetics, and slow enzyme deactivation, the latter being characterized by a double-exponential decay. By extending the Michaelis-Menten framework to space- and time-dependent conditions, we quantify how cumulative enzyme exposure and deactivation shape the degradation dynamics. This work establishes a quantitative framework to understand enzymatic processes in concentrated, beyond-dilute-regime substrates, with implications for the rationalization of biocatalytic systems in industrial and biomedical applications.

authors.name: Vincenzo Ruzzi, Antoine Bouchoux, Carole Antoine-Assor, Donna-Joe Bigot, Salma Menzeh, Maike Petermann, Laurent Leclercq, Herv\'e Cottet, C\'edric Montanier, Claire Dumon, Luca Cipelletti, Laurence Ramos

papers.title: Coupled Electronic Structure and Phonon Transport Driven by Bonding Reconstruction in Ba-B-C Clathrates
papers.summary: Composition-driven changes in electron count, structural symmetry and bonding environment can couple the electronic and thermal responses in a material. Here, with density-functional theory and machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), we compare cubic BaB3C3 with its B-C substituted tetragonal counterpart, BaB2C4. The additional valence electron and accompanying change in crystal symmetry drive a transition from metallic BaB3C3 to semiconducting BaB2C4 and the formation of short/strong C-C bonds. The reconstructed bonding network hardens the phonon spectrum, with the maximum frequency increasing from 800 to 900. At room temperature, the in-plane lattice thermal conductivity increases from 7.6 to 18.7 W/mK, while the thermal transport alters from isotropic to anisotropic for BaB2C4. This enhancement is associated with the strengthened bonding network, higher phonon frequencies/group velocities, longer lifetimes and larger mean free paths. Machine learning potentials accurately reproduced the DFT-level energies and forces with negligible errors, and the harmonic and anharmonic features are benchmarked against explicit first-principles calculations. Our findings demonstrate that minimal B-C substitution provides a viable strategy to link composition- and structure-associated bonding reconstruction with correlated electronic and phononic alterations.

authors.name: Ghulam Hussain, Dario Massa, Muhammad Usman, Rajibul Islam, Magdalena Birowska, Carmine Autieri, Xiaoguang Li

papers.title: Respiratory Mask Testing: Airway Inertance and System Dynamics
papers.summary: Life support equipment coupled to the human lungs forms a complex, nonlinear dynamic system. Current respiratory mask test standards rely on sinusoidal breathing machines and surrogate trachea geometries that substantially reduce physiologically relevant airway inertance. This paper shows that the ISO 16900-5 trachea does not generate physiologically meaningful exhalation momentum, limiting the ability of standard test configurations to reveal valve dynamics relevant to human use. A physiologically motivated "lip-nozzle" surrogate is introduced as a diagnostic tool to restore representative momentum transfer, enabling observation of exhalation behavior that is not observable under existing test conditions. Nonlinear dynamic simulations incorporating this surrogate identify a force-balanced operating regime in which exhalation-jet momentum can offset flow-induced valve resistance. In one representative case, the exhalation mean effective pressure imposed on the wearer falls by approximately 85% and the flow work across the exhalation valve by approximately 92%. Because people do not exhale through a fully open mouth, this momentum is available in normal use. A valve aligned with the exhaled jet can recover part of the energy the wearer has already spent, rather than requiring additional effort. The magnitude of this effect depends on valve characteristics such as efficiency and the relationship between restoring force and lift, making it a design consideration for future valve development. Implications for mask design, valve placement, and future test methods are discussed. This work does not propose new performance limits or acceptance criteria; rather, it demonstrates how current test fixtures suppress inertance- and momentum-driven effects that can materially influence exhalation valve dynamics.

authors.name: Mark M. Koeroghlian, Suraj Pawar, Raul G. Longoria

papers.title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
papers.summary: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $\Omega_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $\Omega_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.

authors.name: Yusheng Zhao, Han Wang, Mingrui Jing, Zhongyi Ni, Hongshun Yao, Xin Wang, Jie Wang, Jinguo Liu

papers.title: Round-Based Contagion Generates Chaos from Oscillatory Dynamics: A Two-Stage Contagion Map
papers.summary: Many social processes unfold in rounds, such as elections, meetings or turns of a game, in which individuals update synchronously. We show that this round structure can turn a regular oscillation into chaos. In Katriel's differential equations, two-stage contagion (adoption after two contacts with adopters) combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos. From the elementary reactions we derive a deterministic map $F_\tau$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $\tau$: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. For short rounds the map follows the relaxation cycle, and the phase of successive outbreaks obeys a circle homeomorphism, which excludes chaos. As the rounds lengthen, this circle map loses invertibility and the invariant curve breaks down; once a round lasts about two mean adoption times, comparable to the duration of an outbreak, the attractor is chaotic, while Katriel's equations remain on a periodic relaxation cycle. With the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis, whereas Katriel's equations oscillate for $0.022<p<0.41$. Chaos is supported by the Lyapunov spectrum (Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$), the correlation dimension, the 0-1 test, ordinal-pattern complexity, saddle periodic orbits and a horseshoe of the phase map. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos.

authors.name: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci

papers.title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
papers.summary: AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.

authors.name: Lixing Wang, Leena Diehl, Spencer Ellis, Marcos Fern\'andez Garc\'ia, Gabriele Giacomini, Vagelis Gkougkousis, Ben Kilminster, Jingyu Luo, Anna Macchiolo, Yajna Mahabeer, Yevhenii Padniuk, Daria Senina, Samantha Sunnarborg, Jessica Tang, Alessandro Tricoli, Don C. Wong, Gaetano Barone

papers.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
papers.summary: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

authors.name: Gourab Panigrahi, Phani Motamarri

papers.title: When Nonlocal Total Derivatives Are Not Variationally Trivial
papers.summary: We study total time derivatives in infinite-order and nonlocal Lagrangian mechanics. In the formal infinite-order setting, such terms remain variationally trivial. For nonlocal functionals on trajectories, however, exactness in the form $L=DW$ is not sufficient to ensure a vanishing nonlocal Euler-Lagrange expression. We exhibit a smooth convolution-type counterexample.

authors.name: Carlos Heredia

papers.title: Galilean cosmologies in two dimensions
papers.summary: Inspired by Carroll black holes, we consider the most general theory of Galilean dilaton gravity in two dimensions. We find generically that the solution space describes cosmological spacetimes. From a limiting perspective, these Galilean geometries connect the white and black hole singularities through the bifurcation surface. The latter turns into a Galilean extremal surface in the limit of infinite speed of light. We also discuss aspects of Galilean tachydynamics and find that the entropy is given by the dilaton evaluated at the Galilean extremal surface.

authors.name: Daniel Grumiller, Kai-Yu Zhang

papers.title: A cubic closed string field theory
papers.summary: The action of closed bosonic string field theory is non-polynomial, and for more than thirty years a no-go theorem of Sonoda and Zwiebach (1990) has excluded a cubic formulation with a single string field, a symmetric vertex and the canonical propagator. We evade it with a Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation and provide an explicit construction of a cubic closed string field theory at all orders. The transformation introduces an infinite tower of auxiliary $k$-string fields $\Sigma_k$, entering at order $g_s^{2 k - 2}$, which turn the vertices with four or more legs into kinetic terms and cubic couplings. The action is cubic, at most quadratic in each auxiliary field, and triangular: eliminating the auxiliary fields by Gaussian integrals recovers the original action order by order at tree level, under invertibility and kernel conditions on the auxiliary kinetic operators. The original gauge symmetry lifts to the cubic action with no new parameter, and we argue that the auxiliary fields add no physical state at generic momentum, wherever their kinetic operators are invertible. On the worldsheet, $\Sigma_2$ is an entangled two-string state: by an operator product expansion, the quartic form reduces to a gluing of two asymmetric cubic vertices dressed by the motion of the local coordinates and defined on states without level matching. We expect this picture to generalize to higher orders, defining a gluing of patches carrying $k$ punctures each. The string vertices, read as products with several outputs, satisfy an extended form of the genus-zero $\mathrm{IBL}_\infty$ relations, including operations with no input or no output, exactly when the string products form a cyclic $L_\infty$ algebra. Finally, we compare our action with the bar--cobar construction of Chiaffrino, Mamade and Zwiebach.

authors.name: Harold Erbin

papers.title: Anatomy of AdS black hole on-shell actions
papers.summary: We revisit the regularized on-shell actions of rotating electrically charged AdS black holes of gauged supergravity via holographic renormalization and background subtraction, with a particular emphasis on the frame in which the radial cutoff is placed. For holographic renormalization, the asymptotically global AdS frame, recently employed in seven dimensions, works equally well in five and six dimensions: the renormalized on-shell action of the AdS$_d$ black holes with $S^1\times S^{d-2}$ conformal boundaries satisfies the quantum statistical relation, up to a parameter-independent Casimir term in odd dimensions, and thereby places the holographic comparisons that so far relied on this relation on a first-principles footing. Background subtraction, in contrast, fails to reproduce this result in the same frame; the mismatch, which we identify exactly in terms of the Casimir term and the counterterms, demands a criterion for the cutoff surface yet to be established. For precision holography, our results settle the choice of frame for holographic renormalization with conformally flat boundaries and delineate the ambiguities that remain in background subtraction and in holographic renormalization for boundaries that are not conformally flat.

authors.name: Junho Hong, Sourav Roychowdhury

papers.title: Time Advances and Dispersive Constraints in Dressed Gravitational Scattering
papers.summary: We derive a low energy group time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering at leading eikonal order with full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile of finite soft scale. Dispersive matching of nonnegative absorption excludes the amplitude's analytic crossing with high energy boundedness. This reflects internal scales growing with energy via string diffusion in quantum gravity and high energy nonlinear graviton rescattering, coupled to soft clouds beyond leading soft order. Interference preserving joint detection of hard particles and coherent soft radiation may reveal the advance.

authors.name: Ziyu Dong

papers.title: Self-gravitating spinning mesonic tubes
papers.summary: In this paper, we construct new self-gravitating solutions for the four-dimensional $SU(2)$ Einstein non-linear sigma model and the Einstein-Skyrme model, both minimally coupled to the Maxwell field, which describes spinning pulsed mesonic tubes. These solutions are gyratonic in the sense that they are characterized by a propagation axis and possess angular momentum. The gyratonic solutions are described by a smooth matter distribution, which is free of curvature singularities. The maximum of the energy density is concentrated on a tube around the propagation axis. We first consider the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to General Relativity and the Maxwell field, constructing asymptotically flat, spinning, pulsed gyratonic solutions. Subsequently, we include the Skyrme term in the analysis. In this case, we show that in order to maintain the resolvability of the matter field equations, the spacetime must be asymptotically de Sitter. It is also shown that, despite the fact that the total topological charge is zero, these solutions possess a non-zero topological charge density.

authors.name: Alex Giacomini, Marcela Lagos, Seung Hun Oh, Aldo Vera

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.summary: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

authors.name: Dmitry Galakhov

papers.title: Casimir Attraction and Repulsion in a Magnetic Domain-Wall Background
papers.summary: We study the one-loop Casimir interaction between two $\delta$--$\delta'$ plates in the fixed one-soliton P\"oschl--Teller background of the sine-Gordon kink. The transverse fluctuation problem is the Gaussian truncation of an $S^2$ sigma model, equivalently an easy-axis antiferromagnet with a domain wall, in which the plates exert no classical force on the wall. For $v\ge2|w|$ the fluctuation operators are non-negative, and strictly stable couplings, $v>2|w|$, also exclude zero modes, so the quadratic field theory is consistent at the fixed sine-Gordon mass. The background-dressed relative determinant factorises exactly into effective, gradient-dependent strengths of the two plates, and the sign of each frequency channel of the interaction energy is fixed by their orientation. Two identical, equally oriented, strictly stable plates switch from attraction near the kink to repulsion away from it under a rigid translation at fixed couplings and separation. The interaction energy and the force conjugate to the separation neither share their sign everywhere nor change sign at the same positions: there are regions of negative energy and repulsive force, so attraction and repulsion must be read from the force. For such plates with $w\neq0$ the force is repulsive at short and attractive at large separation, and the interaction energy has a minimum at a separation that depends on the position of the pair. For $v=1.05$, $w=0.5$ and $d=1.5$ the energy changes sign at $c\simeq-0.44$ and $2.63$, and the force at $c\simeq-0.30$ and $2.00$.

authors.name: In\'es Cavero-Pel\'aez, Beatriz G\'omez-L\'opez, Jose M. Mu\~noz-Casta\~neda, Gonzalo Sancho-Garrido

papers.title: Solving spectral flow in AdS$_3$: from covering maps to pencils
papers.summary: Strings in AdS$_3$ with pure NS-NS flux are described by the exactly solvable SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$) WZW model, yet correlators of winding strings, given by spectrally flowed operators, were so far known only up to three points. We obtain all of them, for any number of insertions and windings, in terms of unflowed correlators, proving the four-point conjecture of Dei and Eberhardt. The key ingredient is a pencil of rational maps from the worldsheet to the boundary which exists for generic insertion points, unwinds all insertions at once, and collapses to the covering map when the latter exists.

authors.name: Sergio Iguri, Nicolas Kovensky, Julian H. Toro

papers.title: Solitons of the intermediate long wave equation with residue source
papers.summary: We revisit the bilinear formulation of the intermediate long-wave (ILW) equation by interpreting its principal-value integrals in the framework of Sato hyperfunctions. When the tau-functions have no zeros inside the relevant contours, the conventional source-free ILW equation is recovered. When zeros enter the contours, their residue contributions must instead be retained, leading naturally to a residue-extended ILW system with self-consistent sources determined by the tau-functions themselves. We introduce a residue index that counts the zeros enclosed in each analytic strip and use it to classify the resulting soliton sectors.
