L\'opez, C. Maiano, S. Marangoni, J. G. Marcos, C. Marrelli, D. Meloni, M. Mezzetto, N. Milas, J. L. Mu\~noz, K. Niewczas, M. Oglakci, T. Ohlsson, M. Olveg{\aa}rd, A. Opanasenko, M. Pari, D. Patrzalek, G. Petkov, Ch. Petridou, P. Poussot, A. Psallidas, F. Pupilli, M. L. Reguera, D. Saiang, E. Salehi, D. Sampsonidis, A. Scanu, C. Schwab, F. Sordo, G. Stavropoulos, M. Stip\v{c}evi\'c, R. Tarkeshian, F. Terranova, T. Tolba, M. Topp-Mugglestone, E. Trachanas, R. Tsenov, A. Tsirigotis, S. E. Tzamarias, M. Vanderpoorten, G. Vankova-Kirilova, N. Vassilopoulos, S. Vihonen, J. Wurtz, V. Zeter, O. Zormpa

papers.title: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
papers.summary: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.

authors.name: Wen-Nian Liu, Duo-Jie Jia, Fu-Quan Dou

papers.title: Dilution of cosmological relics and gravitational waves from a supercooled electroweak phase transition in classically scale-invariant models
papers.summary: In classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model the electroweak scale is generated radiatively, and the absence of tree-level mass terms keeps the symmetric phase metastable down to very low temperatures. We study the resulting phase transition in a model with a real singlet and several additional scalars coupled to the Higgs doublet and to the singlet, in which electroweak symmetry is broken along a Gildener-Weinberg flat direction and a light dilaton appears in the spectrum. Computing the bounce along the two-dimensional tunnelling path and following the false-vacuum fraction through percolation and completion, we find that the transition proceeds in a single, strongly supercooled step and completes above the QCD scale over a region of parameter space consistent with Higgs measurements and perturbativity. Despite the strong supercooling the transition is fast. The bubble walls reach their terminal velocity early, and almost all of the released vacuum energy goes into bulk motion of the plasma, which thermalises and reheats the universe close to the scale set by the vacuum energy. The resulting entropy injection dilutes pre-existing relics by up to several orders of magnitude. It raises the baryon asymmetry that must be present before the transition, relaxes the unitarity bound on the mass of thermal dark matter, and suppresses earlier gravitational-wave backgrounds. If the acoustic description of gravitational-wave production extends to this regime, the signal peaks in the millihertz band, follows an approximate scaling relation between peak amplitude and frequency set by the vacuum energy, and would be observed by LISA throughout the viable region. The results depend on the multiplicity of the new scalars and their Higgs portal coupling at leading order through a single combination, and require the singlet scale to lie at or above the TeV scale.

authors.name: Arnab Chaudhuri

papers.title: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
papers.summary: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $\pi\omega$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $\tau^-\to\pi^-\pi^0\nu_\tau$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $\rho^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{\rho^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $\Gamma_{\rho^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.

authors.name: Florian Herren, Fatemeh Nouri, M\'eril Reboud

papers.title: Nonperturbative Kinetic Description of the Vacuum QGP Production in the Abelian Projection Method
papers.summary: Within the framework of the Abelian projection method in the $SU(N)$ variant of QCD, a system of nonperturbative selfconsistent equations for the back-reaction problem is derived. This system describes the vacuum production of quarks under the influence of strong quasiclassical gluon fields taking into account violating of the electroneutrality condition.

authors.name: V. V. Dmitriev, S. V. Churochkina, S. A. Smolyansky, V. A. Tseryupa

papers.title: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to bottom-pair production in electron-positron collisions
papers.summary: We present the two-loop mixed strong-electroweak virtual corrections to the production of a massive bottom-antibottom quark pair in electron-positron collisions. The evaluation of all the relevant Feynman integrals, including those with up to five internal massive lines with three different mass values, has been worked out relying on semi-analytical techniques, using complex-valued masses for the electroweak gauge bosons. The ultraviolet-renormalized and infrared-subtracted finite correction contributes to the NNLO QCD-EW cross section of the inclusive production of a bottom-quark pair. The methodology adopted in this calculation can be extended to the study of fully electroweak second-order corrections to benchmark precision calculations relevant to both the high-luminosity phase of the Large Hadron Collider and prospective future lepton colliders.

authors.name: Simone Devoto, Chinmoy Dey, Michele Dradi, Justin T. Fagnoni, Ziyang Huang, Xinchen Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Alessandro Vicini, Jiang Zhu

papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $\nu_\tau$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

authors.name: Dibya S. Chattopadhyay, Carlos A. Arg\"uelles, Vedran Brdar

papers.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
papers.summary: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

authors.name: Andrea Valletta, Francesco Crescimbeni, Takuya Katagiri, Francesco Pannarale, Paolo Pani

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Top Taggers from JetClass to a Full-Simulation $Z'\to t\bar{t}$ Search: Transfer, Extrapolation, Sensitivity and Inference Cost
papers.summary: Searches for heavy resonances decaying to \(t\bar{t}\) test physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale, and their reach depends on how well boosted top jets are identified. Machine-learning top taggers are usually compared on fast-simulation samples without pileup and in a narrow jet-\(p_T\) window, so a benchmark ranking does not directly show how much each tagger adds to a real search. This study trains seven taggers under identical conditions on JetClass. They are a boosted decision tree, two image-based networks, ParticleNet, and three particle transformers (ParT, UParT, and GloParT). The taggers are then applied without retraining to a \(Z'\to t\bar{t}\) search with \(m_{Z'}\) between 1.2 and 2.5~TeV, using 2016 CMS Open Data simulated with Geant4 and realistic pileup. The overall benchmark order of the taggers is preserved. However, taggers with similar area under the ROC curve (AUC) differ by up to a factor of three in jet-level discovery significance. The particle transformers extend the mass reach of the search by \(400~\mathrm{GeV}\), and their lead grows with resonance mass. This gain is seen in fully merged top jets and is associated with stable performance at jet \(p_T\) above the training range. Pileup has only a minor effect on all taggers. A small convolutional network achieves competitive discrimination at a much lower computational cost. The gaps between tagger groups hold under retraining and within statistical uncertainties. The results show that a tagger must be chosen on its kinematic coverage, the working point of the analysis, its discovery sensitivity and its cost, and not on its benchmark score alone.

authors.name: Manisha Kumari, Amal Sarkar

papers.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
papers.summary: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

authors.name: Andr\'e A. Costa, Valdir B. Bezerra

papers.title: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
papers.summary: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.

authors.name: Fengwei Yang, Kylar Greene, Aurora Ireland, Yuhsin Tsai

papers.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
papers.summary: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

authors.name: Marco Calz\`a, Andrea Spina

papers.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
papers.summary: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

authors.name: Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Nikolas Cruz-Camacho, Rajesh Kumar, Veronica Dexheimer, Jaquelyn Noronha-Hostler

papers.title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $\tau-\tau_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $\tau-\tau_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.

authors.name: Xiangrun Bao, Lingxiao Wang, Huichao Song

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
papers.summary: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

authors.name: H. C. Das, J. B. Wei

papers.title: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

authors.name: Stanislaw Mrowczynski, Maciej Pylak

papers.title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
papers.summary: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

authors.name: Ashish Pandav, Zhangbu Xu, Bedangadas Mohanty

papers.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
papers.summary: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

authors.name: Jinzi Wu, Michael D\"oring, Maxim Mai

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.summary: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

authors.name: Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Isabelle S. Goldstein

papers.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
papers.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{a\gamma}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

authors.name: S. V. Troitsky

papers.title: Generating the Dark Matter mass from the QCD vacuum: A new approach to the mass aspect of the Dark Matter-Baryon coincidence problem
papers.summary: The comparable abundances of dark matter and baryons imply a deep connection between the dark sector and the QCD sector. In asymmetric dark matter models, the number densities of both sectors are ensured to be similar. However, a complete solution should also include a mechanism relating their masses. In this study, we explore a new mechanism where an $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$ dark matter mass arises from the QCD vacuum. The idea is realized by a strongly coupled chiral dark sector, featuring a light composite fermion as the dark matter. Its mass is generated through the vacuum misalignment induced by QCD, ensuring the mass to be comparable with baryons. The model also features additional light bosons, including GeV-scale dark pions and a composite QCD axion.

authors.name: Yi Chung

papers.title: Space-time Areas and Hadronization Studies
papers.summary: Space-time area laws play a fundamental role in modeling strongly interacting phenomena, such as in relativistic string models, QCD on the lattice, and in hadronization modeling. For the latter, an exact expression for relevant space-time areas related to the final state hadronic events for hadrons of any mass is calculated. Usage of this expression in the UCLA hadronization model helps validate its space-time area law (STAL) principle and unifies the treatment of heavy and light hadrons via a single fragmentation function.

authors.name: S. Abachi, C. Buchanan

papers.title: Reevaluating the $a_1(1420)$ enhancement and its molecular partners in the low-lying axial-vector meson spectrum
papers.summary: We investigate possible axial-vector poles associated with the near-threshold $K^{\ast}\bar K$ interaction, driven by the Weinberg-Tomozawa term and unitarized through the Bethe-Salpeter equation. In the isovector sectors with $I^G(J^{PC})=1^\pm(1^{+\mp})$, we find second-sheet poles below the $K^{\ast}\bar K$ threshold and examine their possible manifestations in the $a_1(1420)$ structure and its possible partner $b_1(1400)$. The corresponding $f_0(980)\pi$ and $\phi\pi$ invariant-mass distributions are compared with the COMPASS and BESIII data, respectively. Within the present framework, the enhancements around 1.4 GeV may be qualitatively understood through the interplay between the triangle-singularity mechanism and the pole-enhanced $K^\ast\bar K$ final-state interaction, although a quantitative description requires a more complete treatment of coupled channels and production dynamics.

authors.name: Mao-Jun Yan, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng

papers.title: New Type of Monopoles in QCD and Standard Model
papers.summary: We present the new monopole solutions in QCD, the Georgi-Glashow model, and the standard model. QCD has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the chromon dressing. The Georgi-Glashow model has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the W boson dressing, in addition to the well-known 'tHooft-Polyakov monopole. Moreover, the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type monopoles which carry the magnetic charge $4\pi/e$ and the electromagnetically neutral type of magnetic monopoles (the naked one and the one with the W boson dressing) which carry the neutral magnetic charge $4\pi/\bae$, where $\bae$ is the neutral charge. We show how to construct the new monopole solutions and clarify the topological origin of the new monopoles. The new monopoles could have deep implications not just in high energy physics but also in condensed matter physics.

authors.name: Liping Zou, Pengming Zhang, Y. M. Cho

papers.title: Heavy Neutrinos across the Electroweak-to-Multi-TeV Frontier via Novel ML-Enhanced Probes
papers.summary: We propose a new strategy to probe heavy neutrinos with non-universal fermion couplings at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) using a novel production mechanism and machine-learning algorithms. Focusing on proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6~\mathrm{TeV}$, we investigate final states containing a charged lepton, missing transverse energy, and two jets. For heavy neutrino masses below $\mathcal{O}(1~\mathrm{TeV})$, production is dominated by the $s$ channel process. At higher masses, vector boson fusion becomes the dominant production mechanism, with cross sections that decrease slowly as the heavy neutrino mass increases. We simulate both signal and Standard Model background events and employ gradient-boosted decision trees to optimize event classification. Assuming an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb^{-1}}$, expected for the high-luminosity, and considering realistic statistical and systematic uncertainties, we find that heavy neutrinos in the mass range $50~\mathrm{GeV}$--$10~\mathrm{TeV}$ can be probed with sensitivity to the mixing parameter $|V_{\ell N}|^2$ spanning from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ to 1. This approach enhances the discovery potential for heavy neutrinos and provides a complementary pathway to existing search strategies.

authors.name: Yin-Fa Shen, Alfredo Gurrola, Francesco Romeo, Denis Rathjens, Andres Fl\'orez

papers.title: Fluctuation-Induced Backreaction on Bubble-Wall Dynamics in Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions
papers.summary: We study bubble-wall dynamics in cosmological first-order phase transitions in a two-scalar-field model, where the wall is formed by the scalar field $\phi$ and an additional real scalar field $s$ is coupled to it through a portal interaction. We evolve the coupled classical field equations on the lattice and consider a prescribed classical stochastic background of $s$ fluctuations at the onset of the phase transition. Through the portal interaction, this patchy background intermittently modulates the local driving pressure on the wall. The wall consequently undergoes alternating episodes of acceleration and deceleration, with a smaller finite-time averaged propagation rate than in the decoupled limit. A wall-frame analysis of the dynamical $s$-sector energy reveals a coupling-dependent crossover from excess energy deposited behind the wall at weak coupling to a front-side bias at strong coupling. These results demonstrate an additional scalar-field source of bubble-wall backreaction and may affect gravitational-wave and baryogenesis predictions.

authors.name: Dongdong Wei, Zong-Kuan Guo

papers.title: MadNIS at NLO
papers.summary: We combine fast amplitude surrogates with neural importance sampling to accelerate NLO calculations. For virtual corrections, a learned ratio to the Born matrix element with calibrated uncertainties guarantees reliable precision across phase space. For real emission, we stick to the standard FKS subtraction and train sector-conditioned surrogates of the regularized integrands away from divergences. MadNIS then uses multi-channel mappings and FKS sectors as conditions. We validate our approach for electron-positron scattering to three and four jets and find significant speed-ups and variance reduction in the integration.

authors.name: Giovanni De Crescenzo, Javier Mari\~no Villadamigo, Nina Elmer, Theo Heimel, Tilman Plehn, Ramon Winterhalder, Marco Zaro

papers.title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$-symmetric Point
papers.summary: We calculate the dimension-six $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme with perturbative short flow-time expansion coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to $\tau(D_s)/\tau(D^0)$ at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$ symmetric point, we obtain $B_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$,$B_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(70)$, $\epsilon_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$ using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path towards higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.

authors.name: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel

papers.title: Squeezed double-$b$ tagging for light hadronic resonances at the LHC
papers.summary: A boosted light resonance decaying into $b\bar b$ can produce a single jet containing two bottom-hadron decay systems. We investigate this squeezed double-$b$ topology using a tracking-based boosted decision tree that distinguishes non-bottom, single-bottom and double-bottom jets. The classifier combines displaced-track multiplicities and momentum fractions with ordered impact parameters and jet kinematics. For the simulated jet samples, the double-bottom tagging response is approximately $83\%$, with corresponding single-bottom and non-bottom mistag responses of $9.7\%$ and $0.5\%$; charm contamination is assessed separately. The tagger is combined with soft-drop mass reconstruction and an event-level classifier using the candidate and recoil jets to identify light hadronic resonances within the QCD background. As an illustrative example, we consider a singlet extension of the flipped two-Higgs-doublet model with pseudoscalar masses of 30, 50 and 60 GeV. The signal samples use a simplified effective-vertex approximation, replacing the momentum-dependent quark-loop production interaction by a local vertex. A resolved loop calculation and higher-order production corrections are beyond the scope of this tagging study. The resulting reconstruction strategy can be applied to different signal hypotheses with their corresponding kinematic acceptance and tagging response.

authors.name: Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Biswarup Mukhopadhyaya, Sirshendu Samanta, Ritesh K. Singh

papers.title: Collisional energy loss distribution of a fast parton in a hot or dense QCD medium
papers.summary: We compute the probability distribution for collisional energy loss of an ultrarelativistic parton crossing a quark-gluon plasma. This collisional quenching weight has not been determined previously, unlike the average collisional loss per unit distance, although it should be a more accurate quantity to use in jet-quenching phenomenology. The quenching weight is obtained from a well-known kinetic equation which resums an arbitrary number of elastic scatterings of the energetic parton with the medium, providing a complete description of the stochastic energy exchange, including the possibility of energy gain from thermal fluctuations. The formulation also naturally extends the standard treatment of collisional energy loss to finite path lengths, which could be relevant not only for heavy-ion collisions, but also for light-ion, and possibly proton-nucleus and proton-proton collisions. We predict the quenching weight in a setup where individual elastic scatterings are described using the hard thermal loop approximation for soft exchanges, with a smooth matching to the hard domain.

authors.name: G. Jackson, S. Peign\'e

papers.title: Particle species dependence of femtoscopic source parameters in high-energy nuclear collisions
papers.summary: High-energy nuclear physics explores the properties of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic collisions of nuclei. Femtoscopy, a subfield of high-energy physics, utilizes quantum-statistical correlations of particles to characterize the space-time geometry of the particle-emitting source. Recent measurements and phenomenological investigations indicated that the shape of the source for identical pions can be well-described by L\'evy-stable distributions. The significant power-law tail of the pion source observed both in experiment and in simulations has been shown to originate from the process of L\'evy walk during the hadronic scattering phase of the collisions. To better understand the physical processes behind the formation of such power laws, an important next step is to investigate particle species dependence, especially the source shape of identical kaon and proton pairs. As a direct continuation of our previous studies, in this Letter, we present a detailed three-dimensional investigation of the two-particle source shape in simulations of Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV per nucleon pair collision energy using the EPOS3 model. We show the dependence of the extracted femtoscopic source parameters on particle species, centrality and average transverse mass. We find that the scale parameters do not show a clear transverse mass scaling between particle species, as there are systematic differences in the overlapping regions. The power-law exponents of pion and kaon pairs are compatible, while for protons it is higher, closer to the Gaussian limit. When new experimental measurements of kaon and proton correlations become available, these results will provide the basis of a data-model comparison.

authors.name: D\'aniel Kincses, L\'aszl\'o Kov\'acs, M\'at\'e Csan\'ad

papers.title: Critique of Breit-Wigner resonance scattering
papers.summary: In the Breit-Wigner approach to scattering the phase shift $\delta$ is to have a form $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ at any real energy continuum scattering resonance. By analytic continuation this leads to complex energy poles in the scattering amplitude at $E_{\rm BW}=E_1-i\Gamma_1$, poles that are identified with unstable physical particles. By solving the square well scattering problem we identify some challenges to this approach. We find that setting $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ is not always a good description of the real energy continuum scattering amplitude, that $\Gamma_1$ can be negative, that $E_{\rm BW}$ is not in fact an energy eigenvalue, and thus cannot be identified with a physical particle. To address these issues we solve the square well Schr\"odinger problem and find explicit complex energy eigenvalues of the form $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ due to the antilinear $PT$ (Parity, Time Reversal) symmetry of the Hamiltonian. However, $E_2\neq E_1$ and $\Gamma_2\neq \Gamma_1$. As Hamiltonian eigenstates with energy $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ these states can be identified with physical particles and correspond to phase shifts of the form $\tan\delta_{PT} =\Gamma_2/(E_2-E)$. Then by analytic continuation to real energy they give the same real energy resonance shape as a standard Breit-Wigner. However, the determined positions and widths of these resonances should be associated with $E_2$ and $\Gamma_2$ rather than with $E_1$ and $\Gamma_1$. We thus recognize two forms of resonance in the real energy scattering amplitude $f(E)$, those associated with the continuum (the complex $E$ plane branch cut) and those due to poles in the complex $E$ plane. Only the latter can be associated with real particles. The continuum resonances are not associated with Breit-Wigner modes, and the number of such resonances correlates with the number of square well bound states.

authors.name: Philip D. Mannheim

papers.title: B Meson Semi-Invisible Decays via Perturbative QCD
papers.summary: This paper focuses on the dark sector decay processes of $B$ mesons ($B\to \mathcal{B}_8\ +$ invisible). Using the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach, we calculate the upper bounds on the branching ratios for decays from $B$ mesons into light baryons and dark baryons within two distinct $B$-Mesogenesis scenarios. A detailed discussion of the form factor $B\to \mathcal{B}_8$ is presented. Based on the derived form factors and effective couplings, we then reach the final numerical analysis. The results show that these upper bounds can reach sizable, especially for $B^0\to n\psi$ in Type-I scenario, with values of orderis $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ . Such processes are expected to facilitate the search for dark matter at hadron colliders and B factories.

authors.name: Han-Bing Liu, Ye Xing, Bin Luo

papers.title: Phenomenology of heavy-flavour jet angularities at hadron colliders
papers.summary: We compute resummed and matched predictions for jet angularities in hadronic Z+jet events, where the jet is initiated by a b-quark. The analysis is performed both with and without grooming the candidate jets using the SoftDrop algorithm. Mass effects are consistently included at both fixed-order and resummed levels. Our theoretical predictions also incorporate non-perturbative corrections from the underlying event and hadronization, implemented through parton-to-hadron transfer matrices extracted from dedicated Monte Carlo simulations with Sherpa. Finally, we compare results for b-jets with the ones from light-flavour jets, in order to quantify the impact of finite-mass effects.

authors.name: Andrea Ghira, Lorenzo Mai, Simone Marzani, Daniel Reichelt, Steffen Schumann, Leon St\"ocker

papers.title: Neutron tagging of heavy lepton pair production at RHIC and LHC energies
papers.summary: We calculated cross sections for $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow \ell^+\ell^-$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) production in ultraperipheral gold and lead collisions and compare our results with recent measurements from the STAR, ALICE, ATLAS, and CMS experiments at center of mass energies $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76 $ TeV, and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. The calculations are performed within lowest order quantum electrodynamics (LO QED) using a Monte Carlo technique for calculating the impact parameter dependent probability, and subsequently combined with neutron emission probabilities associated with Coulomb excitation of the nuclei. These neutron emission scenarios are modeled using a Poisson statistics, allowing the cross sections to be categorized into experimentally relevant neutron classes: 0n0n, 0nXn, XnXn, and inclusive (0n0n+0nXn+XnXn) production. To enable a direct comparison with experiments, fiducial phase space restrictions corresponding to the acceptance of each detector are implemented.

authors.name: Atacan Fatih Candar, Mehmet Cem G\"u\c{c}l\"u

papers.title: Beyond leading-logarithm photon production from two-loop diagrams in a hot QCD medium
papers.summary: We investigate high-energy photon production from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes in a quark-gluon plasma by evaluating the imaginary part of the two-loop photon self-energies in thermal QCD. Working in the imaginary-time formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the leading-logarithmic and beyond-leading-logarithmic contributions to the photon production rate from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. We retain the full Fermi--Dirac and Bose--Einstein statistical factors and compare the resulting Compton and annihilation rates with those obtained from kinetic theory and the closed-time-path formalism. The summed rates agree with the corresponding established results, providing a nontrivial consistency check of the calculation. Furthermore, when we consider the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution for incoming particles, we find that quantum corrections are absent in the individual $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. However, the total rate agrees with that of full statistics.

authors.name: Sumit, Ritesh Ghosh, Munshi G. Mustafa

papers.title: Dynamical flattening of halo density cusps by Q-ball dark matter
papers.summary: Cold, collisionless dark matter successfully explains a wide range of observations, including the formation of large-scale structure. Nevertheless, tensions remain on small, galactic scales, most notably the cusp-core, or inner-mass-deficit, problem and the diversity of inner rotation-curve shapes and central densities at fixed halo mass. These observations suggest that additional dark-sector physics may affect the inner structure of halos, although no generally accepted explanation has yet emerged. Here, making use of a toy but representative model, we investigate how interacting dark-matter Q-balls -- non-topological solitons stabilized by a conserved charge -- modify halo centers and generate a diversity of inner profiles. Our calculations include merger-induced mass and kinetic-energy losses, elastic heat transport, and the gravitational readjustment of the halo; flattening and later recontraction can both occur. Produced in the early Universe in the dark sector, these Q-balls grow in the dense central regions of halos, while their interaction cross section decreases as the soliton mass increases. This process operates preferentially in halo centers, converting part of the rest-mass energy stored in massive Q-balls into relativistic dark-sector particles and thereby modifying the inner mass-density profile. The resulting density-dependent energy loss competes with heat transport and halo response. An ensemble of initial assembly conditions yields very different final densities at fixed microphysics, although neither a universal constant-density core nor a statistical fit to the observed population is established.

authors.name: Alexander Libanov, Sergey Troitsky

papers.title: Heavy neutral leptons beyond the BBN bound: probing the lepton asymmetry of the Universe
papers.summary: Hadronically decaying particles with lifetimes $\tau\gtrsim0.02\,{\rm s}$ are excluded by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis almost independently of their abundance: the mesons from their decays convert protons into neutrons faster than the reverse, and helium is overproduced. For heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), this blankets the couplings the upcoming accelerator searches can reach. We propose a scenario with large lepton flavor asymmetries in which HNLs evade it. A Dirac HNL decays into $\pi^+$ and its antiparticle into $\pi^-$, so an asymmetry between the two populations injects an excess of $\pi^+$, which converts the neutrons back to their standard abundance, while a cancellation between the asymmetries and the HNL decays keeps the shift in $N_{\rm eff}$ small. This opens the parameter space with $m_l+m_\pi\lesssim m_N\lesssim1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $\tau_N\lesssim1\,{\rm s}$, including a substantial region within the reach of SHiP. A discovery there, combined with the BBN and CMB observables, would fix the primordial flavor asymmetries up to one remaining direction. The relic neutrino background and gravitational waves from the QCD transition epoch may probe that direction, and with it the lepton asymmetry of the Universe.

authors.name: Kensuke Akita, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Vsevolod Syvolap

papers.title: Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin $B$-Meson Decays
papers.summary: We compute for the first time the subleading twist correction to the exclusive rare $b \to \left \{s, d \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays from the three-particle $B$-meson distribution amplitude at next-to-leading order accuracy by employing the soft-collinear effective theory. This constitutes the last missing ingredient for the complete factorization analysis of the hadronic matrix element of the weak effective Hamiltonian at leading power in the heavy quark expansion. Incorporating further a variety of the next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the spectator-scattering amplitude and the weak annihilation topology, we then present the improved field-theoretic predictions for phenomenologically interesting observables in the electroweak penguin $B \to \left \{K, \pi \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays.

authors.name: Yong-Kang Huang, Yu-Ming Wang, Xue-Chen Zhao

papers.title: Mixing-angle sensitivity of inclusive $\Xi_{bc} $ and $\Omega_{bc}$ lifetimes
papers.summary: We study the inclusive lifetimes of $\Xi_{bc}^{+}$, $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$, and $\Omega_{bc}^{0}$ with emphasis on the mixing between the spin-zero and spin-one $bc$-diquark configurations. The matrix elements are evaluated in both the homogeneous bag model (HBM) and the nonrelativistic quark model (NRQM). At the benchmark mixing angles $-23.0^\circ$ for $\Xi_{bc}$ and $-23.5^\circ$ for $\Omega_{bc}$, the corresponding lifetime triplets are $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.421^{+0.098}_{-0.093}{}^{+0.007}_{-0.014},0.075^{+0.035}_{-0.017}{}^{+0.004}_{-0.001},0.223^{+0.074}_{-0.046}{}^{+0.018}_{-0.012})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in HBM and $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.367^{+0.076}_{-0.070}{}^{+0.001}_{-0.005},0.100^{+0.032}_{-0.014}{}^{+0.006}_{-0.001},0.229^{+0.066}_{-0.042}{}^{+0.017}_{-0.011})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in NRQM. The first errors are the fixed-angle uncertainties; the second are the envelopes from varying each mixing angle by $\pm10^\circ$ with all other inputs fixed. Relative to the unmixed spin-one reference points, the $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$ and $\Omega_{bc}$ lifetimes decrease by approximately $17\%$-$19\%$. Neither the minimum nor the maximum of the central lifetime curves occurs at a pure $S_{bc}=0$ or $S_{bc}=1$ configuration; the extrema instead lie at mixed angles with $|\phi_{{\cal B}}|\simeq27^\circ$-$63^\circ$. The two pure-spin cases alone are therefore insufficient to characterize the angular dependence.

authors.name: Hai-Yang Cheng, Chia-Wei Liu, Fanrong Xu

papers.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
papers.summary: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.

authors.name: Alex Prygarin, Claudelle Capasia Madjuogang Sandeu, Karam Shekh Yusuf

papers.title: Sub-MeV gamma-ray lines from an endothermic interpretation of the LZ recoil candidate
papers.summary: Endothermic upscattering of heavy dark matter offers a compelling interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil candidate recently reported by LUX-ZEPLIN, with a characteristic recoil energy $E_R \propto \delta$, where $\delta$ is the mass splitting between the dark matter states. Cosmological and experimental constraints motivate the depletion of the primordial heavier state, which can be regenerated in the Galactic halo. We show that, if the heavier state decays radiatively, the same mass splitting sets the energy of a gamma-ray line, $E_\gamma \simeq \delta$. For our benchmark, this leads to a sub-MeV line within the projected reach of the Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), scheduled for launch in 2027. The confirmation of the LUX-ZEPLIN candidate event as a dark matter signal would therefore motivate dedicated searches for sub-MeV gamma-ray lines, with COSI providing a timely opportunity to test this interpretation.

authors.name: Ma\'ira Dutra, Jacinto P. Neto, Clarissa Siqueira

papers.title: M1 Radiative Transitions in the $B_c$ System after the $B_c^\ast(1S)$ Observation: Radial-Node Cancellation and Quark-Line Filtering
papers.summary: The recent ATLAS observation of the $B_c^*(1S)$ meson fixes the photon momentum for $B_c^*(1S)\to B_c(1S)\gamma$. We calculate four $1S$ and $2S$ M1 radiative transitions with relativistic Salpeter wave functions calibrated to the measured ground-state masses, and obtain $\Gamma[B_c^*(1S)\to B_c(1S)\gamma]=5.24\times10^{-2}$~keV. For the hindered $2S\to1S$ transitions, contributions from different radial-momentum regions largely cancel, leaving form factors about 25 times smaller than that of the ground-state allowed transition. The cancellation factors, defined as the ratio of the integral of the absolute radial contribution to the magnitude of the net integral, are approximately 18--20. Nevertheless, the hindered radiative widths are not suppressed, because their much larger photon momenta compensate for the smaller form factors. Separating the photon-emission contributions of the $b$ quark and $\bar c$ antiquark, we find particularly strong cancellation in the $b$ contribution to $B_c(2S)\to B_c^*(1S)\gamma$: only about $0.46\%$ of the integrated absolute radial contribution remains after cancellation, compared with about $4.5\%$ for the $\bar c$ contribution. The unmeasured $B_c^*(2S)$ mass remains the main limitation on the $2S\to2S$ radiative width.

authors.name: Bing-Dong Wan

papers.title: A Chiral Nelson-Barr Relaxion
papers.summary: We present the chiral Nelson-Barr relaxion model, an extension of the Nelson-Barr relaxion framework with a gauged chiral $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. It includes vector-like quarks to cancel gauge anomalies and a scalar whose vacuum expectation value generates their masses. The chiral symmetry forbids the leading operators responsible for the Nelson-Barr and clockwork quality problems. Right-handed neutrinos generate light-neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism and permit thermal leptogenesis. For the particular Nelson-Barr sector Yukawa coupling considered, relaxion phenomenology gives a maximal scale of $CP$ violation $f_{\textrm{max}}^{\textrm{pheno}}\sim 4 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV}$, about an order of magnitude greater than the corresponding phenomenological ceiling in the original model. The model can accommodate thermal leptogenesis if its right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating history satisfy the Davidson-Ibarra bound.

authors.name: Cristien Arzate, Joshua Iascau

papers.title: Magnetars magnetic field evolution with ambipolar diffusion
papers.summary: The magnetic field associated with neutron stars is generally believed to be threaded inside the star. In the presence of a magnetic field, plasma in the interior of the star undergoes a series of processes that result in magnetic field evolution. It is believed that magnetar activities like X-ray, gamma-ray bursts, and giant flares (which release more energy in a few sec than Sun in 10 years), are mainly due to field decay. The most important process of field decay inside the core of the star is the ambipolar diffusion of the charged particles present in the interior plasma. The decay rate due to ambipolar diffusion is directly connected to the ambipolar velocity of the charged particles under the influence of the present magnetic field. The ambipolar velocity of the charged particles depends on the internal dynamics of the particles. We outline a general method to solve the particle dynamics in the presence of a magnetic field to have a magnetohydrodynamics equation from ambipolar velocity. The equation is general and applicable to all possible surrounding conditions temperature, matter states like normal or superfluid, etc.

authors.name: Monika Sinha, Manoj Kumar Ghosh, Yogeesh N

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization
papers.summary: We perform a comprehensive study of the signatures of Lorentz violation in electrodynamics on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropies. In the framework of the minimal Standard Model Extension (SME), we consider effects generated by renormalizable operators, both CPT-odd and CPT-even. These operators are responsible for sourcing, respectively, cosmic birefringence and circular polarization. We propagate jointly the effects of all the relevant Lorentz-violating parameters to CMB observables and provide constraints with the most recent CMB datasets. We bound the CPT-even coefficient to $k_{F,E+B} < 6.02 \times 10^{-32}$ at 95\% CL. This improves previous CMB bounds by more than one order of magnitude. The limits we obtain on the CPT-odd coefficients, i.e. $|k_{(V)00}^{(3)}| < 1.05 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}| < 0.51 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ at 95\% CL, are respectively one and two orders of magnitude stronger than previous CMB-based limits, superseding also bounds from non-CMB searches. This analysis provides the strongest constraints to date on CPT-violating coefficients in the minimal SME from CMB searches.

authors.name: Luca Caloni, Serena Giardiello, Margherita Lembo, Martina Gerbino, Giulia Gubitosi, Massimiliano Lattanzi, Luca Pagano

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Collisions of Fuzzy Dark Matter Solitons
papers.summary: According to the Schr\"odinger-Poisson (SP) equations, fuzzy dark matter (FDM) can form a stable equilibrium configuration, the so-called FDM soliton. The SP system can also determine the evolution of FDM solitons, such as head-on collision. In this paper, we first propose a new adimensional unit of length, time and mass. And then, we simulate the adimensional SP system with $\mathtt{PyUltraLight}$ to study the GWs from collision of FDM solitons when the linearized theory is valid and the GW back reaction on the evolution of FDM solitons is ignored. Finally, we find that the GWs from collisions have a frequency of (few ten-years)$^{-1}$ or (few years)$^{-1}$ when FDM mass is $m=10^{-18}\rm{eV}/c^2$ or $m=10^{-17}\rm{eV}/c^2$. Therefore, future detection of such GWs will constrain the property of FDM particle and solitons.

authors.name: Chen Tan, Jing-Kang Bin, Ke Wang

papers.title: Heavy-Meson Bag Parameters using Gradient Flow
papers.summary: We demonstrate the use of the gradient flow combined with the short flow-time expansion (GF+SFTX) as a renormalization procedure for four-quark operator matrix elements and associated bag parameters relevant to neutral heavy-meson mixing ($\Delta Q=2$) and heavy-meson lifetimes ($\Delta Q=0$). Using six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we calculate for a charm-strange system with physical quark masses flowed bag parameters and match them to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme using perturbative SFTX coefficients up to next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD. We employ a multiscale matching strategy and a renormalization-group improved flow-time evolution which allows for a reliable estimate of systematic uncertainties. For a fictitious neutral $D_s$ meson, we obtain the $\Delta Q=2$ $\overline{\text{MS}}$ bag parameter ${\cal B}^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.7673(123)$, consistent with existing short-distance $D^0$ mixing determinations. For the $\Delta Q=0$ lifetime-ratio operator basis, we find the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ results $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$, $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(71)$, $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$. We provide conversion formulae to re-express these results for an arbitrary choice of evanescent operators. These results demonstrate that GF+SFTX can deliver precise determinations of dimension-six four-quark operators and establish a framework for future lattice computations including more complex operator bases, where the challenge of power-divergent mixing is shifted to the continuum and handled in the SFTX.

authors.name: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel

papers.title: Sequential Bayesian inference with correlated heavy-ion datasets
papers.summary: Bayesian inference provides a natural framework for updating knowledge as new information becomes available, often in a sequential manner by incorporating datasets in stages or reusing previous posteriors as priors. A common implementation uses a factorized update in which datasets are treated as conditionally independent. When datasets have statistically correlated uncertainties, however, this approximation generally becomes inconsistent with the joint likelihood and can lead to distorted posterior constraints. In this work, we investigate this issue in a controlled setting using pseudo-data with a tunable covariance structure. We compare joint inference, factorized sequential updating, and a formulation based on the exact conditional likelihood. We show that factorized updates reproduce the joint posterior under conditional independence, but develop systematic deviations when correlations are neglected, with discrepancies that increase with correlation strength in our numerical examples. In contrast, conditional sequential updating reproduces the joint posterior exactly. To interpret these deviations, we introduce an information decomposition that separates the joint information into contributions from the first dataset and the conditional information provided by the second. By comparing marginal and conditional information, we show that correlations induce structured changes in the constraints on different parameter combinations, reflecting the interplay between covariance structure and dataset sensitivities. This information-based analysis provides a quantitative interpretation of the observed posterior discrepancies. These results provide a practical diagnostic for assessing the consistency of sequential Bayesian inference with correlated datasets and highlight the need for a consistent treatment of correlations within a common probabilistic framework.

authors.name: Lipei Du

papers.title: Higher Mellin Moments of the Unpolarized PDF of the Pion and the Kaon from Lattice QCD
papers.summary: We present results on the Mellin moments of the unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) of the pion and kaon up to the fourth order. The computation is done using one $N_f=2+1+1$ gauge ensemble of twisted mass fermions with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical values. We reconstruct the valence pion and kaon PDFs using the connected contributions to the three Mellin moments. We compare our results on the Mellin moments and the reconstructed PDFs with other lattice QCD and phenomenological determinations.

authors.name: Constantia Alexandrou (Univ. of Cyprus,The Cyprus Inst.), Simone Bacchio (The Cyprus Inst.), Priyajit Jana (Univ. of Cyprus,The Cyprus Inst.), Marcus Petschlies (Univ. of Bonn), Luis Alberto Rodriguez Chacon (The Cyprus Inst.,Univ. of Ferrara), Gregoris Spanoudes (Univ. of Cyprus), Fernanda Steffens (Univ. of Bonn), Carsten Urbach (Univ. of Bonn), Urs Wenger (Univ. of Bern)

papers.title: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
papers.summary: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssim\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.

authors.name: Satyabrata Datta, Rome Samanta

papers.title: Cooling, conduction, and compact objects: Gravothermal evolution of dissipative self-interacting dark matter halos
papers.summary: Many proposed self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models yield radiative processes that can dissipate energy. Understanding their impact on astrophysical objects through simulations and comparing the results with observations may thus constrain SIDM models. We systematically investigated how dissipation alters the gravothermal evolution of isolated SIDM halos by independently varying dissipation and heat conduction and identified potential observational signatures. We present the first extension of the $N$-body formalism for frequent small-angle self-interactions to include effective dissipation. We compared all results for isolated halos with a dissipative gravothermal fluid model to assess the validity and limitations of the latter. We find that dissipation qualitatively changes the gravothermal evolution of SIDM halos beyond simply accelerating collapse. Sufficiently strong central cooling can invert the usual role of heat conduction: the formation of an isothermal core is suppressed such that conduction remains directed inward throughout the evolution. Outer halo regions beyond the scale radius can cool efficiently rather than being heated by conduction, resulting in a larger region of mass infall and a less pronounced indentation between the core and the outer halo in the final density profile. These effects depend strongly on the cooling rate but are comparatively insensitive to the angular dependence of the self-interaction cross section. We further show that weakly dissipative self-interactions can explain the properties of the recently observed strong lens perturber in JVAS B1938+666 with significantly shorter evolution times or, equivalently, smaller cross sections compared to the elastic case. Our results open a new route to connecting halo structure and recently reported compact objects to dark-sector microphysics.

authors.name: Ludwig D. Schmidt, Moritz S. Fischer, Mathias Garny

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.summary: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second, a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP), is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that L\'evy distributions describe the shape of hadron (pion) emission sources at freeze-out the most accurately; however, based on hydrodynamics Gaussian distributions are typically expected. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing L\'evy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations; in particular, the effective temperatures from angle-averaged transverse mass distributions and the femtoscopic radii from two-particle momentum correlation functions are analyzed.

authors.name: Bence Szentkuti, Mate Csanad

papers.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
papers.summary: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

authors.name: Xiaolin Wang, Xingyu Guo, Jinyang Li, Tianyin Li, Enke Wang, Lingxiao Wang, Hongxi Xing

papers.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in Gauss-Bonnet braneworld cosmology
papers.summary: The present study investigates the feasibility of gravitational baryogenesis in a Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) type II braneworld cosmology. The modified expansion rate of the Universe in this scenario evolves through three distinct expansion regimes, the GB regime at early times where the expansion rate $H \sim \rho^{1/3}$ falls more slowly than the standard expansion law $H\sim \rho^{1/2}$ of GR, then the RS type era with an enhanced expansion $H \sim \rho$, before finally reducing to the standard expansion law in the low energy limit. Gravitational baryogenesis depends on $\dot{R}$ and requires $\dot{R} 0$ for the RS regime and successful baryogenesis requires either that the decoupling temperature occurs during the GB regime or that the Universe makes a direct transition from the GB regime to the GR regime. The GB baryon asymmetry $\eta(T)$ is proportional to $\mu (1+w)(1-w)(1+1/\beta)$, where $\mu$ is the energy scale $\mu \equiv 1/l$ associated with the bulk curvature scale $l$, $\beta \equiv 4 \alpha \mu^{2}$, where $\alpha$ is the GB coupling, and $w$ is the equation of state parameter $p=w \rho$. Studies of inflation in GB-braneworld cosmology place constraints on the allowed ranges of the parameters $\mu$ and $\beta$. Guided by these, the asymmetry has been calculated for ranges of $(\mu, \beta, w)$ and it is found that the observed values can be obtained for a value of $\beta$ within the range $(10^{-2} - 10^{-3})$ for $\mu =10^{12}$ GeV, and within the range $(10^{-1}- 10^{-2})$ for $\mu =10^{13}$ GeV. All values of $\eta$ for $\mu=10^{14}$ are too high. The parameter ranges for the decoupling temperatures required to produce the observed asymmetry have also been established.

authors.name: Ian B Whittingham

papers.title: Amplitude analysis of the $\Lambda_c^+\to n K^0_{\mathrm{S}} \pi^+$ decay
papers.summary: We perform the first amplitude analysis of the charmed baryon hadronic decay $\Lambda_c^+\to n K^0_{\mathrm{S}} \pi^+$. The analysis uses $e^+ e^-$ annihilation data corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 4.5~$\rm{fb}^{-1}$ collected with the BESIII spectrometer at center-of-mass energies between 4.600 GeV and 4.699~GeV. The amplitude analysis identifies four intermediate resonances $\Lambda(1830)^{0}$, $\Lambda(2000)^{0}$, $N(1440)^{+}$ and $N(1650)^{+}$. We measure the products of branching fractions: $$\mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{c}^{+} \rightarrow \Lambda(1830)^{0}\pip)\cdot \mathcal{B}(\Lambda(1830)^{0} \rightarrow n \Ks) = (2.4\pm0.7\pm0.5\pm0.1)\times 10^{-3}, \mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{c}^{+} \rightarrow \Lambda(2000)^{0}\pip)\cdot \mathcal{B}(\Lambda(2000)^{0} \rightarrow n \Ks) = (5.4\pm1.7\pm1.1\pm0.3)\times 10^{-3}, \mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{c}^{+} \rightarrow N(1440)^{+}\Ks)\cdot \mathcal{B}(N(1440)^{+} \rightarrow n \pip) = (4.0\pm2.0\pm1.5\pm0.2)\times 10^{-3}, \mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{c}^{+} \rightarrow N(1650)^{+}\Ks)\cdot \mathcal{B}(N(1650)^{+} \rightarrow n \pip) = (5.2\pm1.1\pm0.8\pm0.3)\times 10^{-3},$$ where the first uncertainties are statistical, the second are systematic, and the third are related to the normalizing branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(\Lambda_c^+\to n K^0_{\mathrm{S}} \pi^+)$. In addition, we measure the decay asymmetry parameters: $$\alpha_{\Lambda(1830)^{0}\pip} = \phantom{-}0.93^{+0.07}_{-0.72}\pm0.07,\alpha_{\Lambda(2000)^{0}\pip} = -0.91^{+0.56}_{-0.09}\pm0.14,\alpha_{N(1440)^{+}\Ks} = -0.13\pm0.43\pm0.35,\alpha_{N(1650)^{+}\Ks} = -0.42\pm0.45\pm0.29.$$
