papers.title: Adaptive Matrix-Based Denoising Algorithm Using Local Spatial Support
papers.summary: To address the online data-processing requirements of the high-level trigger (HLT) under high-event-rate and high-background conditions in high-luminosity collider facilities, this paper proposes an adaptive matrix-based denoising algorithm using local spatial support. The algorithm is implemented and tested in the main drift chamber (MDC) of the Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF). Based on tests with five charged-final-state physics channels simulated using the Offline Software of the Super Tau Charm Facility (OSCAR), the rejection rate for discrete point-cluster backgrounds exceeds 90% at low to moderate background levels, while the true-hit retention ratio remains above 98%. Even when the detector efficiency is reduced to 90%, the true-hit retention ratio remains above 98%. These results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm satisfies the stringent online-processing constraints of an HLT upstream denoising module, including low and predictable average processing time, high precision, and high throughput. Because its filtering criterion is derived from local spatial relationships among detector hits rather than predefined track parameters or a model of a specific physical process, the proposed algorithm provides a general research approach for online denoising in regularly structured detectors used in high-luminosity collider facilities.

authors.name: Zhaoli Guo, Qingyu Li, Baolin Zhang, Jiarui Zhao, Aonan Zhu, Liang Peng {\dag}, Huilin Li {\dag}

papers.title: Observation of the $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-$ decay and an improved measurement of the $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ branching fraction
papers.summary: An observation of the rare decay $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-$ is reported from proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2022 and 2023, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.6 fb$^{-1}$. In addition, the branching fraction ratio of $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ relative to $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$ is measured with a precision improved by 44% compared with the previous measurement. The measured branching fraction ratios are $\mathcal{B}(\eta \to\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-)/\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ = [2.89 $\pm$ 0.48 (stat) $^{+0.42}_{-0.29}$ (syst)]$\times$ 10$^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-)/\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ = [0.86 $\pm$ 0.06 (stat) $^{+0.09}_{-0.08}$ (syst)]$\times$10$^{-3}$.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Multi-approach Standard Model Effective Field Theory analyses of top-quark associated production in leptonic final states at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
papers.summary: Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) interpretations of measurements of top-quark associated production processes in leptonic final states are presented using the full Run 2 proton-proton collision dataset recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. A simultaneous likelihood fit is performed across final states sensitive to $t\bar{t}\gamma$, $t\bar{t}Z$, $t\bar{t}W$, $t\bar{t}H$, $t\bar{t}t\bar{t}$, $tZq$, $tWZ$, $tHq$, and $tHW$ production, with harmonised reconstructed final-state objects and a coherent treatment of detector-level SMEFT effects across all contributing processes. Two complementary analysis strategies are investigated: an approach employing a more generic event categorisation based on counting reconstructed objects, and a more complex approach combining orthogonal regions optimised to specifically identify individual processes, as employed by previous dedicated measurements. Constraints are obtained on the Wilson coefficients of dimension-six SMEFT operators affecting top-quark interactions, including top-boson, four-quark and top-lepton operators, together with complex operator contributions. The results do not show a significant deviation from the Standard Model expectation and 95% confidence interval limits are placed in a simultaneous fit to 33 SMEFT Wilson coefficients. The comparison of the two analysis strategies provides new insight into the design of increasingly complex SMEFT interpretations. The second, more complex, approach targeting individual processes results in the best sensitivity to the majority of Wilson coefficients.

authors.name: ATLAS Collaboration

papers.title: Light-Meson Spectroscopy at COMPASS
papers.summary: We report on our latest findings from studying the diffractively produced $\omega\pi^0\pi^-$, $K_S^0K^-$, and $\pi^-\pi^+\pi^-\eta$ final states and determining the associated resonance parameters. A particular focus is on the signal of the lightest hybrid meson candidate with spin-exotic quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$, i.e. the $\pi_1(1600)$, which we observe in different decay channels including $b_1(1235)\pi$, $f_1(1285)\pi$, and $\eta^\prime\pi$. Furthermore, we highlight the observation of a supernumerary state with respect to predictions of quark models in the strange sector with $J^P=0^-$. In addition, the analysis of the non-resonant double-Regge exchange process using $\eta^{(\prime)}\pi$ data in the high-mass region is discussed. It is the first event-based likelihood fit of a double-Regge model and improves our understanding of non-resonant production mechanisms in light-meson spectroscopy.

papers.title: Performance of the ATLAS tau trigger in Run 3 and future prospects
papers.summary: The algorithms and selections used at the trigger level in the ATLAS experiment to select events with hadronically decaying tau leptons are described. The performance of the hadronic tau trigger is presented using proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS experiment in Run 3 at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV at the Large Hadron Collider. In the plateau region of the efficiency curve for a given single tau trigger, efficiency varies between 90-98%. Correction factors for the simulated tau trigger efficiency in Monte Carlo samples were derived using 2022 and 2023 data enriched with hadronically decaying tau lepton final states, and these range from 0.95-1.05 with an uncertainty of 2-3% over a wide range of the transverse momentum of the hadronic tau candidates. In addition, potential improvements and their performance for the identification of hadronic tau candidates at trigger level are discussed using data recorded in 2026, having been implemented in selected tau trigger test chains.

papers.title: MAGI (Multivariate Autoencoder for particle Generative Inference): a generative Machine Learning framework for accelerated multi-stage particle simulations
papers.summary: Monte Carlo particle simulations are hindered by the computational cost of particle transport. This is especially true when large mass surrounds a small sensitive volume. MAGI is a conditional variational autoencoder that learns the joint energy, position and direction distribution of particles crossing a closed surface in a multi-stage simulation, to be resampled and re-injected in a smaller mass model. We validated it generating crossings, variables describing particle features later in the simulation, injecting them into the same Geant4 mass model and comparing the spectrum and counts at detector level with full simulation. Rates per injected crossing agree with unity at $\sim1\sigma$ on our benchmark models. We measure the gain of MAGI with statistical amplification $1/\chi$ and computational speed-up $S$: the first goes from 150 for high-statistics cosmic rays to 12000 for rare radioactive decays, while the latter ranges from 2.1 to almost 240, depending on source type and mass model. These first results validate MAGI v1.0.0 released on GitHub.

papers.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.summary: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.

papers.title: Search for boosted diphoton resonances in the 10 to 70 GeV mass range using 138 fb$^{-1}$ of 13 TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
papers.summary: A search for diphoton resonances in the mass range between 10 and 70 GeV with the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is presented. The analysis is based on $pp$ collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV recorded from 2015 to 2018. Previous searches for diphoton resonances at the LHC have explored masses down to 65 GeV, finding no evidence of new particles. This search exploits the particular kinematics of events with pairs of closely spaced photons reconstructed in the detector, allowing examination of invariant masses down to 10 GeV. The presented strategy covers a region previously unexplored at hadron colliders because of the experimental challenges of recording low-energy photons and estimating the backgrounds. No significant excess is observed and the reported limits provide the strongest bound on promptly decaying axion-like particles coupling to gluons and photons for masses between 10 and 70 GeV.

papers.title: Higgs Physics at a $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV Muon Collider with detailed detector simulation
papers.summary: The Muon Collider is one of the most promising future collider facilities with the potential to reach multi-TeV center-of-mass energy and high luminosity. Due to the significant Higgs boson production cross section in muon collisions at these high energies, the collider can be considered a Higgs factory. It holds the capability to significantly advance our understanding of the Higgs sector to an unprecedented level of precision. However, the presence of beam-induced background resulting from the decay of the beam muons poses unique challenges for detector development and event reconstruction. In this paper, the prospects for various measurements of the Higgs boson production cross sections at a $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV collider are presented using a detailed detector simulation in a realistic environment. The study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving high precision measurements of the Higgs boson production cross sections with the current state-of-the-art detector design. In addition, the paper discusses the detector requirements necessary for obtaining such resolutions and for measuring the Higgs trilinear self-coupling.

papers.title: DrSai: an agentic AI system toward autonomous physics analysis workflows at BESIII
papers.summary: High Energy Physics (HEP) experiments like BESIII produce petabyte-scale data. Extracting physics results requires complex workflows (simulation, reconstruction, statistical analysis, etc.) that traditionally take experts months or years. Current manual methods are labor-intensive, prone to bias, and limit large-scale systematic scans. As data grows, this paradigm slows discovery. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a solution. Their natural language understanding and code generation capabilities allow them to interpret scientific tasks and integrate with HEP tools (e.g., ROOT, BOSS) to act as an "AI partner" for autonomous analysis. We present DrSai, an LLM-powered multi-agent system that translates natural language into rigorous physics workflows. As validation, DrSai performed large-scale re-measurements of ten J/psi decay branching fractions - without manual coding. It successfully navigated the real BESIII computing environment and produced results matching established benchmarks. The article details DrSai's architecture, the validation results, and performance evaluation. This work provides a blueprint for autonomous discovery, with relevance to other data-intensive fields like astronomy and genomics.

papers.title: Search for long-lived particles decaying into muons in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV using data scouting
papers.summary: A search for long-lived particles decaying into muons is performed using proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC in 2022 and 2023, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. The data were collected using dedicated dimuon triggers with low transverse momentum thresholds, recorded with a high-rate data scouting trigger stream. This data stream retains a reduced amount of information at the high-level trigger, to explore otherwise inaccessible phase space at low multimuon invariant mass and nonzero displacement from the primary interaction vertex. No significant excess of events above the standard model prediction is found. Upper limits on branching fractions at 95% confidence level are set for a wide range of mass and lifetime hypotheses in several beyond the standard model frameworks, where the Higgs boson decays into long-lived dark photons or into dark partons that produce showers containing long-lived particles, or where a long-lived scalar resonance is produced from the decay of a b hadron. The resulting constraints improve and extend existing ones in large regions of the parameter space.

papers.title: Search for the $^{16}\text{O}(ppp) \rightarrow ^{13}\text{C} \pi^+ \pi^+ e^+$ Decay Mode in Super-Kamiokande Using Machine Learning Techniques
papers.summary: We report a new partial lifetime limit of $4.2 \times 10^{32}$ years for the trinucleon decay mode $^{16}\text{O}(ppp) \rightarrow ^{13}\text{C} \pi^+ \pi^+ e^+$, obtained from a search conducted using the Super-Kamiokande detector with 0.401 megaton-years of exposure across five operational periods (SK-I: 1996--2001, SK-II: 2002--2005, SK-III: 2006--2008, SK-IV: 2008--2018, SK-V: 2019--2020). This represents an improvement of six orders of magnitude over previous experimental constraints. The analysis utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) incorporating an attention mechanism---a computational technique that enables the model to focus on the most relevant regions of Cherenkov ring patterns---to enhance event classification, thereby improving the sensitivity of the search. This is the first application of a CNN to a nucleon decay search in Super-Kamiokande. Furthermore, the large dataset available in Super-Kamiokande (hereafter "SK") strengthens the statistical power of the study, enabling a more stringent constraint than those set by prior experiments.

papers.title: Corrections to the Smoothness and On-Shell Approximations in Femtoscopy and Coalescence
papers.summary: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions produce femtometer-scale sources whose space-time structure can be constrained using two-particle femtoscopic correlations. Standard implementations rely on the smoothness and on-shell approximations, which effectively remove the relative momentum dependence of the particle emission function. We explore the validity of these approximations by deriving model-independent expansions that quantify the leading corrections for femtoscopy and coalescence with arbitrary sources and final-state interactions. The resulting first- and second-order correction terms can be evaluated with essentially the same numerical complexity as the usual Koonin-Pratt expressions; for angle-averaged correlations the first-order contributions vanish by symmetry. This version of our paper corrects a numerical error in a previous version. We find that the smoothness corrections are numerically larger than previously reported.

authors.name: Isaac G. Smith, Kfir Blum

papers.title: Solar Neutrino Flux Fluctuations Caused by Solar Gravity Modes
papers.summary: We evaluate fluctuations in solar neutrino fluxes induced by gravity (g) modes, extending the earlier first-order perturbative framework to second order within the approximation of linear adiabatic oscillation of a spherically symmetric star. We find that the first-order fluctuation is zero due to geometrical cancellation. We still find that the second-order fluctuation is non-zero, which consists of time-varying and non-time-varying components. The amplitude of the time-varying component is ${\sim} 10^{-9}$ (in relative difference, in the case of $\mathrm{^{8}B}$ neutrino), when we assume the g-mode amplitude parameter $A_{n \ell}$ to be $10^{-5}$, which corresponds to an assumed maximum relative temperature perturbation inside the Sun. Thus, individual g-mode detection through neutrino flux measurements lies beyond the sensitivity of present-generation experiments. Notwithstanding this negative result for individual modes, the cumulative second-order effect of a large number of g-modes that originates from the non-time-varying component could be non-negligible. In particular, since $A_{n \ell}$ may be related to convection amplitude, which could change in accordance with the solar magnetic activity, the net increase in the neutrino flux, which is proportional to $A_{n \ell}^2$, should also change with the solar activity cycle. Such a long-period variation (${\sim} 11$ years) in the neutrino flux could thus be interpreted as evidence for a bunch of solar g-modes. Comparison of the theoretical prediction with the solar neutrino measurements by, e.g., Super-Kamiokande, may help us better understand excitation mechanisms of solar g-modes.

papers.title: Jet-like di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions
papers.summary: Heavy-ion collisions are primarily studied to investigate the properties of hot and dense nuclear matter, known as the quark--gluon plasma (QGP). However, recent observations of hydrodynamic flow-like behaviour in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC suggest the possible formation of QGP droplets even in small collision systems. To bridge the multiplicity gap between small and large systems and to examine the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions, light-ion collisions were performed for the first time at the LHC in 2025. This contribution presents measurements of the near-side peak width of di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions with ALICE, used to search for medium effects. The width of the near-side correlation peak is studied as a function of the average charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity. At low transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$), the near-side peak is broader in OO and Ne--Ne collisions than in pp and pO collisions, and in central collisions its width approaches that measured in Pb--Pb collisions. At higher $p_{\rm T}$ the peak narrows modestly with increasing multiplicity. The results are compared with PYTHIA, AMPT, and JETSCAPE calculations, none of which reproduces the measured widths over the full kinematic range.

papers.title: Automatic O(a) Improvement for Wilson Twisted Mass Fermions in the Hamiltonian Formulation
papers.summary: We apply the recently developed Symanzik effective Hamiltonian framework to Wilson twisted mass fermions. The effective Hamiltonian is constructed solely based on the symmetries of the lattice Hamiltonian without recourse to the Symanzik effective action in Euclidean space-time. We use it to prove automatic $O(a)$ improvement at maximal twist, as well as $O(a)$ improvement via so-called mass and Wilson average. Moreover, we derive the structure of $O(a)$ counterterms pre-requisite for clover on-shell improvement of Wilson fermions. We show how to remove on-shell redundant contributions using canonical transformations, and find that the well known clover term in isotropic Euclidean space time splits into two terms with independent coefficients.

authors.name: Carsten Urbach

papers.title: $N\Omega$ Dibaryon near Unitarity from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
papers.summary: The $N\Omega$ system is a promising dibaryon candidate because its constituents share no valence quarks and therefore avoid valence-quark Pauli repulsion. We determine the $^{5}S_{2}$ $N\Omega$ interaction in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD at physical quark masses ($m_\pi\simeq137~\text{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method. The interaction is attractive over the resolved range and supports a shallow state near unitarity. A direct $T$-matrix pole analysis gives $B_{n\Omega} = 0.61\,(^{+0.41}_{-0.30})\,(^{+0.60}_{-0.18})~\text{MeV}$; including finite-charge-size Coulomb attraction yields $B_{p\Omega} = 1.25\,(^{+0.46}_{-0.39})\,(^{+0.69}_{-0.25})~\text{MeV}$. These results provide a first-principles benchmark for future $N\Omega$ femtoscopy and dibaryon searches.

authors.name: Liang Zhang, Yan Lyu, Sinya Aoki, Takumi Doi, Tetsuo Hatsuda, Song Zhang, Yu-Gang Ma

papers.title: Unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory on a triangular lattice: deconfined fermions in a vison crystal and superfluidity
papers.summary: We investigate an unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory coupled to fermions on the triangular lattice at half filling, using auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The triangular geometry gives rise to a global $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry that acts as an Ising symmetry on the plaquette fluxes. At weak transverse field $h$, this symmetry is spontaneously broken, stabilizing a vison crystal. We argue that this phase is deconfined: fermions, charged under an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field, propagate in an ordered $\pi$-flux background and form a Dirac semimetal. Increasing the transverse field triggers a first-order quantum phase transition to a confined $s$-wave superfluid, at which confinement and global symmetry breaking occur simultaneously. This contrasts with the square lattice, where the corresponding transition is continuous. We extend our analysis to finite temperature and determine the thermal phase boundaries of both ordered phases. The superfluid melts through a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, whereas the vison crystal undergoes a thermal Ising transition. Together, our results establish the $T \times h$ phase diagram and demonstrate how the triangular geometry leads to qualitative changes in both the phases and the criticality of the model.

authors.name: Welberth Kennedy, Jo\~ao C. In\'acio, Fakher F. Assaad

papers.title: Stochastic Path Sampler For Lattice Field Theory
papers.summary: In lattice field theory, target distributions are known only up to normalization, (\tilde{\pi}(\phi)\propto e^{-S(\phi)}), while the partition function is intractable. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations often become inefficient near phase transitions or the continuum limit due to critical slowing down. In this work, we propose a novel sampler based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, called Stochastic Path Sampler (SPS), which can generate configurations for the unnormalized target distribution without requiring training data. The central idea of SPS is to establish a trajectory-level balance for learnable forward and backward stochastic dynamics between two equilibrium states, namely the prior and target distributions. This is achieved by minimizing the path-space variational free energy, equivalently an entropy-production upper bound, defined by the log-ratio of forward and auxiliary backward trajectory measures, thereby enhancing the reversibility of the forward and backward processes. The learned forward process provides independent proposals, which are subsequently corrected by an extended-space Independence Metropolis--Hastings step. In two-dimensional (\phi^4) theory, we demonstrate that our neural sampler can achieve the same sampling quality as HMC but with a much shorter autocorrelation time in the critical region. This sampler offers a stochastic-quantization-inspired route to data-free proposal construction for lattice field theory by leveraging a variational free-energy principle derived from path-space irreversibility.

authors.name: Shiyang Chen, Moxian Qian, Gert Aarts, Biagio Lucini, Kai Zhou

papers.title: Finite size scaling of bitstring probability distributions for Rydberg arrays
papers.summary: We calculate the probabilities $p_{\{n\}}$ of the measured bitstrings $\{n\}$ for the vacuum of Rydberg ladders with $N_q$ atoms. As $N_q$ increases, the $p_{\{n\}}$ decrease but become more dense in the low $p$ region, raising the possibility that their smallness could be compensated by their large number. The importance of the low probability states can be estimated from the cumulative probability distribution $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$, which is the probability to observe any state having a probability $p\leq p_{\Lambda}$. For not too large values of $p_{\Lambda}$, it is possible to approximately collapse the $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$ for successive $N_q$ into a function that resembles the Fermi function when plotted as a function of $-\ln(p_{\Lambda})$. We show that the number of shots necessary to reduce $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$ to a sufficiently low value grows exponentially with $N_q$. We discuss the implications for calculating observables associated with the vacuum. We show how the accuracy of these observables may or may not be robust against the number of shots. The collapsed probabilities occur in other systems, where they typically are on one side of the phase transition, in a basis dependent way.

authors.name: Zane Ozzello, Avi Kaufman, Yannick Meurice

papers.title: MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts
papers.summary: We present \texttt{MAHA-z}, a photometric-redshift (photo-$z$) estimator that combines $k$-nearest neighbour ($k$NN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, \texttt{MAHA-z} performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior $p(z\mid\mathbf{f})$ obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows \texttt{MAHA-z} to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship~2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year~3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship~2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}=0.0148$ with a $0.27\%$ outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}\approx0.023$ with $<1\%$ outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the \texttt{ANNz2} catalogue. \texttt{MAHA-z} processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-$z$ production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

authors.name: Paula S. Ferreira, Ribamar R. R. Reis, Renyue Cen

papers.title: galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch
papers.summary: We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/ .

authors.name: Jo Bovy

papers.title: ViViViT: a Video-to-Video Vision Transformer for Cosmological Lightcone Reconstruction
papers.summary: Moving along the line of sight of a cosmological lightcone also moves through cosmic time, as in a video of cosmic structure traced by an evolving observable. We recast the reconstruction of the underlying matter field from observed lightcones as a video-to-video translation task by introducing ViViViT, a vision transformer that factorizes attention across transverse frames and radial evolution. On reconstructed matter fields from 21cm neutral hydrogen simulations over $z\in[7.66,16.00]$, ViViViT preserves spectral power and phase alignment within a few percent of the ground truth up to the Nyquist scale, and three-point correlations for all triangle configurations with sides up to $k\simeq0.77\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$, outperforming a convolutional 3D-U-Net baseline across all measured statistics. By encoding the evolving geometry of the cosmological observable itself, ViViViT marks a step toward field-level architectures that natively respect cosmic time, opening the path to time-aware reconstruction of cosmic tracers and targeted searches for redshift-dependent signatures in 21cm data.

authors.name: Federico Semenzato, Alvise Raccanelli, Michele Liguori

papers.title: Early-Excess SNe Ia Show Strong C II Absorption
papers.summary: Some type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit an early excess in their rising light curves, but the physical origin of this behavior remains uncertain. The processes driving these excesses affect the ejecta at early times and may also imprint on the outermost layers. We investigate whether early excesses are associated with differences in unburned material by measuring pre-maximum carbon absorption. Using multi-component Gaussian fits to the blended Si II $\lambda6355$ and C II $\lambda6580$ region, we measure pseudo-equivalent widths and velocities for a sample of 35 nonpeculiar SNe Ia with rising light curve categorizations. We find that early-excess objects ($n=13$) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses ($n=22$) at phases earlier than approximately $-13$ d, with a two-sample K-S test of the earliest measurements yielding $p=0.025$. In contrast, the HV Si II components do not clearly separate the two groups. Early-excess SNe Ia tend to be more luminous and decline more slowly, but objects with similar maximum-light properties span a range of C II pseudo-equivalent widths, suggesting that this effect is distinct from the known luminosity-width relation. We show that, at least in some cases, when objects have similar light-curve shape and photospheric temperature, the effect we see is not driven by ionization but by distinct differences in the explosion, such as carbon abundance and density and the efficiency of burning in the WD. Our results provide a new constraint on SN Ia explosion models for early excesses, as they must produce a tendency for stronger early C II absorption.

authors.name: L. P. Derose, W. B. Hoogendam, B. J. Shappee, C. Ashall, D. O. Jones

papers.title: Robustness of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation Peak Position against Monopole Fluctuations in Galaxy Surveys
papers.summary: Precise measurements of the baryonic acoustic oscillation (BAO) peak position are one of the key goals in modern galaxy surveys. We investigate the impact of the monopole fluctuations in galaxy surveys on the BAO peak position in the galaxy two-point redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. The background mean density of a galaxy sample is estimated from the survey itself by averaging the observed galaxy number density, and this averaged number density (monopole) is subtracted to obtain the observed galaxy number density fluctuation, which includes an additional contribution from the monopole fluctuations, propagating to galaxy clustering analysis. We compute the contributions of the monopole fluctuations to the redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. While the monopole contributions in galaxy two-point correlation function are anisotropic and non-negligible in amplitude, the contributions are so smooth around the BAO peak position that they are almost completely absorbed in the BAO broadband model, leaving the BAO peak position unaffected at the sub-percent level. Our results demonstrate the robustness of the BAO analysis against the unknown systematic error.

authors.name: Christopher Magnoli (Z\"urich), Giovanni Piccoli (Z\"urich), Jaiyul Yoo (Z\"urich), Daniel Eisenstein (Harvard)

papers.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
papers.summary: We present the largest uniform study to date of 50 thermonuclear Type Ia supernovae interacting with circumstellar medium (SNe Ia-CSM). As the first paper in a series delineating the population properties of this class, this work focuses specifically on a uniform analysis of their light curves. Our results show that SNe Ia-CSM display a significantly more uniform light-curve morphology than interacting core-collapse SNe IIn, closely resembling the luminous-slow subgroup. The Ia-CSM sample spans approximately an order of magnitude in peak luminosity, total timescale, and radiated energy, with a median optical peak luminosity of $\approx2\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ($\approx-20$ mag). We find a distinct bimodality in the radiated energy distribution: a predominant population of energetic events with $\approx 2\times10^{50}$ erg and characteristic timescales of $\approx100$ days, and a secondary population that is roughly an order of magnitude less energetic with shorter timescales of $\approx50$ days. Decomposition of the luminosity contributions from underlying SN Ia and CSM interaction by the Ia-CSM spectral classification reveals a diverse range of underlying SN Ia subtypes spanning from luminous 1991T-like to faint 1991bg-like. Both SN Ia and CSM properties are broadly consistent with the core-degenerate channel resulting from common-envelope evolution followed by core merger, where the presence of dense CSM is dictated by the delay time between the common-envelope phase and the thermonuclear explosion. Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.

authors.name: Daichi Hiramatsu, Daichi Tsuna, Morgan MacLeod

papers.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
papers.summary: Accretion onto black holes powers some of the most energetic sources in the Universe, yet its behaviour across the luminosity range remains poorly understood. Specifically, as the luminosity approaches the Eddington limit ($L_{\rm Edd}$), the inner accretion disk is expected to depart from the standard thin-disk solution, becoming vertically extended. The luminosity threshold and observational signatures of this transition remain, however, uncertain. We present multiwavelength spectroscopy obtained during the decay of a black hole X-ray binary outburst. At the peak ($\sim 0.2\,L_{\rm Edd}$), a cool optical and near-infrared spectrum dominated by strong recombination lines of hydrogen and He I is observed. However, as the luminosity decreases, it switches to a hot, highly irradiated, nearly featureless spectrum. This puzzling behavior reveals the emergence of a vertically extended inner disk at the outburst peak, shielding the outer regions from high-energy radiation produced near the black hole; a scenario supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra. Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks. Self-shadowing structures at luminosities well below $L_{\rm Edd}$ have major implications for black hole accretion flows and their observational properties, affecting inferred black hole spins, X-ray polarization measurements, and the physical conditions of the outer disk and its associated outflows.

authors.name: M. Armas Padilla, T. Mu\~noz-Darias, J. S\'anchez-Sierras, M. Shidatsu, D. Mata S\'anchez, V. A. C\'uneo, E. A. Saavedra, A. Ambrifi, M. C. Baglio, J. Casares, J. M. Corral-Santana, R. P. Fender, J. A. Fern\'andez-Ontiveros, G. Ponti, D. M. Russell, M. A. P. Torres, Y. Ueda, F. M. Vincentelli, I. Yanes-Rizo

papers.title: Beyond classification: regressing physical merger properties using solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum
papers.summary: Galaxy mergers play an important role in galaxy evolution; they enhance star formation, transform morphologies, and may drive accretion onto black holes. Due to their complex morphological features, identification of mergers poses a significant challenge. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successful at identifying mergers with good accuracy. However, similar to other deep learning techniques such as Vision Transformers, they require large training samples. Current methods are also limited to classification, rather than regression. Here, we apply the solid harmonic wavelet scattering bispectrum, a method that encodes invariances and symmetries in the data which need to be learned by CNNs, as an alternative to CNNs. We apply our methodology to a simulated dataset of galaxies with a wide range of merger properties. We show that this method outperforms standard methodologies, while requiring fewer training samples and being robust to noise. Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously, with uncertainties ~ 0.33 dex uncertainty in merger mass ratio and ~ 0.66 Gyr uncertainty in time since merger. We have therefore shown that solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum presents an alternative to currently used machine learning techniques.

authors.name: Alex Brown, Georgios Exarchakis, Mathilda Avirett-Mackenzie, Carolin Villforth

papers.title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
papers.summary: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N$_2$H$^+$ and C$^{17}$O in this disk. The C$^{17}$O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N$_2$H$^+$, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of $\sim 3.4$ from $0.039^{+0.067}_{-0.018}$ M$_{\odot}$ to $0.011^{+0.011}_{-0.006}$ M$_{\odot}$ if the C$^{17}$O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of $(4.8^{+4.3}_{-2.7} - 17^{+8}_{-8}) \times 10^{-6}$ relative to H$_2$ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N$_2$H$^+$ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.

authors.name: M. Leemker, S. Facchini, F. Zagaria, K. Doi, J. Bae, M. Benisty, H. B. Liu, C. Longarini, V. Pezzotta, L. Rampinelli, L. M. Stapper, R. Teague

papers.title: FRIDA: Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies. I. Programme overview, resolved gas density profiles, and HI mass-size relation
papers.summary: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) provide powerful tests of galaxy formation models at low surface densities. However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) remains poorly constrained, hampering our understanding of this population. We present FRIDA (Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies), a MeerKAT and VLA programme providing high-resolution HI data of 12 gas-rich UDGs. In this paper, we introduce our sample and delve into the associated observations and data reduction. We derive HI fluxes, masses ($M_{\rm HI}$), and resolved surface density profiles ($\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)$). We find extended ($\sim 7-30\ \rm{kpc}$ in radius) and regular HI emission in our UDGs, and we report the discovery of a satellite around one of them. Most UDGs in FRIDA have $\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)$ profiles with flat inner parts reaching $\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)\approx 4\ M_\odot\ \rm{pc^{-2}}$ near their centres, which then decline exponentially in their outer parts. By modelling the HI morphology of the UDGs, we find a median inclination of $43^\circ$, in agreement with theoretical expectations for disc galaxies under UDG selection effects. Moreover, we place our UDGs in the $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm HI}$ and $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm 50,HI}$ mass-size relations, where $R_{\rm HI}$ is radius at which $\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)=1\ M_\odot \rm{pc^{-2}}$, and $R_{\rm 50,HI}$ is the radius enclosing $50\%$ of $M_{\rm HI}$. While our UDGs lie within the scatter of the relations, they systematically fall on their upper side, being slightly (by $\sim 15-25\%$) more extended and of lower mean $\Sigma_{\rm HI}$ (by $\sim 25-35\%$) than average galaxies at similar $M_{\rm HI}$. Moreover, we find that $\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R/R_{\rm HI})$ and $M_{\rm HI}(<R)/M_{\rm HI}$ for UDGs follow an intermediate trend between late-type discs and early-type galaxies, with a large overlap with Sa galaxies.

authors.name: Pavel E. Mancera Pi\~na, Tom Oosterloo, Filippo Fraternali, Elizabeth A. K. Adams, Andrea Afruni, Cecilia Bacchini, Enrico M. Di Teodoro, Lexi Gault, Anastasia A. Ponomareva, Justin I. Read, Barbara \v{S}iljeg

papers.title: Dark matter alters dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies
papers.summary: Dwarf galaxies are the most dark-matter-dominated systems in the Universe, serving as unique laboratories for exploring the fundamental nature of the dark sector. Although the observed diversity in dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies suggests an interplay between dark matter and baryonic physics, this relationship has remained largely unquantified in existing models. Here, we utilize a set of novel cosmological simulations with baryons to demonstrate how dark matter physics directly drives the structural evolution of these galaxies. By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models, we find that the evolution of the central density of dark matter significantly impacts a galaxy's half-light radius, but the signal is dependent on morphology. This causal link establishes galaxy size as a direct signature of the underlying dark matter microphysics. Our findings provide a predictive framework for decoding dark matter particle properties from galactic shapes, offering a roadmap for upcoming wide-field surveys, such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, to probe the dark sector through the statistical analysis of galaxy populations.

authors.name: Akaxia Cruz, Robel Geda, Alyson Brooks, Mariangela Lisanti, Annika H. G. Peter, Thomas R. Quinn, Ben Keller

papers.title: Variations in the Extinction Curve at High Galactic Latitudes as seen by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
papers.summary: The dust extinction curve, characterized by the total-to-selective extinction ratio, $R(V)$, varies with grain size and composition. Accurate $R(V)$ values are crucial for dereddening astronomical colors and understanding the interstellar medium. We measure extinction toward stars with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy using a machine-learning-based relative of the "pair method," matching reddened and unreddened stars. We use XGBoost to predict stars' intrinsic colors from their spectroscopic parameters ($T_\mathrm{eff}$, $\log g$, $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$) and subtract them from observed colors to measure reddening in combinations of the $g$, $r$, $z$, $W1$, and $W2$ bands. This approach directly measures reddening, unlike the common thermal-emission-based method of Schlegel et al. (1998; SFD). The reddening is accurate to roughly 0.02 mag in $g-r$ and $r-z$. We develop a forward model to map $g-r$ and $g-W1$ reddenings to $R(V)$ and find significant variation in $R(V)$, with $\sigma_\mathrm{NMAD}(R(V)) = 0.23$, in dusty regions ($E(g-r) > 0.1$) at high Galactic latitudes observed by DESI. In this footprint, $R(V)$ is bimodal, with modes at 2.9 and 3.4, likely due to large-spatial-scale correlations in the shape of the extinction curve combined with the relatively small number of distinct sightlines with substantial reddening. We find no strong relationship between $R(V)$ and other tracers of the interstellar medium, such as thermal emission, dust temperature, spectral emissivity index $\beta$, and $H\alpha$. However, the error in the SFD-predicted extinction correlates well with $R(V)$, implying that a single optical reddening combined with the far-infrared dust brightness can predict variations in the extinction curve.

authors.name: Sarv Parteek Singh, Edward F. Schlafly, Rongpu Zhou, Sergey E. Koposov, Joan R. Najita, J. Aguilar, S. Ahlen, C. Allende Prieto, D. Bianchi, D. Brooks, A. Carnero Rosell, F. J. Castander, E. Chaussidon, T. Claybaugh, A. P. Cooper, A. Cuceu, K. S. Dawson, A. de la Macorra, Biprateep Dey, P. Doel, S. Ferraro, J. E. Forero-Romero, E. Gazta\~naga, Satya Gontcho A Gontcho, G. Gutierrez, J. Guy, C. Hahn, H. K. Herrera-Alcantar, R. Joyce, T. Karim, R. Kehoe, D. Kirkby, A. Kremin, A. Lambert, C. Lamman, M. Landriau, L. Le Guillou, M. E. Levi, M. Manera, P. Martini, A. Meisner, R. Miquel, J. Moustakas, A. D. Myers, S. Nadathur, J. A. Newman, E. Paillas, W. J. Percival, C. Poppett, F. Prada, I. P\'erez-R\`afols, C. Ravoux, G. Rossi, R. Ruggeri, L. Samushia, E. Sanchez, C. Saulder, D. Schlegel, M. Schubnell, H. Seo, J. Silber, M. Siudek, G. Tarl\'{e}, B. A. Weaver, H. Zou

papers.title: Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole
papers.summary: We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the $3.3$ $\mu$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the $3.3$ $\mu$m PAH feature in each $6''.2$ pixel of a $22^{\circ}$ by $22^{\circ}$ region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting $E(B-V)$ map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical $E(B-V)$ difference of $\lesssim 7$ mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of $\approx11$ mmag in $E(B-V)$ relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to $\sim$10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of $\sim6''$.

authors.name: Dennis Lee (Gemma), Brandon Hensley (Gemma), Tzu-Ching Chang (Gemma), Olivier Dor\'e (Gemma), Matt Ashby (Gemma), Shuang-Shuang Chen (Gemma), Yun-Ting Cheng (Gemma), Yi-Kuan Chiang (Gemma), Brendan Crill (Gemma), Ari Cukierman (Gemma), Andreas Faisst (Gemma), Joe Hora (Gemma), Zhaoyu (Gemma), Huai, Howard Hui, Woong-Seob Jeong, Miju Kang, Carey Lisse, Dan Masters, Gary Melnick, Chi Nguyen, Roberta Paladini, Ji Yeon Seok, Volker Tolls, Michael Werner, Mike Zemcov

papers.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
papers.summary: We derived a geometrical distance of the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 based on X-ray dust-scattering rings associated with its 1992 and 2002 outbursts. We analyzed archival ROSAT and XMM-Newton observations and identified an X-ray dust-scattering ring in each observation, produced by two different dust layers along the line of sight. By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts, we derive a best-constrained distance to 4U 1543-475 of 4.6 $\pm$ 0.2 kpc. This value is substantially smaller than the distance of 7.5 kpc commonly adopted in the literature and has important implications for the inferred physical properties of the system. In particular, the revised distance favors the presence of a low-mass extended-horizontal-branch donor star over a main-sequence star, calling for a reassessment of the dynamical parameters of the binary and, consequently, of the black-hole mass. The smaller distance also affects the inferred properties of the relativistic jet and the estimate of black-hole spin derived from the spectral continuum-fitting.

authors.name: B. Vaia, G. Mastroserio, T. Darie, A. Tiengo

papers.title: Signatures of CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ in the atmosphere of $\beta$ Pictoris b
papers.summary: $\beta$ Pictoris is a nearby (19.7 pc), young ($\sim$ 24 Myr), bright ($V = 3.85$) planetary system hosting three directly imaged planets. Previous high-resolution spectroscopy of $\beta$ Pic b has detected H$_2$O and CO, but not CH$_4$ or NH$_3$. Combining observations across a broad wavelength range has been shown to maximise sensitivity to such weak molecular signals. We searched for previously undetected molecular species in the atmosphere of $\beta$ Pic b using high-resolution near-infrared spectra. We combined 44 CRIRES+ spectral settings covering the H, K, L, and M bands and cross-correlated the extracted planetary spectra with molecular templates. For species with uncertain detectability, we weighted the observations by their molecular information content and data quality, independent of the measured candidate-species cross-correlation functions. We recover H$_2$O and CO at cross-correlation S/N values of approximately 200 and 50, respectively. We additionally identify tentative CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ signals near the expected radial velocity of $\beta$ Pic b, with S/N values of approximately 5.3 and 5.7. Equivalent extractions at the same projected separation on the opposite side of the star show no comparable peaks. We classify the CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ signals as tentative because their cross-correlation S/N values do not fully account for possible residual systematics. If confirmed, these would be the first detections of both species in the atmosphere of $\beta$ Pic b.

authors.name: A. Barone, M. Janson, A. Brandeker, T. Stolker, A. Vigan, K. Hoy, P. Molliere, A. Denis, H. Anwand-Heerwart, Y. Charles, J. C. Costes, A. Costille, M. El Morsy, J. Garcia, M. Houll\'e, M. Lopez, G. Murray, E. Muslimov, G. P. P. L. Otten, J. Paufique, M. Phillips, U. Seemann, A. Viret, G. Zins

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: I. Population Synthesis Framework and Illustrative Examples
papers.summary: The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte-Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick $v_{\rm NK} > 100$ km s$^{-1}$. The neutron-star system, GX 301-2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s$^{-1}$. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between $v_{\rm NK}$ and $v_{\rm sys}$, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

authors.name: Cordelia Dashwood Brown, Poshak Gandhi, Christian Knigge, Yue Zhao, Phil Charles, Pornisara Nuchvanichakul, Katelyn Breivik, Akarsh Sahay, Siddharth Malu

papers.title: Hydrolyzed Hazes on Water-rich Exoplanets: Composition and Prebiotic Chemistry
papers.summary: Although photochemical hazes complicate the spectroscopic analysis of sub-Neptunes, the very presence of hazes can teach us about the habitability of these planets. Aside from affecting a planet's atmospheric and surface dynamics, hazes offer a source of organics potentially including prebiotic molecules like amino acids, nucleobases, and sugars. These organics are particularly compelling for temperate, water-rich planets where hazes may react with liquid water in condensate clouds or surface reservoirs. Hydrolysis reactions drive molecular reorganization and oxygenation, increasing the chemical complexity of the prebiotic inventory. This water-based evolution of hazes in their environment is largely unexplored and will have consequences for their chemical and optical behavior. In this work, we examine the chemical evolution of temperate water-rich exoplanet haze analogs in liquid water. High-resolution mass spectrometry finds thousands of CHNO molecules with bonding behaviors and chemical complexities distinct from the unaltered haze analogs. The oxygen weight percent increases significantly in the soluble fraction and moderately in the insoluble fraction after hydrolysis, with different carbon bonding structures demonstrating the redistribution of functional groups. The hydrolyzed samples exhibit a broader distribution in H/C and O/C ratios, and the molecular formulas suggest complex carbohydrate chemistry that challenges current theories of prebiotic organic delivery.

authors.name: Cara Pesciotta, Sarah M. H\"orst, Michael J. Radke, Sarah E. Moran, B. P. Blakley, Chao He, V\'eronique Vuitton, Laur\`ene Flandinet, Kathy Dubuc

papers.title: On the Excitation of Sloshing Oscillations in Hot Coronal Loops
papers.summary: Observations of hot coronal loops have often shown the presence of compressive plasma oscillations. These oscillations are usually preceded by a flare-associated localised brightening in the vicinity of one of the footpoints of the coronal loop. The flare heating produces an impulsive injection of plasma into the coronal loop, along with a plasma perturbation that bounces back and forth between the two footpoints, termed as sloshing oscillations. While the association of these oscillations with flares is apparent, the pertinent connection between their excitation and the flare characteristics remains poorly understood. In this study, using data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present a unique set of observations, where the response of a single coronal loop due to repeated flares in the same active region is evident. Our analysis reveals that in three out of five flare events, sloshing oscillations are triggered, while in the other two events, only plasma flows are observed. By examining the duration of plasma injection associated with each flare, we find that sloshing oscillations occur when the injection duration is shorter than the travel time of the plasma perturbation across the loop. In contrast, no oscillations are observed when the injection duration is comparable to the travel time. These results reveal the dependence of sloshing oscillation excitation on the temporal characteristics of flares.

authors.name: Arpit Kumar Shrivastav, S. Krishna Prasad

papers.title: CosmoSim: Lens-parameter estimation of the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 using machine learning
papers.summary: CosmoSim is an open-source tool for simulating gravitational lenses and reconstructing lens mass distributions, either by ray tracing a parametric lens model or through a Roulette expansion of the lens potential. It is also used to generate the large, labelled synthetic image sets needed to train machine-learning (ML) parameter estimators. We present the first application of CosmoSim to real data. A convolutional neural network trained only on CosmoSim images estimates Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid lens and source parameters directly from observed images. We test the pipeline on 21 images of 19 strong lenses from Euclid and the AGEL survey, after removing the foreground lens light with a custom decontamination tool built on AstroPy. As a case study we reconstruct the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 both from the lens model published by the discovery team and from parameters predicted by our ML model. Both reconstructions recover the observed four-image structure, and the ML-based reconstruction performs at least as well as the literature-based one: it scores better on masked structural similarity, intersection-over-union and Chamfer distance, with an essentially equal Hausdorff distance. Across the ensemble, the predicted Einstein radii are consistent with catalogued values within the quoted uncertainties (mean relative difference 0.08 for Euclid and 0.19 for AGEL lenses), and the enclosed masses agree to within a median of 0.12 dex. The predicted ellipticities differ systematically from the catalogued values, while the comparison of orientations is inconclusive. These results establish CosmoSim as a tool that can be applied directly to observational data.

authors.name: Ben David Normann, Oda Hjemli, Hans Georg Schaathun

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
papers.summary: Natal kicks - kinematic impulses to neutron stars and black holes at birth - play a decisive role in the end-stage evolution of binaries hosting massive stars, in determining the global phase-space properties of compact objects, and in setting expected merger-rates detectable through gravitational-wave observations. Inferring the kick ($v_{\rm NK}$) for individual systems requires well constrained binary system properties and centre-of-mass kinematics, which must then be modelled to constrain likely system characteristics at supernova. As a result, population-wide studies of kicks remain few and far between. Here, we model plausible evolutionary histories for 68 accreting binaries, encompassing almost all black-hole and neutron-star X-ray binaries with 3D kinematics measurements, constraining allowed $v_{\rm NK}$ distributions for each source using a simulation framework presented in our previous paper. The resultant $v_{\rm NK}$ distribution for the sample can be simply represented by a broad Gamma distribution with mean $v_{\rm NK}$ = $128^{+17}_{-15}$ km s$^{-1}$ and scatter $\sigma$ = 117 km s$^{-1}$. Intriguingly, the distributions for black-hole vs. neutron-star systems are found to be formally indistinguishable. Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s$^{-1}$). There is a hint, but no statistically significant evidence at present, for $v_{\rm NK}$ scaling inversely with black-hole mass. Our work suggests either that similar physics drives kicks and shows evidence for effects beyond simplistic fallback-moderated scaling for black holes, or that selection effects conspire to erase differences between remnant types in current accreting-binary samples. Larger samples are needed to provide robust discriminatory tests between these possibilities.

authors.name: Cordelia Dashwood Brown, Poshak Gandhi, Christian Knigge, Yue Zhao, Phil Charles, Katelyn Breivik, Pornisara Nuchvanichakul, Siddharth Malu

papers.title: Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems
papers.summary: Gaia DR4 will, for the first time, provide epoch astrometry. When analysing these data, binary sources must be treated carefully, as modelling their astrometry as single stars can bias parallax and proper motion estimates. We developed the vimbinary tool, a framework to simulate and interpret epoch astrometry of unresolved binary systems and to evaluate the impact of model assumptions on the resulting astrometric parameters. We simulated Gaia DR4-like epoch astrometry for a sample of 17 well-characterised unresolved binary systems, including both non-pulsating binaries and systems containing one photometric variable component - variability-induced movers (VIMs). We show that both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements, with the magnitude of the effect strongly dependent on the orbital period, photocentric amplitude, and flux ratio of the specific system. We also show that larger time coverage does not necessarily improve parallax precision, in contrast to proper motion, for which precision generally improves with longer baselines. Instead, parallaxes retrieved with binary-system fitting are more accurate than those obtained within the single-star framework.

authors.name: K. Sivkova, P. Kervella, A. Gallenne, L. Decin, N. Nardetto, F. Arenou, A. M\'erand, N. R. Evans, B. Apostolova, M. C. Bailleul, R. S. Rathour, W. Kiviaho, G. Bras, V. Hocd\'e, L. Breuval, C. Vert, D. P. Gonz\'alez

papers.title: DIISC-VIII: Chemical Signatures of Gas Accretion in Star-Forming Galaxies
papers.summary: We investigate anomalously low-metallicity (ALM) star-forming regions in 11 galaxies from the Deciphering the Interplay between the Interstellar Medium, Stars, and the Circumgalactic Medium (DIISC) survey. We combine optical spectroscopy of 542 H$\alpha$-bright regions from MMT/Binospec with imaging from the Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope and H I 21 cm imaging from the Very Large Array. We find 75 ALM regions: 19 identified using deviations from each galaxy's radial metallicity gradient, 27 using the resolved mass--metallicity relation (rMZR), and 29 via both methods. Regions identified by both methods are metal-poor relative to their galactocentric positions and local stellar mass surface densities by $>$ 0.1 dex, making them the strongest candidates for localized metallicity dilution. We estimate accreted masses of $5.6<\log(M_{\rm acc}/{\rm M_\odot})<7.5$ for the 48 radial-gradient-selected regions, comparable to observed and simulated high-velocity cloud masses. We calculate a mean hydrogen accretion rate of $1.02\ {\rm M_\odot yr^{-1}}$ per galaxy, which is comparable to the mean star formation rate of the sample. The strongest ALM candidates lie within or near $R_{25}$, while rMZR-only regions dominate the outer population. We find no evidence that circumgalactic Ly$\alpha$ absorption along a single sightline traces disk chemical structure, as quantified by either the radial metallicity gradient or the fraction of radial-gradient-selected ALM regions. These results suggest that localized accretion of low-metallicity gas can sustain star formation in galaxies and demonstrate that ALM regions provide a spatially resolved indirect view of ongoing gas cycling.

authors.name: Alejandro J. Olvera (School of Earth and Space Exploration, Arizona State University, Tempe, USA), Sanchayeeta Borthakur (School of Earth and Space Exploration, Arizona State University, Tempe, USA), Mansi Padave (Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics, University of California, San Diego, LaJolla, USA), Hansung B. papers.title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
papers.summary: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

authors.name: Lael Shin, Daniel Apai, Yifan Zhou, Joshua D. Lothringer, Daphne Broski-Laing, Sarah L. Casewell, Siyi Xu, Ben W. P. Lew, Xianyu Tan, Jenni R. French, Vivien Parmentier, Mark S. Marley, L. C. Mayorga

papers.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
papers.summary: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

Blake, Olivia Curtis, Megan Delamer, Jiayin Dong, Mark R. Giovinazzi, Arvind F. Gupta, Samuel Halverson, Kamil K. Kalinowski, Shubham Kanodia, Daniel M. Krolikowski, Sarah E. Logsdon, Marcus L. papers.title: The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor
papers.summary: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$\alpha$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

authors.name: \'A. K\'osp\'al, D. J. Lengyel, P. \'Abrah\'am, B. M. Marosi, F. Cruz-S\'aenz de Miera, E. Fiorellino, T. Giannini, S. Kraus, A. Labdon, P. W. Lucas, Th. Moore, Zs. Nagy, M. Siwak, A. Udalski

papers.title: Characterization of the mechanical vibrations of the Schmidt Camera at the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory
papers.summary: Mechanical vibrations in astronomical telescopes can degrade image quality, making their detection and characterization essential. This work presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable vibration monitoring system based on MEMS accelerometers interfaced with a microcontroller. The system integrates sensor acquisition and data analysis capabilities and was evaluated through controlled laboratory tests. The system was subsequently deployed at the historic Schmidt Camera of the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory in Mexico. After more than 80 years of operation, this study represents the first characterization of its mechanical vibrations. Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality. Understanding the vibrational environment of astronomical telescopes is essential for the successful integration of new instrumentation. Identifying vibration frequencies and amplitudes can support the development of mitigation strategies, data filtering techniques, and numerical simulations to predict image quality degradation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost inertial sensing for monitoring heritage-class telescopes and provide a foundation for future instrumentation and preservation efforts at the Tonantzintla Observatory.

authors.name: Miguel Antonio Nieto-Suarez, Daniel Ferrusca R

papers.title: Origins of Satellite-System Building Blocks I: Solid Delivery During Jupiter's Growth
papers.summary: Jupiter's satellites formed within a circumplanetary disk (CPD), but the origin and delivery of the solids from which they accreted remain uncertain. Here, we investigate the delivery of planetesimal material to the CPD while consistently accounting for the growth of Jupiter and the evolution of its surrounding planetesimal reservoir. Using N-body simulations coupled to an evolving CPD model, we quantify the solid mass supplied through planetesimal ablation and direct capture. We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr. Under efficient ablation, the mass deposited in the CPD can reach approximately 1 Me, about one order of magnitude higher than the mass delivered through direct capture. However, the low efficiency of pebble accretion within the CPD implies that forming the Galilean satellites from ablated material alone may require a very large pebble reservoir. Directly captured planetesimals, despite contributing less total mass, can instead provide satellitesimals that grow through mutual collisions and serve as seeds for subsequent pebble accretion. Our results therefore favor a hybrid formation pathway in which the Galilean satellites grow through a combination of satellitesimal and pebble accretion. We further demonstrate that even a planetesimal reservoir containing less solid material than the minimum-mass solar nebula can supply sufficient building blocks to form the Galilean satellites. The balance between the ablation and direct capture depends sensitively on the efficiency of aerodynamic heating: if ablation is weaker than commonly assumed, direct capture can become the dominant source of satellite building blocks. These results connect the formation of Jupiter and its satellites by showing how Jupiter's growth regulates both the duration and form of solid delivery to its CPD.

authors.name: Sho Shibata, Andre Izidoro

papers.title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
papers.summary: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 \sigma$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

authors.name: R. Zinn (Department of Astronomy, Yale University), P. S. Coppi (Department of Astronomy, Yale University, Department of Physics, Yale University), C. Baltay (Department of Physics, Yale University), D. Rabinowitz (Department of Physics, Yale University), E. P. Bellinger (Department of Astronomy, Yale University), K. Bettwy (Department of Astronomy, Yale University)

papers.title: VIDE 2.0: Robust, Scalable Void Finding for Extremely Large Galaxy Surveys
papers.summary: Current and future spectroscopic and photometric galaxy surveys will deliver unprecedented numbers of galaxies, with expected counts in the tens of millions. To answer the computational challenges posed by these surveys, in this paper we present VIDE 2.0, a significantly improved and enhanced void finding algorithm and analysis pipeline based on VIDE. Leveraging the parameter-free identification of voids via a Voronoi tessellation and watershed scheme, we implement a robust mechanism for handling survey boundaries and incompleteness without relying on vast numbers of boundary particles. This new method identifies edge galaxies and flags voids contaminated by their presence. The mechanism is fully deterministic, producing bit-for-bit reproducible catalogs from identical inputs. An automatic rule for setting the mask resolution renders the entire pipeline parameter-free. Combined with other performance enhancements to the underlying VIDE engine, we find significant ($>100\times$) speedups and a dramatic reduction in memory usage compared to previous versions: a 12-million-galaxy DESI Y1-class mock catalog now completes in roughly 15 minutes on a single laptop, where VIDE 1.0 could not run a catalog of even $10^6$ galaxies on the same hardware. We are also able to identify voids existing closer to survey boundaries via deterministic per-void contamination flags, maximizing their statistical potential.
