We exercise the upgraded pipeline on two large mock suites (MultiDark-Patchy DR12 and AbacusSummit DESI Y1 ELG), demonstrating converged cosmic-variance covariances for the void number function, the void-galaxy cross-correlation, and the void ellipticity distribution -- key ingredients for Stage IV void cosmology. VIDE 2.0 is now well suited to handle large numbers of galaxies in mock and real observations, and ready to tackle the challenges of future campaigns.

authors.name: Paul M. Sutter, Benjamin D. Wandelt

papers.title: Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
papers.summary: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity ($\sigma_c$) and normalized residual energy ($\sigma_r$) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, $\sigma_c$ shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfv\'en wave energy, whereas $\sigma_r$ displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in $\sigma_r$, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of $\sigma_r$ from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

authors.name: Yuliang Ding, Marco Velli, Chen Shi, Zesen Huang, Nikos Sioulas

papers.title: Accurate calibration method of the Back-linked Fabry Perot interferometer using null channel for space-based gravitational wave antenna
papers.summary: Accurate calibration of the detector response is essential for precision gravitational-wave (GW) observations. In the Back-linked Fabry-Perot Interferometer (BLFPI), which employs Fabry-Perot cavities to achieve high GW sensitivity, accurate calibration of the cavity response is particularly important because residual calibration errors directly limit the suppression of laser frequency noise. However, no practical calibration strategy for the cavity response has yet been established. In this paper, we propose a method for calibrating the cavity response using a null channel constructed from the three interferometer outputs of the triangular laser-link configuration. In null channel, GW signals are canceled and residual laser frequency noise indicates errors in the cavity response estimates. Therefore we can estimate the cavity response by optimizing the response parameters to minimize the integrated power of the null channel. We derive the estimation bias introduced by technical noise analytically and evaluate the performance of the proposed method numerically. The results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed BLFPI sensitivity throughout the observation band. This demonstrates that the proposed null-channel calibration method achieves the accuracy required for effective subtraction of laser frequency noise.

authors.name: Yusuke Okuma, Shoki Iwaguchi, Ryosuke Sugimoto, Yutaro Enomoto, Kiwamu Izumi

papers.title: Self-interacting Dark Matter signatures from stars extremely magnified by galaxy clusters
papers.summary: The spatial distribution of cluster-lensed star transients with respect to the macroscopic critical curve (CC) is sensitive to underlying substructures predicted by different classes of dark matter (DM) models. \citet{Broadhurst_2025} have shown that wave-like DM composed of ultra-light bosons better explains both the width and negative skewness (towards the interior of the CC) of the lensed star spatial distribution discovered in the ``Dragon'' lensed galaxy ($z = 0.73$) in the Abell 370 (A370, $z = 0.375$) cluster field, compared with the case of regular cold dark matter (CDM) subhaloes. In this work, we consider the case of self-interacting DM (SIDM) and investigate how the lensed star spatial distribution depends on the velocity-dependent self-interaction cross-section of SIDM particles, and whether constraints can be placed on the cross-section strength at relevant velocities. Establishing a cross-section strength-dependent (sub)halo gravothermal core-collapse probability, we found that the SIDM appears to be the only known class of models thus far in which the sign of skewness is set by its own particle parameters. The observed lensed star distribution in the Dragon galaxy can be well explained, in terms of both skewness and width, when a significant fraction of subhaloes have undergone core collapse and exhibit a steep power-law density slope. Given the cluster redshift, this qualitatively favours an (effective) cross-section strength of $500 -1000\,\textrm{cm}^{2}/\textrm{g}$ for halos with mass $10^{6} - 10^{8}\,M_{\odot}$ (velocity dispersion of $\sim 1-10\,\rm{km}/\rm{s}$), when the role of environmental effects on the core-collapse (de)acceleration is not considered, and limits the three-dimensional inner density slope of the collapsed halo to $\Gamma \gtrsim 2.5$ (Bayes factor of $\sim 10^{2}$).

authors.name: Sung Kei Li, Yuxuan He, Yi-Ming Zhong, Jose M. Diego, Jeremy Lim, Amruth Alfred, Thomas Broadhurst, Sangjun Cha, Birendra Dhanasingham, Leo W. H. Fung, Patrick Kelly, Richard Massey, Paloma Morilla, Jose M. Palencia, Derek Perera, Liliya L. R. Williams

papers.title: A Taxonomic Characterization of Targets in the Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt
papers.summary: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) will investigate seven main-belt objects to improve our understanding of the distribution and evolution of water and metal-rich materials within the asteroid population. Understanding asteroid properties prior to the mission helps anticipate potential surface activity or hazards and optimize data acquisition during brief flyby windows, while also providing essential context for interpreting in-situ measurements within the broader asteroid population. We present visible-wavelength spectra (0.40-0.95 um) and corresponding taxonomic classifications for all seven EMA targets using Chi2 comparison with the visible portion of the Bus-DeMeo class templates. Notably, our analysis identifies two B-type asteroids, a relatively rare class, providing opportunities for future compositional comparisons between EMA targets and OSIRIS-REx observations of the organic-rich asteroid Bennu. We identify the remaining targets to be S-/L-, X-/C-, and D-types. The suite of asteroids selected for EMA offers a unique opportunity to investigate both intra-class variability and compositional differences across multiple taxonomic types, advancing our understanding of chemical and mineralogical heterogeneity in the asteroid belt.

authors.name: Laura M. Lee, David E. Trilling, Theodore Kareta, Cristina Thomas, Gerard van Belle, Christopher S. Edwards, Christopher Haberle

papers.title: Earth accreted increasingly oxidized material as it grew constraining Theia to be small and relatively oxidized
papers.summary: Many different Solar System formation scenarios successfully reproduce the main astrophysical properties of the inner Solar System. Here, we use the chemistry of Earth's mantle to determine whether proposed Solar System formation scenarios can produce Earth and to constrain the characteristics of both the Proto-Earth and the Moon-forming impactor, Theia. To do this, we use a coupled N-body accretion and core-mantle differentiation model (Rubie et al., 2011, 2015b) applied to a range of proposed formation scenarios (Classical, Annulus, and Grand Tack scenarios). This model calculates the mantle chemistry of Earth-like planets in Solar System formation simulations and adjusts the initial redox state of the building blocks in a synthetic protoplanetary disk until the mantle of the simulated Earth closely matches the bulk silicate Earth. We find that a strong oxidizing gradient among the initial solids of the protoplanetary disk is favored to reproduce the chemistry of Earth's mantle, in agreement with Rubie et al. (2015b). The Solar System formation scenarios examined here successfully reproduce the composition of Earth if two related conditions are met: 1) there is a strong positive oxidation gradient with distance in the inner protoplanetary disk and 2) Earth accretes increasingly more oxidized material (on average) as it grows. Furthermore, in simulations that successfully reproduce Earth's composition, Proto-Earth and Theia may possess a wide range of mantle compositions and mass ratios. However, because late accretion is oxidizing across all proposed Solar System formation scenarios, Theia and Proto-Earth cannot both possess mantles that are more oxidized than the present-day Earth's mantle. Similarly, Theia's mantle may be significantly more oxidized than present-day Earth's mantle, but only if it is relatively small compared to the Proto-Earth.

authors.name: Gabriel I. Nathan, Hung D. Nguyen, Seth A. Jacobson

papers.title: How Intensity Threshold Shapes the Velocity Dispersion-Size Relation in Molecular Clouds
papers.summary: The velocity dispersion-size relation of molecular clouds, $\sigma_v = C\,(R/1\,{\rm pc})^{\gamma}$, has been reported with a power-law index ranging from $\gamma \approx$ 0.38 to 0.5 or higher, and a correspondingly varying normalization coefficient $C$, but the role of the intensity threshold in producing this scatter has not been quantitatively characterized. Using 4916 $^{13}$CO clouds identified with GDCluster (Liu & Du 2025) in the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting (MWISP) survey, we derive $\gamma$ and $C$ as functions of the intensity threshold $T_{\rm th}$. The index $\gamma$ increases monotonically with threshold, reaching a saturation value $\gamma_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.56 for the full sample; splitting the sample by spiral arm gives higher values, $\gamma_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.62 and 0.70. The normalization $C(T_{\rm th})$ declines monotonically, saturating at $C_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.35 km/s and implying a surface density of ~46 Msun/pc^2 under a virial approximation. On the $\gamma(T_{\rm th})$ curve, $\gamma \approx$ 0.38 (Larson 1981) and $\gamma \approx$ 0.5 (Solomon et al. 1987) correspond to a low threshold ($T_{\rm th} \approx$ 1.2 K) and a near-saturation one (2.6 K), respectively, roughly consistent with the $^{13}$CO-equivalent boundary temperatures of these two studies. These two historically debated values, together with the broader $\gamma \approx$ 0.38-0.7 range reported in the literature, may largely reflect different positions along this single threshold-dependent curve and differences in sample composition. This threshold effect should therefore be considered when using Larson-type relations to assess the roles of turbulence and gravity. As an independent check, DBSCAN-identified $^{13}$CO and $^{12}$CO samples show the same monotonic trend in $\gamma$, though the curve shape differs quantitatively.

authors.name: Yaru Qi, Xin Liu, Fujun Du

papers.title: Influence of Alfven wave turbulence dissipation in stellar winds of the Sun and M dwarfs
papers.summary: The physics of M-dwarf stellar winds is increasingly being investigated within the framework of wave-driven models. In the case of the solar wind, Alfven-wave turbulence (AWT) is believed to play a crucial role in heating and accelerating the plasma. In this study, we perform one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar and M-dwarf winds using a model that incorporates shock heating generated by mode conversion and treats AWT as an optional component. For the solar wind, we confirm that including AWT reproduces the observed predominance of outwardly propagating Alfven waves, supporting the role of turbulent dissipation in driving the wind. We further validate this AWT-driven solar wind directly against Parker Solar Probe observations, finding good agreement in both the location of the Alfven point and the level of the normalized cross helicity in the fast solar wind. In M-dwarf simulations, we find that AWT dominates the overall heating budget within the investigated parameter range. A parameter survey of coronal magnetic field strength reveals that the dependence of the mass-loss rate on Bcor differs qualitatively between cases with and without AWT, highlighting the importance of chromospheric dissipation. In the absence of AWT, the resulting mass-loss rates are broadly consistent with previous studies and observations. In contrast, when AWT is included, the mass-loss rate is significantly reduced because turbulent dissipation decreases the Alfven-wave (Poynting) flux entering the corona. These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.

authors.name: Kaito Suzuki, Takaaki Yokoyama, Munehito Shoda

papers.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
papers.summary: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX~J1808.4--3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst \citep{2023ApJ...948..117C}, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5\% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14\% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25\% to 41\% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

authors.name: Yu-Peng Chen, Long Ji, Shu Zhang, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Hua Feng, Jing-Qiang Peng, Wen-Zhong Li, Bo-Yan Chen, Lian Tao, Ming-Yu Ge

papers.title: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
papers.summary: The non-detection of neutrinos associated with gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has placed significant constraints on the physical parameter space of GRB jet models. However, most of these constraints have been derived using the time-integrated spectra. In this paper, we adopt time-resolved spectra, which provide a more detailed description of the prompt emission spectral structure, to calculate the neutrino emission, and investigate how they affect the constraints on GRB physical parameters. By selecting three GRBs (i.e., GRBs 090902B, 110721A and 080916C) whose spectra are composed of different components (e.g., thermal, thermal + non-thermal, and non-thermal), we find that the expected neutrino event numbers from the summed time-resolved spectra are lower than those from the time-integrated approach in the region of relatively low dissipation radius $R$ and bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma$, while the opposite trend is found at high $R$ and high $\Gamma$. Moreover, we also use GECAM-C data to calculate the neutrino emission of the brightest GRB 221009A, and find that the expected number of neutrino events calculated from the summed time-resolved spectra is approximately three times that from the time-integrated spectra in the high-$R$ and high-$\Gamma$ regime. More details of constraints on the physical parameters are also discussed. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved spectra for future GRB neutrino studies.

authors.name: Yang-Dong-Jun Ou, Hou-Jun L\"{u}, Hao-Yu Yuan, Si-Xue Ren, Xue-Zhao Chang, Yan-Qiu Zhang, Shao-Lin Xiong, En-Wei Liang

papers.title: Sky Monitor AI: classifying night-sky conditions from an observatory all-sky camera with a CNN ensemble, label-free sky types and exact evidence maps
papers.summary: Small and remotely operated observatories must decide every night whether the sky is clear enough to observe. We classify frames of the auxiliary all-sky camera of the Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory as clear or cloudy, using 8806 frames from 32 nights. A circular sky mask removes a printed date stamp that would act as a shortcut, and all evaluations use whole held-out nights. On six test nights, hand-crafted sky statistics reach 77.1% accuracy, a small CNN trained from scratch 84.3%, and a validation-selected ensemble of the small CNN and two ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 variants 86.7% (AUC 0.924) with the smallest night-to-night scatter. Moonlight is the dominant difficulty: across Moon altitude the ensemble's accuracy varies by 5 percentage points, the hand-crafted model's by 20. Fine-tuning deeper ResNet layers overfits with about 24 training nights, underlining the need to match model capacity to the number of independent nights. The labels were assigned in blocks of 1-2 h, and many remaining errors are mislabelled or partly cloudy frames. Without labels, clustering of pretrained CNN embeddings recovers the clear/cloudy split with 87% purity and isolates frames with water droplets on the camera dome. Gradient-based maps and a rim test indicate that the networks rely on sky regions. For networks ending in global average pooling, the decision decomposes exactly into local logits, giving gradient-free evidence maps and a cloud-cover estimate. We release Sky Monitor AI, an open-source application for single frames, whole nights and live cameras.

authors.name: Muhammad Waqas

papers.title: A Failed Filament Eruption and Associated Active Region Heating Driven by External Magnetic Reconnection
papers.summary: We investigate a failed filament eruption and associated coronal heating in NOAA Active Region 12353 on 2015 May 23, focusing on the relationship between magnetic confinement and external reconnection. Coordinated observations from the Goode Solar Telescope and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, together with nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, allow us to trace the event from the merging of two low-lying filamentary structures to the failed eruption of the resulting elongated filament. Before the rapid rise, the modeled flux rope had entered a regime susceptible to kink instability, while low-atmospheric internal reconnection had already occurred; both may have contributed to the initial acceleration. The rising flux rope remained below the torus instability threshold and was confined by a strong, asymmetric overlying field that compressed it against the overlying loops. An elongated interface brightening, bidirectional plasmoid-like motions, newly brightened loop systems, and progressive weakening of the filament are consistent with external reconnection that changed the magnetic connectivity, removed magnetic flux from the rope, and disrupted its coherent structure. Differential emission measure analysis indicates that the external reconnection heated the active region loop system. A transient, localized structure with high-temperature emission was observed at the interaction interface, consistent with the expected location of a current sheet associated with external reconnection. These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation, enabling external reconnection to disrupt the flux rope and heat the active region loop system.

authors.name: Yudi Ou, Yuandeng Shen, Dongxu Liu, Reetika Tiwari

papers.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
papers.summary: Supermassive neutron stars ($M \gtrsim 2\ M_{\odot}$) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period $P\approx 1218\pm3$ days and a comparatively low eccentricity $e\approx 0.09\pm0.01$ (with $1 \sigma$ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from {\it Gaia} DR2 and DR3 catalogues, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle $i\approx73^{\circ}\pm11^{\circ}$. The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8--2.8 $M_{\odot}$ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of $2.20^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ $M_{\odot}$. This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

authors.name: Xinlin Zhao, Song Wang, Guang-Yao Xiao, Meng Sun, Roberto Soria, Kyle Akira Rocha, Seth Goggage, Pengfei Wang, Hongliang Yan, Xuan Mao, Yang Huang, Maosheng Xiang, Shuai Liu, Dan Qiu, Meng Zhang, Xue Li, Fabo Feng, Xihong Luo, Xiaohong Yang, Jifeng Liu

papers.title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
papers.summary: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China's Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Roman. For the Rubin WFD survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify $\sim0.12-0.68$ short-period ($<5$\,yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying $\sim0.4-5.3$ systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to $10.6$, $8.9$, and $1.2$ systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and $2.3$, $1.9$, $0.3$ systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

authors.name: Zekun Li, Changshuo Yan, Youjun Lu, Zhiwei Chen

papers.title: Evolutionary Characteristics of the Solar Coronal Rotation: Revealed by a Century of Observations
papers.summary: The 10.7 cm radio flux time series from 1874 May 9 to 2017 June 30, the longest available observational proxy of the solar corona, is used to systematically investigate the multi-scale evolution of coronal rotation period lengths (RPLs) using wavelet analysis and linear regression. Throughout the time interval considered, the coronal rotation is characterized by a dominant synodic period of approximately 26.72 days, which varies in a complex manner with the advancing solar cycle. The relationship between the coronal RPLs and sunspot number (SN) changes over time: anticorrelation during 1874.9-1943.1, correlation during 1943.1-1958.2, anticorrelation during 1958.2-1987.4, and correlation during 1987.4-2016.9. Overall, RPLs show a negative correlation with SN, but their relationship is complex. This scenario is reflected in the phase dependence of the RPLs on the solar cycle. The variation of RPLs is complex, but a distinct pattern emerges: during weak activity phases, coronal rotation is slower, whereas during strong activity phases (approximately years 3 to 6 of the solar cycle), it becomes faster. Several statistically significant periods are detected in RPLs. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet coherence further confirm that the complex evolutionary pattern of RPLs fundamentally results from the combined modulation of two factors: the direct and dominant effect of the ubiquitous small-scale magnetic fields on the coronal rotation, and the modulation of the entire solar atmospheric rotation by the solar magnetic activity level.

authors.name: N. B. Xiang, X. H. Zhao, S. W. Feng, C. Y. Shi, X. Y Yu

papers.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
papers.summary: Whether all fast radio burst (FRB) sources repeat, or whether some produce only a single burst, remains an open question. Using 3,950 bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure how the numbers of apparently single and repeating sources change with observing time, correcting for the declination-dependent, beam-weighted exposure and possible variations in the detection rate. Both source counts increase approximately linearly over 300--44,000~hr, as $N_{\rm s}\propto\Delta t^{0.98\pm0.02}$ for single sources and $N_{\rm r}\propto\Delta t^{1.06\pm0.14}$ for repeaters. Consequently, the observed repeater fraction remains nearly constant at $2.6^{+0.4}_{-0.6}\%$. We interpret these results using population models that account for a distribution of detected burst rates and temporal clustering. The source counts are reproduced by a population spanning a range of rates, including sources expected to produce approximately one detectable burst over the observing time. Its detected burst rates follow a distribution close to $r^{-2}$ over 0.01--1.5~hr$^{-1}$. The burst timing and burst multiplicities provide additional constraints. Among 77 repeaters, only 6 have their first two detected bursts within a single CHIME transit, the median interval between them is 101 days, and 31 of the 52 repeaters with at least three bursts have five or more. These observations support this population and favor moderately clustered emission (Weibull shape $k\simeq0.5$) and active phases lasting months to about a year. Our results are consistent with both a single population of repeaters whose rate distribution steepens below the range probed by CHIME and a mixed population that includes genuinely one-off sources. Thus, the current data do not require a one-off population, but cannot exclude one. Longer observing baselines are needed to distinguish these possibilities.

authors.name: Shotaro Yamasaki, Tetsuya Hashimoto, Tomoki Wada, Tomotsugu Goto

papers.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
papers.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic transients in the Universe, but prompt MeV--sub-GeV observations remain challenging with current gamma-ray observatories. Here, using unsaturated HEPP-H measurements on board CSES-01 and cross-calibrating with likewise unsaturated GECAM-C data, we reconstruct the continuous spectral evolution of GRB 221009A over 2--255 MeV. We identify an unusual spectral bump at $\sim$2 MeV in the first light-curve peak. We also confirm a narrow emission line whose energy decreases from $\sim$40 MeV following a $t^{-1}$ evolution, and whose flux shows a ``rise-then-fall'' profile, implying weak emission from the central jet. These findings hint that a magnetically dominated, central-empty jet exists in the BOAT.

authors.name: Zhi-Qiang Ding, Zhenxia Zhang, Yanqiu Zhang, Rui-Ze Shi, Xinqiao Li, Zhuo Li, Zhenghua An, Shaolin Xiong, Roberto Battiston, Shuangnan Zhang, Hua Feng, Dali Zhang, Yanbing Xu, Ping Wang, Xiaoyun Zhao, Yuqian Ma, Hong Lu, Xiangyang Wen, Yongjie Zhang, Xuhui Shen, Shigeng Yuan, Siquan Yang, Rongxue Kang, Chao Zheng, Yan Huang, Wen Su, Shengli Liu, Hui Wang, Xiaohua Liang, Jinzhou Wang, Ke Gong, Xiaojing Liu, Yaqing Liu, Sheng Yang, Zeren Zhima, Jianping Huang, Wei Chu, Na Zhou, Roberto Iuppa, Francesco Maria Follega, Marco Cristoforetti, Wangchen Xue, Lu Wang, Jiaqi Zheng, Jiacong Liu, Chenwei Wang, Wenjun Tan, Zhenghang Yu, Shujie Li, Hao Hong

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Reacceleration and Gamma-Ray Emission via the Cloud-Wind Interaction in the Galactic Halo
papers.summary: The interaction between cosmic rays (CRs) and multiphase gas in the Galactic halo may play an important role in shaping the hard gamma-ray spectrum of the Fermi bubbles. We investigate the interaction between a hot Galactic wind and a cold, dense gas clump with a relative velocity of $300\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ using two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations coupled with momentum-dependent CR transport. The system produces a bow shock and wind reacceleration region downstream, where the wind flow is faster than the initial velocity. For a CR pressure comparable to the gas pressure (CR-rich), the wind acceleration and turbulence behind the clump are enhanced. When CR pressure is dynamically weak, strong gas compression leads to significant CR spectral hardening. In contrast, for the CR-rich case, CR pressure gradients weaken the gas compression and suppress further CR reacceleration. We estimate the gamma-ray intensity from CRs, and find that reaccelerated CRs penetrate the dense clump and enhance hadronic gamma-ray emission. The gamma-ray intensity reaches $\sim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$ in the 1--10 GeV band, and the gamma-ray spectra become significantly harder, consistent with the Fermi bubbles' emission. These results suggest that an ensemble of dense gas clumps interacting with the Galactic wind may contribute to the gamma-ray emission of the Fermi bubbles.

authors.name: Ryohei Inamoto, Jiro Shimoda, Katsuaki Asano

papers.title: Low-Cost Streetlight Shields for Dark-Sky Protection at a Stargazing Camp
papers.summary: Road lighting at stargazing camps can cause glare and stray light that interfere with observation. We installed directional shields on existing solar-powered streetlights at Bayan Gol Starlight Camp in Inner Mongolia, China, and compared SQM-L measurements before and after installation at the camp center (P1) and a site approximately 500~m away (P2). Measurements were taken at elevations of $0^\circ$, $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $90^\circ$. At $0^\circ$, the mean SQM reading across four directions at P1 increased by 1.624~\sqmUnit{}, and the reading toward the camp at P2 increased by 2.312~\sqmUnit{}. These changes correspond to reductions of approximately 77.6\% and 88.1\% in the equivalent SQM signal within the measured fields of view. The largest changes occurred at $0^\circ$; changes at $30^\circ$ and above were smaller. Photographs taken with identical exposure settings showed less visible glare around the shielded lamps. The measurements indicate that the changes were concentrated in low-elevation views. Directional shields provide a relatively low-cost way to reduce unwanted light while retaining the existing road-lighting system.

authors.name: Xiaoyong Liu, Ruobin Ding, Sixuan Zhang

papers.title: The SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project: Short Lags in the COSMOS Field
papers.summary: We present the first reverberation mapping (RM) measurements in the COSMOS field included in the SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project. Using $\sim$6 months of plate-based spectroscopy (from late 2020 to mid-2021) and accompanying ZTF+DECam \emph{gri}-band photometric light curves, we analyze the variability of over 250 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) out to $z \sim 3$. We successfully recover reliable $\lesssim$ 200d time lags for 22 AGNs ($z \lesssim 2.5$) in H$\alpha$, H$\beta$, MgII, or CIV, using a combination of multiple lag detection methods and significance tests. Our measurements are consistent with the radius-luminosity relations from recent large-scale RM programs, providing measured masses of $10^{7-9} M_{\odot}$ for these AGNs. These results and upcoming long-baseline SDSS-V spectroscopy lay the groundwork for large-sample AGN studies in conjunction with other facilities covering the COSMOS field, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and Roman Space Telescope.

authors.name: Zachary Stone, Yue Shen, Scott F. Anderson, Roberto Assef, Franz E. Bauer, W. N. Brandt, Joel R. Brownstein, Megan C. Davis, Jason Dexter, Tom Dwelly, Xiaohui Fan, Catherine J. Grier, Norman A. Grogin, P. B. Hall, Lorena Hern\'andez-Garc\'ia, Keith Horne, Yasaman Homayouni, Anton M. Koekemoer, Dhanesh Krishnarao, Jennifer Li, Diego Mardones-Soto, Mary Loli Mart\'inez-Aldama, Knox Long, Sean Morrison, Leonardo Olivares Latorre, Theodore Pena, B. M. Peterson, Donald P. Schneider, Benny Trakhtenbrot, Matthew J. Temple, Jonathan R. Trump, Qian Yang

papers.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
papers.summary: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

authors.name: Teppei Minoda, Yi Mao, Shohei Saga, Hayato Shimabukuro

papers.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
papers.summary: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $\gamma$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $\gamma$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $\gamma$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

authors.name: Y-Z. Shen, B. Liu, Y. Chen

papers.title: UOCS. XVI. Census of post mass-transfer binaries across various evolutionary phases in M67
papers.summary: M67 is a well-studied, solar-metallicity, old open cluster that hosts a diverse set of exotic stellar populations formed via mass transfer (MT). While Case A, B, and C MT systems have been individually examined in several clusters, a comprehensive investigation of all MT types across different evolutionary stages within a single cluster remains limited. This study aims to detect the presence of post mass-transfer systems using two different methods and thereby obtain a holistic view of binary evolution and mass-transfer mechanisms prevalent in M67. We constructed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for 141 UV-detected stars in M67 using far-UV data from AstroSat/UVIT, combined with archival data from Swift/UVOT, GALEX, Gaia, 2MASS, WISE, and other sources. Furthermore, we performed a detailed chemical abundance analysis of cluster members using high-resolution spectroscopy from the GALAH DR3+ survey. We identified 11 new MS+WD binaries with previously undetected hotter companions, effectively doubling the known MS+WD binary population in M67. This includes five confirmed ELM WDs with orbital periods of 100-200 days and no chemical peculiarities, confirming Case A or B post-MT systems. We also detected 13 long-period SB1 systems with orbital periods longer than 1000 days and enhancements in s-process elements (Ba, La, Y), indicating Case C post-MT systems enriched by thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companions which have evolved into undetected WDs. This study demonstrates that M67 hosts a diverse population of post-mass transfer binaries formed via Case A, B, and C mechanisms. The unified view makes M67 a key benchmark for studying binary star evolution and highlights the role of UV observations and high-resolution spectroscopy in uncovering hidden stellar histories.

authors.name: Harshit Pal, Vikrant V. Jadhav, Arumalla B. S. Reddy, Annapurni Subramaniam

papers.title: Diffuse interstellar bands in nearby galaxies with MaNGA: environmental trends with metallicity, extinction, ionization, and star-forming activity
papers.summary: Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are absorption features of uncertain origin observed in the optical and near-infrared spectra of stars and galaxies. Although their correlation with dust extinction is well established, the physical conditions governing their strength across different interstellar medium (ISM) environments remain poorly understood. We investigate the environmental dependence of the DIB $\lambda5780$ using spatially resolved MaNGA spectroscopy for 837 nearby galaxies spanning a broad range of stellar masses, star-formation rates, and ISM properties. Stellar and nebular parameters are derived via spectral fitting, while DIB absorption is measured from high-signal-to-noise spatially binned residual spectra. We detect the DIB $\lambda5780$ in 159 galaxies and report the most distant spatially resolved DIB detection to date, at 232 Mpc. The DIB $\lambda5780$ equivalent width correlates positively with both stellar and gas-phase extinction. DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected in regions of high extinction, near- or super-solar metallicity ($12+\log({\rm O/H})\gtrsim8.5$), and moderate specific star-formation rates ($-10.5\lesssim\log({\rm sSFR}/{\rm yr}^{-1})\lesssim-9$). By contrast, it falls below our detection threshold in metal-poor or strongly ionized environments. It is rarely detected in regions with little or no recent star formation, with the few detections in such environments occurring primarily in regions driven by composite ionization. Our results indicate that DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected, within the sensitivity limits of the MaNGA data, in dust-rich, chemically evolved, and moderately ionized environments.

authors.name: Konstantinos Kouroumpatzakis, Santiago Jim\'enez, Boris Deshev, Richard W\"unsch, Pavel J\'achym, Jan Cami, Ji\v{r}\'i Kub\'at, Ane\v{z}ka Srbljanovi\'c

papers.title: Performance Analysis of a Dual-Polarised Bowtie Antenna in the Low RF Band: A Low-Cost Undergraduate Laboratory Experiment
papers.summary: We have set up a simple experiment to characterise a dual-polarised bowtie dipole antenna at St. Stephens College as part of undergraduate radio astronomy experiments. The antenna provides two orthogonal linear polarisation responses, allowing us to investigate the polarisation properties of radio-frequency signals using a simple and affordable experimental setup. In this article, we present our analysis of the performance of the antenna and demonstrate its use through polarisation-rotation measurements. This antenna is part of the Sky Watch Array Network (SWAN) and this analysis helps us understand the response of each individual array element in the setup.

authors.name: Robin Sen, Akshay Bhatia Neriyanuri, Geetanjali Sethi

papers.title: Statistical Characterization of CME Interaction Responsible for Successive Type II Solar Radio Bursts
papers.summary: Successive type II solar radio bursts are often considered as diagnostics for the evolution of CME-driven shocks and their interaction with the structured solar corona. However, the physical mechanisms driving these successive type II emissions are not well understood, with prior studies mostly limited to single event. In this work, we provide the first statistical analysis of successive type II radio bursts over Solar Cycles 23, 24 and the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25 (1997-2025). We have constructed a catalogue of 73 independent successive type II events using radio dynamic spectra and SOHO LASCO coronagraph observations. The events were divided into three observational classes, based on the inferred physical interaction mechanisms: CME-Streamer interaction, CME-CME interaction and Single-CME. Statistical analyses were performed on the 56 events with clear physical classification. CME-streamer interactions constitute the largest class among the physically classified event, highlighting the potential importance of the ambient coronal environment in shaping successive type II radio emission. Comparative statistical analyses indicate that the CME linear speed has marginal differences among the physical classes, but the CME angular width is significantly different between the CME-CME and CME-Streamer populations. Other factors, such as shock evolution and the ambient coronal environment, are important for the production of successive type II radio burst. The catalogue presented here provides a statistical framework for the investigation of CME-driven shock evolution.

authors.name: Anshu Kumari, Divya Paliwal, Jaydeep Kandekar

papers.title: The Distant Milky Way Halo from the Southern Hemisphere: Spatially broad and closer stellar debris associated to the Magellanic Stream
papers.summary: The Magellanic Stream (MS) is a gaseous structure extending over $150^\circ$ across the sky, likely formed through interactions between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) as they fell into the Milky Way (MW). Its predicted stellar counterpart would provide a collisionless record of these interactions, but few candidate members have been identified. To expand this sample, we constructed a catalog of 87,763 distant K-giant candidates using DELVE DR2 and VHS DR5 photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry, and analyzed VLT and Magellan spectra of 51 targets along the trailing MS. Combining radial velocities, spectrophotometric distances, and proper motions, we identify five new MS candidates at 58--95 kpc. Their metallicities are consistent with the outskirts of the SMC, while orbit integrations in a time-dependent MW--LMC--SMC potential support a possible Magellanic origin. Combined with previously identified candidates, these stars span a substantially broader range of Magellanic latitude than predicted by existing models, suggesting an extended debris field rather than a narrow stream. The candidates also lie predominantly closer than the simulated debris. More recent, less eccentric SMC orbits may help explain this distance discrepancy, although new simulations are required to test their implications for the stellar debris, along with larger spectroscopic samples.

authors.name: Manuel Cavieres, Jes\'us Torres, Camila Navarrete, Himansh Rathore, Julio Chanam\'e, Gurtina Besla, Nicol\'as Garavito-Camargo, A. Katherina Vivas

papers.title: VISTA Magellanic Clouds deep observations of Classical Cepheids: Precision distances and a collision-driven SMC
papers.summary: The central regions of the Magellanic Clouds are crucial for understanding galaxy interactions and calibrating the cosmic distance scale, yet they remain observationally challenging due to extreme stellar crowding. We utilised deep VISTA observations (VMCDeep) to determine the highest-precision near-infrared Period-Luminosity (PL) and Period-Wesenheit (PW) relations to date for Classical Cepheids (delta Cep class, DCEPs) in the dense central regions of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC). We analysed J and Ks time-series data covering the central 1.77 deg^2 of each galaxy. Utilising approximately 40 epochs per filter and PSF-based photometry, we derived high-quality light curves for 573 and 2090 DCEPs in the LMC and SMC, respectively. We derived exceptionally precise PL and PW relations, exhibiting the lowest photometric dispersion published so far for the Magellanic Clouds. Fourier parameters calculated from the light curves indicate that pulsational models incorporating a mildly non-canonical mass-luminosity relation and a mixing-length parameter of alpha = 1.7 best reproduce the observations. Age derivations confirm a bimodal star formation history in the SMC centre. Crucially, we discovered a striking line-of-sight spatial dichotomy within the young SMC DCEP population (t < 116 Myr), which is bifurcated into two distinct structures separated by ~4 kpc. This provides independent stellar evidence tracing a recent direct collision with the LMC. Finally, by unifying fundamental and first-overtone pulsators, we derived a highly constrained relative distance between the Clouds. Comparing this to detached eclipsing binary distances, our data suggest a moderate metallicity correction for the Leavitt Law with gamma ~ -0.2 mag/dex.

authors.name: V. Ripepi, R. Molinaro, M. Marconi, M. -R. L. Cioni, J. Th. van Loon, R. de Grijs, A. Omkumar, J. Storm, T. Sicignano, J. Oliveira, V. Ivanov, M. A. T. Groenewegen, G. De Somma, F. Cusano

papers.title: Discrete Supernovae and the Limits of Continuous Models in Low-Mass Dark Matter Halos
papers.summary: Many galaxy formation models represent supernova feedback by a continuous energy injection rate averaged over the stellar initial mass function (IMF). This approximation can fail in low-mass dark matter halos, where single, discrete supernovae can unbind more gas than the reservoir holds. We investigate this using a one-zone model that characterises continuous and discrete supernova feedback at redshifts $z\geq5$. Both feedback modes inject the same expected energy per unit stellar mass formed. In the discrete model, individual supernovae are resolved and energy is injected instantaneously; in the continuous model, supernovae are IMF-averaged and energy injection is spread over a finite time interval. Once stars form, a supernova can unbind 1.5-2.7 times the gas present. Continuous feedback begins removing gas after $\sim 4$ Myr, whereas the first discrete supernova occurs after $\sim 10$ Myr, which produces a stellar mass excess before feedback takes effect. The excess persists because the reservoir responds nonlinearly: an event removes at most the gas present, and star formation halts once it is empty. It depends strongly on halo mass: from 135 per cent at $10^7\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to 15 per cent at $10^8\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to negligible at $10^9\, \rm{M}_\odot$ by $z=5$. Fixing the number and timing of supernovae does not remove the stellar excess, which indicates that it is not caused by stochastic IMF sampling. Instead, it vanishes when the same energy is divided among more, smaller events. Matching the energy released per unit stellar mass therefore does not guarantee equivalent feedback in halos that retain gas until the first supernova.

authors.name: C. Power (ICRAR-UWA), S. Balu (U Seville)

papers.title: Magnetically Deformed Neutron Stars and Gravitational Waves
papers.summary: We study the geometric figures of neutron stars and magnetars with spin periods from milliseconds to seconds and magnetic fields from $10^{12}$-$10^{15}$ G to hypothetical values near the Chandrasekhar-Fermi virial scale, $10^{18}$ G. In Newtonian theory, we find the equilibrium figure of a rotating incompressible fluid with a current-free uniform interior magnetic field matched to an exterior dipole field by surface currents. For aligned axes, an oblate spheroid is obtained by minimizing the total gravitational, rotational and magnetic energy at fixed mass, volume, angular momentum and frozen magnetic flux. Its ellipticity is the sum of rotational and magnetic contributions, recovers the Ferraro limit for a weak magnetic field, and has a magnetic weight that depends on the eccentricity for large deformation. For misaligned magnetic and spin axes, we introduce a quadrupolar shape tensor and diagonalize it to find a triaxial ellipsoid whose principal axes are tilted by magnetic pressure. The tilt angle and eccentricities are computed analytically as functions of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities and the misalignment angle. The magnetic energy of the misaligned configuration is obtained in closed form in oblate spheroidal harmonics for arbitrary eccentricity and obliquity. Its weak-field deformation, up to $10^{15}$ G, is proportional to $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, which fixes the magnetic forcing tensor, and its finite-eccentricity form gives a generalized Ferraro-Maclaurin relation for rotation-dominated misaligned stars. In the weak-field regime, the triaxial eccentricity is determined by the Ferraro eccentricity and the harmonic mean of order 2 of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities. The deformation parameters give the quadrupole moments and hence the continuous gravitational-wave amplitudes, luminosity and spin-down torque of the triaxial configuration.

authors.name: Remo Ruffini, Sang Pyo Kim, Yu Wang, Shurui Zhang

papers.title: Minimum observations for accurate Exoplanetary mass estimation with Radial Velocity Analysis (MINERVA)
papers.summary: Precise planetary mass measurements are essential for constraining the internal structure and envelope properties of exoplanets and to break key degeneracies in atmospheric retrievals. Estimating the observational effort needed to reach a desired mass precision is therefore fundamental for the optimisation of current and future radial velocity (RV) surveys. We present MINERVA, a tool designed to estimate the required number of RV observations to measure transiting planet masses to a given precision, providing a robust scheduling framework for large-scale samples. MINERVA simulates realistic RV time series for targets orbiting FGKM-type stars. The code ingests real-world observational timestamps to account for weather interruptions and seasonal visibility gaps. To model stellar activity, the pipeline draws ages from local neighbourhood distributions, uses empirical calibrations to derive rotation and magnetic activity levels, and translates these into time-varying RV signals. We also derived a new empirical calibration between chromospheric activity and RV dispersion for K-type stars, using Global Architecture of Planetary Systems (GAPS) and Ariel Mass Survey (ArMS) data. We validated MINERVA on targets with known planetary masses, yielding required observational efforts highly consistent literature values. To demonstrate its capabilities on statistically significant samples, we applied the code to a subsample of the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample. Adopting HARPS-N/TNG as the reference instrument, we estimated the observing nights necessary to achieve a 30% planetary mass precision, providing an optimised observational roadmap for atmospheric characterisation. MINERVA's probabilistic and flexible architecture allows the optimisation of ongoing RV campaigns, the evaluating of undersampling risks in active stars, and the dynamic guidance of population-wide characterisation strategies.

authors.name: C. Di Maio, S. Benatti, S. Colombo, G. Piccinini, R. Spinelli, V. Fardella, R. Claudi, G. Micela

papers.title: Low effective-temperature diminution of H$\alpha$ emission from metallic centrifugal magnetospheres fed by ion-runaway winds
papers.summary: Main-sequence B-stars with a strong magnetic field and moderately rapid rotation form centrifugal magnetospheres (CMs), which often exhibit distinct H$\alpha$ line emission, as well as circularly polarized radio. For CMs of early-type B-stars with $T_{\rm eff} \gtrsim 17$ kK, the onset and strength of the H$\alpha$ emission is well explained in terms of a centrifugal breakout (CBO) model, in which mass fed into the CM by the star's radiatively driven stellar wind builds up to a density that is sufficient for centrifugal forces to overwhelm magnetic confinement. The analysis here now argues that the observed diminution and disappearance of the H$\alpha$ emission for CM B-stars with $T_{\rm eff} \lesssim 17$ kK can be explained by the failure of their lower luminosity to drive hydrogen-rich winds; instead they develop an ion runaway of heavier metal ions that are the seat of line-driving, which thus feed a metallic CM (mCM) for which the requisite hydrogen is diminished or even absent. For mid-B-type stars in a narrow transition range of effective temperature $T_{\rm eff} \approx (16.8 \pm 0.3)$ kK, hydrogen can still be driven to a sufficient speed to coast into the inner CM, which we show can explain the reduced strength and width of H$\alpha$ line emission in the transition CM star $\rho$ Oph C. But even in regions with no hydrogen, the build-up of metal density to CBO levels can still drive the magnetic reconnection needed to produce the observed radio. We discuss whether such build-up of metals could give rise to direct observational signatures.

authors.name: Stanley P. Owocki, Jiri Krticka, M. E. Shultz, Asif ud-Doula

papers.title: 3D dust attenuation effects in galaxies: structural biases and induced negative color gradients
papers.summary: Radial surface brightness profiles (SBPs) and color gradients are useful tools for studying galaxy structure, formation, and evolution. While it is usually assumed that they are primarily driven by stellar properties, such as mass, age or metallicity, their dependence on 3D dust attenuation is not fully understood or accounted for. We analyze how 3D dust attenuation affects galaxy observations by hindering the estimation of intrinsic properties. We examine dust-induced shifts in surface brightness and color. Using SKIRT radiative transfer models, we simulated simple S\'ersic galaxies, with spherically-symmetric stellar densities, constant stellar-to-dust ratios, and a spatially constant spectral energy distribution (SED). We find that attenuated SBPs differ significantly from dust-free profiles, particularly in the central galaxy regions. These differences become more pronounced at bluer wavelengths and for higher core dust densities, leading to variations in the fitted S\'ersic index of up to ~25%. This can lead to incorrect conclusions about the intrinsic stellar distribution and mimic a central mass deficit. For galaxies with very centrally-dense dust distributions, a core-S\'ersic model results in a better fit of the attenuated SBP. For dust masses as low as ~2*10^6 $M_{\odot}$, dust-induced negative color gradients reach the same order of magnitude as those commonly observed in galaxies, which a dust-screen fails to account for. This occurs even for a spatially invariant SED and can lead to wrong conclusions about intrinsic stellar populations and related astrophysical questions, such as their formation histories or the mechanisms of inside-out star formation quenching. A full 3D approach is necessary to properly model attenuation effects, which, if not accounted for, can bias inferences made about stellar populations, their evolutionary histories, and spatial distributions.

authors.name: Jo\~ao Duarte, Santiago Gonz\'alez-Gait\'an, Polychronis Papaderos, Ana M. Mour\~ao, Rita P. Santos

papers.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
papers.summary: We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive (> 0.3 Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect - a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model - the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN 1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than -3 in the outer layers of about 0.9 Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass (< 0.01 Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

authors.name: V. P. Utrobin (NRC "Kurchatov Institute", Moscow, Russia, Institute of Astronomy, Moscow, Russia), N. N. Chugai (Institute of Astronomy, Moscow, Russia)

papers.title: Energetic Particle Confinement In Black Hole Accretion Disks
papers.summary: Using tracer particles propagating in the environment provided by general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, this paper addresses fundamental questions related to the confinement and acceleration properties in accretion disks around compact objects. By varying the spin parameter of the central black hole and the accretion regime of the disk, a comprehensive picture is obtained for particles whose Larmor radius is comparable to the gravitational radius of the system. It is found that such particles can escape the system at the outermost boundary of the simulations, though, depending on the accretion regime, the time it takes them to escape, and the energetic dynamics along the trajectory can vary significantly. Dynamics near the black hole are even more sensitive to environmental details as black holes with higher spin values generate stronger magnetic fields, which influence particle motion in non-trivial ways. The primary acceleration mechanism is identified as turbulent scattering, with the jet-sheath emerging as the dominant site for particle energization

authors.name: Daniele Villa, Frank Rieger, Frank Jenko, James Stone

papers.title: $r$-Largest Order Statistics for Galaxy Cluster Cosmology I: Reconstruction of the high-mass end of the Halo Mass Function
papers.summary: We introduce the $r$-largest order statistics ($r$-LOS) framework for galaxy clusters, a generalization of the standard extreme value statistics (EVS) approach. While conventional EVS focuses on the probability distribution of the most massive cluster within a given volume, the $r$-LOS framework exploits the additional statistical information encoded in the joint distribution of the $r$ most massive clusters, ranked in descending order of mass. We develop the corresponding mathematical formalism, discuss its asymptotic properties, and derive a set of relations relevant to galaxy cluster cosmology. In particular, we demonstrate that the high-mass end of the halo mass function (HMF) can be reconstructed from the generalized extreme value (GEV) parameters inferred using an extension of the block maxima method that incorporates the $r$ most massive clusters in each volume. This provides a means of recovering the high-mass tail of the HMF using only a small subsample of the halo population. We validate these relations using both comoving and light-cone halo catalogues from numerical simulations. Finally, we investigate the sensitivity of the $r$-LOS framework to primordial non-Gaussianity, focusing on its impact on the statistics of massive clusters.

authors.name: T. Gayoux, P-S. Corasaniti

papers.title: Origin of the Fe K$\alpha$ red excess in IC 4329A with XRISM and multi-wavelength spectroscopy
papers.summary: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of the bright local Seyfert 1 galaxy IC 4329A obtained with \textit{XRISM}/Resolve, supported by simultaneous \textit{NuSTAR} data and quasi-simultaneous optical/near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Resolve separates the Fe K$\alpha$ line into a narrow core and a broad component exhibiting a red excess. We examined three scenarios for this red excess: (1) a redshifted X-ray broad line region (xBLR), (2) relativistic disk reflection, and (3) an unshifted xBLR partially absorbed by a mildly ionized absorber. All three models reproduce the X-ray spectra equally well. Our optical (H$\beta$) and NIR (Pa$\beta$) spectroscopy shows that the broad lines are redshifted by $v \sim +640\text{--}1050\text{ km s}^{-1}$, close to the solution of the redshifted xBLR model ($v_{\rm shift} = +1700_{-800}^{+1700}\text{ km s}^{-1}$). Motivated by this, we constructed a hybrid model in which the xBLR shares the velocity structure of the optical/NIR BLR and the remaining red excess is attributed to a relativistic disk line, which also provides an acceptable fit. The inferred xBLR radius is $R_{\rm BLR} \sim (3\text{--}6) \times 10^3\ R_g$ ($\sim 12\text{--}22$ light-days). From the narrow Fe K$\alpha$ core in the hybrid model (${\rm FWHM} = 870_{-280}^{+260}\text{ km s}^{-1}$), we estimate a torus distance of $R_{\rm torus} \sim 0.9_{-0.4}^{+1.0}$ pc ($\sim 1100$ light-days), close to the dust sublimation radius. Furthermore, two ultra-fast outflow (UFO) absorption features are identified with $v_{\text{wind}} \sim -0.30c$ and $-0.24c$, both confirmed at $>99\%$ confidence.

authors.name: Misaki Mizumoto, Yuya Nakatani, Satoshi Yamada, Yoshihiro Ueda, Taiki Kawamuro, Shoji Ogawa, Yuto Mochizuki, Kanta Fujiwara, Fumihide Iwamuro, Shogo Otsubo, Noriyuki Matsunaga, Daisuke Taniguchi, Hideyo Kawakita

papers.title: From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra
papers.summary: Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

authors.name: Rapha\"el Kou, Antony Lewis

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.summary: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

authors.name: Maksim Kleimenov, Yuan Li, Gwenael Giacinti, Dmitri Semikoz

papers.title: A giant dark matter core extending far beyond the stars of a dwarf galaxy
papers.summary: In the standard cosmological model, the distribution of cold dark matter (CDM) can be reshaped by baryonic processes through gravity, as gas outflows alter the central potential and transform steep cusps into nearly constant-density cores. However, such feedback-generated cores are generally expected to have sizes comparable to the visible stellar body of a galaxy. Here we report the discovery of an exceptionally extended dark matter core in a nearby gas-rich dwarf galaxy UGCA 320. We combine high-resolution MUSE H$\alpha$ kinematics in the inner region with high-, medium-, and low-resolution MeerKAT HI observations from the MHONGOOSE survey tracing the galaxy out to large radii. After accounting for an additional non-circular kinematic component identified in the central HI spectra, we construct an extended rotation curve to constrain the dark matter distribution. The resulting rotation curve is poorly reproduced by a cuspy Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) halo but well described by cored pseudo-isothermal (ISO) and Burkert halo models. Consistently, a fit with a generalized NFW model yields an inner density slope of $\gamma=0.36\pm0.12$, quantitatively supporting a shallow central density profile. The best-fit ISO model gives a dark matter core radius of $7.62\pm0.80$ kpc, approximately four times the stellar half-light radius and substantially larger than typically found in dwarf galaxies. We investigate the main systematic uncertainties and find that the resulting core radii remain large, all lying within 3$\sigma$ of the fiducial fit. The exceptionally large core in UGCA 320 may pose a challenge to the standard CDM paradigm. While its properties are broadly consistent with self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), they may be difficult to reconcile with warm and fuzzy dark matter models, as well as the stellar feedback-driven core formation scenario.

authors.name: Qinwei Yuan, Yong Shi, Xin Li, Zhiyu Zhang, Zhiyuan Zheng, Qiusheng Gu, Xiaoling Yu, Fuyan Bian

papers.title: A Joint Study of Epoch Astrometry and Radial Velocities of Gaia-4b
papers.summary: Gaia-4b is the first confirmed exoplanet discovered with Gaia astrometry, based on its identification as a possible exoplanet in the solution in Gaia Data Release 3 and subsequent confirmation with radial velocity. In this work we present a \texttt{python} framework called \texttt{pyGaiafits} that can jointly analyze astrometric time series and radial velocities. We use this to combine the precise along-scan astrometric time series for Gaia-4 from the Gaia DR4 pre-release with 44 radial velocities (RVs) obtained over three years from four independent spectrographs (HPF, HARPS-N, NEID, and FIES). By jointly fitting these two complementary datasets that collectively span a 12-year baseline ($\sim$7 orbital periods of Gaia-4b), we refine the system parameters and determine the true mass of Gaia-4b to be $10.70\pm0.32$~$M_J$. Critically, we do not find significant evidence for the long-term quadratic RV trend previously reported in the literature, recovering $\ddot{\gamma} = 5.5^{+8.3}_{-6.7}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-2}}$ consistent with zero. We discuss how this discrepancy likely arises from a degeneracy between orbital period and long-term trends when RVs span only $\sim$1.5 orbital cycles --- a degeneracy that is broken by anchoring the ephemeris with early Gaia astrometry.

authors.name: Shubham Kanodia, Suvrath Mahadevan, Gudmundur Stefansson, Domenico Barbato, Joe P. Ninan, William D. Cochran, Rachel B. Fernandes, Caleb I. Canas, Andrea S. J. Lin, Leonardo A. Paredes, Matteo Pinamonti, Paul Robertson, Christian Schwab, Alessandro Sozzetti

papers.title: Long-period longitudinal oscillations in a solar filament beyond the theoretical period limit
papers.summary: Solar filaments exhibit oscillatory motions in different directions, including large-amplitude longitudinal oscillations (LALOs), which are commonly interpreted as magnetoacoustic oscillations with gravity providing the main restoring force In the standard pendulum model, the magnetic-field geometry imposes an upper limit on the oscillation period of approximately 167 min near the solar surface. Here, we report a longitudinal oscillation observed in a solar filament using SDO/AIA 193 and 171 angstroms observations, with periods ranging from 178-184 min. These values are longer than the near-surface cut-off period derived under the assumptions of the standard pendulum model. To investigate this discrepancy, we consider two possible effects: the prominence height above the solar surface and the three-dimensional geometry of the magnetic field. The former increases the theoretical cut-off period by reducing the local gravitational acceleration, while the latter can modify the longitudinal restoring force through the inclination of the plane containing the local field-line curvature. Specifically, a locally concave-down field-line geometry can reduce the restoring force and permit longer periods, provided that the equilibrium remains stable. However, the available observations do not allow us to independently constrain the prominence height, field-line curvature, and inclination. This result highlights the importance of considering the three-dimensional geometry and curvature of filaments when interpreting their longitudinal oscillations. Since LALOs provide a potential seismological diagnostic for estimating the magnetic-field strength supporting filaments, neglecting their curvature may introduce systematic errors in such estimates. Therefore, accounting for the geometry of the oscillating structure is essential for the accurate application of filament seismology.

authors.name: Miguel Rojas-Quesada, Manuel Luna, Lela Talishvilli, Heidy Gutierrez

papers.title: Model-dependent metallicities of young stellar populations in TIMER galaxies
papers.summary: Stellar populations in the central regions of disc galaxies provide key constraints on their formation and secular evolution. We investigate the properties of young stellar populations in the centres of nearby barred galaxies from the TIMER survey, using four stellar population models, two based on empirical (MILES, X-Shooter) and two on theoretical (Starburst99, HR-pyPopStar) stellar libraries, complemented by independent gas-phase metallicities from emission-line diagnostics. The inferred stellar metallicities depend strongly on the adopted model. Measured as the 5th-to-95th percentile spread across the three galaxies analysed in detail, the empirical libraries recover variations of 1.11 and 0.98 dex, whereas the theoretical ones return 0.40 and 0.49 dex; the gas in the same regions spans 0.49 dex. Gas metallicities are indeed lower in the central star-forming regions, but the amplitude of that depression (about 0.3 dex in NGC 1097) exceeds what bar-driven inflow of disc gas can account for, given typical abundance gradients in literature. The age-metallicity relations consistently reveal two distinct components: an older population consistent with a self-enrichment scenario, and a younger population formed from gas inflows with a different chemical enrichment history. The empirical libraries produce a monotonic decline of metallicities from old to young populations, which would require a sustained inflow of metal-poor gas outpacing its own enrichment. The theoretical libraries instead recover a young component whose metallicity departs from the older populations only at the most recent ages and by a few tenths of a dex, compatible with a single dilution episode. Our results demonstrate that model choice critically affects inferred metallicities, with empirical stellar libraries recovering age-metallicity relations that demand physical conditions the gas measurements cannot sustain.

authors.name: Geraldo Gon\c{c}alves, Paula R. T. Coelho, Luiz A. Silva-Lima, Lucimara Martins, Marie Martig, Dimitri A. Gadotti, Camila de S\'a-Freitas, Jairo M\'endez-Abreu, Patricia S\'anchez-Bl\'azquez, Jes\'us Falc\'on-Barroso, Glenn van de Ven, Adriana de Lorenzo-C\'aceres, Isabel P\'erez

papers.title: Measuring Milky Way Mass with RR Lyraes and Blue Horizontal Branch Stars
papers.summary: Measuring the mass of the Milky Way is essential for understanding galaxy formation and evolution, characterizing the Galactic potential and assembly history, and probing the nature of dark matter. We derive the enclosed mass profile of the Milky Way out to Galactocentric distances of $\sim80\,\mathrm{kpc}$ using two halo tracers with full 3D kinematics: RR Lyraes (RRLs) and blue horizontal-branch stars (BHBs). Our sample consists of 7,550 RRLs and 8,230 BHBs constructed from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), spanning Galactocentric distances from $10$ to $100\,\mathrm{kpc}$. We estimate the enclosed mass using two independent methods: the spherical Jeans equation and the tracer mass estimator (TME). The two tracers yield consistent results, with $M(<81.7\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.76 \pm 0.23)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M(<82.8\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.66 \pm 0.35)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. Adopting an NFW profile to extrapolate the enclosed mass beyond the outermost radius probed by our tracers, we infer virial masses of $M_{200} = 8.12^{+0.72}_{-0.65}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 8.13^{+0.78}_{-0.67}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. We further validate our methodology using mock RRL and BHB samples constructed from two Auriga halos, finding that the inferred masses are underestimated by $15.5\%\pm2.8\%$ for RRLs and $11.9\%\pm3.4\%$ for BHBs, respectively. After correcting for these systematic errors, the Milky Way virial masses are $M_{200} = 9.79^{+0.93}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 9.24^{+0.95}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs.

authors.name: Xiangyu Li, Yang Huang, Jifeng Liu, Xinyi Li, Qikang Feng, Haozhu Fu, Shenglan Sun, Jiahui Wang

papers.title: A new indirect approach for oxygen abundance determinations across a wide range of physical conditions
papers.summary: In this work we present a new approach to derive HII region metal abundances based on sulfur emission lines. We select M101 as benchmark galaxy to test our new methodology along the wide metallicity gradient of this huge face-on star-forming spiral. Based on previous studies, we compile a sample of 151 HII regions and compare their properties base on the galaxy radial profile. The new methodology is based on the derivation of the electron temperature of the double ionised sulfur, either by the direct measurement of the [SIII] auroral line or, at supersolar metalicities, from the $SO_{23}$ parameter. This new indirect method is able to extend the abundance gradient up to the very centre of the M101 galaxy (0.04 $R_e$).
