Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

authors.name: Filippo Camilloni, Konrad Topolski, Keneth Miler, Luciano Rezzolla

papers.title: Post-adiabatic effects sourced by radiation reaction for inspiraling, eccentric binaries in post-Newtonian theory
papers.summary: The adiabatic approximation, in which eccentric binaries evolve under orbit-averaged fluxes, is widely used in gravitational-wave and astrophysical modeling. We use resummed multiple-scale analysis, which is closely related to near-identity averaging transformations, to derive post-adiabatic corrections from leading-order radiation reaction and explain how the accuracy of the adiabatic approximation depends on the initial orbital phase. While the secular evolution equations for the eccentricity and semi-major axis receive no explicit first post-adiabatic corrections, their solutions acquire such corrections through the initial conditions. We also derive the change in the functional form of the gravitational-wave polarizations that cancels the gauge dependence of the orbital elements at first post-adiabatic order, ensuring agreement between waveforms evaluated at the same physical event in different coordinates. At a radial turning point, the first post-adiabatic oscillations of the semi-major axis and eccentricity vanish, so the initial osculating energy and angular momentum agree with their orbit-averaged values up to second post-adiabatic corrections. When initialized elsewhere along the orbit, the adiabatic approximation can accumulate significant dephasing, which the first post-adiabatic approximation can substantially reduce. Both dephasings can change sign across parameter space, consistent with competing contributions from successive orders. Accounting for initialization is therefore essential for assessing the accuracy of these approximations, particularly for long-lived, highly eccentric binaries.

authors.name: Rohit S. Chandramouli, Nijaid Arredondo, Lidia J. Gomes Da Silva, Nicol\'as Yunes

papers.title: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
papers.summary: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $\omega$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(\rho)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $\Theta = dI/d\omega = \widetilde{\Theta}/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tilde{\Theta}$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $\Theta$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation. The adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.

authors.name: A. A. Uleiev, A. G. Magner, S. P. Maydanyuk, A. Bonasera, H. Zheng, S. N. Fedotkin, A. I. Levon, U. V. Grygoriev, T. Depastas

papers.title: Highly spinning binary black holes: promise and pitfalls for parameterized tests of general relativity
papers.summary: Highly spinning binary black holes exhibit complex inspiral dynamics and offer a powerful opportunity to probe gravity in a stronger-field and more dynamical regime than non-spinning binaries. Gravitational-wave signals from such systems enable stringent parameterized tests of deviations from the source dynamics predicted by general relativity. We show that highly spinning, mass-asymmetric binaries can provide enhanced sensitivity to deviations entering at higher post-Newtonian orders, which remain comparatively poorly constrained. Using NR simulations from the SXS catalog, we first recover the injected signals within general relativity using $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM-SpinTaylor}$, $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPNR}$, and $\texttt{SEOBNRv5PHM}$, finding model-dependent biases in the inferred masses, spins, and spin orientations. We then analyze the same signals with the $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM}$-based inspiral parameterized test of general relativity framework, TIGER, and find that these waveform-systematic biases can lead to apparent deviations from general relativity, which become significant for loud signals. Our results highlight that highly spinning binaries offer powerful tests of higher-order post-Newtonian deviations, but waveform inaccuracies can lead to false signs of new physics.

authors.name: Soumen Roy, Maria Haney, Justin Janquart

papers.title: Eccentricity detectability in Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.

authors.name: Maria Gon\c{c}alves Salgado, Lorenzo Speri, Elena M. Rossi

papers.title: Population inference of eccentric binary black holes using asymptotic constants of motion
papers.summary: In standard gravitational-wave population analyses of compact binaries, source parameters are defined at a reference frequency. For quantities that evolve during the inspiral, this means constructing a population of systems at different evolutionary stages, which complicates the astrophysical interpretation of the results. The past-time infinity, or zero-frequency, limit provides a mathematically well-defined reference where all sources enter the population fit on equal footing. This approach was first proposed for spin tilts, which evolve due to spin precession but converge to constant values as binaries are back-propagated. The orbital eccentricity also evolves throughout the inspiral and approaches unity in the zero-frequency limit for all binaries, making it unsuitable as a common reference point for population analyses. On the other hand, the Newtonian orbital angular momentum is an asymptotic constant of motion of the relativistic two-body problem and remains finite in this limit. In this paper, we make use of this known asymptotic behavior to reformulate eccentric population inference in terms of orbital angular momentum rather than eccentricity and demonstrate this approach on simulated gravitational-wave data. Our work constitutes the first example of eccentric population inference using only asymptotic constants of motion. Importantly, after the inference has been performed using this consistent reference, the results can be propagated to any preferred frequency for comparison with astrophysical predictions.

authors.name: Chiara Anselmo, Giulia Fumagalli, Davide Gerosa

papers.title: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
papers.summary: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $\alpha$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $\alpha$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $\alpha$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.

authors.name: Shulin Tang, Yibin Qian, Chong Qi, Ramon A. Wyss, Roberto J. Liotta, Dong Bai, Jianjun He, Tao Wan, Bo Zhou, Chang Xu, P\'{e}ter Kanizsai, Maria Lugaro, Zhongzhou Ren

papers.title: Exceptional point excitation by a plunging particle
papers.summary: We investigate the excitation of a second-order exceptional point (EP) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum by a plunging particle. Starting from a gravitational action, we derive the master equation with a Gaussian bump modified potential. For the odd-parity mode $(\ell,m)=(2,1)$, we compute the waveform numerically and derive an analytic expression for the EP contribution to the ringdown waveform directly from the particle source. Comparison with the numerical waveform shows that the particle excites the EP response, which, together with its mirror contribution, dominates the intermediate ringdown stage. We use waveform fitting and Bayesian analysis to assess the limitations of conventional QNM templates for EP ringdown. In the fitting, the EP template recovers the complex frequency $\omega$ more accurately than the ordinary template. In Bayesian analysis, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $\rho=100$, the ordinary template yields a narrow frequency posterior whose $90\%$ credible region excludes the true EP frequency, whereas the broader EP-template region contains it. The Bayes factor nevertheless favors the ordinary template at lower SNRs and the EP template only at higher SNRs. These results show that in the EP case a narrow posterior and favorable Bayesian evidence do not guarantee accurate frequency inference when a conventional template omits the characteristic EP ringdown structure.

authors.name: Xia-Yuan Liu, Liang-Bi Wu

papers.title: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
papers.summary: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.

authors.name: Jian-Hao Shi, Bao-Jun Cai, Yu-Gang Ma

papers.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
papers.summary: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted. We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained. We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0. Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

authors.name: Daniel Williams, Michael Williams

papers.title: Rapid Multiparameter Gravitational-Wave Tests of General Relativity with Neural Posterior Estimation
papers.summary: Multiparameter gravitational-wave tests of general relativity (GR) are limited by strong correlations among post-Newtonian (PN) phase deformations and the computational cost of Bayesian inference. We present DINGO-TGR, a neural posterior estimation framework that jointly infers binary-source parameters and six PN phase deformations within the TIGER parametrization, using IMRPhenomXPHM waveforms with spin precession and higher-order modes. Importance sampling reweights the neural proposal samples, while principal component analysis (PCA) identifies two well-constrained combinations of PN deformations. We validate the framework using 16 zero-noise GR injections and 12 beyond-GR injections, recovering GR-consistent posteriors in the former and leading-mode shifts consistent with the injected deformations in the latter. For GW150914 and GW250114, our results agree with independent \texttt{bilby-tgr} analyses using \texttt{dynesty}. After training, inference including importance sampling takes approximately 38 minutes and 4.4 hours, respectively, compared with 177 and 238 hours for conventional sampling. GW150914 exhibits a mild offset from GR in the leading PCA mode, whereas GW250114 is consistent with GR. To assess the significance of the GW150914 offset, we analyze 1000 GW150914-like GR injections with independent Gaussian-noise realizations and fixed detector power spectral densities. The resulting empirical upper-tail $p$-value is $11.5\%$, indicating that the observed offset does not reject the adopted GR null model at the 5\% significance level. Our results demonstrate the potential of importance-sampling-corrected neural inference for efficient multiparameter GR tests and large-scale injection-based significance assessments.

authors.name: Hong Su, Tao Yang, He Wang

papers.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
papers.summary: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

authors.name: Aditya Kumar Sharma, Alicia Calafat, Rodrigo Tenorio, David Keitel, Alicia M. Sintes

papers.title: Modification from Noncommutative Inflation
papers.summary: We explore the noncommutative effect on single field inflation and compare with WMAP five-year data. First, we calculate the noncommutative effect from the potential and dynamical terms, and construct the general form of modified power spectrum. Second, we consider the leading order modification of slow-roll, DBI and K-inflation and unite the modification, which means the modification is nearly model independent at this level. Finally, comparing with the WMAP5 data, we find that the modified can be well realized as the origin of the relative large spectral index and the quite small running.

authors.name: Hong-Guang Zhang, Jie Ren, Xin-He Meng

papers.title: $^{56}$Ni production in long-lived binary neutron star merger remnants
papers.summary: We investigate the nucleosynthesis and kilonova emission based on numerical-relativity binary neutron star merger simulations that incorporate a two-moment neutrino-transport scheme. Unlike in previous works with simpler neutrino treatments, a massive, fast (up to $v=0.3c$), proton-rich neutrino-driven wind develops in the postmerger phase of the simulations as long as the merger remnant does not collapse to a black hole. We evolve the ejecta for 100 days after the merger using 2D ray-by-ray radiation-hydrodynamics simulations coupled in situ to a complete nuclear network. The most abundant nucleosynthesis products are He, $^{56}$Ni, and $^{56}$Co. We find a total yield of $\sim 10^{-3} M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni for all mergers that produce massive neutron star remnants, independently of the mass ratio and equations of state. After a few days, the decay of $^{56}$Ni and later $^{56}$Co becomes the primary source of heating in the matter expanding above the remnant. As a result, the kilonova light curve flattens on timescales of days for polar observation angles. This is an important effect that should be included in future models of kilonova light curves. Furthermore, the observation of a $^{56}$Ni-$^{56}$Co feature could serve as a clear indicator for the presence of a long-lived neutron star remnant in future kilonova observations.

authors.name: Maximilian Jacobi, Fabio Magistrelli, Eleonora Loffredo, Giacomo Ricigliano, Leonardo Chiesa, Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Albino Perego, Almudena Arcones

papers.title: Flare genesis in relativistic jet: Disentangling the drivers of variability in the blazar 4C +27.50
papers.summary: Recently, blazar 4C +27.50 was found to be flaring in gamma-rays since its detection with Fermi-LAT in 2008. For the first time, a dedicated temporal and spectral study of the blazar 4C +27.50 has been performed in this work to understand the nature of this object. We used the Bayesian block algorithm to identify four flaring states and one quiet state in the 4-year-long Fermi-LAT light curve. Simultaneous broadband flaring episodes have been observed, and a significant correlation is seen between optical and $\gamma$-ray emission, suggesting the co-spatial origin of the broadband emission. The variation of fractional variability amplitude with respect to frequency shows a nearly double hump structure similar to broadband SED. The fastest flux doubling time in the 1-day binned $\gamma$-ray light curve is found to be about 7.8 hours. A curvature in $\gamma$-ray spectra has been observed, possibly caused by a stochastic particle acceleration process rather than radiative cooling. No evident correlation was found in the $\gamma$-ray flux-index plot, but a clear harder-when-brighter trend is observed in the X-ray flux-index plot. A one-zone leptonic model has been implemented to understand broadband emission during the quiet and flaring states, and the variation of the jet parameters has been investigated. Broadband SED modeling suggested that an enhancement in the magnetic field and particle energy density, together with a harder particle spectrum, might have caused the flaring events, while the bulk Lorentz factor shows no systematic change.

authors.name: Joysankar Majumdar, Sakshi Maurya, Raj Prince

papers.title: Benchmarking the expected performance of Bayesian parameter inference on Kilonovae
papers.summary: In the study of optical transients, parameter inference is a part of the process of extracting physical information, i.e. constraints on the source's characteristics, by comparing the observed lightcurves to the predictions of different astrophysical models and finding the model and parameter combination that make the closest match. In the developing field of the study of kilonovae (KNe), systematic uncertainties in modeling are still very large. Current-day models still struggle to fit adequately the whole multi-wavelength dataset of the AT2017gfo kilonova, associated to the Binary Neutron Star (BNS) merger GW170817, and thus obtain wide posterior distributions on the inferred source parameters. After reviewing the many sources of uncertainty embedded in KN analyses and the process of Bayesian parameter inference, we discuss how to quantify the performance of parameter inference analyses using metrics on information gain from prior to posterior. We highlight the systematic error margin hyperparameter $\sigma_{\rm sys}$, which correlates to a model's goodness-of-fit, and exhibit its major influence on Bayesian inference performance metrics. Using the example of two KN models from the literature with the Nuclear Multi-Messenger Astronomy (NMMA) Bayesian inference framework, we simulate the expected information gains that dedicated KN follow-ups with telescope networks could reasonably reach, for various observational cadences and error margins: we show that the wind ejecta's mass and electron fraction are the easiest KN parameters to constrain. We finally apply our KN analysis to the dataset of AT2017gfo to show that our information gain predictions match results on real data and discuss the complementarity of multi-messenger approaches.

authors.name: Thomas Hussenot-Desenonges (Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS/IN2P3, IJCLab), Marion Pillas (Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris, Sorbonne Universit\'e), Sarah Antier (Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS/IN2P3, IJCLab, Observatoire de la C\^ote d'Azur), Patrice Hello (Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS/IN2P3, IJCLab), Peter T. H. Pang (Nikhef, Institute for Gravitational and Subatomic Physics)

papers.title: Rotation Periods for Stars in Open Cluster NGC 6819 From Kepler IRIS Light Curves
papers.summary: We present an updated catalog of stellar rotation periods for the 2.5 Gyr open cluster NGC 6819 using the Kepler IRIS light curves from superstamp data. We present two modeling techniques: one for measuring rotation periods from light curves in crowded fields, and one for fitting a gyrochronology relation. Our analysis uses Gaussian Process modeling to extract robust rotation signals from image subtraction light curves, allowing us unprecedented data access and measurement precision in the crowded cluster field. After applying stringent quality and contamination cuts, we identify 152 reliable rotation periods. Compared to previous work, which relied on only ~30 stars, our catalog extends the gyrochronological sequence of NGC 6819 with an order of magnitude more measurements and improved precision. The expanded dataset reveals both the expected temperature-dependent spin-down trend and substantial scatter at fixed effective temperature, including a tail in the period distribution revealing some abundance of fast rotators. These results strengthen this cluster's role as a benchmark for stellar spin evolution, while also highlighting the limitations of traditional gyrochronology at older ages. The final catalog and the model implementations are all available on Zenodo.

authors.name: Sabina Sagynbayeva, Isabel L. Colman, Will M. Farr

papers.title: Spatial Profiles of 3I/ATLAS CN and Ni Outgassing from Keck/KCWI Integral Field Spectroscopy
papers.summary: Cometary activity from interstellar objects provides a unique window into the environs of other stellar systems. We report blue-sensitive integral field unit spectroscopy of the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS from the Keck-II-mounted Keck Cosmic Web Imager on August 24, 2025 UT. We confirm previously reported CN and Ni outgassing, and present, for the first time, the radial profiles of Ni and CN emission in 3I/ATLAS. We find a characteristic $e$-folding radius of $593.7\pm14.8$ km for Ni and $841.0\pm15.4$ km for CN; this suggests that the Ni emission is more centrally concentrated in the nucleus of the comet and favors hypotheses involving easily dissociated species such as metal carbonyls or metal-polycyclic-aromatic-hydrocarbon molecules. Additional integral field spectroscopy after perihelion will offer a continued opportunity to determine the evolution of the radial distributions of species in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.

authors.name: W. B. Hoogendam, B. J. Shappee, J. J. Wray, B. Yang, K. J. Meech, C. Ashall, D. D. Desai, K. Hart, J. T. Hinkle, A. Hoffman, E. M. Hu, D. O. Jones, K. Medler, C. Pfeffer

papers.title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
papers.summary: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on our online science platform. It spans a diverse range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, modeling assumptions, redshifts, and numerical simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of weak absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.

authors.name: Dylan Nelson, Celine Peroux, Philipp Richter, Matthew M. Pieri, Sebastian Lopez, Rongmon Bordoloi, Siwei Zou, Joseph N. Burchett, Rebecca L. Davies, Rahul Ramesh, Matthew C. Smith, Sanchayeeta Borthakur, Christopher W. Churchill

papers.title: Effect of ionizing photon escape fraction in faint galaxies on modeling reionization history of the universe
papers.summary: We present model calculations of the reionization history of hydrogen using star formation histories, computed with a galaxy formation model which reproduces properties of local dwarf galaxies and UV luminosity functions of galaxies at $z=5-16$. We use the ionizing photon density functions predicted by the model along with different models for the escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, to study the effects of ionizing photons from faint galaxies and different assumptions about $f_{\rm esc}$ on the evolution of hydrogen ionized fraction with redshift, $Q_{\rm HII}(z)$. We show that accounting for the contribution of faint galaxies with UV luminosities $M_{1500}>-13$, and with a constant ionizing photon escape fraction of $f_{\rm esc}=0.1$ results in the hydrogen reionization history consistent with all current observational constraints. Comparing results of the $f_{\rm esc}=0.1$ model and two alternative models shows that the model with a strong luminosity dependence of $f_{\rm esc}$, which assigns high $f_{\rm esc}$ to faint galaxies, results in early reionization inconsistent with observational constraints. However, the model in which $f_{\rm esc}$ follows a universal redshift-independent correlation with the recent maximum specific star formation rate, motivated by the results of the SPHINX galaxy formation simulation, results in the reionization history in good agreement with existing observational constraints, even though this model produces a sizeable ionized hydrogen fraction of $Q_{\rm HII}\approx 0.15-0.2$ at redshifts $z=8-12$. Our results show that the relative contribution of faint dwarf galaxies to reionization depends sensitively on assumptions about the escape fraction for galaxies of different luminosities, and that this is the main source of uncertainty in modeling hydrogen reionization.

authors.name: Zewei Wu, Andrey Kravtsov, Harley Katz

papers.title: NGDEEP: A New Nonparametric Measure of Local Star Formation and Attenuation at Cosmic Noon
papers.summary: We introduce a new non-parametric technique to quantify the spatially-resolved relationship between the local star formation rate (SFR) and dust attenuation. We apply it to 12 star-forming galaxies at 1.0<z<2.4 using JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy from the NGDEEP survey. First, we construct spatially resolved (~1 kpc per pixel) Balmer decrement ($\Ha/\Hb$) maps of these galaxies and derive their corresponding dust attenuation and intrinsic SFR maps. We rank-order the map pixels by attenuation and construct a cumulative distribution curve of the total SFR as a function of increasing attenuation. We define $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$, $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$, and $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{90\%}$ as the dust attenuation levels behind which 10%, 50%, and 90% of the total integrated SFR is screened, respectively. These metrics quantify the probability that a given star-forming region lies behind a given level of attenuation. Across the sample, 50% of the local star formation occurs behind an attenuation of 2.9 mag or higher ($\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$) on average. This indicates that the bulk of star formation in these galaxies is significantly attenuated by dust. The value of $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$ equals 0.6 mag for the average profile, indicating that even the least attenuated star-forming regions are still highly attenuated. The globally measured attenuation more closely matches $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$ than $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$. This suggests that the global value is weighted toward the least dust-obscured star-forming regions and significantly underestimates the typical attenuation a star-forming region encounters. Our results demonstrate a new approach for understanding the extremely dusty local conditions of the star-forming interstellar medium in star-forming galaxies at cosmic noon.

authors.name: Grace M. Forrey, Raymond C. Simons, Jonathan R. Trump, Lu Shen, Anton M. Koekemoer, Micaela B. Bagley, Steven L. Finkelstein, Casey Papovich, Nor Pirzkal

papers.title: Formation and evolution of planetary systems
papers.summary: Various problems of the formation and evolution of planetary systems are studied. Most of the studies are devoted to the Solar System. The collapse of the presolar cloud and the accumulation of planets are studied. The author considers the formation of the Earth-Moon system, binary trans-Neptunian objects, and the axial rotations of planets. He discusses the formation of asteroid and trans-Neptunian belts, including the evolution of resonant asteroid orbits and the formation of the Kirkwood gaps in the asteroid belt. The book discusses the migration of bodies during the formation of the Solar System and at present, including a discussion of the delivery of icy bodies from beyond the ice line to the terrestrial planets and the formation of craters on the Moon. The Deep Impact mission is discussed; during this mission the impact module of the spacecraft collided with the comet Tempel 1. The book studies the migration of dust in the Solar System and the formation of the zodiacal belt, as well as the migration of bodies and dust particles ejected from the terrestrial planets and the Moon. The author considers the migration of bodies in some exoplanetary systems (Proxima Centauri, Trappist 1, and Gliese 581), the spectra of Earth-like exoplanets with different rotation periods, as well as the efficiency of exoplanet searches using microlensing observations with various telescopes. Files with both Russian and English texts of the book were submitted.

authors.name: S. I. Ipatov

papers.title: An azimuthally resolved study of sloshing cold fronts in three nearby galaxy clusters
papers.summary: We present a detailed analysis of sloshing cold fronts in a sample of three nearby galaxy clusters (Abell 496, Abell 2029, and Abell 1644) observed with the $Chandra$ X-ray Observatory. Cold fronts manifest as sharp edges in the X-ray surface brightness of the intracluster medium (ICM) in galaxy clusters. In the residual X-ray surface brightness maps, where the global ICM distribution has been subtracted, cold fronts generated by gas sloshing are observed at the boundaries of the spiral excesses. We perform a systematic and comprehensive study of the surface brightness edges along the spiral excesses. We find the deficit of the thermal pressure radially inward of the brightness edges, in contrast to stripping cold fronts that typically exhibit higher thermal pressure in brightness edges. Assuming that the non-thermal pressure support entirely comes from the gas motions, we estimate the velocity dispersions across the edges and do not find statistically significant azimuthal variations along the sharpest edges. With an assumption that the non-thermal pressure support is completely attributed to the magnetic pressure, we derive the upper bounds on the strength of magnetic fields, yielding $6\,\mu\mathrm{G}$, $15\,\mu\mathrm{G}$, and $5\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for Abell 496, Abell 2029, and Abell 1644, respectively. We discuss several systematic uncertainties in characterizing the sloshing cold fronts and find that the choice of spectral extraction regions has an effect for subtle cold fronts observed with shallow X-ray data.

authors.name: I-Hsuan Li, Shutaro Ueda, I-Non Chiu, Keiichi Umetsu

papers.title: Group Pre-processing in J1611+4026: Minor Rejuvenation of a Massive ETG fueled by Interaction-driven Gas Transfer
papers.summary: Interactions within galaxy groups are fundamental drivers of galactic evolution, and establishing a direct observational link between the dynamical processes of satellite galaxies and the rejuvenation of massive host galaxies remains challenging. We present a multi-wavelength work of J1611+4026, a unique triple system characterised by a massive early-type host galaxy, Component C and two gas-rich companions, Components A and B, which are currently undergoing a major merger in its near environment. Utilising deep optical imaging from DESI-LS and spectroscopic data from DESI and P200, we employ 2D morphological decomposition using \textsc{GALIGHT} alongside joint spectrophotometric synthesis modelling with \textsc{BAGPIPES} and \textsc{CIGALE} to deconstruct the structural properties and star formation histories of the member galaxies. Crucially, we identify an asymmetric tidal tail extending $\sim$15.15 kpc from Component A, confirming the ongoing interaction between the companions. Although Component C appears quiescent in both morphology and spectroscopy, we reveal a subtle robust signal of ``minor rejuvenation'', characterised by significant internal dust extinction of $E(B-V) \sim 0.53$ and a UV excess. The reconstructed star formation history indicates a recent ($\sim$100 Myr) starburst that contributes a negligible fraction to the total stellar mass ($f_{\rm burst} < 0.1$ per cent). We propose that this activity is fueled by the accretion of metal-enriched gas stripped from the interacting companions. These results strongly suggest group pre-processing, where interactions between satellite galaxies drive low-level star formation in the massive host through gas transfer, providing a quantitative benchmark for interaction-driven evolution in dense environments.

authors.name: Yaosong Yu, Qihang Chen, Zizhao He, Limeng Deng, Liang Jing, Jianhui Lian

papers.title: Observational Tests for Distinguishing Classes of Cosmological Models
papers.summary: We investigate observational tests that can be used to distinguish between broad classes of cosmological models. This is achieved using curvature-consistency tests of the Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) models, which we investigate in two scenarios where they can be violated; (i) when the optical properties of the cosmology deviate from the expectations of FLRW, and also (ii) when the large-scale expansion of the cosmology is different from FLRW. We identify useful ways to determine the properties of these alternative scenarios in terms of the violation of the curvature-consistency tests, and propose a new null test that can be used to isolate cosmologies with non-FLRW observational relations. The characteristic signatures we find can be used, together with the results of recent and upcoming cosmological observations, to probe and/or rule out large classes of cosmological models. This becomes an increasingly important task as the number of proposals in the literature increases, as cosmologists attempt to explain tensions, anomalies, and the dark sector of the Universe. Our approach provides a clear route for telling apart these different proposals, and offers a new opportunity for using precision cosmological data to efficiently discriminate between cosmological models.

authors.name: Asta Heinesen, Timothy Clifton

papers.title: Apparent Stability in Self-Gravitating Turbulence and the Evolution of Molecular Clouds
papers.summary: Recent observations of hydrostatic structure and virial equilibrium in supersonically turbulent, self-gravitating molecular clouds imply a stability that contrasts with the transcience of turbulent structure. To investigate this contradiction, we model a molecular cloud as a turbulent eddy and study its evolution as a dynamical system. In a two-dimensional phase space of structure and energy, we find that the dynamical equilibrium is a saddle point, stable in the direction aligned with force balance, but unstable in the direction of energy balance because of the combination of the turbulent dissipation and the negative heat capacity of self-gravitation. Near the saddle point, evolutionary trajectories follow a characteristic pattern that first approaches the equilibrium before departing in the direction of instability. Since the phase-space speed is proportional to the virial and energy imbalance, trajectories slow near the equilibrium resulting in a local overdensity of clouds. Also, near equilibrium, the relaxation to force balance is faster than the growth rate of the instability in energy. Consequently, more clouds are observed in near equilibrium states with hydrostatic structure even though the equilibrium is metastable. This resolves the apparent contradiction of equilibrium structure observed in dynamically unstable, self-gravitating turbulence.

authors.name: Eric Keto

papers.title: Caustic Skeleton and the Local Cosmic Web: the Coma Cluster node and the Pisces-Perseus ridge
papers.summary: We apply caustic skeleton theory to the Manticore-Local simulations, which are Bayesian constrained reconstructions of the Local Universe from the 2M++ galaxy catalogue, and extract the three-dimensional multi-scale caustic skeleton of two canonical weblike structures in our Local Universe, namely the Coma Cluster and the Pisces-Perseus ridge as they represent the most prominent cluster node and filamentary artery in the nearby Universe. We show that the Caustic Skeleton network of caustic singularities accurately reproduces the observed large-scale organisation of galaxies in redshift space for one of the Manticore realisations. The hierarchy of caustic features allows us to establish a multi-scale classification of the large-scale environment in which observed 2M++ galaxies reside. One of the most interesting aspects of the theory is that it predicts two topologically distinct classes of filaments (A_4 swallowtail and D_4 umbilic caustics) that form through fundamentally different folding histories. We find that the A_4 filaments form the most outstanding filamentary features of our local universe, whereas D_4 filaments appear to largely collect at cluster regions identified in the galaxy distribution. Thus, a preliminary galaxy classification scheme presented in this study finds indications of a higher proportion of galaxies in D_4/Node-dominated environments in the Pisces-Perseus Supercluster, which may be indicative of more clumpy substructure along its ridge, compared to the extended weblike structure around the Coma Cluster. [Shortened]

authors.name: Amelie Read, Job Feldbrugge, Celine Boehm, Rien van de Weygaert, Benjamin Hertzsch

papers.title: Non-Gaussian Halo Bias from Tensor-Induced Density Perturbations
papers.summary: Primordial gravitational waves induce matter density perturbations at second order. Because this sourcing is quadratic in tensor modes, the induced density field is intrinsically non-Gaussian even for Gaussian tensor modes. Here we compute the scale-dependent halo-bias correction generated by this tensor-induced density bispectrum for a Gaussian-bump tensor spectrum with a peak tensor-to-scalar ratio $r_*=0.002$. At low wavenumbers, both the induced density power spectrum and the bispectrum form factor approach finite, nonzero constants. Their ratio consequently produces a large-scale plateau in the bias correction defined relative to the tensor-induced density power spectrum. Over the sampled scales, the fractional Eulerian correction reaches a maximum of $1.85\times10^{-10}$. When evaluated relative to the total matter power spectrum, the fractional correction remains below $4.0\times10^{-25}$ across the sampled scales and halo populations. Its scale dependence differs from that of the standard local, equilateral, and enfolded primordial non-Gaussianity templates.

authors.name: Mariam Abdelaziz, Pritha Bari, Sabino Matarrese, Angelo Ricciardone

papers.title: Suppression of star formation at the centre of barred AGN galaxies
papers.summary: We measured the Concentration (C) index of H\alpha and CO (J = 2-1) in 17 nearby star-forming galaxies from the PHANGS survey. We have found four barred spiral galaxies with a C(H\alpha)/C(CO) ratio of ~ 0.3-0.4, while the other 13 galaxies exhibit ratios of ~ 1 (range from 0.7 to 1.3). All four barred galaxies with low ratios host active galactic nuclei (AGNs), consistent with a scenario in which star formation is suppressed by mechanical and radiative feedback from the AGN. Therefore, negative feedback is effective in these four barred galaxies with a low molecular gas mass fraction (< 0.1), even when AGN activity is relatively weak. The formation of bar structures causes molecular gas to collect in the central region, leading to starburst activity. However, after the starburst, the remaining gas becomes inefficient for star formation rapidly due to AGN feedback. It can mean the quenching process occurs more rapidly in AGN-barred galaxies. Furthermore, since gas remains in the central region, AGN activity is likely to continue. These quenching processes are a unique mechanism found in barred spiral galaxies and are essential to understanding galaxy evolution.

authors.name: Takashi Yamamoto, Nario Kuno, Daisuke Iono, Takuya Hashimoto, Sophia K. Stuber, Daizhong Liu, Thomas G. Williams, Akio K. Inoue

papers.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
papers.summary: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.

authors.name: Bo-An Chen, Bei You, Giovanni Miniutti, Ning Jiang, Zhen Pan, Tao Yang, Xi-Long Fan, Kai Liao, Xu-Heng Ding, Zong-Hong Zhu, Shuai-Kang Yang, Sai-En Xu, Han He, Xiao Fan

papers.title: HERMES: HiERarchical Modelling for Exoplanet Science
papers.summary: ESA's Ariel Space Mission will characterise the atmospheres of approximately 1000 exoplanets to quantify population-level trends. We present HERMES (HiERarchical Modelling for Exoplanet Science), a multidimensional Bayesian framework that probes population-level correlations across multiple axes of diversity. The specific use case we present is the multidimensional relation between stellar metallicity, planetary mass, and atmospheric metallicity. Starting from the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample, we select confirmed planets with available masses and stellar metallicity, inject plausible multidimensional trends and demonstrate successful parameter recovery. Simulated surveys are generated with a variety of leverage and sample size, in the presence of intrinsic astrophysical scatter and measurement noise. By fitting independent Bayesian models to each survey, we confirm that survey leverage remains a reliable predictor of trend precision even in multiple dimensions and in the presence of intrinsic astrophysical scatter. For an Ariel Tier 2 transit survey of at least 400 planets, HERMES robustly recovers the correlation between stellar and planetary metallicity despite intrinsic scatter in planetary abundances as large as 1.2 dex. These results establish HERMES as a practical tool for survey design and science yield forecasting in preparation for Ariel and other surveys probing population-level trends.

authors.name: Wasi M. F. Naqvi, Nicolas B. Cowan

papers.title: The Doppler effect of the Milky Way rotation on mHz gravitational waves
papers.summary: We model the stellar density and the rotation curve of the Milky Way and compute the gravitational-wave spectrum of its unresolved binaries as a function of direction. Because the Galaxy rotates, the waves emitted along each line of sight are Doppler-shifted by a different amount, and we derive for the first time the resulting observed anisotropic spectrum, which no longer factorizes into a spectral shape times an angular template. We then quantify the observability of this distortion with space-based interferometers. With their nominal noise budgets, neither LISA nor a LISA+Taiji network can detect it: the residual between the models that include and neglect the rotation has a signal-to-noise ratio ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq0.2$ and $0.7$ after two years, and the induced bias on the foreground parameters stays below $0.1\sigma$. A tenfold better noise amplitude, of the order contemplated for post-LISA concepts, raises the residual to ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq4.6$ for the network, where the effect becomes measurable and displaces the spectral cutoff by half of the statistical error.

authors.name: Giorgio Mentasti, Quentin Baghi

papers.title: The Incidence of Large Ionized Bubbles at Redshift 13
papers.summary: Ionized bubbles around the first galaxies connect early galaxy growth, ionizing photon escape, intergalactic-medium topology, Ly$\alpha$ visibility, 21~cm structure, and reionization timing. We model the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at $z\approx 13$ using JWST UV luminosity functions, taking the Ly$\alpha$ source reported by Witstok et al. as a benchmark for the relevant scale. We quantify regions with comoving radius $R\ge 2.5$~cMpc through their sky surface density $\Sigma_{\ge 2.5}$. For our continuously active fiducial case, using the Donnan et al. UVLF with $f_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.2$, $\log\xi_{\mathrm{ion}}=25.5$, $f_{\mathrm{active}}=1$, and $C=3$, we find $\Sigma_{\ge 2.5}\simeq 8.10\times 10^{-3}$ arcmin$^{-2}$ per $\Delta z=1$. For $f_{\rm active}=0.2$ or $f_{\rm time}=0.2$ with 10~Myr mean on-times, the incidence falls by factors of 4.1 and 2.9, respectively; longer correlated episodes strengthen the tail. Merging overlapping spheres raises the fiducial incidence by $9.5\%$. The simulations show that Witstok-sized regions can arise in UVLF-calibrated galaxy-driven models. This is a population-level statement, and the specific Witstok source may still require unusual effective ionizing efficiency, recent fading or burstiness, or a non-stellar ionizing contribution.

authors.name: Peter Ziwei Hu, Massimo Stiavelli, Colin Norman

papers.title: First measurement of narrow-line flux ratios for a lensed quasar with JWST/NIRSpec IFS
papers.summary: Strong gravitational lensing is a powerful probe of dark matter (DM) structure on subgalactic scales: in particular, statistics of flux-ratio anomalies (discrepancies between mass model predictions and observed flux ratios) in quadruply imaged quasars are sensitive to perturbations by low-mass DM halos down to $\sim 10^6 M_\odot$. Studies leveraging these anomalies require high-quality flux-ratio measurements from an emission region insensitive to stellar microlensing. In this paper, we present the first measurement of narrow-line flux ratios for a gravitationally lensed quasar using JWST/NIRSpec with Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS), targeting the well-studied system RXJ1131$-$1231. Flux ratios are extracted from the [S III] 9071/9533 $\r{A}$ narrow-line doublet - the first use of this doublet for substructure studies - by performing a full lens model reconstruction to isolate the unresolved nuclear emission from extended narrow-line emission. The resulting spectra are jointly modeled using $\texttt{lensqso-specfit}$, a publicly available software package introduced in this work for the simultaneous spectral fitting of multiple lensed quasar images. We achieve $\sim$ 5% uncertainties on the flux ratios, comparable to the precision of JWST/MIRI warm dust measurements, and detect a clear anomaly in the cusp images relative to a standard smooth lens model. Our results are in good agreement with previous narrow-line measurements and broadly consistent with JWST/MIRI warm dust flux ratios, with marginal ($\sim 2-3\sigma$) deviations. We illustrate how such shifts between differently sized emission regions may be enhanced by small ($\sim 10$ pc) spatial offsets. Our method is generalizable to other systems with existing or future IFS observations, and the combination of narrow-line and warm dust flux ratios offers a new avenue for improving DM constraints with flux-ratio anomaly statistics.

authors.name: Hadrien Paugnat, Tommaso Treu, Anna M. Nierenberg, Anowar J. Shajib, Shawn Knabel, Daniel Gilman

papers.title: Signatures of Periodic Dissipation in Warm Inflation: Power Spectrum, Non-Gaussianity, Gravitational Waves and Primordial Black Holes
papers.summary: In warm inflation the inflaton loses energy to a hot bath of radiation, and this loss acts as a friction on its motion. If the couplings behind the friction depend periodically on the inflaton, as an approximate shift symmetry allows, the friction rises and falls as the field rolls. We study what this does to the primordial fluctuations, following the coupled fluctuations of the inflaton, the radiation and the metric on a plateau potential. The scales seen in the cosmic microwave background are unaffected, because the friction is negligible when they leave the horizon, and the model gives $n_s\simeq0.964$ and $r\simeq5\times10^{-3}$; reshaping the plateau there raises $n_s$ to $0.974$ without changing the rest. On smaller scales, where the friction stays strong for several e-folds, its oscillation leaves a regular, log-periodic ripple on the power spectrum, a comb that changes the power by about 34 percent. The size of the comb depends on how the coupled system responds to a friction that varies in time. We measure this response directly and find that it predicts the comb to within 7 percent across five versions of the model. The comb also appears in the three-point function, which oscillates with it, and in the gravitational waves induced by the enhanced fluctuations between $0.2$~Hz and $0.9$~kHz, where an idealized detector of the BBO class could resolve it with a signal-to-noise ratio of 6--16 if the foreground from neutron-star binaries is removed. A separate, localized rise of the friction gives a peak in the spectrum that, for a tuned height, produces asteroid-mass primordial black holes making up a large share of the dark matter, together with induced gravitational waves near $19$~mHz.

authors.name: Mayukh R. Gangopadhyay

papers.title: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
papers.summary: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Pseudo Double-Source Plane Lenses (PDSPLs): pairs of independent single-source plane lenses with self-similar deflectors. This generalizes the DSPL formalism to the $\sim 10^5$ galaxy-galaxy lenses expected from LSST, Euclid, and Roman. Unlike true DSPLs, PDSPLs are free from the intermediate source mass problem by construction, eliminating the associated secondary MSD and the need for multi-plane ray tracing. We incorporate the deflector MSD into a hierarchical population model to forecast dark energy constraints in Flat $w_0w_a$CDM, showing that MSD severely degrades constraints from small DSPL samples and motivates our PDSPL statistical approach. Assuming unbiased Gaussian photo-z errors of $\sigma_z/(1+z)=0.03$, the mock LSST Y10 photometric sample yields $\sigma(w_0)\sim0.45$, constraining the population-mean MSD parameter and deflector power-law slope to $\sim2\%$. A prior $\Omega_m\sim\mathcal{N}(0.3,0.05)$, representing combination with external cosmological probes such as CMB, BAO, or SNe Ia, improves this to $\sigma(w_0)\sim0.29$, comparable to Stage III weak lensing. The statistical advantage over smaller spectroscopic subsets (e.g., 4MOST) assumes unbiased photo-zs. Real-data use requires spectroscopic photo-z calibration and validation of how paired deflectors' mass-profile differences affect Einstein-radius ratios.

authors.name: Paras Sharma, Simon Birrer, Narayan Khadka, Timo Anguita, Adam Bolton, Sydney Erickson, Phil Holloway, Tian Li, Phil Marshall, Dieu D. Nguyen, Graham P. Smith, Crescenzo Tortora, Bryce Wedig, the Strong Lensing Science Collaboration, the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for the Ly$\alpha$ Forest: CNN-Based Absorber Detection and Characterization
papers.summary: The Ly$\alpha$ forest is a powerful probe of the intergalactic medium and small-scale matter distribution, but deriving absorber properties traditionally requires computationally expensive Voigt-profile fitting. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN) that identifies and characterizes H I Ly$\alpha$ absorbers directly from quasar spectra. The model is trained on synthetic spectra generated from the IllustrisTNG simulation and fitted with the VIPER Voigt-profile fitting code to provide training labels. The network simultaneously predicts absorber presence, column density ($N_{\rm HI}$), Doppler parameter ($b_{\rm HI}$), and line centroid. On simulated spectra, the CNN reproduces the viper reference catalogue with an F1 score of $\sim$0.8, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.18 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.10 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. It reproduces the H I column density distribution function and the $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ relation obtained from viper, recovering similar CDDF slopes and a lower-envelope relation with an RMS difference of only 0.36 km s$^{-1}$. Applied to UVES spectra, performance decreases to an F1 score of $\sim$0.5, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.35 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.22 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. Latent-space analysis reveals a significant domain shift between the simulated and UVES spectra, contributing to the reduced performance. Nevertheless, the CNN reproduces the observed CDDF and $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ distributions obtained from the viper catalogue, yielding CDDF slopes consistent with VIPER and a lower-envelope RMS difference of 3.20 km s$^{-1}$ relative to viper. Monte Carlo dropout is implemented during inference to quantify predictive uncertainties. Together with its computational efficiency, the method provides a scalable and uncertainty-aware framework for Ly$\alpha$ forest analysis in upcoming spectroscopic surveys.

authors.name: Paryag Sharma, Vikram Khaire, Ting-Yun Cheng, Hum Chand, Prakash Gaikwad

papers.title: Anisotropic separate universe : Long-wavelength perturbations and conserved quantities
papers.summary: We study the superhorizon evolution of linear perturbations in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe with a scalar field coupled to a U(1) gauge field. The analysis employs the spatial gradient expansion in the uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ gauge, in which the local number of $e$-folds is unperturbed. In this gauge, the complete set of leading-order long-wavelength solutions, including both even- and odd-parity perturbations, can be constructed from variations of homogeneous Bianchi type I solutions, subject to the momentum and Gauss constraints. The conserved Wronskian found in isotropic multi-field inflation is generalized to the anisotropic system. Together with the shear and electric-flux integration constants, it allows the curvature perturbation on uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ hypersurfaces to be expressed in terms of background variations and time integrals. The conserved comoving curvature perturbations are then obtained by adding this intrinsic curvature contribution to the familiar $\delta N$ contribution arising from the change of time slicing. We also derive a relation between the curvature perturbation and a metric perturbation that reduces to the plus-polarized tensor mode in the isotropic limit, and discuss a nonlinear extension of the formalism.

authors.name: Daiki Saito, Atsushi Naruko

papers.title: Mean-field interpretation of star-in-a-box simulations of red giants
papers.summary: Context: The origin of magnetic fields and the dynamo mechanism in red giants are still not fully understood. Aims: We aim to interpret the dynamo behaviour of global 3D simulations of red giants using mean-field dynamo models. Methods: We use mean-field models constrained by the differential rotation profile extracted from 3D simulations. We perform $\alpha^2$, $\alpha\Omega$, and $\alpha^2\Omega$ mean-field dynamo simulations, varying the strength of the $\alpha$ effect and the differential rotation. Results: The mean-field models can reproduce the growth rate of several 3D runs. The morphology of the large-scale magnetic field is better reproduced for the slowly rotating 3D cases than for the rapidly rotating ones. Faster rotation enhances dynamo action and it also modifies the dominant mode of the dynamo. Rapidly rotating 3D runs produce predominantly non-axisymmetric equatorial dipoles instead of axisymmetric fields at slower rotation. Mean-field models are supercritical even in the absence of differential rotation, indicating $\alpha^2$ dynamo action. By contrast, models using the $\alpha\Omega$ approximation require sufficiently strong differential rotation to become supercritical. Conclusions: Our results suggest that the magnetic field in red giants requires dynamo action. In our mean-field runs, differential rotation speeds up the magnetic decay, disfavouring the idea of a persistent fossil magnetic field in red giants as the explanation for the observed surface fields.

authors.name: Carolina A. Ortiz-Rodr\'iguez, Axel Brandenburg, Petri J. K\"apyl\"a

papers.title: Beyond Spin: QCD Magnetars
papers.summary: We present a unified framework in which anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs), soft gamma-ray repeaters (SGRs), superluminous supernovae (SLSNe-I), luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), and fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from quark deconfinement in the core of a massive neutron star (NS). Spontaneous ferromagnetism in the deconfined phase generates ~10^18 G core fields, producing a highly magnetized hybrid star (HS) -- the ``QCD magnetar'' -- whose surface field is set by NS mass, not birth spin. The Quark-Nova (QN) that forms the HS ejects ~ 0.01M_sun of neutron-rich outer layers, powering a kilonova and leaving the HS crustless for centuries. During this phase, magnetic instabilities at the hadron--quark interface release rising flux ropes that power X-ray-quiet FRBs; as the crust reforms, the source evolves into an X-ray-loud AXP&SGR. Two parameters govern the model: a critical mass M_dec triggering deconfinement, and a critical period P_fast separating fast and slow rotators. Fast rotators inject spin-down energy into the QN ejecta, producing an LFBOT -- directly observable once the SN ejecta is optically thin, or via binary accretion with no preceding SN; otherwise the LFBOT is reprocessed by the SN ejecta into an SLSN-I. A Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis reproduces the observed rates of AXPs\&SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~ 2.1M_sun and P_fast ~ 5.5 ms, and predicts non-merger r-process signatures and kilonovae from isolated NSs, with or without an LFBOT. The QN ejecta also carries its own DM and RM, independent of environment, predicted to appear as excess dispersion and rotation measure in FRBs in addition to the Galactic, host, and intergalactic contributions. These provide direct observational tests of the hadron--quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

authors.name: Rachid Ouyed (Department of Physics,Astronomy, University of Calgary, Alberta, Canada)

papers.title: Comparison of the Neutron Star Birth Function from Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations with Observations
papers.summary: Using the mapping between progenitor core structure and the gravitational mass of neutron stars derived from sophisticated 3D supernova simulations, we construct the theoretical mass distribution of neutron stars at birth and investigate how it might comport with neutron star mass function measurements. In the process, we explore the effects of islands of black hole formation and subsequent mass accretion. We show that supernova theory can explain the observed neutron star mass function from its lower-mass peak near $\sim$1.35 $M_{\odot}$ to its higher-mass tail. Moreover, we suggest, but do not prove, that the lower predicted kick speeds expected during the birth of lower-mass neutron stars and the higher expected kick speeds expected on average for higher mass neutron stars may together sculpt the observed mass function in desired directions. The upshot of all these influences is to imprint upon the measured neutron star mass function features that reflect the varied physics of both neutron star origins and the neutron-star/black-hole dichotomy. Very approximately, we derive a black hole birth fraction of $\sim$19.6\%. In summary, we suggest that supernova theory can now be used to explain, however provisionally, various measured attributes of the population of compact objects and that an era of productive engagement between supernova theory and observation is at hand.

authors.name: Waly M Z Karim, Adam Burrows, David Vartanyan, Anthony Fisher, James Burry

papers.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Passband Measurements with an Analysis of Systematic Errors
papers.summary: We present measurements of the spectral response of the four Advanced ACTPol (AdvACT) multichroic detector arrays, which observed in frequency bands centered near 30, 40, 90, 150, and 220 GHz. The passbands were measured with a Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS) combined with coupling optics that direct and match the output of the FTS to the AdvACT receiver. We perform optical simulations of the FTS and coupling optics in order to model frequency-dependent systematic effects in this system, examining the systematics of each individual measurement component in detail. We use these simulations to apply corrections to the measurements and evaluate the remaining systematic uncertainty. We combine these systematic estimates with statistical errors to determine the measured passbands and their uncertainties from our FTS measurement, which are typically $0.75$ to $1.5\%$ per detector array for the central frequency. We present the passband characteristics for all measurements made by ACT in a common framework. Additionally, we discuss in detail limits set by the systematics in our measurements as well as ways to minimize the systematics of each component to improve passband measurements in the future.

authors.name: Thomas Alford, Rahul Datta, Erminia Calabrese, Steve K. Choi, Shannon M. Duff, Adriaan J. Duivenvoorden, Rolando D\"unner, Joseph Golec, Matthew Hasselfeld, J. Colin Hill, Johannes Hubmayr, Jeffrey McMahon, Michael D. Niemack, Lyman A. Page, Suzanne T. Staggs, Alex Thomas, Cristian Vargas, Yuhan Wang, Edward J. Wollack

papers.title: AI-Assisted Extraction of Follow-up Observations from GCN Circulars in Astro-COLIBRI
papers.summary: We present a new Astro-COLIBRI component that converts free-text GCN Circulars into structured, event-linked follow-up records and combines them with reports submitted directly by the community. A continuously running listener associates new Circulars with transient events, applies deterministic pre-analysis, and invokes a schema-constrained large language model to extract photometry, contacts, redshifts, and related metadata. The records are normalized into a common event-level database and exposed through the web and mobile interfaces as report summaries, contact tools, optical-afterglow context figures, and downloadable CSV or VOTable products. All 1,775 Circulars of an operational evaluation corpus covering the first half of 2026 completed the workflow without failures. An internal human audit of 210 Circulars found 223 of 231 assessed reports (96.5%) fully confirmed, each of the eight remaining ones containing at least one incorrect field, predominantly associated with observation timing and facility attribution. Extracted redshifts agree with three published compilations for 91.7 to 99.3% of the events they share, every disagreement tracing to a limit, a candidate-host estimate, or a later-refined value rather than to a misread Circular. The extraction also recovers 90 to 97% of the redshifts those compilations list for bursts it processed. Applied to the GCN archive since 2016, the pipeline yields 68,393 observations from 26,811 reports across 5,787 transient events, and now runs in real time on new Circulars. The reusable parsing and normalization pipeline is released as the open-source Python package astro-colibri-circular-parser.

authors.name: Fabian Sch\"ussler, S. Bisero, M. Cellier, A. Ciric, B. Cornejo, I. Jaroschewski, A. Kaan Alkan, W. Kiendr\'eb\'eogo, A. Saint-Paul

papers.title: The Road to Normalcy: Environment-Driven Evolutionary Pathways for Primordial Black Holes
papers.summary: We investigate how cosmological environment regulates the evolution of primordial black hole (PBH) seeds in the early universe using a suite of hydrodynamical simulations. PBHs, formed during the radiation dominated epoch, offer a possible source of early BH seeds that does not require prior star formation. We find that PBHs follow distinct evolutionary pathways depending on the gas supply and halo assembly history. In underdense regions, limited inflow suppresses both accretion and star formation, producing faint, metal-poor systems, while in overdense environments, sustained gas inflow drives rapid BH growth and the formation of compact, centrally concentrated stellar components. These differences lead to large variations in BH-to-stellar mass ratio, metallicity, and morphology, collectively bracketing a range of possible evolutionary pathways for PBH-seeded systems. Some pathways pass through a phase with compact stellar structure and elevated BH-to-stellar mass ratio that resembles observed Little Red Dots, before evolving into more extended galaxy--AGN systems. Our results suggest that both the initial seed properties and cosmological environment jointly shape early BH--galaxy co-evolution, while subsequent environmental regulation can erase the memory of the initial seeding channel.

authors.name: Saiyang Zhang, Junehyoung Jeon, Boyuan Liu, Volker Bromm, Priyamvada Natarajan

papers.title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
papers.summary: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of $\sim$0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on relatively shallow photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 131 spectra of red giant and red clump stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure $\rm [Fe/H]=-0.63\pm0.03\,$dex, $\overline{v_{los}} = 50.8^{+0.8}_{-0.7}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$, and $\sigma_v = 3.3^{+1.4}_{-1.9}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a $\sim$3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius ($R_h=8.8^{+1.1}_{-1.3}\,$pc), a small flattening ($e<0.26$, 68\% upper limit), and low luminosity ($M_V = -5.0 \pm 0.4$). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique GC system.

authors.name: Chiara Crociati, Annette M. N. Ferguson, Raffaele Pascale, Sebastian Kamann, Silvia Martocchia, Jess M. Howell, Pete B. Kuzma, Dougal Mackey, Sakurako Okamoto, Masato Onodera

papers.title: JWST/NIRSpec Reveals Diverse Nuclear Environments in Dwarf Galaxies Hosting AGN
papers.summary: Dwarf galaxies, in the $\Lambda$CDM framework, are expected to dominate the galaxy number density at all redshifts. As such, studying AGN in these systems, including characterizing their local environments and emission properties, is essential in obtaining a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their influence on their host galaxy. To this end, we present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M$_\star<$10$^{9.5}\;$M$_\odot$) with evidence of AGN activity. Utilizing the improvements in resolution and sensitivity offered by JWST, we investigate the emission features of the central kiloparsec of these dwarfs. Our findings include the detection of over 100 emission lines across our sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials greater than 300 eV. The nuclear spectra show diverse emission features. In two galaxies, we measure strong contributions from hot dust to the infrared continuum. We also detect both PAH and coronal line emission within 100 parsecs of the nuclei in three galaxies. We estimate the hot H$_2$ gas mass to be between 1--20 M$_\odot$ within 300 pc across our sample, where both thermal and non-thermal excitation are involved. Lastly, spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures across all observed gas phases, ranging from radial symmetry around the nucleus to elongated plumes. Kinematic maps also show each galaxy has unique velocity structures despite all being isolated, affirming the diversity of rotation curves problem, a long standing tension between simulations and observations. These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments that can be found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN.

authors.name: Thomas Bohn, Archana Aravindan, Gabriela Canalizo, Aditya Togi, Shobita Satyapal, Tohru Nagao, Matthew Malkan, Thomas S. Y. Lai, Hanae Inami, Weizhe Liu, Marina Bianchin, Tanio Diaz-Santos, Aaron Evans, Sean T. Linden, Vivian U, Lee Armus, Loreto Barcos-Munoz, Kirsten Larson, Yiqing Song, Sabrina Stierwalt, Jason Surace

papers.title: Beyond Pebble Isolation: Diverse Pathways to Giant Planet Formation Across Stellar and Orbital Scales
papers.summary: Context. Giant planet formation requires reaching crossover mass, i.e., when the mass of the gaseous envelope becomes equal to the mass of the core, within the disc's lifetime. The formation process depends critically on the orbital distance and stellar mass. Aims. We simulate planet formation via pebble accretion up to crossover mass around stellar hosts with masses of 0.1-1.5 M_Sun considering a range of formation locations, with and without Type I migration. Methods. We use a modified version of MESA that couples pebble accretion, gas accretion, and disc evolution. Results. We find that cold/warm Jupiters form, whereas in-situ formation fails at short orbital separations: viscous heating raises the isolation mass enough to assemble adequate cores, but the accompanying high disc temperature prevents cooling and suppresses gas giant formation. This supports migration-based explanations for the origin of hot Jupiters. At large orbital distances, crossover can be reached before pebble isolation mass. This is possible due to efficient envelope contraction in the cold, low-opacity outer disc. Inferred core masses at crossover range between about 1 and 20 M_Earth. Conclusions.
