We further discuss other applications to information-theoretic tasks, including quantum communication, quantum state merging, and the algorithmic implementation of the Petz recovery map, providing a comprehensive evaluation of their computational costs.

authors.name: Takeru Utsumi, Yoshifumi Nakata, Qisheng Wang, Ryuji Takagi

papers.title: Probabilistic perfect pure quantum state transfer via state restoring and ancilla measurement
papers.summary: We propose the protocol for the probabilistic perfect state transfer of an arbitrary multiqubit pure quantum state along the spin-1/2 chain governed by the Hamiltonian preserving the excitation number in the system. We show that the multiqubit $k$-excitation pure sender's state can be restored at the receiver using only the local transformations over the qubits of the extended receiver. The restored state appears in the superposition with other states which form garbage. This garbage can be easily removed by including the ancilla, whose state labels the garbage, and then measuring the ancilla state with desired output. The resulting state of the receiver coincides with the initial sender's state. Then, to transfer an arbitrary multiqubit pure state of some system $S^{(0)}$, we encode this state into the $k$-excitation state of the sender, transfer and restore this state and finally decode the restored $k$-excitation state of the receiver into the state of another subsystem $R^{(0)}$. After labeling and removing the garbage via the ancilla-state measuring with certain success probability we complete the algorithm for the probabilistic perfect transfer of an arbitrary pure state.

authors.name: E. B. Fel'dman, J. Wu, A. I. Zenchuk

papers.title: Adversarial Thermodynamics
papers.summary: In thermodynamics, an agent's ability to extract work is fundamentally constrained by their environment. Traditional frameworks struggle to capture how strategic decision-making under uncertainty, particularly an agent's tolerance for risk, determines the trade-off between extractable work and probability of success in finite-scale experiments. Here, we develop a framework for nonequilibrium thermodynamics based on adversarial resource theories, in which work extraction is modeled as an adversarial game for an agent extracting work. Within this perspective, we consider a Szilard-type engine as a game isomorphic to Kelly gambling, an information-theoretic model of optimal betting under uncertainty -- but with a thermodynamic utility function. Extending the framework to finite-size regimes, we apply a risk-reward trade-off to find an interpretation of the Renyi divergences in terms of extractable work for a given failure probability. By incorporating risk sensitivity via utility functions, we show that the guaranteed amount of work a rational agent would accept instead of undertaking a risky protocol is given by a Renyi divergence. This provides a unified picture of thermodynamics and gambling, and highlights how generalized free energies emerge from an adversarial setup.

authors.name: Maite Arcos, Philippe Faist, Takahiro Sagawa, Jonathan Oppenheim

papers.title: Hybridized-Mode Parametric Amplifier in Kinetic-Inductance Circuits
papers.summary: Parametric amplification is essential for quantum measurement, enabling the amplification of weak microwave signals with minimal added noise. While Josephson-junction-based amplifiers have become standard in superconducting quantum circuits, their magnetic sensitivity, limited saturation power, and sub-kelvin operating requirements motivate the development of alternative nonlinear platforms. Here we demonstrate a two-mode kinetic-inductance parametric amplifier based on a pair of capacitively coupled Kerr-nonlinear resonators fabricated from NbTiN and NbN thin films. The distributed Kerr nonlinearity of these materials enables nondegenerate four-wave-mixing amplification with gains approaching 40 dB, gain-bandwidth products up to 6.9 MHz, and 1-dB compression powers two to three orders of magnitude higher than those of state-of-the-art Josephson amplifiers. A coupled-mode theoretical model accurately captures the pump-induced modification of the hybridized modes and quantitatively reproduces the observed signal and idler responses. The NbN device exhibits a significantly larger Kerr coefficient and superior gain-bandwidth performance, highlighting the advantages of high-kinetic-inductance materials. Our results establish coupled kinetic-inductance resonators as a robust platform for broadband, high-power, and magnetically resilient quantum-limited amplification, offering a scalable route for advanced readout in superconducting qubits, spin ensembles, quantum dots, and other microwave-quantum technologies.

authors.name: Danial Davoudi, Abdul Mohamed, Shabir Barzanjeh

papers.title: Single-LED-pumped, room-temperature, solid-state maser
papers.summary: Optically-pumped, solid-state (OPSS) masers show promise as quantum sensors, oscillators, and amplifiers -even when operating at room temperature. Here we show that the brightness (i.e., the luminance emitted at the surface) of a light-emitting diode (LED) is sufficient to pump such a maser above threshold. Specifically, we demonstrate pulsed maser oscillation in a microwave cavity at room temperature containing a crystal of pentacene-doped para-terphenyl (ptc:ptp) pumped by a single, commercial, chip-scale LED emitting green-yellow light. The LED is driven by discharging a physically small, low-voltage capacitor, resulting in a bench-top maser that is more compact, and a good deal cheaper to make, than existing embodiments. The ptc:ptp crystal is pumped invasively through a fused-quartz waveguide whose outputting facets are shaped like the tip of a spear. An alternative butt-coupled geometry was also tried but failed to mase. Towards explaining our results, the established mean-field formula for a maser's cooperativity is extended to account for a spatially varying optical pump intensity (thus excitation rate) across a spatially varying a.c. magnetic field B(r) (of the cavity's TE_01delta maser mode). This extension leads to a dimensionless figure of merit, we call the ``strike fraction'' (appearing as a factor in the cooperativity), that quantifies how well the applied optical pump targets those regions of the maser crystal where B(r) is strongest. We go on to show how, provided the spatial profile of B(r) is known (through electromagnetic FEM-based simulation), the strike fraction can be straightforwardedly estimated, via Monte Carlo integration, from the data set of an optical ray-tracing simulation of the pump light. These developments allow a Tavis-Cummings-like model (master equation), encompassing terms up to 2nd-order in quantum cumulants, to simulate the process of masing.

authors.name: Michael Newns, Shirley Xu, Mingyang Liu, Yifan Yu, Zike Cheng, Vanessa Ussalim, Zitong Qin, Ziqiu Huang, Max Attwood, Mark Oxborrow

papers.title: Reversing Heat Flow by Coherence in a Multipartite Quantum System
papers.summary: The second law of thermodynamics dictates that heat flows spontaneously from a high-temperature entity to a lower-temperature one. Yet, recent advances have demonstrated that quantum correlations between a system and its thermal environment can induce a reversal of heat flow, challenging classical thermodynamic expectations. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that internal quantum coherence in a multipartite spin system can also reverse heat flow, without relying on correlations with the environment. Under the collision model with cascade interaction, we verify that both the strength and the phase of the coherence term determine the direction and magnitude of energy transfer.These results enable precise control of heat flow using only local quantum properties.

authors.name: Keyi Huang, Qi Zhang, Xiangjing Liu, Ruiqing Li, Xinyue Long, Hongfeng Liu, Xiangyu Wang, Yu-ang Fan, Yuxuan Zheng, Yufang Feng, Yu Zhou, Jack Ng, Xinfang Nie, Zhong-Xiao Man, Dawei Lu

papers.title: Stochastic phase-space simulation of multimode cat states via the positive-P representation
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of the transient dynamics of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states in dissipatively coupled resonator arrays using the positive-P phase-space method. By employing the positive-P representation, we derive the exact stochastic differential equations governing the system's dynamics, enabling the simulation of system sizes significantly larger than those accessible via direct master equation simulation. We demonstrate the utility of this method by simulating transient dynamics for networks up to N=21 sites. Furthermore, we critically examine the method's usefulness and limitations, specifically highlighting the computational instability encountered when estimating the state parity in the systems. Our results provide a pathway for scalable simulations of non-Gaussian states in large open quantum systems.

authors.name: Yi Shi, Alex Ferrier, Piotr Deuar, Eran Ginossar, Marzena Szymanska

papers.title: Ground state and persistent oscillations in the quantum East model
papers.summary: For the 1D quantum East model with open boundary and no global conserved charge, we show that in the limit $s \to -\infty$, the ground state is approximately captured by a simple spin-polarized product state. The polarization angle changes as we approach the quantum phase transition at $s = 0$ where the ground state becomes an exact product state polarized along the X-axis. For $s \to -\infty$, we further identify a low-entanglement excited eigenstate that differs from the ground state only by a $\pi$-rotation of the first spin and is well approximated by a spin-coherent state. For $-1\lesssim s<0$, this spin-coherent state overlaps mainly with two eigenstates separated by a system size-independent energy gap, leading to long-lived coherent oscillations of local observables near the edge. These oscillations originate from boundary physics and are distinct from quantum many-body scars and hypercube-like Fock-space mechanisms.

authors.name: Adway Kumar Das, Achilleas Lazarides

papers.title: The stabilizer ground state and applications to quantum simulation
papers.summary: The stabilizer ground state is the lowest energy stabilizer state with respect to a given Hamiltonian. This is useful in quantum simulation contexts as it allows for a Clifford circuit approximation of a ground state that can be further refined towards the true ground state. However, in many cases it is highly degenerate and does not give a unique stabilizer state. In this paper, we define and investigate methods to prepare the optimal stabilizer ground state (OSGS), which is the stabilizer ground state that has the highest fidelity with the true ground state. We show how the optimal stabilizer ground state may be evaluated by classically selecting the optimal stabilizer group and employing the stabilizer tableaux formalism.We show applications of the OSGS in the context of measurement-based deterministic imaginary time evolution, where it is used as a highly efficient initial state for the evolution towards the true ground state. Candidate commuting subsets are generated from the target Hamiltonian using a genetic search guided by energy evaluations incorporating an inner optimization over generator signs. Once a complete signed generating set is specified, the corresponding state can be efficiently prepared using Clifford gates. Complexity analysis further shows that the algorithm's resource scales polynomially with system dimension, highlighting its efficiency and potential quantum advantage.

authors.name: Yuping Mao, Jiaxing Feng, Yimeng Mao, Tim Byrnes

papers.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
papers.summary: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

authors.name: Faisal Alam, Marcos Crichigno, Elizabeth Crosson, Steven T. Flammia, Filippo Maria Gambetta, Max Hunter Gordon, Michael Kreshchuk, Ashley Montanaro, Alberto Nocera, Raul A. Santos

papers.title: Experimental realization of a $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit
papers.summary: Symmetry-based selection rules make some atomic states remarkably long-lived, a protection superconducting circuits usually lack. We report coherent control and single-shot readout of a 13.6 MHz $\cos 2\varphi$ qubit in the soft-transmon regime. It consists of an island shunted to ground through an interferometer of Josephson junctions and superinductances that favors tunneling of pairs of Cooper pairs, so that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects the qubit from dielectric loss. We measure a qubit charge matrix element over 100 times smaller than that of the circuit's unprotected plasmon transition, placing the dielectric limit on the qubit lifetime above 10 ms. The measured $T_1 = 70\,\mu$s is instead predicted, with no free parameters, by the $1/f$ flux noise in the interferometer loop that limits dephasing ($T_{2\mathrm{E}} = 2.5\,\mu$s). This experiment demonstrates that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects against the dielectric loss it targets, and that the remaining limit is the interferometer's sensitivity to flux noise, which larger superinductances are predicted to reduce without compromising protection.

authors.name: Erwan Roverc'h, Alvise Borgognoni, Marius Villiers, Kyrylo Gerashchenko, W. Clarke Smith, Christopher Wilson, Benoit Dou\c{c}ot, Alexandru Petrescu, Philippe Campagne-Ibarcq, Zaki Leghtas

papers.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
papers.summary: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.

authors.name: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

papers.title: Adaptive Negativity Estimation via Collective Measurements
papers.summary: This paper explores an efficient method for entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit quantum systems based upon the framework of collective measurements in conjunction with machine learning. We introduce an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically adjusted based on prior measurement outcomes aiming to optimize the inference precision given a limited number of these measurement settings. The procedure makes use of the Long Short-Term Memory networks to recurrently process collective measurements on two copies of the investigated states. Obtained results demonstrate the tangible benefits of the adaptive measurements in comparison to previously described non-adaptive strategies.

authors.name: Martin Zeman, Vojt\v{e}ch Tr\'avn\'i\v{c}ek, Anton\'in \v{C}ernoch, Jan Soubusta, Karel Lemr

papers.title: Quantum metrological advantage of high-order squeezed states
papers.summary: Quantum correlations can be harnessed to improve the precision in parameter estimation beyond classical capabilities. Under a standard interferometric or rotation protocol, it is well established that the optimal single-mode Gaussian state is a standard squeezed vacuum, which enables Heisenberg-limited precision. In this work, we investigate the potential metrological advantage of two distinct families involving high-order squeezing, namely, mth-phase and multisqueezed states. Our results show that these non-Gaussian states can grant a significant metrological advantage with respect to the optimal squeezed vacuum under equivalent conditions, i.e., at equal occupations. Their advantage holds at both low and large occupations, but its behavior critically depends on the chosen family of high-order squeezing. While higher squeezing orders enhance the advantage, this comes at the cost of higher-order observables in the measurement for full metrological performance. Finally, we study their robustness to standard decoherence channels, i.e., pure dephasing and zero-temperature damping. Employing standard squeezing as reference state, our results indicate a reasonable robustness against damping up to a certain noise strength, while their metrological advantage becomes fragile under pure dephasing. Our work shows the potential enhancement in quantum metrology beyond Gaussian states, carefully detailing the main challenges and limitations.

authors.name: Rub\'en Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, Ricardo Puebla

papers.title: Spectrum analysis with quantum dynamical systems. II. Finite-time analysis
papers.summary: The prequel to this work [Ng et al., Phys. Rev. A 93, 042121 (2016)] proposes the method of spectral photon counting to enhance noise spectroscopy with an optical interferometer. While the predicted enhancement over homodyne detection is promising, the results there are derived by taking an asymptotic limit of infinite observation time; their validity for a finite time remains unclear. To validate the theory, here we perform a numerical study of a finite-time model. Assuming that the signal is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process with an unknown variance parameter, we evaluate the Fisher information for homodyne detection, a lower bound on the Fisher information for spectral photon counting, and a quantum upper bound, all without taking the infinite-time limit. To confirm that the Fisher-information quantities are satisfactory precision measures, we also compute the errors of the maximum-likelihood estimator by Monte-Carlo simulations. The results demonstrate that the Fisher-information quantities and the estimation errors all smoothly approach their asymptotic limits, and the advantage of spectral photon counting over homodyne detection can remain substantial for finite times.

authors.name: Xinyi Sui, Mankei Tsang

papers.title: Tuning of quantum nanoscaled friction within the Prandtl-Tomlinson model
papers.summary: Nanoscaled is a fundamental tribological phenomenon with complex behavior of its dynamical force. Here, we utilize the Prandtl-Tomlinson framework to investigate systematically the different means of control of the frictional force at the quantum and classical levels. It is found that the frictional dynamics can be controlled by the corrugation and characteristic length ratio parameters dependent upon properties of the nanoparticle-chain system. In addition to the stick-slip regime, other types of motion are uncovered, highlighting the richness of the frictional dynamics. The importance of Landau-Zener tunneling for the quantum motion is also analyzed. These findings provide valuable insights for interpreting experimental observations and controlling quantum frictional behavior in nanoscale systems.

authors.name: Dai-Nam Le, Lilia M. Woods

papers.title: Weak ergodicity breaking captured from short-time dynamcis and graph theory
papers.summary: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.

authors.name: Heiko Georg Menzler, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner

papers.title: Wave packet landscape in open quantum systems
papers.summary: We formulate a landscape theory for the long-time wave packet spreading of free and harmonically trapped particles with quantum fluctuations and its related dissipation. We show that the diffusion, localization, and collapse of wave packets arise from symmetry structures of an underlying landscape in covariance space. The geometry of this landscape determines the asymptotic fate of the wave packet. In the quantum landscape description, the trapping potential and bath fluctuation break the landscape symmetry in distinct ways: the former lifts the valley-like landscape of a fluctuation-free free particle into a bowl-like landscape, leading to collapse, whereas the latter tilts the valley and turns localization into diffusion. The resulting landscape symmetry breaking accounts for the noncommuting long-time limits and abrupt changes in the asymptotic wave-packet width. This establishes landscape symmetry breaking as a unified geometric origin of wave-packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in quantum Brownian motion.

authors.name: Kang Xu, Miao-Miao Yi, Zi-Hong Yan, C. P. Sun

papers.title: Identifiability and endpoint reconstruction of time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from projective trajectory jets
papers.summary: We study the identifiability of smooth time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from phase-resolved Schrodinger trajectories. When the initial state is localized at a chain endpoint, we prove that the projective trajectory jet through order M+1 uniquely determines the first M couplings, their logarithmic time derivatives, and the associated diagonal energy differences at preparation. This derivative order is necessary in the unrestricted real-Jacobi class. If only the first K projective coordinates are observed, even their full Taylor jets leave every deeper instantaneous layer undetermined. We also construct evolutions that are indistinguishable on an observation window separated from preparation but have different endpoint coupling scales and rates. We identify two ways to restore local identifiability: first-order projective and reference-population data at generic times, or second-order data from ceil(M/2) suitable site preparations for independent coupling rates. Statistical distinguishability bounds and finite-window simulations quantify the effects of noise, nuisance coefficients, and acquisition design.

authors.name: A. M. Tishin

papers.title: Measuring Entanglement in Qubit System
papers.summary: An operational way of measuring entanglement in a balanced two-path interferometers is presented, where path information is carried by some internal degree of freedom which, in turn, gets entangled with an ancilla system. The analysis is based on a tripartite description involving paths, an internal qubit degree of freedom, and some ancillary states entangled with the internal degree of freedom. It is then applied to two physically distinct experimental situations: a modified Stern-Gerlach interferometer with spin-1/2 particles and a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with photons carrying polarization. The ancilla degree of freedom may not be experimentally accessible. Tracing out the ancillary system, and employing a quantum erasing procedure based on the internal degree of freedom, it is demonstrated that a concurrence-based measure of the entanglement, between the internal degree of freedom and the ancilla, can be extracted directly from measurable asymmetry of the two output channels. These results show that loss of coherence, quantum erasure, and entanglement estimation in interferometric experiments arise from the same underlying correlation structure and provide a compact experimentally accessible framework for quantifying entanglement in qubit systems.

authors.name: Vignesh S, Tabish Qureshi

papers.title: Quantum Correlation Hierarchy and Teleportation in Dephased Hydrogen Hyperfine System
papers.summary: We study the dynamics of quantum correlations in the hydrogen hyperfine spin system subject to Markovian phase noise. Treating the electron and proton spin degrees of freedom as an open two-qubit system governed by an isotropic hyperfine Hamiltonian and local dephasing, we obtain the exact time-dependent density matrix and derive analytical expressions for the full X-state family. We compute concurrence($C$), trace-distance measurement-induced nonlocality (Trace MIN--$\mathcal{N}_1$), and average steering coherence (ASC) in closed form and establish their strict ordering $ C(t)\leq \mathcal{N}_1(t)\leq \mathrm{ASC}(t) $ at all times. Entanglement is identified as the most fragile resource, undergoing sudden death at a finite time. Trace MIN exhibits dephasing-immune freezing for states with nonzero population imbalance, while ASC is the most robust quantity, persisting longest in every scenario studied.We additionally demonstrate that the dephased thermal hyperfine state serves as a resource for quantum teleportation, deriving a closed-form expression for the average fidelity and establishing that the teleportation advantage window coincides exactly with the entanglement survival interval, $\mathcal{F}_A > 2/3 \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{C} > 0$, for the full X-state family with maximally mixed marginals. We identify four distinct dynamical regimes and map all three correlation measures onto directly measurable Pauli spin correlators, enabling experimental reconstruction of the full hierarchy without full state tomography.

authors.name: Geerthana Thiyagarajan, R. Muthuganesan

papers.title: A Universal Telecom-Band Quantum Memory Enabled by Cross-Phase Modulation
papers.summary: Quantum memories capable of storing and retrieving photonic quantum states on demand are essential for quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and the synchronization of probabilistic quantum processes. All-optical loop-based memories offer broadband operation and compatibility with telecommunication infrastructure, but their performance is often limited by switching losses and the noise introduced by active control mechanisms. Here, we demonstrate a universal all-fiber quantum memory based on two Sagnac interferometers acting as dynamically controlled mirrors through cross-phase modulation. This all-optical switching mechanism enables an input/output transmission as high as 90% (0.46 dB insertion loss), a round-trip transmission of 94.6%, and a characteristic storage lifetime of $18.54 \pm 0.21 \mu s$. The memory exhibits an operational spectral range exceeding 12.5 THz, while keeping noise to negligible levels across the whole telecom C-band. We experimentally demonstrate the preservation of time-bin-encoded heralded photons and time-bin entanglement, as well as compatibility with polarization- and frequency-bin-encoded optical states. Furthermore, we demonstrate the simultaneous storage of over 200 temporal modes and the selective retrieval of independently addressable modes. Our results establish low-noise switching as a promising approach to broadband quantum memories combining high transmission, encoding versatility, and programmable temporal-mode control.

authors.name: Domenico Compagnini, Noemi Tagliavacche, Sara Congia, Andrea Bernardi, Marco Liscidini, Matteo Galli, Daniele Bajoni

papers.title: Graph-Spectral Entanglement
papers.summary: We introduce a unified graph-spectral framework for quantifying multipartite entanglement, built upon an entanglement graph and its associated entanglement matrix. The framework accommodates general subsystem and partition structures of composite quantum systems, while offering a complementary geometric and network perspective on characterizing multipartite quantum correlations. We prove that the resulting graph-spectral entanglement satisfies the requirements of an entanglement measure. Furthermore, we derive a multipartite monogamy relation and, based on the resulting spectral hierarchy, introduce residual graph-spectral entanglement for arbitrary multipartite states. This establishes a general construction of residual entanglement beyond conventional qubit-based formulations and provides a new approach to investigating, quantifying, witnessing, and classifying multipartite entanglement in both theoretical and experimental settings.

authors.name: Vahid Azimi-Mousolou

papers.title: Multi-stage Quantum Amplifier Readout Chain
papers.summary: Multi-stage cryogenic readout chains with a wide bandwidth and added noise within a few quanta of the quantum limit are frequently constructed using traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) as the first stage, and a semiconductor amplifier as the second stage. Unfortunately, for highly-scaled superconducting detector arrays, or quantum information systems, and space-based observatories, the power dissipation of the semiconductor amplifier becomes problematic from the perspective of available cryogenic cooling power near 3 K. Here we demonstrate a readout chain based on a two-stage kinetic inductance TWPA (KTWPA). This quantum-amplifier-based-readout-chain (QARC) provides sufficient gain that a cryogenic semiconductor follow-on amplifier can be eliminated without degradation of the system noise. Due to the ultra-low dissipation of KTWPAs and their higher output-power-to-total-power ratio, the QARC dissipates approximately three orders of magnitude less power than readout chains containing semiconductor amplifiers while adding noise of less than 2 quanta over a 1 GHz bandwidth. In addition, by leveraging the high power handling of kinetic inductance technology, the QARC maintains an input compression point of -93 dBm, which exceeds that of many contemporary Josephson-junction-based parametric amplifiers.

authors.name: Logan Howe, Andrea Giachero, Michael Vissers, Corwin Shiu, Shannon Duff, Jason Austermann, Johannes Hubmayr, Joel Ullom

papers.title: Filon Methods for Highly Oscillatory Controlled Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems is a central challenge in the design and control of quantum computers, but the highly oscillatory dynamics of these systems severely limit the efficiency of standard numerical methods. To address this, we adapt Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals into two numerical methods, called Filon and Controlled Filon, for solving linear systems of ODEs with highly oscillatory solutions. We tailor both methods for efficient implementation in controlled quantum systems, and the Controlled Filon method additionally accounts for the oscillatory structure of the control pulses. We show by numerical experiments that these methods significantly reduce the computational cost of accurately simulating systems of superconducting transmon qubits by decreasing the number of timesteps needed to reach a given level of precision, with only a modest increase in the cost per timestep. For a realistic simulation of the dynamics of a CNOT gate, the Controlled Filon method is the most efficient method tested at every target accuracy, outperforming the best Hermite method by up to 6x and the Hermite method of the same order by up to 500x.

authors.name: Spencer Lee, Daniel Appel\"o

papers.title: No Finite NPA Level Characterizes the Complete Quantum Set in the Simplest Bell Scenario
papers.summary: The Navascu\'es--Pironio--Ac\'in (NPA) hierarchy provides increasingly tighter semidefinite outer approximations to the set of quantum correlations, while its dual programs give sum-of-squares certificates that can establish exact quantum bounds for Bell inequalities and yield self-testing relations. We show that no finite level of the NPA hierarchy can exactly characterize the set of quantum correlations, even in the simplest Bell scenario. For the symmetric doubly tilted CHSH inequality, the maximal quantum violation vanishes cubically as the tilting parameter approaches its critical value, while the error of every fixed NPA level relative to this violation diverges. We construct a family of two-qubit strategies for which the gap between the exact quantum bound and the attained Bell value, divided by the quantum violation, tends to the Motzkin polynomial in rescaled measurement angles. If the relative error remained bounded, the fixed-level NPA certificates would yield a sum-of-squares representation of this limiting polynomial plus a nonnegative constant, which is impossible.

authors.name: Anubhav Chaturvedi

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Metrology for Probing the Unruh Effect with Uniformly Accelerated Two-Level Atoms
papers.summary: We develop a quantum metrological framework for optimizing the probing of the Unruh effect using uniformly accelerated two-level atomic probes. The acceleration-dependent factor generated during the atom--field interaction is encoded in the atomic state and can be estimated through repeated quantum measurements. For a fixed total probe time, which characterizes the available measurement resource, we optimize the interrogation time of individual probes, the initial atomic state, and the corresponding measurement basis to minimize the estimation uncertainty. We show that the achievable precision is governed by the Fisher information accumulated per unit probe time. Under a fixed total probe time, shorter evolution times of individual probes allow for more sequential measurements, leading to a significant improvement in the estimation precision. The optimal initial state depends on both the acceleration factor and the probe evolution time. In particular, the excited state provides superior sensitivity in the weak-acceleration and small probe time regime. Furthermore, we determine the minimum total probe time required to resolve the acceleration-dependent signal associated with the Unruh effect and demonstrate that this requirement can be substantially reduced by employing atomic systems with larger transition dipole moments. Our results establish an optimized quantum metrological strategy for probing acceleration-induced quantum effects and provide a systematic approach toward the experimental investigation of the Unruh effect.

authors.name: Yao Jin

papers.title: High-purity entanglement mediated by magnons despite weak coupling
papers.summary: Entangling distant spins via a shared magnonic bus typically faces a tradeoff: stronger spin-magnon coupling increases the entanglement fidelity, but also the spin decay rate. We propose a protocol that breaks this tradeoff. The magnons couple only to a transition outside the computational basis, in which the Bell state is created. Our protocol is probabilistic, and weak coupling reduces the success probability but not the fidelity. We analyze a setup where the spins are two nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near a magnetic wire. In the absence of NV dephasing, the protocol reaches unit fidelity with a maximally entangled state, for arbitrarily weak coupling. In our simulations via the Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach, the NV-magnon coupling is taken to be one-third of the magnon linewidth. Considering finite NV dephasing, we predict a fidelity of >0.99 for a state-of-the-art rate, and an optimal fidelity of 0.91 for a moderate rate, both at 0.6% success probability.

authors.name: Sanchar Sharma

papers.title: Effect-valued measurement models and contextuality
papers.summary: We generalize the Abramsky--Brandenburger sheaf-theoretic treatment of contextuality by replacing probability distributions with distributions valued in a convex effect algebra \(A\). This yields a notion of \(A\)-valued measurement model encompassing probabilistic, deterministic, and quantum measurement structures within a single framework. States \(\sigma:A\to[0,1]\) induce ordinary empirical models, allowing observable behaviour to be viewed as arising from effect-valued measurement data. This leads to a distinction between internal contextuality of \(A\)-models and observable contextuality after state evaluation. We analyze the relationship between these notions and identify coherence conditions under which observable classical explanations assemble into internal ones. Using the ordered-vector-space representation of effect modules, we show that non-contextuality is characterized by feasibility of an associated cone program, generalizing the linear-programming formulation of contextuality in the probabilistic case. We also introduce an effect-valued contextual fraction and study its relation to observable contextuality witnesses. We show how cone duality leads to a notion of Bell witnesses for contextuality as a direct generalization of Bell inequalities. Finally, we analyze sharp realizability and uniform dilation for measurement models, clarifying the relationship between general POVMs and projective measurements, and show how resource-indexed effect structures induce graded monads generalizing the quantum monad.

authors.name: Samson Abramsky, Lucas Stinchcombe

papers.title: Two-photon interference from as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots under detuned excitation
papers.summary: In this study, we investigate as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots emitting in the third telecommunication window. The investigated quantum dots are embedded directly in an aluminium-free InP matrix without additional barrier material. A large excitation-emission detuning of 32 meV enables efficient suppression of scattered laser light while retaining several advantages of near-resonant excitation. The single-photon nature of the emission is confirmed by a Hanbury Brown and Twiss experiment, yielding a raw second-order autocorrelation value of $g_{\mathrm{raw}}^{(2)}(0)=0.076(6)$. A Hong-Ou-Mandel measurement is used to determine the degree of indistinguishability of single photons and reveals as-measured visibilities of $V=0.038(8)$ and $V=0.108(18)$ for excitation pulse separations of 13.1 ns and 5.3 ns, respectively. We observe finite photon indistinguishability in as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots under detuned quasi-resonant excitation, without deliberate Purcell enhancement.

authors.name: Maja Wasiluk, Anna Musia{\l}, Pawe{\l} Mrowi\'nski, Johann Peter Reithmaier, Mohamed Benyoucef, Wojciech Rudno-Rudzi\'nski

papers.title: SWAP Gate Between Polarization and Time-Bin Qubits on a Single Photon
papers.summary: Multi-degree-of-freedom photonic quantum processing requires coherent routing between qubit encodings on a single photon. We propose a SWAP circuit between polarization and time-bin qubits using polarization-dependent delays and synchronized electro-optic modulation, analyzing phase-calibration, voltage-accuracy, and timing requirements for experimental realization. The architecture follows a three-CNOT SWAP decomposition, using two polarization beam splitter (PBS)--delay--PBS stages to produce polarization-controlled time-bin parity flips. Between these stages, an electro-optic modulator (EOM) driven by a voltage waveform synchronized to a time-bin grid flips polarization in odd bins while leaving even bins unchanged. A final PBS--delay--PBS compensation stage delays the $H$-polarized components by $2\Delta t$, aligning the relevant $H$ and $V$ amplitudes in common output time bins. We describe an infinite grid of repeating early/late time-bin pairs, labelling early bins as even ($\ket{E}$) and late bins as odd ($\ket{O}$). Throughout, we use these even/odd labels without explicit pair indices. A delay of one bin spacing $\Delta t$ moves an even bin to the following odd bin and an odd bin to the following even bin, corresponding to the early slot of the next pair in a traditional early/late encoding. Tracking the polarization and time-bin states through the complete circuit, we establish the resulting SWAP transformation. We identify the optical phase conditions required for coherent operation and discuss their calibration and compensation. We also quantify the effect of EOM voltage errors on polarization-flip probability and present an illustrative timing budget based on switching, detector resolution, and timing jitter.

authors.name: Adam Sultan, Connor Kupchak

papers.title: Quantum fluctuation relations in first-detection processes
papers.summary: We derive three quantum fluctuation relations for systems undergoing repeated projective measurements. These fluctuation relations characterize the work that can be extracted from a quantum device when a first-detection event triggers a mechanical operation leading to positive work production. The correction to the standard quantum Jarzynski equality depends logarithmically on the mean first-detection time for the time-reversed dynamics. Application of Jensen's inequality leads to fundamental limits on both the total work involved in the repeated measurements and final mechanical operation, and the extracted work alone. An analogous inequality is derived for the work performed exclusively during the sequence of repeated projective measurements. The general case of a device connected to an external environment is also considered.

authors.name: A. Imparato

papers.title: Controlled dynamics of a multi-component discrete-time quantum walker
papers.summary: We investigate a discrete-time quantum walk of a three-component quantum particle on a one-dimensional lattice. As coin operators, we employ parameterized rotations generated by the Gell-Mann matrices, which enable systematic tuning of the couplings between the internal components. We analyze how these couplings influence and control the dynamics by systematically exploring the position-space probability distribution across a broad region of the parameter space. To quantify the impact of different inter-component couplings, we further examine the ratio of the mean position to the variance in each half of the lattice. Our results indicates that the system supports a rich variety of transport regimes, ranging from nearly symmetric, rapidly spreading walks to strongly anisotropic dynamics with partial localization. This framework thus provides a new avenue for engineering targeted spreading and trapping behavior in multicomponent discrete-time quantum walks.

authors.name: Vikash Mittal, Tomasz Sowi\'nski

papers.title: The form of dissipation shapes what a quantum reservoir remembers
papers.summary: Dissipation sets how long a quantum reservoir computer remembers its past inputs, and its rate is the usual control. Here we show that its form matters as much, for how a memory is stored, written and read. When the qubits decay independently, stronger loss shortens the memory. When they decay collectively, the quantum Zeno effect holds the system in dark states that do not decay, and stronger loss prolongs the memory. A longer memory is harder to write, because it leaves more time for new inputs to mix with the inputs already stored. We prove that the number of inputs mixed into a stored signal is, on average, the memory lifetime times the fraction of the signal that one input mixes. We also prove that this number stays fixed, however long the memory lasts, when the input amplitude falls as the inverse square root of the lifetime. A weaker input leaves a fainter signal to read out, so the form of the dissipation, the input amplitude and the measurement budget have to be chosen together.

authors.name: Markus Baumann, Itamar Fink, Johannes Wittmann, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien, Jonas Stein

papers.title: Anti-Zeno boost in an autonomous quantized-piston thermal machine
papers.summary: Anti-Zeno enhancement of quantum heat machines has been established for working fluids driven by an external classical field, but whether it can enhance extractable-work accumulation in an autonomously evolving quantized piston remains an important question. Here we study an autonomous thermal machine in which a two-level working fluid is coupled to a quantized harmonic piston and to two spectrally separated reservoirs, without external modulation. We derive a finite-time master equation for the resulting carrier and sideband channels, whose rates interpolate between the Zeno, anti-Zeno, and Markovian regimes as the coupling time is varied. For an initially coherent piston, the machine charges the piston and generates more ergotropy than the Markovian reference in the anti-Zeno window. Reversing the same retained channels turns the device into a finite-resource refrigerator with enhanced cooling. The anti-Zeno effect therefore increases the rate of operation while leaving the underlying carrier and sideband energy ratios unchanged. These channel ratios remain consistent with the usual Carnot bounds over the operating regimes considered here. Our results establish finite-time reservoir sampling as a mechanism for enhancing autonomous thermal-machine operation with a quantized piston.

authors.name: M. Tahir Naseem

papers.title: Dissipative framework for subsystem dynamics of noninteracting quantum chains
papers.summary: When only local observables of a many-body quantum system are of interest, it is desirable to formulate a reduced description within the Hilbert space of the corresponding subsystem, with the remaining degrees of freedom traced out and acting as an environment. Assuming initially uncorrelated states and Gaussian environments, we develop a framework for reconstructing the local dynamical generator of noninteracting quantum chains, with polynomial computational effort. As an application, we consider two representative models: a bipartitioned Kitaev chain and a Kitaev chain boundary-coupled to a fully connected free-fermion environment. In both models, strong subsystem-environment coupling leads to non-Markovian dynamics characterized by ballistic spreading of the Lindblad dissipator support within the subsystem. On the other hand, weak coupling to a fully connected environment yields predominantly boundary-localized, Markovian dissipation. Our work highlights the implications of subsystem-environment correlations on the generator of local dynamics, beyond the conventional weak-coupling approximations.

authors.name: Michele Coppola, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Zala Lenar\v{c}i\v{c}

papers.title: Collective photon echoes in the Tavis-Cummings model: distribution independence, two detuning regimes, and the Dicke ladder
papers.summary: An ensemble of $N$ two-level molecules prepared in its ground state and sharing a lossless cavity with a weak field does not simply absorb: the intensity collapses and then recurs, in a train of collective photon echoes. Working from the exact solution of the Tavis-Cummings model in the few-photon regime $\bar n<N$, we confirm the echo time $\tau_E=4\pi\sqrt{N+\Delta}/g$ at resonance from $N=5$ to $N=400$, and separate it from the alternative $4\pi\sqrt{N-\bar n+\Delta}/g$ by a direct test: the recurrence period is independent of $\bar n$ to $0.8\%$ across a factor of six in $\bar n$, where the alternative predicts shifts of up to $17\%$. The initial state, the ground state, requires no preparation. The echo time is independent of the initial photon distribution - coherent, thermal, squeezed and oscillatory-squeezed distributions with variances from 2 to 34 all recur together - but the echo amplitude is not: it varies at the tens-of-percent level at fixed mean, including a factor of 1.8 with the squeezing phase. Detuning organizes the dynamics into two clean regimes separated by a fragmented crossover; the echo time in the dispersive branch is exactly one-half that of the resonant branch, a factor derived from second-order dispersive perturbation theory with leading correction $5Ng^2/\delta^2$, and sufficient detuning removes the dependence on the initial Dicke state. For arbitrary initial $|r=N/2,m\rangle$, emission replaces absorption at $m\simeq-N/2+\bar n$, and the echo envelope acquires one component per step up the ladder. Lindblad simulations with all loss channels acting simultaneously, and full-Hilbert-space disorder simulations, show the first echoes to be observable at $N\sim5$-$20$ on an existing five-qubit superconducting device: the echo survives cavity decay with contrast $\sim e^{-\kappa\tau_E/2}$, photons being shielded while resident in the emitters.

authors.name: Michael Tavis

papers.title: Reading Convivial Solipsism: Towards a Logic of Perspectival Facts
papers.summary: Convivial Solipsism is easily misunderstood. Because it denies the absoluteness of observed events while preserving the universality of quantum mechanics, it invites objections that are often formulated in a classical, non-perspectival language. Some objections arise from importing assumptions that Convivial Solipsism rejects; others challenge whether those rejections yield an adequate account of observers, communication, and scientific practice. This article distinguishes these two kinds of criticism. In particular, it reconstructs a family of objections that arise in discussions of Convivial Solipsism, especially in connection with Wigner's friend and extended Wigner's friend scenarios. The objections are useful because they identify the conceptual discipline required by any interpretation that takes non-absolute facts seriously. The central claim is that observational facts must be indexed to perspectives. The mistake consists in removing these indices and then treating the resulting expressions as if they belonged to a single global factual domain. This leads to apparent contradictions and to false dilemmas concerning consciousness, communication, other minds, and intersubjectivity. When that is taken into account, it appears that Convivial Solipsism is a discipline of perspectival discourse. The paper also develops an analogy between two restrictions on global descriptions. Quantum contextuality prevents certain families of measurement statistics from being represented within a single noncontextual Kolmogorovian probability model. Likewise, Convivial Solipsism requires a perspectival logic governing the formation and combination of observational statements, while retaining classical reasoning for well-formed indexed propositions. A detailed formalization of the perspectival logic outlined here will be provided in a forthcoming paper.

authors.name: Herve Zwirn

papers.title: From Quantum Cryptography to Intuitionism and beyond: relativity, many-worlds and non-locality
papers.summary: After a recollection of some of my encounters with Gilles Brassard, on the occasion of his 70th birthday I present, first, a new idea on creation of new information at a limited rate. Next, I develop the idea that "indeterminacy is relative" [Entropy {23} 1326 (2021)] and how this illuminates the compatibility between relativity and non-locality.

authors.name: Nicolas Gisin

papers.title: Bottom-Up Design of Quantum Optical Experiments Using Discrete Generative Models
papers.summary: Designing quantum optical experiments requires searching over discrete circuit topologies and continuous parameters, often leading to multiple possible realizations of the same target state. Graph-based methods commonly address this problem by optimizing a dense graph and pruning it toward a single circuit. We introduce \texttt{Grinch}, a bottom-up reward-driven generative framework that learns to sample optical graphs directly from fidelity-based rewards without relying on a pre-existing training dataset. We demonstrate the framework on multipartite entangled states, graph and cluster states, and nonlocal photonic-gate targets, obtaining multiple high-fidelity optical graphs. For nonlocal photonic gates, we obtain Toffoli constructions requiring two ancillas and alternative CNOT and Toffoli designs when connections between ancilla nodes are restricted. For state preparation, we identify asymptotic solutions for targets that cannot be generated exactly by graphs. Using the discovered topologies, we derive analytic families of optical experiments with explicit interference mechanisms and fidelity--rate relations, showing how generative design can support interpretable scientific discovery. These findings illustrate a reward-driven approach to quantum optical inverse design, exploring alternative circuit topologies while directly incorporating connectivity constraints into the search process.

authors.name: Isaac L. Huidobro-Meezs, Sim\'on Paiva-Ortega, Rodrigo A. Vargas-Hern\'andez

papers.title: Spectral Core-Tail Architecture for Locally Certified Gibbs-State Preparation
papers.summary: We develop a constructive method for designing Gibbs-state preparation circuits near tractable reference models, together with an explicit local error analysis. The spectral core-tail architecture (SCTA) combines a tractable thermal core and a unitary tail, defining a core-frame residual that measures the Hamiltonian mismatch from the target. We derive a local Gibbs-state error bound from the residual using the Kubo-Mori response theory. This bound is volume uniform when the response meets a shell summability condition and the relevant local data remain uniform with system size. We present three anchor Hamiltonian classes that admit exact core-tail constructions with zero residuals. For small deformations around an exact anchor, we employ a Schrieffer-Wolff-type reduction procedure that updates the core and constructs a correction to the tail. We prove that, under locality and solvability assumptions, the first-order reduction leaves a residual whose strength is quadratic in the deformation strength, with bounds independent of system size. A formal recursion extends the construction to arbitrary perturbative order at fixed volume, conditional on order-by-order solvability. Finite-size numerical tests on deformed graph-stabilizer Hamiltonians verify the quadratic suppression of both the residual and the local Gibbs-state error in the perturbative regime. The correction generators also provide a useful variational ansatz beyond perturbative control.

authors.name: Rui-Hao Li

papers.title: High-fidelity conditional-squeezing gate in superconducting circuits via refocusing
papers.summary: We propose a conditional-squeezing gate for superconducting circuits, which squeezes one or two modes of a resonator along a direction determined by the state of a dispersively coupled qubit. We show that the fidelity of this gate can be substantially improved by a refocusing protocol, in an architecture accessible with current technology whose key element is a SQUID-terminated resonator. The refocusing protocol relies on a symmetry of the Hamiltonian that is absent in the previously proposed controlled-squeezing gate, which squeezes the resonator only for one state of the control qubit and, ideally, acts trivially otherwise. We apply the refocused gate to encode an arbitrary qubit state into superpositions of single- and two-mode squeezed vacuum states, in which single-photon losses are detectable through parity measurements. Including nonlinearities and dissipation, the conditional gate consistently outperforms the controlled-squeezing gate, and, for optimistic but achievable experimental parameters, the encoding reaches fidelities above 0.99 for all qubit states.

authors.name: Roman Schiaffino, Fernando C. Lombardo, Juan Pablo Paz

papers.title: Universal Defect Statistics in Reverse Quenches
papers.summary: We extend the generalized Kibble-Zurek mechanism (gKZM) to reverse quench protocols using a stochastic description of defect formation finding that the mean defect density after a reverse quench equals twice the forward quench defect-number variance per unit volume. This relation, universally valid within the stochastic framework of the gKZM, makes the forward quench variance accessible through a reverse quench defect density measurement. We verify the equality analytically and numerically in the uniform one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, and numerically in its bond-disordered variant, including a regime where defect scaling departs from a pure power-law in quench time. Our result also suggests an experimental route to probing quantum critical behavior: reverse quenches that begin and end in the paramagnetic phase may allow to reveal critical exponents using global magnetic-field control and magnetization measurements, without resolving individual defects.

authors.name: Eduard J. Braun, Daniel Rubin, Margaux Cartier, Gerhard Z\"urn, Matthias Weidem\"uller

papers.title: Feature-Adaptive Fusion in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Robust Biomedical Image Classification
papers.summary: Hybrid quantum--classical neural networks offer a promising framework for integrating quantum circuits into machine learning in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era. However, fixed or globally shared fusion strategies used in many existing hybrid models may limit the effective integration of complementary classical and quantum information. To address this limitation, we propose a Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum--Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. The proposed model combines a classical deep feature encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) and employs a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically weight classical and quantum predictions across samples and classes. Under the evaluated settings, FAF-HQNN achieves competitive accuracy on PathMNIST and BloodMNIST compared to internal variants and external hybrid quantum--classical baselines. On PathMNIST, FAF-HQNN achieves higher aggregate mean accuracy than all evaluated baselines under both Gaussian and Poisson noise. These results suggest that feature-adaptive fusion may help improve classification performance within the evaluated framework.

authors.name: Yan-Yan Hou, Jian Li, Chongqiang Ye, Hengji Li, Zhuo Wang, Qinghui Liu

papers.title: A complete classification of the existence of finite-dimensional quantum solutions to inconsistent linear constraint systems
papers.summary: Linear constraint systems (LCS) provide a compact algebraic language for nonlocal games and state-independent contextuality. In the binary case the Mermin--Peres square shows that inconsistent LCS can be solved by promoting variables to local Pauli operators, whereas a series of no-go results excludes analogous Pauli-, Clifford- and monomial unitary-based constructions at odd prime modulus. We first isolate the reason for this difference: for tensor-product quantum solutions, the obstruction to a classical solution of a LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ decomposes into obstruction classes carried by the individual factors. As a consequence, a genuinely global obstruction cannot arise solely by tensoring locally unobstructed systems. The argument is specific to odd modulus; at even modulus the reordering phase need not vanish, as in Pauli-based examples. Given this distinction, we instead associate LCS to finite arrangements of rank-one projectors and resolutions of the identity in finite-dimensional vector spaces. Quantum solvability for such LCS is automatic and the search for a quantum-classical gap rests entirely on proving classical unsatisfiability of the underlying modular incidence problem of the arrangement. By relating such LCS with group-valued frame functions, we identify a family of examples in the work of [Harding, Jager, and Smith, Int. J. Theor. Phys. 44, 539 (2005)]. To establish the (non)existence of classically unsatisfiable LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with quantum solutions in all dimensions $d$ and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we further construct explicit examples for the cases $d=n$ prime. Our main result thus positively resolves the existence problem of such LCS beyond the binary case: such systems exist if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $\gcd(n,d)>1$. Moreover, we establish the existence of LCS with a quantum-classical gap over finite fields if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $p\mid d$.

authors.name: Markus Frembs

papers.title: Encrypted Quantum Cloning Beyond Maximal Entanglement: Exact Classification of Multipartite Resources
papers.summary: Encrypted quantum cloning distributes an unknown $k$-qubit state among $m$ individually concealed signals, each permitting exact recovery when combined with a common quantum key. While canonical constructions rely on maximally entangled resources, they do not establish which multipartite states are necessary or sufficient for this task. Here we derive necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing all pure resources compatible with a prescribed sector-wise two-Pauli encoder for $m\geq 2$, with necessity holding for arbitrary completely positive trace-preserving recovery maps. The classification reveals a sharp parity dependence: even $m$ requires maximal signal--key entanglement, whereas odd $m$ admits nonmaximally entangled resources when their residual signal correlations belong to an encoder-selected commuting algebra. Beyond this architecture, we show that exact recovery from every authorized subsystem under arbitrary unitary encoders acting on the input and signals while leaving the key untouched necessarily implies perfect individual concealment, requires at least $(m-1)k$ ebits of signal--key entanglement, and imposes spectral constraints on the resource. For graph states, the classification reduces to an exact cut-kernel criterion, enabling binary certification and constructive Clifford recovery. In particular, a rank-deficient three-output resource in the YZ/ZY branch attains the general entanglement lower bound with two ebits rather than three. We also exclude the entire Dicke family, including $W$ states, within the two-Pauli architecture. Together, these results distinguish fundamental entanglement requirements from encoder-dependent correlation constraints, providing an exact characterization of resource admissibility and a constructive recovery framework for graph states.

authors.name: Pritam Roy, Shashank Gupta

papers.title: A Three-Party W-State Quantum Secret Sharing Protocol with X-Gate Encoding and Forbidden-Outcome Detection
papers.summary: We propose a new three-party quantum secret sharing (QSS) protocol based on a three-qubit W state for distributing a predetermined sequence of classical bits. Alice encodes each bit using X gates and randomly applies Hadamard gates to the transmitted qubits. Her Hadamard-gate choices and the measurement bases independently chosen by Bob and Charlie determine the type of each round (information, test or semi-information) during transmission, without designating test rounds in advance. Suitable semi-information rounds provide additional opportunities for secret transmission and improve efficiency. The protocol combines secret transmission and tests for forbidden outcomes within the same ensemble of encoded W states. In the ideal model without an attack, transmitting an n-bit secret requires an average of 3n protocol rounds, giving a qubit efficiency of 1/9. We analyze intercept-and-resend and entangle-and-measure attacks by an internal adversary and derive their single-round and cumulative detection probabilities. For the entangle-and-measure attack, we relate the information obtainable through an ancillary system to the probability of forbidden test outcomes. The protocol is implemented in Python using Qiskit and evaluated through ideal simulation and experiments on IBM Quantum hardware. The simulation results are consistent with the theoretical predictions, while hardware measurements characterize round efficiency, reconstruction errors, forbidden-outcome probabilities and the information obtained through the specified ancilla measurement. A calibrated statistical criterion accounts for forbidden outcomes caused by hardware noise, with detection and false-alarm probabilities evaluated using a binomial model with measured rates. This analysis connects the ideal protocol predictions with a finite-sample assessment under the specified attack models and statistical assumptions.

authors.name: Timur R. Teregulov, Elena R. Loubenets

papers.title: Quantum Complexity of Ancilla-Free Unitary Embeddings for Nonlinear Dynamics via Generalized State-Dependent Double-Bracket Flows
papers.summary: Simulating nonlinear dynamics with quantum computers has gained increasing attention. In general, such simulations require additional quantum resources because unitary quantum evolution is linear. A fundamental question is how nonlinear dynamics can be embedded into fully coherent, ancilla-free unitary circuits and how the complexity of the dynamics governs the required quantum resources. In this work, we generalize the ancilla-free double-bracket quantum algorithm for imaginary-time evolution by replacing its state-independent Hamiltonian with a state-dependent Hermitian operator. Our framework recursively calls an initial state preparation oracle and its inverse, and prepares the target solution to any prescribed accuracy using a fully coherent, ancilla-free unitary embedding. We relate the query cost to the complexity of the nonlinear dynamics, specifically their sensitivity to initial conditions. We obtain query upper bounds of $\exp(O(T))$, $\exp(O(T^2))$, and $\exp(\exp(O(T)))$ when the distance between solutions contracts at least exponentially (contractive), does not increase (nonexpansive), or grows at most exponentially (expansive), respectively, where $T$ is the target evolution time. For the discrete Gross--Pitaevskii equation, our ancilla-free double-bracket circuit achieves optimal worst-case query complexity $\Theta(e^{gT/2})$ over a specified family of single-qubit initial states, where $g>0$ is the nonlinearity strength. These results connect the complexity of nonlinear dynamics to the query cost of coherent quantum simulation and provide a foundation for designing ancilla-free unitary embeddings with optimal query complexity.

authors.name: Yuki Ito, Hideaki Hakoshima, Keisuke Fujii

papers.title: Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation for General Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.summary: Low-depth syndrome extraction for Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check codes can be formulated as a proper ordered edge-coloring problem subject to quantum parity constraints. A proper edge-coloring of the CSS Tanner graph ensures that each data or ancilla qubit participates in at most one two-qubit gate per layer, but does not guarantee a valid interleaving of the X- and Z-check measurements as for every overlapping X/Z check pair, the number of shared data qubits on which the X interaction precedes the Z interaction must be even. The minimum number of colors in a proper ordered edge-coloring satisfying the quantum parity constraints equals the minimum two-qubit depth when each stabilizer check is measured with a single ancilla. We introduce local automorphism-aware syndrome compilation (LocalASC), which reduces the constraint system to edge-orbit variables under a subgroup of the Tanner graph automorphisms and lifts each feasible orbit assignment to the full graph. Although the $6$-layer degree lower bound is unattainable for the published weight-$6$ IBM bivariate bicycle codes, we show that this is not universal among two-block CSS codes. Among code instances for which the maximum check weight equals the maximum Tanner graph degree, LocalASC finds depth-optimal syndrome-extraction schedules for several two-block CSS codes with odd component weights, including instances with unequal odd weights. We also obtain lower-bound-saturating syndrome-extraction schedules for several quantum Tanner codes satisfying the same degree condition. To obtain the subgroups used by LocalASC without computing the full automorphism group of the Tanner graph, we construct translation subgroups for two-block group-algebra CSS codes over abelian groups. For quantum Tanner codes, we give conditions under which square-complex symmetries extend to Tanner graph automorphisms.

authors.name: Eugenio Durazo Rocha, Olai \AA. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes

papers.title: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation with optimal dependence on the maximum column Euclidean norm
papers.summary: We give a quantum algorithm for simulating a $d$-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$, assuming known upper bounds $\Lambda$ on its maximum column Euclidean norm $\|H\|_{1\to2}$ and $\Lambda_{\max}$ on its maximum entry magnitude. For every $t\ge0$, simulation with operator-norm error $\epsilon$ uses \[ O\!\left(t\Lambda\sqrt d +\sqrt{td\Lambda_{\max}\log(2/\epsilon)}+\log(2/\epsilon)\right) \] sparse-oracle queries. This removes the subpolynomial overhead in Low's algorithm [STOC 2019]. For $d>1$ and $t\Lambda\ge\log(2/\epsilon)$, the bound matches the worst-case lower bound. A known spectral-norm upper bound may also be used in place of $\Lambda$. The number of 1- and 2-qubit gates is linear in the query scale, up to oracle costs and polynomial overhead in the input bit lengths and logarithmic precision parameters. As applications, we obtain $O(\kappa\sqrt d\,\mathrm{polylog}(\kappa/\epsilon))$ queries for solving $d$-sparse quantum linear systems with $\|A\|\le1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|\le\kappa$, under standard sparse and state-preparation access. We also give a gate-efficient implementation of black-box unitaries with at most $d$ nonzero entries per row and column using $O(\sqrt{d\log(2/\epsilon)}+\log(2/\epsilon))$ queries, given sparse access to the unitary and its adjoint. At constant error, the query bound is optimal and yields $\Theta(\sqrt N)$ queries for arbitrary $N\times N$ unitaries, resolving the open question on black-box unitary implementation posed by Berry and Childs [QIC 2012].

authors.name: Zecheng Li, Chunhao Wang

papers.title: Root-sparsity scaling for Hamiltonian simulation, differential equations and linear-system solvers
papers.summary: We give quantum algorithms for time-independent and time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation, linear differential equations and linear systems, all with complexity that has only square-root dependence on matrix sparsity. Our algorithms retain optimal scaling in other relevant parameters such as time, condition number and precision. For several cases we prove matching lower bounds on the joint parameters and show that the additional gate overhead is only polylogarithmic in the inverse precision. The common primitive connecting our algorithms is the Cayley transform, which provides a cheap unitary embedding of the sparse matrices. For Hamiltonian simulation and differential equations, we then use transducers to construct the desired evolution operators. For linear systems, we instead encode the solution in the kernel of a matrix and use the Cayley transform to construct a projector onto that kernel.

authors.name: Dominic W. Berry, Abhishek Rawat, Sophia Simon, Guang Hao Low

papers.title: The Mermin-Peres Magic Square Game With Three or More Players
papers.summary: We present a generalization of the Mermin-Peres magic square game to $N$ players, in which the square is replaced by an $N$-dimensional hypercube. We show that the winning probability of the optimal classical strategy remains $8/9$ for all $N$, while for $N \ge 3$, a generalization of the quantum strategy for $N = 2$ achieves a winning probability between $1/3$ and $3/4$. This loss of quantum advantage for $N \ge 3$ is a consequence of monogamy.

authors.name: Itamar Lorian, J. E. Avron

papers.title: The parliament of observers - Against the observable axiom of quantum mechanics
papers.summary: The 'unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences' may at times give the impression that natural science, especially modern theoretical physics, is all but a formal apparatus. However, a key challenge of physics remains to align everyday notions of experience -- be it directly or mediated through instruments of arbitrary sophistication -- with their mathematical formalisation. This applies in particular to quantum theory, arguably the most successful theory of physics ever invented. One of its core assumptions postulates: $(Sharp)\ observables\ correspond\ with\ self-adjoint\ operators.$ Here, we argue that already this most basic premise about the quantum formalism falls apart under careful scrutiny, at least when understood for all observables at once. In other words, we challenge the role of the noncommutative algebra of bounded operators as an adequate formalisation of the 'algebra of observables', understood as (equivalence classes of) measurement procedures that admit a coherent empirical interpretation.

authors.name: Markus Frembs, Andreas D\"oring

papers.title: No-Disturbance-without-Uncertainty generates the Quantum set in the simplest Bell scenario
papers.summary: Characterizing the set of quantum nonlocal correlations through information-theoretic constraints is a central problem in quantum foundations. We show that the convex hull of no-signalling behaviors in a bipartite Bell experiment satisfying a common-overlap no-disturbance-without-uncertainty condition is exactly the finite-dimensional quantum set whenever one party has two binary measurements and the other has an arbitrary finite number of settings, each with an arbitrary finite number of outcomes. In the simplest binary input-output Bell scenario, this characterizes the full eight-dimensional set of quantum behaviors, including the local marginals. The proof constructs a quantum realization directly from the conditional probabilities and no-signalling. The characterization also reduces optimization of any linear Bell expression in these scenarios to maximization over a one-parameter family of second-order cone programs. The results establish a connection between local uncertainty-disturbance constraints and quantum nonlocality, mediated by no-signalling and shared classical randomness.

authors.name: Ravishankar Ramanathan

papers.title: Extensively degenerate superradiant phase in a giant-atom quantum Rabi ring
papers.summary: We show that an $N$-site quantum Rabi ring with matched giant-atom couplings has $2^N$ degenerate superradiant configurations as the atomic-to-cavity frequency ratio $\eta=\Delta/\omega$ tends to infinity. Each atom couples to two cavities separated by two lattice spacings, and the photon hopping carries a phase $\pi/2$. Matching the ratio of the two coupling strengths to the dimensionless photon hopping reduces the mean-field energy to a sum of single-site Rabi energies, with a common critical coupling for all momentum-pair sectors. The degeneracy survives quadratic quantum fluctuations despite a dispersive excitation spectrum. At large but finite $\eta$, second-order processes involving the local cubic anharmonicity generate a same-sublattice Ising coupling of order $\omega/\eta$, selecting ferro- and antiferro-superradiant configurations. This quantum order-by-disorder effect has no classical counterpart. Four-site calculations retaining all spin states quantitatively support the predicted energy coefficients. The separation between the induced coupling and the excitation gap allows a broad temperature interval with macroscopic photon occupation and short-range correlations between displacement signs.

authors.name: Shu He, Li-Wei Duan

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Galerkin Solvers for Elliptic Partial Differential Equations on Curved Geometries with Hardware Validation
papers.summary: Sample-based quantum solvers measure time-evolved Krylov states and solve the problem classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for the positive-definite linear systems of elliptic partial differential equations. A Galerkin solve on the sampled Fourier modes gives the solution. We derive energy-norm error bounds that connect the measured outcome law to the solution error, a sample complexity, and a support-completeness theorem. The theorem shows that time averaging recovers solution modes that are hidden from every selection based on the source. For curved cross sections we give a constructive procedure: conformal coordinates fix the matrix class, isometries of the cross section give postselection rules that keep every solution mode, and the Lie derivative of the metric bounds the error from geometric uncertainty. We apply the method to pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts and to non-separable problems with up to 16 qubits. On 16 qubits the sampler reaches 0.2% error with 3% of the Fourier modes, while a selection from the source stalls at 13% error. At these sizes a classical residual-greedy selection is more accurate, but its cost grows with the full dimension, whereas the sampler and the reduced Galerkin solve scale with the number of sampled modes. On IonQ and IBM processors with six and eight qubits, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model with a common decay of about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity rule derived from the geometry detects noisy shots at the predicted rate.

authors.name: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Villa Park, California, USA), Byeongyong Park (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

papers.title: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
