authors.name: Haoran Ji, Zheyuan Xie, Yaqi Chen, Guangdi Zhou, Keyi Liang, Rui Liu, Mengqiao Geng, Meixuan Li, Longxin Pan, Heng Wang, Haoliang Huang, Jun Ge, Yi Liu, Yang Liu, Guang-Ming Zhang, Yihua Wang, Ziqiang Wang, Qi-Kun Xue, Zhuoyu Chen, Jian Wang

papers.title: Odd-Parity Altermagnetism Originating from Orbital Order
papers.summary: Odd-parity spin splitting plays a central role in spintronics and unconventional superconductivity, yet its microscopic realization in collinear magnetic systems remains elusive. We propose a general symmetry-based strategy for realizing odd-parity altermagnetism by stacking two noncentrosymmetric monolayers in an interlayer antiferromagnetic configuration. In this setting, odd-parity spin splitting originates from nonrelativistic complex orbital order rather than spin-orbit coupling. By exploiting lattice symmetries, our framework enables the realization of both $p$- and $f$-wave altermagnets with nontrivial topological properties. Depending on the symmetry principles governing the bilayer stacking, the resulting altermagnet can host either quantum spin Hall or Chern insulator phases. Our work expands the landscape of altermagnetic phases and opens new avenues for discovering fascinating physical phenomena.

authors.name: Zheng-Yang Zhuang, Di Zhu, Dongling Liu, Zhigang Wu, Zhongbo Yan

papers.title: A stochastic heat engine driven using a nonlinear protocol
papers.summary: A colloidal particle confined in a time-dependent optical trap can function as a microscopic heat engine, with optimization strategies offering a route to enhanced performance. Here, we numerically investigate a Stirling heat engine operating in passive and active environments using a protocol inspired by Engineered Swift Equilibration (ESE). We analyze various fluctuating parameters throughout the cycle to validate the robustness of the engine, and demonstrate a significant enhancement in performance compared to conventional Stirling engines. Most crucially, we observe that the nonlinear protocol can even transform a heat pump-like operation into a genuine heat engine under strong activity, thereby surpassing bounds imposed on efficiency by high-temperature and quasi-static conditions. In contrast to the standard Stirling protocol, we observe that the nonlinear protocols appear to suppress the finite-time relaxation lag of the system from reaching an instantaneous equilibrium distribution, thereby improving engine performance at short cycle times. An analytical analysis of the variance dynamics where we quantify the relaxation lag between the actual and instantaneous equilibrium states clearly vindicates our understanding about the improved efficacy of the non-linear protocols. The proposed protocol is designed with experimental feasibility in mind, providing a practical route toward efficient microscopic heat engines.

authors.name: Amrutayani Panda, Biswajit Das, Shuvojit Paul, Arnab Saha, Ayan Banerjee

papers.title: Dynamics of $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ skyrmions
papers.summary: We derive several exact results for the dynamics of CP$^{N-1}$ skyrmions with arbitrary $N$. Fractonic continuity equation is shown to hold for arbitrary CP$^{N-1}$ fluid implying the conservation of the topological charge and the dipole moment. Inclusion of the Gilbert damping modifies the continuity equation, resulting in the violation of the dipole moment conservation but not of the topological charge. Thiele's equation for the CP$^{N-1}$ skyrmion follows from the modified continuity equation. The Girvin-MacDonald-Platzman (GMP) algebra in the long-wavelength limit is derived for arbitrary CP$^{N-1}$ fluid. In the case of CP$^2$ skyrmions, we construct a finite-size skyrmion with dominant ferromagnetic moments. We find that its magnetic dipole texture carries a nonzero CP$^1$ charge equal to half the CP$^2$ skyrmion charge and argue that the topological Hall effect of electrons should exist due to their coupling to the ferromagnetic part of the CP$^2$ texture.

authors.name: Seungho Lee, Hyojae Jeon, Jung Hoon Han

papers.title: Magnetocaloric effect for the altermagnetic candidate MnTe
papers.summary: We experimentally investigate magnetocaloric effect for single crystals of altermagnetic candidate MnTe at the transition to the state with spontaneous spin polarization, i.e. well below the N\'eel temperature of MnTe. The isothermal magnetic entropy change $\Delta S$ is calculated from the experimental magnetization curves by using Maxwell relation. We observe well-defined magnetocaloric effect as a narrow $\Delta S$ peak around the critical temperature $T_c\approx 81$~K, which reflects the sharp magnetization jump. This behavior is unusual for standard ferromagnetic transitions, so it confirms the predicted spin-orbit-induced spin polarization in the MnTe altermagnetic state and, therefore, confirms MnTe as a prototypical altermagnet candidate.

authors.name: N. N. Orlova, V. D. Esin, A. V. Timonina, N. N. Kolesnikov, E. V. Deviatov

papers.title: Demon's variational principle for informational active matter
papers.summary: The interplay between information, dissipation, and control is reshaping our understanding of thermodynamics in feedback-regulated systems. We develop the informational Onsager-Machlup principle, a generalized variational framework that unifies energetic, dissipative, and informational contributions within a single formalism. This framework introduces a conditioned Onsager-Machlup integral to quantify path entropy under specified memory states and enables the derivation of cumulant generating functions for arbitrary observables in systems with measurement and feedback. Our formulation is consistent with stochastic thermodynamics and information thermodynamics. To demonstrate the utility of the IOMP, we apply it to an information swimmer and show that it systematically reproduces the analytical expressions for the mean velocity and higher-order cumulants obtained by a direct approach, while also enabling the calculation of entropy production in the single-measurement case. For repeated measurements and the steady state, we derive approximate analytical expressions by using a Gaussian closure for the distribution of measured velocities. Our analytical results show good agreement with numerical results, except for cases of extreme drag asymmetry.

authors.name: Kento Yasuda, Kenta Ishimoto, Shigeyuki Komura

papers.title: Equation of state for hard sphere fluids across stable and metastable regimes
papers.summary: We review selected equations of state (EOSs) for three-dimensional hard-sphere fluids and revise a closed-virial construction to describe stable and metastable disordered states.

authors.name: Can Cui, Jianxiang Tian

papers.title: Predicting Coherent B2 Stability in Ru-Containing Refractory Alloys Through Thermodynamic Elastic Design Maps
papers.summary: The development of next-generation refractory superalloys is fundamentally constrained by competing requirements of high thermodynamic stability and low interfacial energy. Ru-based B2 intermetallics possess strong intrinsic ordering, but their use as coherent reinforcing phases requires balancing formation enthalpy against elastic strain. Here, we present a physics-guided machine-learning framework that integrates high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), Random Forest screening, and symbolic regression to map this design space. The approach addresses the "binary paradox" observed in recent experimental studies, where strongly ordered Ru-refractory compounds do not necessarily achieve the highest solvus temperatures. The resulting closed-form relation, T_solvus ~ 0.11(Delta H/Delta S) - 20000|delta|, quantifies the competing effects of thermodynamic stabilization and lattice misfit. Because the electronic-structure calculations are static 0 K calculations, the relation is treated as an effective calibrated design equation rather than a directly calculated finite-temperature free-energy boundary. The model is benchmarked against published B2 solvus measurements, while calculated formation enthalpies and lattice parameters are independently compared with calorimetric and diffraction data. Within the fitted relation, a 1% lattice misfit corresponds to an effective solvus penalty of approximately 200 degrees C. Al/Si substitution further shows that improved lattice matching is accompanied by reduced thermodynamic stabilization, with zero misfit near 11 at.% Al and 7 at.% Si for Nb75V25.

authors.name: Avik Mahata

papers.title: Manipulating anomalous transport via crystal symmetry in two-dimensional altermagnets
papers.summary: Anomalous transports, including the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE), are typical manifestations of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking responses in materials. In general, the two Hall states with opposite Hall conductivities can be regarded as time-reversal pairs coupled to magnetic order, and switching between them relies on reversing the magnetization via an external magnetic field or electric current. Here, we introduce an approach for manipulating anomalous transport through crystal symmetry engineering in two-dimensional (2D) altermagnetic systems. Through symmetry analysis and lattice models, we show that for systems with out-of-plane N\'eel vectors, breaking the symmetry that connects two magnetic sublattices will induce an anomalous Hall response. Crucially, the signs of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst conductivities can be flexibly controlled via symmetry-breaking perturbations, enabling the realizing tunable sign-reversible anomalous transport. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate crystal-symmetry-controlled anomalous transport in the 2D altermagnetic materials V$_{2}$STeO and Cr$_{2}$O$_{2}$. The results indicate that these systems with out-of-plane N\'eel vectors exhibit pronounced AHE and ANE signals under uniaxial strain. Remarkably, the sign of the anomalous transport coefficients can be reversed by simply rotating the strain direction by $\pi/2$, thus enabling the switching of anomalous transverse currents without an external magnetic field. Our findings provide a new strategy to manipulate anomalous transport, and should have significant potential applications.

authors.name: Dan Li, Shuaiyu Wang, Jiabin chen, Zeling Li, Chaoxi Cui, Lei Li, Lei Wang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Xiaodong Zhou, Xiao-Ping Li

papers.title: Magnon equilibrium spin current in collinear antiferromagnets
papers.summary: We theoretically predict that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction can induce a magnon equilibrium spin current in collinear antiferromagnets. Such a current, being a response to the effective magnon vector potential, can be considered the magnon analog of the supercurrent in superconductors. The large amplitude of the predicted effect may compensate for the smallness of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, making the equilibrium spin currents experimentally observable. Importantly, we show that the current being the ground state property isn't zero at zero temperature. We suggest that an external electric field can play the role of an effective flux that magnons interact with, and we propose an experiment based on the interference of magnons in a ring geometry to verify the concept.

authors.name: Vladimir A. Zyuzin

papers.title: Boundary-Sculpted Arctic Surface in the Cubic Ice Model
papers.summary: In square ice, domain-wall boundaries freeze the corners behind an arctic curve; strings of reversed arrows, unable to pass each other, give it Tracy-Widom fluctuations. In 3D, they pass around one another. Monte Carlo simulations calibrated on exact 2D results show that boundaries still sculpt an arctic surface in cubic ice, enclosing, by a lower bound, 3% of the box at the largest size. If local equilibrium holds up to it, it lies where the local field reaches the bulk Kasteleyn threshold. Its fluctuations are not Tracy-Widom along lines, and much closer than in 2D to independent strings.

authors.name: Benjamin Canals

papers.title: Interfacial charge-transfer in 3d/5d complex oxide heterostructures
papers.summary: Interfacial charge transfer (ICT) provides a powerful route to engineer electronic phases in correlated oxide heterostructures, yet predictive design principles remain elusive. Here, we systematically investigate superlattices composed of the 5d spin orbit coupled semimetal SrIrO3 and a series of correlated 3d perovskites (LaMnO3, LaFeO3, and LaCoO3), thereby establishing a quantitative framework for ICT across 3d/5d interfaces. Combining Ir L2,3 edge X ray absorption spectroscopy with spatially resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy, we estimate the electron depletion in the SrIrO3 layers and the corresponding electron accumulation in the 3d layers. The magnitude of ICT follows the trend expected from electronegativity mismatch, supporting electronegativity driven band alignment as the dominant contribution in this series. Beyond interfacial doping, we find that strong 3d,5d hybridization induces a low spin to high spin conversion in the cobaltate layers, hinting to interface controlled spin state engineering without chemical substitution. These results establish electronegativity mismatch as a predictive design parameter for correlated oxide interfaces and provide a materials platform for tailoring band filling, orbital hierarchy, and spin configurations in quantum oxide heterostructures, paving the way towards advanced oxide electronics and next-generation information technologies.

authors.name: Arun Kumar Jaiswal, Di Wang, Ji Soo Lim, Shruti Roy, Fabrice Wilhelm, Vanessa Wollersen, Andrei Rogalev, Matthieu Le Tacon, Dirk Fuchs

papers.title: The Mpemba effect likes to hit a wall
papers.summary: The original Mpemba effect refers to the counterintuitive possibility that a system prepared at a higher temperature relaxes to a colder equilibrium faster than one prepared at a lower temperature. In microscopic classical realizations, this phenomenon has been studied for overdamped particles in external potentials and observed experimentally. We show that, for a particle in an asymmetric polynomial double-well potential, the one-dimensional Mpemba effect is controlled not by the double-well structure or metastability itself, but by the high-energy confinement: a hard boundary, or more generally a sufficiently steep confining tail, on the shallow side can induce the required population inversion. For the polynomial potentials considered here, the effect disappears when both hard boundaries are taken to infinity, whereas sufficiently asymmetric soft tails can play the same role as walls. We identify the underlying mechanism as a redistribution of the initial equilibrium population when it begins to probe the high-energy tails of the potential, a picture that also extends to single-well and symmetric double-well potentials.

authors.name: Yue Liu, Tan Van Vu, Rapha\"el Ch\'etrite, Fr\'ed\'eric van Wijland, Hisao Hayakawa

papers.title: Quasi-1D Planar Magnetic Topological Heterostructure
papers.summary: We theoretically introduce a quasi one dimensional magnetic heterostructure of alternating 2D topological and normal insulator strips. Such a structure can be realized by special fabrication techniques or may emerge naturally in twisted bilayers of certain transition metal dichalcogenides. Its low-energy physics is governed by a hybrid Hamiltonian intertwining the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and Shockley models, with spin-momentum locking and local Zeeman splitting. Symmetry analysis places it in class AIII, characterized by chiral symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}$ topological invariant. Computing the winding number from the block-off-diagonal structure of the Hamiltonian reveals topological phases characterized by invariants $\nu = 0$, $1$, and $2$. Furthermore, a single magnetic defect acts as a sensitive local probe, whose in-gap spectrum provides a spectroscopic fingerprint to distinguish global topological phases. We show that the frequency-dependent optical absorption induced by such a defect exhibits distinct features in the topological and trivial phases, offering an independent, experimentally accessible local indicator of the global topological order. Extending the platform to a multilayer geometry uncovers a nonsymmorphic projective symmetry that gives rise to M\"obius band topology.

authors.name: Z. Z. Alisultanov

papers.title: Effect of subcritical fluid shear flow on granular bed strength
papers.summary: Interactions between fluids and granular materials are prevalent on the Earth's surface. In the case of fluid flow over a sediment bed, the fluid imparts a shear stress to the granular materials. When the applied shear stress is above a critical value, the grains become entrained in the fluid flow. Prior experimental studies have shown that granular beds subjected to a subcritical fluid flow can strengthen in the same direction as the subcritical flow. In contrast, granular beds can become weaker in the direction opposite to the subcritical fluid flow. To investigate the grain-scale mechanisms that control directional strengthening and weakening, we perform discrete element method (DEM) simulations of granular beds subjected to model fluid flows in two (2D) and three (3D) dimensions with varied inter-particle static friction coefficients and conditioning flow speeds. In these studies, the subcritical grain motion does not cause significant bed compaction. Instead, we find that the strength of a granular bed in a particular direction is highly correlated with the fraction of {\it surface} grains that can be dislodged by a fluid force applied in that direction. Further, the anisotropic bed strength only persists over a finite time scale that is set by the Shields number. We also show that inter-particle static friction is not required for bed strength anisotropy, but varying the friction affects the magnitude of the anisotropy. This research enhances the grain-scale understanding of erosion of granular beds caused by fluid flows and underscores the importance of tracking the history of the fabric of the bed surface since it couples strongly to bed strength.

authors.name: Dong Wang, Sophie Bodek, Nicholas T. Ouellette, Mark D. Shattuck, Corey S. O'Hern

papers.title: Topological antiqued mechanical toy
papers.summary: {\it Jacob's ladder} -- a classic children's toy -- is a simple mechanical frame comprising rigid blocks connected by strings that shows curious unidirectional flipping waves. Nonetheless, its physical origin remains elusive. By combining experiment, numeral simulation, and theory, we show that understanding the underlying design principle of this toy requires diverse physical ideas. First, we conduct a water-tank experiment that excludes the collision-based mechanism, thus defying widespread expectations. Subsequently, we analytically demonstrate that the toy is bistable under gravity, thus implying its kink wave as a class of topological solitons. The waves are surprisingly reminiscent -- both experimentally and theoretically -- to those in the Kane--Lubensky topological chain, owing to the stiffening of zero modes by the pretension under gravity. However, a close examination based on the index theorem reveals that the similarity remains superficial and that the floppiness of the toy underlies the kink and antikink coexistence -- a forbidden mode in the topological chain. By analyzing a generalized asymmetric toy, we reveal that its symmetric connection renders it topologically singular, thus resulting in amusing motions. We demonstrate these ideas by experimentally observing a dramatic pair annihilation of kink and antikink waves.

authors.name: Hirofumi Wada, Hayato Mizobata, Shuto Ueno, Taiju Yoneda

papers.title: Hidden Quantum-Geometric Connection between Injection and Shift Currents
papers.summary: Injection current (IC) and shift current (SC) are generally regarded as distinct nonlinear optical responses with different microscopic origins. Here, within the clean limit, based on an independent-particle interband description, we uncover a general hidden connection between the IC and SC responses. The generalized-derivative sum rule is used to show that the SC response separates into an injection-determined contribution associated with velocity asymmetry and a genuine shift-current (GSC) contribution associated with real-space wave-packet displacement. In systems with approximately linear electronic dispersion near the Fermi level, the corresponding tensor combinations of SC and IC can become effectively equivalent at low photon energies, governed by the same interband quantum-geometric dipole. Crystal symmetry can also eliminate the injection-determined contribution, enabling direct access to the GSC component. Extending our approach to second-harmonic generation reveals analogous response relations, suggesting a route toward a broader network of quantitative connections among the various nonlinear optical responses.

authors.name: Mohammad Yahyavi, Tay-Rong Chang, Md Shafayat Hossain, Arun Bansil, Naoto Nagaosa, Guoqing Chang

papers.title: Microscopic origin of Boson peak in two-dimensional scalar spring network
papers.summary: We proposed a non-analytic model to explain the microscopic origin of the anomalous vibrational density of states (DOS), the Boson peak (BP), in amorphous solids based on the scalar dynamical matrix of a network with springs and nodes. We argue that disorder can be classified into two factors: fluctuation of spring strength and fluctuation of coordination numbers (the number of springs connected to a node). The results suggest that BP originates from fluctuation of coordination numbers, while the fluctuation of spring strength only contributes to the effect of damping and has very limited effect on low frequency DOS. This work converts complexity into simplicity and provides a direct answer to the puzzle of the microscopic origin of BP in amorphous solids.

authors.name: Cunyuan Jiang

papers.title: Evaluation of External Magnetic Flux Density in Piezo-Flexomagnetic Nanobeams Using a Hybrid 1D-2D Finite Element Framework
papers.summary: Most theoretical models of piezo-flexomagnetic nanostructures forcibly impose magnetic isolation at the structure-air interface, neglecting the external magnetic domain entirely. This mathematical compromise limits the model's capability to account for stray-field behavior in non-contact applications. To overcome this gap, our study proposes a fully coupled hybrid finite element formulation combining a 1D Timoshenko beam model with a 2D magneto-static problem, encompassing both the beam body and the surrounding air domain. By continuously mapping 1D structural kinematics into the 2D space to define the mechanically induced magnetic flux, and subsequently integrating the resulting 2D scalar potential back into 1D static generalized magnetic loads, this framework enhances the capability of the simple 1D beam model. The results present the distribution of an external magnetic flux in piezo-flexomagnetic structures and identify the material parameters driving this. Ultimately, the proposed computational method extends the boundary of a 1D beam model to an infinite-domain multiphysics environment.

authors.name: Lala Samprit Ray, Bishweshwar Babu

papers.title: Finite-temperature micromagnetic model bridging atomic- and macro-scale magnetism
papers.summary: A multi-scale finite-temperature micromagnetic model is presented, based on the Landau-Lifshitz equation and the Bernoulli differential equation. This model accurately reproduces classic Maxwell magnetostatics of paramagnets for high temperatures and accurately reproduces standard micromagnetics described by the conventional Landau-Lifshitz model in ferromagnets. The Landau-Lifshitz-Bernoulli (LLBe) model can, by design, directly couple atomic-scale simulations with micromagnetics and output consistent predictions of bulk magnetic properties at finite temperatures, from below to above the material's Curie temperature. The LLBe model is validated against established solvers: MUMAX3 for zero-temperature micromagnetics, and FEMCE for high-temperature classic magnetostatics. We present an application of the LLBe model by simulating Heat-Assisted magnetic recording on a thin magnetic track with local heating, demonstrating the multi-scale finite-temperature capabilities of the LLBe.

authors.name: R. Kiefe, J. S. Amaral

papers.title: Predicting the conditions for observing the Mpemba effect
papers.summary: The Mpemba effect, a counterintuitive phenomenon where a hotter system relaxes faster than a colder one, has been widely observed in various nonequilibrium systems. Despite this progress, the fundamental structural features of the energy landscape required for its emergence remain a subject of debate. In this study, we investigate the conditions for the Mpemba effect within one-dimensional overdamped Langevin dynamics. We classify the potential landscapes based on the presence of single or double wells, their symmetry properties, and the existence of walls. We establish that the existence of the effect is primarily driven by the presence of boundaries, either hard or soft, rather than the specific internal structure of the potential landscape, such as metastability or the number of minima. By employing a spectral decomposition of the Fokker-Planck operator, we analyze the behavior of the first nontrivial eigenmode and demonstrate that its derivative acts as a Dirac delta peak in the low-temperature regime. This helps us elucidate the mechanism underlying the Mpemba effect: it appears as the interplay between this behavior and the initial population dynamics in a non-trivial way induced by the presence of the wall. Our analysis provides a unified classification across single- and double-well potentials, highlighting the crucial role of boundary conditions and asymmetry. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this framework allows for the engineering of potential landscapes capable of producing multistage Mpemba transitions.

authors.name: Yue Liu, Tan Van Vu, Rapha\"el Ch\'etrite, Fr\'ed\'eric van Wijland, Hisao Hayakawa

papers.title: Atomic-scale visualization of the toroidal order in a trimeric Dy(III) single-molecule toroic
papers.summary: Single-molecule toroics (SMTs) offer a unique platform for next-generation quantum devices utilizing head-to-tail spin alignments in the compounds. Presence of toroidal moments in SMTs has been essentially based on magnetometry and ab initio calculations. Here, we report observation and probe of the toroidal moment in [Dy3(OH)(teaH2)3(paa)3]Cl(OMe) [teaH3: triethanolamine; paaH: N-(2-pyridyl)-acetoacetamide] from mapping of Dy3+ magnetic susceptibility tensors by polarized neutron diffraction (PND). Neutron diffraction under variable magnetic fields demonstrates field-induced magnetization along the c-axis with toroidal moments anti-parallelly stacked, providing definite proof of the toroidal moment. Magnetometry studies confirm the toroidal ground state. For the first time, the combined use of PND, variable-field neutron diffraction, ab initio calculations, and magnetometry is introduced as a robust and quantitative methodology to probe molecular-scale toroidal magnetism. This integrated approach overcomes limitations of earlier indirect methods, establishes a benchmark framework for investigating SMTs, and provides valuable insights for the design of molecular quantum materials.

authors.name: Michael J. Jenkins, Madalynn G. Marshall, Jie Xing, Muthu Satheeshkumar, Brandon D. Watson-Sanders, Xiaoping Wang, Christina M. Hoffmann, Gopalan Rajaraman, Huibo Cao, Rongying Jin, Zi-Ling Xue

papers.title: Dynamics of repeated BEC formation and extraction in dimple traps
papers.summary: We investigate repeated Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) formation and extraction in a dimple trap embedded in a reservoir of thermal atoms using a kinetic model. The model includes pulsed extraction, evaporation, three-body losses, and thermal-atom replenishment. Three extraction protocols are compared: extraction of all atoms from the dimple (BEC and thermal atoms), full and partial extractions of the BEC, but not of the thermal atoms. Residual atoms in the dimple after extraction seed subsequent Bose-stimulated growth and reduce the recovery time between extractions, but also enhance density-dependent losses. For all protocols, repeated extraction of BECs can be achieved without replenishment, but the number of BEC formations is limited by reservoir depletion and heating. With continuous replenishment, the system can reach a periodic steady-state regime, after an initial transient period, controlled by the externally imposed rates of extraction pulses and thermal-atom input. Within the explored parameter range, partial BEC extraction gives the highest efficiency, particularly for short extraction periods and high input rates. These results identify seeding by residual populations of BECs and thermal atoms as a kinetic mechanism for improving repeated condensate production in dimple traps.

authors.name: Kyrylo Kovalchuk, Dominik Pfeiffer, Ludwig Lind, Mark Edwards, Alexander Yakimenko, Gerhard Birkl

papers.title: Nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang dynamics of grain boundaries
papers.summary: The kinetic roughening of driven grain boundaries (GBs) is mediated by the collective behavior of disconnections, whose long-range 1/r elastic interactions distinguish them from conventional growing surfaces. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations show that the roughness of driven GBs undergoes a sharp crossover as the applied strain increases, with the Hurst exponent (H) increasing from approximately 0.33 to 0.8. We develop a nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (fKPZ) theory to describe this low-temperature behavior, where the 1/r nonlocal elasticity behaves as the fractional relaxation of the GB morphology. The results show that the spatially-correlated noise associated with disconnection avalanches interacts with the KPZ nonlinearity to produce the post-crossover roughening observed in atomistic simulations. The post-crossover roughness exponent (H ~ 0.8) is comparable to values reported for dynamic fracture, suggesting the underlying physics shared by the collective behavior of defects (e.g., disconnections, dislocations) and interfacial roughening.

authors.name: Kai Zhao

papers.title: Nonlinear Static Screening of Positive Charges in an Electron Gas: Contact Hartree Potential
papers.summary: We investigate nonlinear static screening of a proton in a homogeneous electron gas, focusing on the induced density and contact Hartree potential $V_{\rm H}(0)$, an $r$-weighted moment of the entire screening cloud rather than a strictly local quantity. Thomas--Fermi, RPA, and local-field-corrected linear response are compared with nonlinear DFT-LDA and DFT-PBE calculations. The Estreicher--Meier LDA density fit reproduces the contact Hartree potential closely and resolves its core and Friedel contributions, despite an approximate cusp. Kaplan--Kukkonen and Corradini--Del Sole--Onida--Palummo local-field factors give nearly identical contact predictions for the states examined, without implying general insensitivity to local-field corrections. We extend the variable-phase approach with a companion amplitude equation to reconstruct the quantal induced density from bound and continuum states of constrained screened potentials. Friedel-constrained Yukawa, hydrogenic, and Hulth\'en potentials satisfy the same total-screening condition but yield different contact densities and Hartree potentials. In the two-parameter Apagyi--Nagy construction, the cusp constrains an auxiliary Poisson density, whereas the reconstructed quantum density obeys the Coulomb cusp automatically; neither the Friedel sum rule nor the cusp uniquely fixes the screening cloud. Model-potential contact results approach nonlinear DFT toward high density but deviate increasingly as $r_s$ grows. By contrast, density-informed Popovi\'c--Stott potentials reproduce historical Hartree-only and exchange--correlation-modified contact values within $0.05\%$ without refitting. These findings distinguish global scattering constraints, local cusp behavior, and full-density information, and establish a one-center baseline for future two-center screening calculations.

authors.name: M. Sherafati, G. Rodway-Gant, A. X. Chen

papers.title: Near itinerancy and slow singlet formation in the triangular lattice NaRuO2
papers.summary: NaRuO$_2$ forms a delafossite-like structure that contains triangular sublattices of edge-sharing RuO$_6$ octahedra. It shows no evidence of magnetic order down to 100~mK and persistent spin fluctuations, suggestive of a quantum disordered magnetic ground state. In order to characterize the physical regime from which this disordered state arises, we use resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) at the Ru-$L_{2,3}$-edge, along with pulsed high-field magnetization to characterize both the local electronic structure and the magnetic interactions. We infer significant spin-orbit coupling from XAS measurements. With RIXS, we observe intraorbital excitations, which are damped due to the near itinerancy of the band and suggestive of strong charge fluctuations. Corroborated by models of the high-field magnetization to a random singlet model, we propose a picture of a nearly itinerant system with strong magnetic and charge fluctuations that destabilize long-range magnetic order.

authors.name: Charles C. Tam, Alon Hendler Avidor, Pritam Bhattacharyya, Yongseong Choi, Daniel Haskel, Sven Luther, Hlynur Gretarsson, Liviu Hozoi, Stephen D. Wilson

papers.title: Fractionalized Fermi liquids with the ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz
papers.summary: Fractionalized Fermi liquids ($\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$), elusive metallic states characterized by fractionalized quasiparticles alongside conventional ones and defying Luttinger's theorem, are prime candidates for the pseudogap regime of underdoped cuprates. We show that a $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$ phase emerges in the single-band $t$-$J$ model through a simple ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz, optimized at the cost of a mean-field calculation. The resulting temperature-doping phase diagram encompasses a low-doping $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$, a $d$-wave superconducting dome, and an overdoped conventional Fermi liquid, thereby reproducing key qualitative features of cuprate phenomenology.

authors.name: Ivan Pasqua, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Michele Fabrizio

papers.title: Thermo-elastic properties of hydrated epoxy-graphene nanocomposites from ensemble-based molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: Epoxy-based materials are inherently hygroscopic, absorbing moisture from the environment, which can significantly alter their short and long-term performance. The presence of graphene is often considered as a potential candidate to act as a microscopic barrier, mitigating the adverse effects of hydration on the matrix. This study investigates the impact of hydration on the glass transition and elastic mechanical properties of epoxy resins and their graphene nanocomposites, focusing on water content up to 5 %wt. Using large-ensemble molecular dynamics simulations, we analyze the temperature-driven glass transition and mechanical response of both neat epoxy and epoxy-graphene systems under varying hydration levels. Our results reveal a distinct threshold at 3 %wt water content: below this, hydration primarily reduces the glass transition temperature, while mechanical properties remain unaffected. Beyond 2 %wt, however, the mechanical properties deteriorate, highlighting a non-linear sensitivity to water uptake. Furthermore, we emphasize the critical role of ensemble size in ensuring the reliability of molecular dynamics predictions for such heterogeneous systems. Our simulations demonstrate that ensembles substantially larger than current state-of-the-art standards are necessary to achieve converged distributions of the predicted mechanical properties, particularly in highly heterogeneous hydrated epoxy-graphene nanocomposites. These findings provide novel insights into the hydration behavior of epoxy-based materials and underscore the limited potential of graphene to enhance their environmental resistance. This work also advances the understanding of structure-property relationships in polymer nanocomposites, offering guidance for the design of more robust materials in humid environments.

authors.name: Maxime Vassaux, Werner A. M\"uller, James L. Suter, Alexandros Anastasiou, Martin Simmons, David Tilbrook, Peter V. Coveney

papers.title: Statistical mechanics of a three-body Hopfield model with finite connectivity
papers.summary: A three-body Hopfield model defined on sparse random graphs with finite mean connectivity is studied using a replica-symmetric (RS) analysis. By extending the functional replica framework for conventional two-body finite-connectivity Hopfield models, self-consistent equations for the local-field distribution are derived and solved numerically by population dynamics. At low memory load, the RS analysis shows a discontinuous transition between paramagnetic and retrieval states, accompanied by coexistence of distinct fixed points and an upper spinodal of the retrieval solution. Starting the RS population dynamics from an uninformative finite-amplitude field distribution also leads to a spin-glass-like (SG-like) fixed point at low temperatures, even though the paramagnetic fixed point remains locally stable. As the number of embedded patterns increases, the retrieval solution disappears, while the SG-like RS solutions are found at high load. However, the local instability and thermodynamic inconsistencies of the low-temperature RS solutions indicate the limitations of the RS description of the glassy regime. Finite-size Monte Carlo simulations using population annealing agree well with the RS description of the retrieval branch during heating but exhibit glassy trapping behavior under cooling. Such trapping can occur even for a single embedded pattern, where conventional cross-talk noise among stored patterns is absent, indicating the importance of sparse connectivity and three-body interaction. The characteristic number of embedded patterns separating different solution regimes grows approximately linearly with the mean connectivity, corresponding to finite characteristic load ratios. These results clarify how sparse connectivity and many-body interactions influence the stability and accessibility of retrieval states in associative memory.

authors.name: Yushi Sugawara, Koji Hukushima

papers.title: Magnetic Modulation of Ionic Transport in a Multistate Channel Model
papers.summary: We study the magnetic modulation of ionic transport in an idealized multistate channel model. The channel can occupy different structural states, each with its own ionic current and magnetic response. We assume quasi-equilibrium Boltzmann populations for the structural states, while ionic transport is driven by an externally imposed electrochemical potential difference. Using a statistical-mechanical linear-response approach, we relate changes in the average current to magnetic perturbations of the structural states. The response is determined by the covariance between the state-dependent ionic currents and their magnetic-response coefficients, which controls both its sign and magnitude. We also examine the magnetic and thermal sensitivities, illustrate the results with a three-state model. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that the predicted effect for a single channel is extremely small at millitesla magnetic fields. Overall, the results provide a quantitative criterion for assessing magnetic modulation of transport within this idealized model and may help in considering possible effects in real ion channels and other multistate transport systems.

authors.name: Tina Arabi, Ehsan Noruzifar

papers.title: Hidden symmetry at the diabolical points of a biaxial spin
papers.summary: In a rotated frame the biaxial spin Hamiltonian $k_1S_x^2+k_2S_y^2-\mathbf{h}\cdot\mathbf{S}$ is a finite tight-binding chain whose hopping amplitudes are tuned by the applied field. A chain with no vanishing hopping has a nondegenerate spectrum, so a degeneracy can occur only where the field severs the chain. At every point of the diabolical-point lattice proven exact by Ke\c{c}ecio\u{g}lu and Garg, the chain is severed in two different rotated frames, at two bonds that are labeled independently. We write the two severings as two spectral-cut projectors. These are explicit polynomials in two field-independent spin components; they commute with the Hamiltonian at that point but not with each other. This gives a concrete form to the hidden symmetry anticipated by Garg: on the degenerate subspace the two projectors generate a pseudospin SU(2) that commutes with the Hamiltonian. The rank of a pairing operator built from them gives the multiplicity of every lattice point, without the continuity and topological argument used previously. Because the two partners of a doublet occupy disjoint stretches of the chain, the splitting determinant factorizes exactly and has a fixed negative sign. Every degeneracy of the model is therefore a linear cone, all cones have the same orientation, and the lower level carries Chern charge $-1$ for the Berry connection $i\langle\psi|\nabla\psi\rangle$.

authors.name: Shadan Ghassemi Tabrizi

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Random Matrix Theory of Jamming in Active Disordered Media
papers.summary: We develop a non-Hermitian random-matrix description of active jammed systems in which a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by non-reciprocal Ginibre couplings. Within a Hermitized self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA), we derive a scalar susceptibility equation predicting \(J\sim\alpha_0^{-6/7}\) at the marginal point. Direct random-matrix calculations confirm that the mechanically relevant response is governed by singular values rather than complex eigenvalues. They further reveal strong finite-size fluctuations: near marginality, a large fraction of the total susceptibility is typically carried by the smallest singular value. These results distinguish the smooth large-\(N_c\) SCBA response from the extreme singular-value statistics of finite non-Hermitian systems.

authors.name: Hisao Hayakawa

papers.title: Local B-site chemistry controls oxygen-vacancy energetics in Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn perovskites for thermochemical hydrogen production
papers.summary: Two-step thermochemical water splitting driven by concentrated solar heat is a scalable route to renewable hydrogen, but it requires oxides whose oxygen-vacancy formation energies balance facile reduction with favorable reoxidation. Perovskite solid solutions can tune this balance, but the relationship between bulk stoichiometry and local defect energetics remains poorly understood. Here we map oxygen-vacancy formation energetics across Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn (CCTM) perovskites by combining first-principles calculations with a coverage-constrained special quasirandom structure approach that realizes all fifteen symmetry-distinct oxygen nearest-neighbor environments, an interpretable crystal-feature model whose fitted coefficients directly encode the underlying Born-Haber thermochemistry, and a fine-tuned defect graph neural network. Local B-site chemistry dominates the oxygen-vacancy formation energy $E_\mathrm{v}$: varying the nearest-neighbor Mn fraction shifts $E_\mathrm{v}$ by 1.0-1.5 eV depending on local Ce content, whereas A-site Ce variation contributes a smaller, Mn-dependent shift of 0.2-0.6 eV. Short-range B-site cation order, if it can be established and kinetically retained through processing, is therefore a candidate means of tuning redox performance without changing bulk composition. Composition-space maps identify a Ce/Mn-balanced region (~29-33% Ce on the A site and 58-67% Mn on the B site) combining a high fraction of vacancy sites within the targeted $E_\mathrm{v}$ window with phase stability and solubility, whose predicted redox cycle capacity matches or exceeds the ceria benchmark at 1350 $^\circ$C rather than the roughly 1600 $^\circ$C ceria requires. Measurements on three CCTM compositions show cycle capacity increasing monotonically with Ce content under protocols close to the model conditions. The design rules are expected to transfer to related perovskite families.

authors.name: Manish Kumar (Washington University in St. Louis), Natalia Ali (Arizona State University), Matthew D. Witman (Sandia National Laboratories), Shang Zhai (The Ohio State University), James E. Miller (Arizona State University), Ivan Ermanoski (Arizona State University), Ellen B. Stechel (Arizona State University), Robert B. Wexler (Washington University in St. Louis)

papers.title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
papers.summary: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive probe of anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid systems.

authors.name: S. Feyrer, V. Dimic, I. Lobato, A. Kirchner, P. Drexler, L. Rupp, D. Bougeard, T. Lindemann, S. Gronin, G. Gardner, M. J. Manfra, G. F. R. Ruiz, C. A. Balseiro, L. Arrachea, M. Aprili, N. Paradiso, C. Strunk, L. Tosi

papers.title: Unconventional Pressure Evolution of Spin-Density-Wave State in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$
papers.summary: The discovery of pressure-induced high temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has raised the question of how its spin-density-wave (SDW) state evolves toward the superconducting regime. Here, we report a systematic electronic Raman study of La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51~GPa. Both the SDW gap energy and the transition temperature $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ show an overall increase with pressure, while the dimensionless coupling ratio $2\Delta_{\mathrm{SDW}}/(k_{\mathrm B}T_{\mathrm{SDW}})$ remains approximately pressure independent, indicating a robust strong-coupling character of SDW state. At the same time, the SDW-related Raman peak broadens as pressure is applied, indicating the enhanced damping of the associated electronic excitation. These results reveal an unusual pressure evolution in which the SDW energy scale is enhanced while the SDW state becomes progressively less coherent, providing spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations relevant to superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

authors.name: Xiaoxiang Zhou, Shiyu Xie, Liangxin Qiao, Hengyuan Zhang, Jun Shu, Rui Liu, Mengwu Huo, Deyuan Hu, Hengjie Liu, Chuansheng Hu, Ge He, Zeming Qi, Meng Wang, Dong-Lai Feng, Zengyi Du

papers.title: Room-Temperature Polarity Control of the Anomalous Nernst Effect in a High-Magnetic-Anisotropy Topological Nodal-Line MnAlGe
papers.summary: Controlling the polarity of anomalous Nernst thermopower is a promising strategy for enhancing the performances of thermoelectric applications. However, realizing such control at room temperature (RT) in topological ferromagnets with high magnetic anisotropy (Ku) remains challenging. Here, we report RT polarity control of the anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) in quasi-two-dimensional nodal-line MnAlGe epitaxial thin films through Al/Ge compositional tuning while preserving robust high Ku. This polarity reversal originates from intrinsic Berry curvature contributions modulated by sublattice-selective carrier doping, as supported by spin-resolved electronic band structure analysis and hard X-ray photoemission spectroscopy. To demonstrate the practical feasibility, we also fabricated a meander-structured device combining MnAlGe with positive and negative polarity enhanced the thermoelectric output. Our results demonstrate that tuning the Fermi level relative to the nodal-line electronic structure while preserving high Ku enables controllable ANE polarity reversal within a single material, providing a route toward RT transverse thermoelectric devices.

authors.name: Nanhe Kumar Gupta, Keisuke Masuda, Masaaki Kakoki, Benugopal Bairagya, Satoki Tazawa, Weinan Zhou, Hirofumi Suto, Ryo Toyama, Akio Kimura, Yuya Sakuraba

papers.title: Exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size
papers.summary: We present exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size. Some properties of exact expressions obtained are discussed. The fundamental property of the Ising model that the long range order emerge as the temperature decrease is shown clearly; expressions of the correlation functions in the thermodynamic limit varies depending on the order of taking limits of two parameters L and N; the impact of different sizes on correlation functions is illustrated with the aid of diagrams. Expressions of the correlation function discussed in this paper in the thermodynamic limit has been presented by previous researchers, and we prove that expressions obtained in this article is identical in form to expressions provided by previous researchers in the thermodynamic limit.

authors.name: Mei Tao

papers.title: Field-free precessional magnetization dynamics in a multidomain magnet driven by light-induced strain
papers.summary: Ultrafast lattice excitation offers a route to controlling magnetization through magnetoelastic coupling, yet its ability to drive large-amplitude dynamics within pre-existing multidomain states remains less explored. Here, we show that a single 5-ps mid-infrared pulse induces a large-amplitude, reversible magnetic response in cobalt-doped yttrium iron garnet at zero applied magnetic field. Time-resolved magneto-optical microscopy reveals a transient reversal of the out-of-plane magnetic contrast within approximately 2 ns, followed by recovery of the initial state, while the labyrinthine domain morphology remains largely preserved. Concurrent polarization microscopy reveals a localized, long-lived strain-sensitive response and a propagating acoustic wave. The correlated structural and magnetic responses, together with micromagnetic simulations, support a mechanism in which transient strain modifies the magnetic anisotropy and drives precessional reorientation within existing domains. These findings establish single-pulse magnetoelastic excitation as a route to reversible, large-amplitude magnetization dynamics without substantial domain reorganization or an externally applied magnetic field.

authors.name: H\'elo\"ise Damas, Carl S. Davies, Tomasz Zalewski, Petr M. Vetoshko, Vladimir I. Belotelov, Andrzej Stupakiewicz, Andrei Kirilyuk

papers.title: de Almeida-Thouless Stability and Replica Symmetry Breaking in a Hybrid Watermarking Model with Image and Message Decoding
papers.summary: We investigate the de Almeida-Thouless (AT) stability of the replica symmetric (RS) solution for a spread-spectrum watermarking model incorporating Bayes-estimation-based image restoration. In our previously proposed model [1], which simultaneously performs message decoding and image restoration under Gaussian channel noise, a discrepancy between the theoretical predictions of the RS solution and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations was observed in specific parameter regimes. In this paper, by analyzing the blind case where both the original message and image are unknown, we explicitly derive the conditions for the AT stability of the RS solution by clarifying the structure of the replicon eigenspace for the hybrid system. Our results reveal that AT stability is broken precisely in the parameter region where the RS solution deviates from MCMC simulations, thereby successfully explaining the mechanism underlying this discrepancy in terms of replica symmetry breaking (RSB). [1] M. Kawamura, T. Uezu, K. Hayashi, and M. Okada, ``Statistical mechanical evaluation of a spread-spectrum watermarking model with image restoration,'' Phys. Rev. E \textbf{99}, 062132 (2019).

authors.name: Tatsuya Uezu, Kao Hayashi, Masaki Kawamura

papers.title: Curvature-Enhanced Polarization in Transition-Metal Dichalcogenide Janus Nanowrinkles
papers.summary: Strain-gradient engineering via out-of-plane wrinkling offers a powerful route to tune electronic and electromechanical properties in two-dimensional (2D) materials. Here, we systematically investigate the electronic and polarization response of wrinkled Janus MoSSe/MoSeS monolayers using density functional theory (DFT) calculations coupled with continuum elastica modeling. Exploring varying wrinkle sizes and compressive strain levels ($5\%$ -- $20\%$), we show that the global out-of-plane polarization follows a linear behavior when parameterized by the projected aspect ratio of the nanowrinkles. On this basis, we develop a physically grounded geometric model incorporating an effective 2D electromechanical coupling coefficient, which accurately predicts DFT polarizations without requiring higher-order nonlinear parameters. Atom- and orbital-resolved charge density analyses reveal the microscopic origin of this behavior: while the central Mo $4d$ projected weight remains approximately constant, local curvature drives continuous, chemically asymmetric charge transfer between the S $3p$ and Se $4p$ sublayer manifolds. Our findings establish clear geometric design rules for harnessing polarization in Janus monolayers for flexible nanoelectronics and optoelectronics.

authors.name: Stefan Velja, Surender Kumar, Domenico Corona, Caterina Cocchi

papers.title: Trajectory Statistics Govern Mechanical Power Transfer in Active Baths
papers.summary: In active media, a moving passive object can experience negative drag and receive positive mechanical power from the bath, in contrast to the dissipative response in equilibrium. For a probe moving at velocity $\mathbf{V}$ and interacting weakly with an ideal active bath, we show that free-particle trajectory statistics determine the density response and the resulting bath force. The probe--particle interaction sets the wave-vector weighting, while the imposed motion selects frequencies $\omega_{\mathbf q}=\mathbf q\cdot \mathbf V$, separating bath dynamics from probe properties. The sign of the response spectrum yields probe-independent constraints for mechanical power transfer. Applying this framework to representative active-particle models reveals distinct power-transfer behavior despite identical displacement variances. For prescribed probe motion, the relation predicts drag reversal, motion-induced density distortions, and velocity-dependent friction, in quantitative agreement with simulations. Beyond the mean force, the free-particle trajectory statistics also determine the force autocorrelation. These results provide a route to predict the mechanical response of probes from single-particle trajectory statistics measured in the absence of the probe.

authors.name: Chul-Ung Woo, Jiwon Choi, Heiko Rieger

papers.title: Magnetic Quadrupole Lens and Current-Induced Quadrupolar Dynamics of Antiskyrmion
papers.summary: We demonstrate that antiskyrmions can serve as magnetic quadrupole lenses that focus or defocus electric currents traversing them. We showcase the antiskyrmion core as a focal point where electron beams converge for specific injection directions, leading to anisotropic and nonuniform current distributions. Thus the current-induced antiskyrmion dynamics is profoundly modified by the magnetic quadrupole lensing via the spin-transfer torque. By incorporating quantum transport and micromagnetic simulations iteratively, we self-consistently capture the coupled dynamics of conduction electrons and antiskyrmions. Our results unveil a quadrupolar antiskyrmion Hall effect that is highly anisotropic with respect to the current direction and can be effectively tuned by the spin-orbit coupling. In particular, the current focusing (defocusing) dramatically enhances (suppresses) the antiskyrmion speed while simultaneously reducing its Hall angle, thereby overcoming a key challenge for antiskyrmion racetrack memories. Our work establishes the intrinsic current lensing as a powerful mechanism for manipulating topological magnetic textures and opens new avenues for antiskyrmion-based spintronics.

authors.name: Linfeng Du, Yang Liu, Peng Yan, Ying Su

papers.title: Intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in graphene stacks
papers.summary: The effect of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in monolayer graphene has been thoroughly studied in the past. Its impact is commonly disregarded since the electronic structure of graphene is almost unaffected. Consequently, SOC has also been ignored in other graphitic systems. In this work, we calculate the intrinsic SOC in stacks of graphene layers from a model that includes all the valence orbitals of carbon as well as the intra-atomic SOC.The leading spin-orbit term in a graphene multilayer combines a Rashba-like spin-flip process with interlayer hopping. We find that this intrinsic term modifies the phase diagram and Fermi surfaces of finite rhombohedral stacks, and it leads to a distinct density-dependence of the magnetization in weak magnetic fields. This Letter shows that, unlike in the single-layer case, SOC has important consequences in multilayer graphitic systems and it should not be neglected when studying their physical properties.

authors.name: Guillermo Parra-Martinez, Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Ady Stern, Jose Angel Silva-Guill\'en, Francisco Guinea

papers.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
papers.summary: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed N\'eel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. We reveal the uniqueness of the altermagnet by comparing with the anisotropic antiferromagnet. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the N\'eel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

authors.name: Koki Mizuno

papers.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
papers.summary: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

authors.name: G. G\'orski, V. Pokorn\'y, T. Doma\'nski

papers.title: 10 kV $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
papers.summary: $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. The ON/OFF ratio increases with optical power density but exhibits a nonmonotonic bias dependence, reaching approximately 15-16 near 5-7 kV. At 10 kV, increased OFF-state conduction and non-ideal transient behavior reduce the switching contrast. These results demonstrate near-infrared photoconductive switching but also highlight critical trade-offs in photoconductive thresholds for impurity states.

authors.name: Imteaz Rahaman, Hunter Ellis, Afrouz Taherian, Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Botong Li, Berardi Sensale Rodriguez, Michael A. Scarpulla, Kai Fu

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms
papers.summary: Ab initio extensive calculations were used to simulate the atomic stages of the vapor growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors (GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb) from their components. The structural and electronic properties of the stoichiometric polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors (GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb), i.e. metal- and nonmetal-terminated were determined. Adsorption of the components was simulated, shown to be atomic. At low coverages adatoms occupy H3 sites, considerably stabilizing the surfaces, at high coverage, the adatoms are located in the skewed on-top positions creating the first layer necessary for growth (with the exception of nitrogen admolecules). The second adlayer is adsorbed differently: on a Ga-terminated surface it does not create pyramid structures due to strong interaction within the first NM adlayer, thus preventing effective growth. On NM terminated Ga covered surface the second NM adlayer atoms create a stable pyramid structure which is an effective vehicle for surface diffusion. Growth of III-V semiconductors occurs via the attachment of the pyramids to steps by glue atoms, i.e. additionally attached NM adatoms. The NM glue atom connection process requires additional electrons, which leads to strong dependence of the process and the entire growth on the Fermi level at the NM terminated surface

authors.name: Pawel Strak, Stanis{\l}aw Krukowski

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
papers.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

authors.name: Pawel Strak, Stanis{\l}aw Krukowski

papers.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
papers.summary: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $\rho T$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor. The theory is tested against molecular dynamics results for the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and the truncated and shifted Lennard-Jones (LJTS) fluids in the supercritical region, for densities up to $\rho^*=0.8$, using equations of state based on perturbation theory. For the LJTS fluid, the mean absolute percentage error is below 8\% for all the temperatures considered. For the LJ fluid, the predictions are compared with those of the revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids, using the same equation of state: TTT gives smaller errors at almost all temperatures, with a significant improvement at low temperatures, where the errors are reduced approximately by a factor between two and three.

authors.name: Miguel Hoyuelos, Alejandro Al\'es

papers.title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
papers.summary: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

authors.name: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen, Yixin Wang, Xiaoyu Guo, Keisuke Takemoto, Dusan Ivanovic, Avari Roy, Yongge Yang, Grey Christoforo, Rebekah Fraser, Seongrok Seo, John O'Sullivan, Ha Kyung Park, Jack M. Woolley, Ji-Seon Kim, Ruy S. Bonilla, Henry J. Snaith, Qing Shen, Aditya Sadhanala, Lydia H. Wong, Robert L. Z. Hoye

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
papers.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the initial site energy and the activated complex state energy. The detachment energy of the NM adatom was obtained assuming a final state in atomic and molecular form. The energy barrier for detachment to the atomic state is high for all atoms, on the order of 5 eV. For the molecular state these barriers are different: smaller for nitrogen, on the order of 1 eV, which is related to the high dissociation energy of the N2 molecule. For P and As the barrier is above 2 eV. For Sb it was not determined. Accordingly, the surface diffusion length is macroscopically large, indicating that all NM adatoms arrive at the steps.

authors.name: Pawel Strak, Stanis{\l}aw Krukowski

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
papers.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

authors.name: Pawel Strak, Stanis{\l}aw Krukowski

papers.title: The maximum packing fraction of disordered bidisperse discs: theory and predictions
papers.summary: Predicting the highest packing fraction that disordered packing of bidisperse discs can achieve, $\phi_{max}$, is an important unresolved problem. Such a predictive theory is hindered by the density dependence on the packing protocol and by ensuring disorder. In bidisperse packings, this is more complicated because $\phi_{max}$ is not a number but a function of the disc species size ratio, $D$, and one of the disc species concentration, $p$. These difficulties have been overcome in monodisperse disc packings by using the cell order distribution (COD)~\cite{Bl21}. Focusing on size ratios that prohibit rattlers, a COD-based theory is constructed here. It introduces bidisperse statistical closure equations, which combine an explicit disorder criterion with consistent cell and edge statistics, and yields $\phi_{max}(p,D)$ and structural predictions. The a-priori disorder-guaranteeing criterion proposed here ensures fast exponential a decay of the occurrence probability of ordered clusters with size. Using a constrained maximum-entropy analysis to ensure maximum disorder, the occurrence probabilities of all the possible cell and edge configurations are derived in terms of $p$ and $D$ and they are found to be binomial. All the results are assembled to yield an exact prediction of $\phi_{max}(p,D)$.

authors.name: Raphael Blumenfeld

papers.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
papers.summary: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

authors.name: Alberto Brollo

papers.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
papers.summary: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/{\pi} phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.

authors.name: Chongzhou Wang, Zhengda Jing, Weichao Yu

papers.title: Devitrification: crystal nucleation and growth mechanisms in glasses
papers.summary: If a liquid is cooled rapidly, it may fall out of equilibrium before it can crystallize. It may, however, crystallize later from the nonequilibrium glassy state. Using the Random First-Order Transition (RFOT) theory of glasses, we discuss a variety of mechanisms of crystallization as a route to devitrification. Ordinary nucleation is sped up by the frozen in energy of the glass relative to the liquid. At sufficiently low temperatures, a mechanism of nanonucleation appears, producing nanometer scale crystal inclusions in the glass. Nanocrystallization depends strongly on the local fluctuations in stability, and the transition from classical nucleation and growth to nanocrystallization occurs dominantly through rare, less stable glassy regions that percolate through space, producing an additional dramatic speedup in the crystal nucleation and growth rates. Similar fluctuations in local stability also explain anomalies of crystal growth in deeply supercooled systems.

authors.name: Max Brown, Peter Wolynes

papers.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
papers.summary: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathit{\Gamma}\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

authors.name: Hari Bhandari, Kevin Allen, Kuan-Sen Lin, Yuan Fang, Arushi, Karthik Rao, Mounica Mahankali, Sanu Mishra, Jian-Xin Zhu, Christopher Lane, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan

papers.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
